madam president! cohesion policy is the most important instrument for reducing regional disparities and promoting harmonious development throughout the european union. cohesion policy is our hope for overcoming the recession that has hit the old continent. it is therefore essential that it be sufficiently flexible, as this is the only way to take account of regional and territorial differences, and that the amount of cohesion funding in the new financial perspective be high enough to achieve the objectives pursued. as the co-rapporteur of the report by derek vaughan, i have repeatedly pointed out that in order to encourage the regions to use european funds and to enable them to implement them effectively, the procedures and administrative burdens involved need to be simplified and reduced. the rules must be clear and transparent to maximise the use of the funds. it is also very important to involve citizens more and encourage them to benefit from eu funds, inter alia by promoting community-led local development as a tool to stimulate growth, which is an opportunity to unlock the potential of civil society and local communities. i believe that now is a good time to discuss and take action to enable local cooperation mechanisms to be activated to create stability, jobs and better living conditions in their immediate environment, following the motto of the irish presidency which is 'providing stability and security leading to economic growth and increased employment in europe'. each country, region and area of the european union, both urban and rural, has unique characteristics and assets that make it competitive. we therefore need to make decisions to ensure that this potential is well exploited and that the strengths of each area of the european union are highlighted in a way that targets growth, boosts innovation and maximises the flow of knowledge and good practice between regions and countries, thereby maximising the use of eu funds.
as s&ds, we would like to draw attention to a few basic issues. first, we want to put particular emphasis on combating poverty, including energy poverty, as part of cohesion policy. the application of concrete measures from cohesion policy resources should translate into equal access for european union citizens to energy in their homes and workplaces, of course at favourable prices. secondly, we are committed to not giving up on ambitious climate policy goals. in the european union, and especially in its least developed regions, we still need new solutions based primarily on renewable sources, which are the future of energy and the basis of european competitiveness. at the same time, energy efficiency should be pursued, but the two objectives cannot be set against each other. finally, thirdly, we try to make cohesion policy as inclusive as possible and to offer a range of solutions tailored to the individual conditions and needs of each region. we support small, local power generation, but we don't want to limit funding for large power plants that produce energy from renewable sources. they are also very necessary. we also do not want to close the door on energy sources such as gas or biogas, which can and do meet local needs in the poorest regions, including rural areas. we therefore believe that cohesion policy in its energy dimension should be a package of solutions open to european diversity.

in writing. − cities are becoming centres of economic development, so maintaining their dynamism is becoming an important factor in ensuring economic growth in the eu. this is why it is so important to maintain a further increase in cohesion policy and regional development funding. it is these funds, invested in transport, broadband and the construction of new research and business hubs, that can help cities and be a strong support for the return of europe as a whole to growth. that is why i supported the report. the poor and marginalised regions and regions affected by structural poverty, such as the failure of a major, or sometimes only, industrial plant, are particularly poorly covered.
in writing. - 80% of europeans now live in urban areas and this figure is increasing. in addition, the outflow of people from rural areas to cities is also being exacerbated by the impact of the crisis, which is more difficult to 'survive' outside urban areas. cities today form extensive archipelagos which, if they are to radiate properly to other areas, must be developed in a responsible, sustainable way. one of the fundamental problems is to define the right strategy for not disrupting the functioning of the urban fabric. the migration of people from old neighbourhoods to new areas on the outskirts of cities is a cause for concern. this process often leads to the desertification of central urban areas. therefore, policies aimed at recalling the historical and symbolic value of abandoned neighbourhoods, combined with reforming housing policies, are effective in blocking worrying trends. tomorrow's problems must be thought of today. the development of new european legislation, which takes account of the achievement of medium and long-term objectives, is therefore timely. prompt support for such projects will help avoid a situation where the escalation of problems leads to the creation of much more serious challenges.
in writing. − local development is a key part of our cohesion policy since it is the level closest to the eu’s citizens. it is also at this level that the challenges we face are extremely demanding. citizens feel more attached at the local level and there exist certain intangible assets, such as historical and cultural ties and links. there are many issues that need to be addressed: energy efficiency in buildings, disposal management, migration, population ageing, etc. new approaches to urban policies are something that the eu must seriously consider. more than two thirds of the european population live in urban areas. promoting urban regeneration (the creation of wealth and opportunities) should be one of the main challenges the european union must respond to. this includes reinforcing the bond between cities and development and between urban centres and the surrounding territory. for this reason, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - a coherent policy for urban areas is a priority at the moment, as the majority of the union's population lives in cities. at the same time, the local dimension is important in this policy, as it is at this level that citizens feel more connected to the environment in which they live. the rapporteur stressed the need for local development, but also noted that, given the nature of the issue, it should be multi-faceted and cover a range of issues, as only then could it make a real contribution to economic growth.
in writing. - as you know, the world economy is slowing down. the european union is also increasingly hearing about the serious economic and financial crises in individual member countries. the standard example of a bad situation is greece, which avoided bankruptcy only because the community agreed to provide financial assistance. the draft resolution on urban development as a contribution to economic growth tells us that two thirds of the union's population live in cities. therefore, it seems to be entirely justified to promote urban centres in the fight against the economic crisis. such areas are much easier to run than the outskirts, mainly because the urban areas or areas close to them are in most cases suitably prepared for investment. i hope that the cohesion policy measures for these urban areas will at least partially fulfil their purpose, contributing to the improvement of the economic situation.
in writing. − cities are becoming centres of economic development, and maintaining their dynamism is becoming an important factor in ensuring economic growth among eu member states. this is why it is so important to maintain a further increase in cohesion policy and regional development funding. it is this money invested in transport, broadband and the construction of new research and business hubs that can support cities and be a strong support for the return of europe as a whole to growth. that is why i supported this interesting report, despite some shortcomings. the poor and marginalised regions and regions affected by structural poverty, such as the failure of a major, or sometimes only, industrial plant, are particularly poorly covered. i think it is worthwhile to supplement the document in question with the necessary records.
in writing. − i supported this own initiative report because it explores effective and efficient mechanisms to create synergies between the european funding programmes covered in the commission’s common strategic framework. i believe that integrating the delivery of funding programmes may improve the effectiveness of european funding at local and regional levels. it should also be emphasised that implementing strategies at local level should be the responsibility of local actors and authorities, with the aim of ensuring that economic and social needs are met at the level closest to the eu citizen.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr vaughan because i believe that the report he has prepared is a comprehensive and reliable document. the challenges facing europe today require efficient and effective instruments. i believe that the key issue is to reduce unemployment, especially among young people. i therefore support the proposal to clarify the rules for allocating funds to create new, sustainable jobs. i also agree with the call for improved conditions for start-ups. i believe that it is necessary to provide a flexible approach to the definition of regional and local development objectives, taking into account the specific needs and potential of each region. i believe that greater flexibility will simplify project preparation and implementation, and will help to move away from excessive bureaucracy and focus on results rather than procedures. like mr vaughan, i would like to stress the need to focus on the measurable effects of cohesion policy, to ensure the sustainability of investment and, therefore, the effectiveness of eu-funded interventions.
in writing. −this report focuses on finding effective and efficient mechanisms to create synergies between european funding programmes under the common strategic framework. personally, i support the instruments set out in the common provisions regulation (cpr) which aim to increase the size of cohesion policy, increase the focus on territorial cooperation and present a better coordinated approach at all levels of government. the changes proposed in the report address several issues such as the role of regional and local authorities in preparing, implementing and monitoring funding programmes, strengthening existing and promoting new urban-rural links, the need to better link territorial cooperation programmes with the 8 territorial strategies, the role of the joint action plan in integrating young people into the labour market, increasing the role of financial instruments in the future financial plan, integrating the common strategic framework with other eu instruments such as the horizon 2020 framework programme, life+ and the connecting europe facility. i and the s&ds believe that providing local authorities with more than one european funding programme will make project funding more efficient and easier to access.
in writing. − article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union reads: 'in order to promote the harmonious development of the union as a whole, the union shall develop and pursue actions aimed at strengthening its economic, social and territorial cohesion.' the territorial cohesion referred to in that article is the result of the last treaty amendment, linked to the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. territorial cohesion requires greater involvement of local and regional authorities at every stage of planning, development and implementation of european programmes. the report by derek vaughan also makes a strong case for ensuring that member states, local and regional authorities can benefit from more than one european funding programme. its implementation should contribute to making european funds more efficient, simplifying them further and making it easier for potential beneficiaries to access funding. this is particularly important in the coming years, when cohesion policy will play a major role in the european union's crisis management policy. in these circumstances, cohesion policy funds must be used in an optimal way. europe cannot afford to waste or overspend. in view of these circumstances, i have decided to support the report by mr vaughan.
in writing. - cohesion policy is one of the most important objectives pursued by the european union. the main objective of this policy is to promote measures which lead to a level playing field in the social and economic conditions of all the member states of the community. particular emphasis shall be placed on reducing disparities at regional level and on eliminating the backwardness of the least favoured areas, including rural areas. the main instruments for implementing cohesion policy are the operational programmes in the form of grants to regions in the european union. in the current economic downturn, a cohesion policy for the financial perspective could be the panacea for the current crisis. however, the very important issue raised by the rapporteur is simplification and the use of a more results-oriented approach. providing beneficiaries with the possibility of benefiting from more than one european programme could also be an additional factor in improving the situation in individual regions. i believe that such actions will make a significant contribution to reducing economic and social disparities between regions in the period 2014-2020.
in writing. - cohesion policy is the european union's most important tool in dealing with the crisis. it is a pro-innovation, pro-social tool that strongly supports investment and economic development. it is therefore so important to continue and extend it, and these objectives can only be met by developing its funding in a new perspective for 2014-2020. the report voted on today is a very good reflection of the developmental nature of cohesion policy, especially in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. unfortunately, it does not cover all the barriers that prevent it from reaching its full potential. such a barrier is certainly the excessive limits on co-financing of investments from the budget of the member state or the investor. in the new perspective, this problem should be solved. this will allow more resources to be committed to developing production capacity and freeing up funds for much-needed investments in europe. increasing them is the most important way to achieve greater territorial cohesion and to overcome the inequalities that have plagued europe since the beginning of its post-war division into two zones.
in writing. − in its 10 years of operation, the solidarity fund has provided financial assistance to tackle the consequences of 49 natural disasters. it is therefore an important mechanism to support citizens in crisis situations. however, the number of applications for fund support has been steadily increasing in recent times. the reform aimed at simplifying and making the rules on eligibility more transparent, based on experience, should take into account the improvement of the effectiveness of the fund itself. of course, the proposals to reduce administrative procedures are noteworthy, and will greatly reduce the time needed to respond to a natural disaster. it should be noted that most of the applications submitted concerned disasters of regional scope, of which a significant number were rejected. it therefore seems important to clarify the rules for granting aid to individual regions, taking into account their level of prosperity. i support the report in the hope that it will improve the functioning of the fund.
in writing. − the eu solidarity fund, set up in 2002 to provide financial support to countries affected by major natural disasters, is an important instrument for helping member states in crisis situations. this fund deserves recognition. it is intended to show solidarity with the people living in regions affected by major disasters, and to provide concrete financial assistance and the necessary support in such difficult times, as was the case for example in the italian republic, which was hit by the earthquake in may 2012. however, the changing circumstances, including the financial crisis, and the analysis of the fund's past activities require some modifications, which is why i support the draft report by mrs rosas estaràs ferragut on the amendment of the current eu solidarity fund regulation. i hope that the proposed changes will help to improve its functioning and efficiency without generating additional costs, so that it will be an even better tool for assisting member states affected by major natural disasters.
in writing. − the european solidarity fund has repeatedly proved to be an excellent instrument for helping regions affected by natural disasters. in 2009, poland, the czech republic, and hungary were hit by floods that caused millions of dollars in damage. in 2010, the solidarity fund allocated over eur 100 million to help the affected regions. thanks to community funds and state budgetary support, poland has been able to develop its flood protection and early warning systems. in order to continue to operate actively, the fund must be guaranteed a stable funding.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs rosa estaras ferragut. i believe that the solidarity fund is an extremely important and well-received instrument of the european union, but it is necessary to improve its effectiveness. i agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to improve administrative procedures and to introduce the possibility of making advance payments after the state has lodged an aid application. it is also necessary to clearly define the scope of the fund's activities, to define the term 'disaster' at regional level and to define the criteria for qualifying disasters, taking into account the difference between natural and man-made disasters. but above all, i agree with ms ferragut that focusing on disaster prevention is the cheapest way to reduce risk.
in writing. − the european solidarity fund, which represents the principle of solidarity under the lisbon treaty, is an instrument of great importance, not only because of the concrete financial benefits for regions affected by natural disasters. this instrument is a perfect example of the union's solidarity as an institution and a community with citizens in difficulty. as with all newly introduced union instruments, it is important to ensure that the fund functions properly and does not cause bureaucratic problems. in particular, in the face of unpredictable and changing problems, such as climate change, such as the scale and specificity of natural disasters, the instruments should be regularly monitored and improved. i therefore agree with the amendments proposed by the rapporteur. improving the efficiency, flexibility and efficiency of the fund by simplifying bureaucratic processes is essential, especially in cases requiring an immediate response. i agree with the idea of clarifying the definition and scope of the fund in order to improve the functioning of the fund. it is also a response to the current economic situation and the related concerns of many member states. the proposed reform will make the instrument more effective, allowing for more effective and faster assistance to citizens who are affected.
in writing. - the solidarity fund was set up to enable a rapid response to major natural disasters. it is also an example of european solidarity towards the people of the community affected by the aforementioned disasters. the creation of the fund was prompted by the floods that hit central europe in 2002. the main task of the solidarity fund is to repair damage that is not covered by insurance. so it's road infrastructure, water, sewerage, or telecommunications. the increasingly frequent and violent weather events show that the solidarity fund is urgently needed. as the rapporteur stressed, the solidarity fund is one of the european union's most valued instruments. i hope that in the future the fund will fulfil its tasks, at least to the same extent as in the past.
in writing. − the european solidarity fund has repeatedly proved to be an excellent instrument for helping regions affected by natural disasters. in 2009, after heavy rains, poland, the czech republic, and hungary were hit by floods that caused millions of dollars in damage. in 2010, the european parliament allocated over €100 million to help the affected regions. thanks to community funds and state budgetary support, poland has been able to develop its flood protection and early warning systems. to continue to operate actively, the fund must be guaranteed a steady source of funding, outside the uncertain eu budget, which will give it the certainty and stability to operate in any, often unpredictable, conditions. there should also be the possibility of accumulating contributions from subsequent years.
in writing. - more than two years after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the issue of good administration in article 298 is the only new article in the treaty on which the commission has not taken any action. the initiative to create a uniform administrative law applicable to the union's institutions and bodies was the subject of a special working group set up within the parliament's legal affairs committee on 23 march 2010. the focus was on administrative procedures and on creating a minimum safety net by providing guarantees for citizens and businesses in direct contact with the administration. this initiative was approved by the legal affairs committee in a working document on 21 november. now further steps are needed to ensure that this project is properly implemented, and i therefore call on the european commission to present binding legislative proposals in this area. i also agree that such legislation should be confined to the direct administration of the union and should apply as a lex generalis to all the union institutions and all areas of union activity. the introduction of practical, general rules of procedure will contribute to greater transparency and understanding of the law and to increased trust of citizens in the union administration.
in writing. − the conduct of the european administration is governed by a variety of codes of conduct and lex specialis, resulting in a lack of harmonisation of the basic standards which are applied in respect of good governance. as, more and more often, citizens and businesses are engaging directly with the european union’s administration in the course of their daily activities, the eu must find new solutions which would improve the legal certainty and clarity for the citizens and businesses concerned when they are dealing with the european administration in its many forms. this extends across a great number of sectors, and particularly applies in areas where european agencies have been given responsibilities covering industrial practices and thus businesses are directly impacted by their activities. i believe that the european administration should be held accountable according to the important principles of good governance and transparency, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − administrative procedure in the union is characterised by the principle of institutional and procedural autonomy, i.e. in the absence of a rule of community law, proceedings for claims arising from community law are governed by national law. this means that member states can determine the structure of the bodies themselves and decide on the procedural rules to be applied. to improve relations between citizens and administrations, the right to good administration, i.e. to an effective and independent administration, based on the principles of european legislation on administrative procedures, should be established. i hope that the establishment of the principles of good administration will create a minimum number of basic procedural rules that the administration should apply when dealing with cases. the creation of new rules should be based primarily on principles such as transparency and accountability, which will result in increased public trust in the administration.

in writing. - i voted for the report on company restructuring, information and management of employees for a number of reasons. it is fortunate that this matter has been favourably received by a large part of the european parliament. in a period of weak economic growth, we should create a law aimed at improving the economic situation. we need to build a stronger framework for business operations and a more stable future for workers. ensure that employees are informed of the changes, receive training, and are facilitated in their transition, and that dismissals are treated as a last resort. without such guarantees, workers' rights cannot be effectively protected. i support the solutions developed in the committee on employment and social affairs, because they will improve the situation of businesses and workers in the member states in a practical way. let us not forget that a well-executed restructuring is first and foremost about more competitive companies, a more secure market and more skilled workers. the creation of rigid rules restricting restructuring would have the opposite effect. let's remember that the process of change is the way to fight the crisis. let's do it flexibly, but responsibly.

in writing. the ongoing crisis of confidence in financial markets has shown the extent to which countries' credit ratings affect the perception of their financial credibility. the european parliament today said that, given the significant implications for financial stability, there is a need for much better regulation of the activities of credit rating agencies, particularly in terms of the quality of credit ratings and the timing and frequency of their publication. credit rating agencies will now be required to provide a timetable for publication in advance, and the publication of credit ratings will be permitted only after markets are closed. increased restrictions on the quality of methodologies and the obligation to limit references to external ratings in community law should in future counteract the rapid and cascading reactions of financial institutions to changes in credit ratings by credit rating agencies. it is also worth noting that the package of regulations adopted today also introduces new quality in areas such as the civil liability of credit rating agencies towards investors, the reduction of conflicts of interest in the 'issuer pays' model, and the ownership structure of credit rating agencies.

in writing. − on 16 january, meps adopted a new revised calendar for 2013, returning to the practice of 12 plenary sessions of equal length to be held in strasbourg. i do not hide the fact that this is a failure of the strategy of establishing a single seat for the european parliament. the modification of the calendar was necessary following a ruling of the european court of justice of 13 december 2012 which annulled the amendments to the calendar of plenary sessions for 2012 and 2013 voted by parliament on 9 march 2011. the dispute concerned the establishment of two two-day sessions instead of four in october, which was to meet the requirements of holding 12 plenary sessions in strasbourg. this solution, which was considered to be in line with the procedure, was to allow for considerable savings, since the maintenance of the three separate establishments is estimated to cost up to eur 180 million. unfortunately, the french and luxembourg governments opposed the savings by bringing an action to annul our 2012 and 2013 work calendars before the court, which ruled that the 12 ordinary plenary sessions per month must be of the same length and reiterated that only member states have the right to change the seat of the institution. to change this absurd situation, we must continue to make a strong case and persuade the member states to make the necessary changes to the treaties to allow the european parliament to have a single seat.
in writing. − the existing dangerous goods directive regulates the classification, packaging and labelling of preparations consisting of two or more chemical substances. in particular, the distribution of hazardous materials requires precise rules and labelling to ensure that it is carried out in a proper manner and without endangering citizens and the environment. the adoption of the lisbon treaty has led to a number of provisions requiring updating and adaptation, including the issues covered in this report. the proposed changes are not political but are merely the result of commitments made by the states. i voted in favour of the resolution, hoping to strengthen the protection needed in the trade in chemicals.
in writing. − the rules on the packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations and substances are designed to protect health and the environment. the creation of such provisions was also intended to allow for a freer flow of such goods. however, the continuous change of the rules, including the treaties, has meant that the 2008 regulation needs to be amended. in addition, new legislation in this area will be compatible with the system comprising the un globally harmonised system.
in writing. − the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources is primarily about protecting individual fish species against 'predatory' fishing policies. it is also an opportunity to create long-term profitability in the fisheries sector. to ensure the harmonious development of the industry in europe, the european union has developed a series of rules governing access to community waters and, most importantly, the exploitation of resources and the reduction of fishing effort. of course, some communities may be opposed to the introduction of fishing restrictions because they say it could reduce their income. however, i hope that the changes adopted will contribute to improving the fisheries policy management system by better integrating fishermen and that the so-called ecosystem approach to fisheries will have a positive impact on the overall protection of the marine environment.

in writing. − the cartagena protocol is the first international agreement to regulate the transboundary movement of genetically modified organisms. the main aim of the protocol is to regulate international trade and the handling and use of genetically modified organisms that could have adverse effects on human health. i hope that the conclusion of the nagoi/kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and compensation will make a significant contribution to raising the level of safety for human health and to achieving the objectives of the said protocol and the convention on biological diversity.
in writing. − the cartagena protocol, which entered into force in 2003, is an additional agreement to the 1993 convention on biological diversity and provides a safety framework for the transport and use of living modified organisms (lmos). it provides for the provision of information to states to enable them to take an appropriate decision on the authorisation of the introduction of those organisms into their territory and provides for the establishment of a biosafety clearing-house. the nagoya supplementary protocol adopted in 2010 sets out the rules and procedures for liability for damage caused by living modified organisms. they indicate the appropriate course of action in the event of a threat to biodiversity and human health. in the european union, these regulations fall within the scope of directive 2004/35/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 2004, which applied the 'polluter pays' principle, according to which environmental damage is paid for by the entity that caused it. the precautionary principle, which is the main message of the cartagena protocol, remains the overriding principle of european biosafety legislation. i support the rapporteur's position and the council's decision to sign the nagoya/kuala lumpur supplementary protocol and hope that it will be ratified by all countries in a timely manner.
in writing. − the cartagena protocol is the first international agreement to regulate the transboundary movement of genetically modified organisms. the main aim of the protocol is to regulate international trade and the handling and use of genetically modified organisms that could have adverse effects on human health. i hope that the conclusion of the nagorno-karabakh additional protocol on liability and reparation will make a significant contribution to raising the level of safety for human health and to achieving the objectives of the said protocol and the convention on biological diversity.
mr. chairman, please! it is a fact that for the third time in the last two years the european parliament has stooped down and dealt with the activities of the credit rating agencies. this is not only a sign of the complexity of the problem, but also of the fact that we are not yet able to restore full credibility to these institutions. i emphasize the word credibility on purpose, because credit rating agencies should be and unfortunately they are not always institutions of trust. the regulation, in my view, is a regulation that is moving in the right direction. these are good guidelines, but i would like to point out that this regulation does not solve all the problems associated with the functioning of these agencies. still, it deserves our support.
in writing. − this is the third piece of eu legislation concerning credit rating agencies (cras) since the beginning of the economic crisis. cras are widely blamed for having erroneously giving good ratings for many us mortgage-backed securities. the activities of cras have a far-reaching impact of the behaviour of economic and financial players and on the life of public institutions. i share the opinion that their ratings should be treated as information to take into account and that the agencies themselves should not enjoy special status or automatically influence the activities of economic and financial operators and public institutions. i voted in favour of this report, but i would like to draw attention to the fact that the new sovereign ratings rules (that limit the number of times a cra may issue a rating to three times a year) which are meant to decrease volatility (as certain rating downgrades have caused turmoil in the markets) may actually increase volatility because they may necessitate more severe downgrades. this may also limit the freedom of cras to act on their best judgement as to when ratings should be modified. this is something that we must monitor closely.
in writing. − the financial crisis in europe has shown that the recommendations of credit rating agencies cannot always be relied upon. many financial institutions have taken these recommendations as guidelines in their decisions, and they have been proven wrong, and they have caused chaos in the market. this is a serious problem because it has not only disrupted the financial market, but it has also undermined the agency's credibility. i therefore agree with the assumption that the recommendations of credit rating agencies should be treated with much more caution and not as a self-evident oracle. the credit risk assessment of the credit rating agency should be verified by the entity and the entity should formulate its own credit risk assessment. no one should exempt economic operators from carrying out their own analyses and from taking responsibility for their own decisions. i support the draft directive of the european parliament and of the council, because it rightly emphasises this aspect of the decision-making process.
in writing. − cod is one of the most fished species in the baltic sea and is of great economic importance, making regulation of cod fishing a priority fisheries issue and a major political issue in the baltic states. the cod is equally valuable to the european union as a whole, with its fisheries accounting for almost 10% of the community's total catch over the last decade (70,000 tonnes, up from over 700,000 in 2004). that is why it is so important that we constantly monitor the state of cod in the baltic and that we keep the rules on fishing standards up to date. the proposal concerns the 2007 long-term plan for cod and cod fisheries and suggests amendments which aim, inter alia, to adapt the regulation to the current cod stocks, to adapt the catch limits to the recommendations in force in the relevant geographical areas or to adapt the legislative procedures to the current rules. it also introduces a regulation allowing small-scale coastal fishing during protection periods, which does not have a negative impact on spawning grounds, which will improve the economic situation of the fishing fleets in the member states.
in writing. − although this is an alignment report following the new comitology procedure set out in the lisbon treaty (delegated vs. implementing acts), the rapporteur decided to go beyond the scope of a simple alignment and introduced some changes that aim to make the cod management plan in the baltic more flexible and compatible with the most recent scientific recommendations. it is for this reason that the rapporteur proposes, among other, to increase temporarily the fishing mortality rate for baltic cod stocks. this and other modifications included in the report are justified in light of the commission's inability to come up with a new long-promised management plan for cod in the baltic sea. for this reason, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr jarosław wałęsa because i think it is a very good document, taking account of both the new legal situation introduced by the lisbon treaty and the increase in cod stocks in the baltic sea. i think it is beneficial to allow small-scale cod fishing also during the closed season, especially during the summer months. i believe that this is an important solution from the point of view of the local economy and that it can have a positive impact on the economic situation of many coastal enterprises, often small family businesses, thus contributing to the improvement of the living standards of local communities. i agree with the rapporteur on the amendment of the legislative procedure. the multiannual plans are the most important element of the regulation and should therefore be amended, if necessary, by the ordinary legislative procedure. in addition, the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries and the baltic sea regional advisory committee should be involved in the evaluation process of the multiannual plan. i also believe it is extremely important that any future changes be implemented in cooperation with the social and economic partners. i believe that the entry into force of the regulation, with the amendments proposed by the rapporteur, will contribute to improving the exploitation of cod resources, both economically, socially and environmentally.

in writing. − the possible introduction of stabilisation bonds in any form will be a landmark decision in the history of economic and monetary integration. thus, the discussion on the form, assumptions and potential action plan should be based on reliable data and objective simulations. in my opinion, the recommendations in the report by mrs goulard go too far. it is not possible today, given our current state of knowledge, to say that the introduction of eurobonds is crucial to the recovery of the euro area. all we know today is that a common bond issuance system can be either beneficial or harmful, depending on the design assumptions adopted. that's far too little to make a definite judgment. i expected the resolution to call on the european commission to develop a comprehensive feasibility study for this idea, without evaluation. by defining priority actions, the report limits the commission's flexibility and unjustifiably narrows the range of possible solutions within the concept of debt communalisation. i think that this approach does not allow us to build a stable political support for this concept, even in its least revolutionary form.
in writing. − eurobonds, or as some call them, stability bonds, are nothing more than securities in which the issuer (i.e. in this case a euro area country) states that it is the debtor of the bond. the issuer (i.e. the debtor) commits itself to the obligor to make a specific service in the future, namely to buy back the bonds in question. the idea of issuing eurobonds is now gaining more and more support, especially in countries where public finances are at risk. the so-called nordic countries (france and germany) are concerned that the issuance of these bonds will increase the cost of servicing their debt. it seems that at this point, the issuance of european bonds could create a debt that europe would not know how to get out of. an additional factor against emissions is that countries like greece and spain will slow down their public finance reforms. therefore, the introduction of eurobonds is not a good solution at the moment.

in writing. i'm concerned about the rights of the passengers. some airlines change the rules for using their services at will. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 30 june 2012 and that the agreement with ryanair was signed on 1 july 2012. sometimes luggage gets lost or arrives after a few days. the additional problem is the creation of limits related to the weight, size and type of hand luggage. the simplest terms are changed to mislead the passenger. one day, hand luggage means one thing, the next, something completely different. the changes, the mistakes, the customer pays for them. statistics show that during the global crisis, network carriers in europe experienced a decrease in passenger numbers, while low-cost carriers experienced an increase. in 2010-2011, it was as high as 10%. this tendency is very thought-provoking. according to studies, the share of low-cost airlines in the european market could reach up to 50% by 2020. let's support business growth, but at the same time protect consumer rights. we cannot allow airlines to create confusion and mislead their customers. passengers should be given true information about their rights and be able to appeal quickly and effectively. in europe, there must be a uniform concept of hand luggage. let's just call it one definition. this will increase the transparency and quality of air transport use.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. first of all, i would like to thank and congratulate mrs ulrice rodust for the enormous amount of work she has put into this difficult report. the compromise reached shows the extraordinary commitment of the rapporteur. the need to reform the common fisheries policy is felt by all: fishermen, processors, the coastal community and the environment. the current common fisheries policy overshadows the concept of central management of resources without taking account of the specific characteristics of individual waters. the most significant and incomprehensible effect of the current common fisheries policy is the waste of thousands of tonnes of healthy fish by the discarding of discards. this is the biggest paradox of the common fisheries policy, which contributes to the degradation of the environment and the fishing industry. the common fisheries policy is based on several basic pillars. the main one is regionalization, which will shape the rules for individual waters to a much greater extent than in the past. it is worth mentioning here the weakness of the lisbon treaty, which makes it impossible to carry out full regionalisation, which confirms the need for changes. the second essential element of the common fisheries policy is to leave the decision on fishing rights to the member states. mandating the european commission to sell quotas would be extremely damaging to the future of fisheries and create private waters where resources would have only financial value. another element of the common policy is the protection of small-scale fisheries, which are mainly family businesses and are particularly sensitive to the preservation of the common market. for many coastal areas, small-scale fishing offers the opportunity to create many, many jobs while maintaining a sustainable approach. the last element is aquaculture, which must complement the fishing industry and its development significantly increases the labour market. the new common fisheries policy creates opportunities for aquaculture. at the same time, i want to say that the ecr group will support the report under discussion.
in writing. the reform of the common fisheries policy, which is being negotiated in parliament, will improve the state of the environment and the situation of fishermen in the european union. the introduction of a binding ban on overfishing and the stopping of fish overfishing is a great achievement of parliament, and in particular of the socialist group. the european union needs reform that will protect and save the environment from destruction, while ensuring decent incomes for the fisheries and fish processing sectors. overfishing is not just a problem for the environment, but also for fishermen and consumers. the reason for the disadvantage of the former is the setting of fishing quotas. each year, the fisheries ministers of the member states set the quotas too high, often simply to avoid losing their electorate. parliament's negotiators have, however, managed to reach a compromise that will ensure that the reform is not just a vague promise to improve the situation of fishermen, but also to provide consumers with easier and cheaper access to fish. since the last reform of the common fisheries policy 10 years ago, the subject has been developing slowly. the council makes more rational decisions. the reform we have supported today goes a step further by committing member states to a sustainable and rationalised fixing of quotas. the introduction of maximum sustainable yield from 2015 will help protect our seas from overfishing and provide a sense of stability for fishermen and consumers.
in writing. thank you for your vote and thank you to mrs rodust and all the co-rapporteurs for their work on this important report. unfortunately, despite the long hours of work, it is still not sustainable, especially when it comes to the implementation of environmental legislation. i believe that there is a hierarchy between fisheries policy and environmental protection, although they should be on an equal footing. for example, you cannot make money from the european maritime and fisheries fund dependent on the administrative efficiency of the ministry of the environment. and such provisions to the disadvantage of fishermen will appear in mrs rodust's report. another very important issue is regionalization, i.e. fisheries management at regional level, taking into account the specificities of individual waters. the reform should contribute to the separation of roles in this area. the eu legislators will define the main legal framework and basic principles, while the actual implementing decisions will be taken at a lower level, closer to the fisheries reality. regionalization should be a pillar of the reform of the common fisheries policy. unfortunately, the shape proposed by the rapporteur is unsatisfactory. in the vote on wednesday, i will support the idea of reform and i will vote for mrs rodust's report. i would like to stress, however, that i do not think that the report is optimal. i will support it, however, because it is the european parliament's position on the reform of the cap and it is the starting point for further negotiations. but i expect it to be greatly improved in the next stages of development.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. this regulation provides agricultural measures that are intended to address the challenges faced by those farming on greek islands in the aegean sea (with the exception of crete and evia). the measures included in this regulation have two key aims: assist with the additional costs involved in transporting certain agricultural products between the islands and the mainland and foster the development of local production, cultural heritage and traditional characteristics of production methods. it is important to remember that the particularly difficult farming conditions on the smaller aegean islands are being compounded by external pressures as a result of illegal migration. the dispersal of the islands and their position in relation to each other within the archipelago creates obstacles to supply and trade, resulting in greatly increased transport costs. existing transport networks are inadequate and undermined by structural weaknesses (ageing fleets, high fares).
in writing. - the aegean islands are divided into several archipelagos. most of them belong to greece. this fragmentation of the area increases the cost of transportation in food supplies and trade. additional problems are high fees and an outdated fleet. moreover, the lack of raw materials, as well as the unusual geophysical location (the union's external borders) and climate (dry, rocky soils) further exacerbate the problems of the local population. the supply of basic products to the inhabitants of the smaller aegean islands is therefore an important issue in the context of the aid granted by the european community. of course, this aid is implemented by the greek institutions with the approval of the european commission. however, it should also be considered to apply this aid to such an extent that it is compatible with community law and policies (given, however, the poor experience in this area in the past). i am thinking mainly of the common agricultural policy. i hope that the forces and resources that are being deployed in that region will have a positive impact on the lives of the communities there.

in writing. − smes are economic operators, regardless of their legal form. the main factors determining whether a company can be considered an sme are the number of employees and the annual turnover or the total annual balance sheet. thus, medium-sized enterprises are those with fewer than 250 employees and an annual turnover of less than eur 50 million or an annual balance sheet total of less than eur 43 million. small enterprises are those with fewer than 50 employees, an annual turnover of eur 10 million or a total annual balance sheet of less than eur 10 million. the sme sector is one of the economic pillars of the european union. currently, around 67% of the union's workforce is employed in smes. in the current difficult economic downturn, it is much more difficult for small firms to operate in the market than their larger counterparts. this is because it is much more difficult to obtain credit for further development in the face of a crisis, especially when it comes to the development of an innovative company, which often requires a large financial outlay. the growing unemployment, particularly in the peripheral countries of the european union, can raise anxiety and concern about the future of the community. therefore, the aid to access finance for the sector in question appears justified. because only by creating new jobs can europe emerge from the economic crisis with a strong hand.
in writing. - the sme sector has been going through a difficult period recently. the shifting of production and the progressive deindustrialisation of europe are reducing the number of orders and weakening the trade and intermediation sector, which are the driving force behind the whole sector. moreover, the crisis has deprived smes of previously saved financial resources. that is why the union must send a clear message today, a signal of support. the provision that 20% of the funding from horizon 2020 is to be allocated to boosting innovation and smes is certainly one of them. i think that's a good thing to do.
madam president! i would like to support the report by mr schwab. although parliament has already called twice for a deeper single market, the european institutions are still not doing enough. there are still a number of cumbersome administrative burdens. the fewer obstacles entrepreneurs and jobseekers face, the faster and more efficiently the community market will develop. i would remind you that this is a key mechanism for economic growth, which translates directly into jobs. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new legislation. a more efficient rate of transposition would bring significant savings. full implementation of the services directive alone is estimated to generate a gain of 2.6% of eu gdp. the alignment of legislation in this area is beneficial for national economies, competitiveness and consumers. the current disparities imply difficulties for entrepreneurs seeking to raise capital. the single market is conducive to the development of innovation and it is therefore necessary to regulate the free flow of knowledge. scientific exchange, openness to inspiration and the universality and accessibility of achievements, especially in the field of modern technologies, are essential for raising the standard of living in the countries of the union. the increasingly widespread exchange of goods and services on the internet is a stimulus to the economy. the effect of moving a business to the internet is to increase its area and productivity. the elimination of barriers on this plane should be intensified.
madam president, i do not share the views of my predecessor and i am not at all despairing of european policies on this matter. of course, we have to face the crisis together, and the stability and growth pact must help us to do so. we must get out of the crisis. to this end, investment policies are extremely important. i must also say that growth policies did not wait until 2012 to be put in place, since as early as 2010, in the will we drew up for this europe 2020 policy, we already talked about building growth. but the real problem is the return to work or the fight against the weakening of the employment of the employees who are working today. i would like to draw your attention, in the european semester policy, to the fact that we must be extremely careful in supporting the european social fund. as rapporteur, i would draw your attention to the fact that the european social fund is the political lever for the return to employment of the most vulnerable. that is why i am advocating that we should all be mobilized, that 25% of the cohesion funds should be directed towards social cohesion, otherwise we will miss the target. i must therefore say that if we are to combat the social crisis, if we are to invest and stimulate growth, it is through the social fund that we must preserve these policies and that 25% of the cohesion funds must be allocated to social policies. we could not possibly pursue policies which support employment in europe and our efforts would be useless if we did not have this firm and determined will.
madam president! we know from the reports, analyses and observations in the regions that as the crisis deepens, poverty levels and various forms of social exclusion increase. increasingly, these problems are affecting working people as well. the situation is particularly dire for young people. the unemployment rate reached 20% and in some countries as high as 50%. many economists are critical of the union's implementation of crisis management methods that focus, and often limit, to reducing debt and budget deficits. not only do they fail to deliver the expected results, but they also exacerbate social problems, especially among the most vulnerable. with regard to the european semester, it is worth noting that both rapporteurs, from the committee on employment and social affairs and the committee on monetary affairs, note the negative impact of consolidation on economic growth. interestingly, even the monetary committee recommends delaying and limiting the fiscal consolidation path. i think it is high time that the next six-monthly guidelines give top priority to job creation. cohesion policy is the tool that makes this possible.
madam president! the internal market has enormous potential, but it is not yet exploited, and it is our task to tap into that potential. the single market is a means of improving competitiveness and achieving economic growth in the union. the single market rules are already quite extensive and the main emphasis should therefore be firmly on their enforcement and implementation. unfortunately, the data show that member states are far behind in transposing eu law. insufficient implementation of the rules results in the creation of barriers to the internal market and the failure to exploit its potential. i welcome the commission's efforts to improve the governance of the internal market, but i agree with the rapporteur that they should be even more ambitious, especially in terms of coordination or the introduction of the 'single market test'. priorities for implementation and monitoring are also needed. while it is clear that all legislation needs to be properly implemented, the focus for the immediate future should be on issues of importance to the economy and overall growth. i think it is a very good way to look at the internal market in the context of the european semester, because it will make it easier to identify the obstacles still faced in this market and to monitor progress. i'm sure the individual approach is a huge factor. each member state should be looked at individually and solutions tailored to the problems encountered. it will be more effective to define recommendations for each member state separately, as this approach will better highlight the real problems.
madam president! the high and rising rate of unemployment in the european union, especially among young people, is a very worrying phenomenon and requires mobilization and action by all actors involved. the measures taken so far are not producing the visible and expected results. a coherent approach is needed, combining both smart fiscal consolidation that does not jeopardise investment in future growth, and sound macroeconomic policies and active employment strategies that ensure social cohesion. the fontagné report lists a number of actions that member states should take to actively involve themselves in the fight against unemployment and job creation. i would like to draw particular attention to those activities which are aimed at young people. i believe that a range of tax breaks and business start-up aid can be an opportunity for young entrepreneurs who want to use their talents and make a living from them. support for smes will undoubtedly also indirectly help young people. research shows that jobs that could be filled by young people with little work experience are created primarily within existing enterprises. reform of labour markets, which will also include improving the efficiency of public employment services and developing a system of individual career guidance, will be an important element in supporting jobseekers. in conclusion, i would like to mention once again the fundamental element that will contribute to the actual integration of people into the labour market, namely effective cooperation between employers, governments and educational institutions.
the european semester, the process of informing member states of draft national budgets and subsequent recommendations by the european commission, is an important element of the economic governance of the european union. i agree with the previous speakers that we should be careful not to forget the common market in this management. the report which will be put to the vote tomorrow aims to make the management of the european single market an important part of the semester. the semester should contain clear recommendations for deepening the common market and better implementing the directives. it should also contain recommendations for member states on how to do this better. all this is necessary so that citizens and businesses can feel firsthand that the european project benefits us all, because the single market concerns us all. and that's why it's so important that it's not missing from national budgets. and member states should adopt a broader perspective than just their own. it is worth considering, when designing the budget, whether the so-called gilding of the provisions of the directive does not bring more harm than good. does the addition of obligations to undertakings in national legislation going beyond the directive help or hinder competition in the common market, a market of 500 million citizens? a good test of this will be the implementation of the consumer directive in the member states, which should take place by the end of the year. and i hope that all member states will succeed in keeping the spirit of this directive, and the spirit is to simplify consumer law and to contribute to increasing sales, to ensuring the safety of buyers, especially online. this requires a more european approach. i wish the member states and the european commission courage and a profound european approach to this matter.

to combat the economic crisis and the resulting unemployment, it is not enough to take sensible action in the fiscal field, nor is it enough to design the budgets of individual countries in a sensible way. it is necessary to take measures to limit the over-regulation of the economies of individual countries of the european union. unfortunately, the efforts of the european commission and the european parliament sometimes backfire. their intentions are noble - they are about improving the functioning of the economy, simplifying - but unfortunately this often leads to completely different effects, to greater complications, to much higher operating costs, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. this has negative consequences, which is why we need to do everything we can to simplify the economy and reduce over-regulation. it will also make a significant contribution to the positive development of the european economy.
in writing. the annual growth survey aims to identify economic priorities for 2013 and marks the beginning of the european semester procedure, which is intended to contribute to better coordination of member states' economic policies so that their objectives are in line with the stability and growth pact. the main message of the growth analysis is that while ad hoc anti-crisis measures are starting to deliver positive effects in terms of deficit reduction and financial market sentiment, continued reforms are essential to achieve sustainable growth and job creation in the long term. the five priorities identified by the commission as key to overcoming the crisis and restoring growth, namely diversified and smart fiscal consolidation; restoring normal lending to the economy; promoting growth and competitiveness; tackling unemployment; and modernising public administration, should be positively assessed. at the same time, in the report prepared by the econ committee, we call on the commission to put forward concrete proposals in the report to be presented to the european council, in addition to the strategy for implementing sustainable fiscal discipline, to promote private investment, to improve the efficiency of tax systems and to create jobs. the need for structural labour market reforms to increase the flexibility needed to effectively mitigate shocks and reduce youth unemployment by better matching skills to labour demand has become particularly evident in recent times.

on behalf of the ppe group. the budget of the european parliament and the other institutions is a very small part of the budget of the european union, but there is certainly room for savings. in times of crisis, each of us must cut back on our spending. this also applies to the european parliament itself. it should be made clear that over the last few years the ep's budget has been reduced in real terms. we have achieved this by reorganising parliamentary work, in particular by cutting travel costs, by reducing the duration and number of business trips, by increasing the use of videoconferencing and other similar tools, and by optimising translation services. to give two examples: we have frozen all the benefits for members at the 2011 level until the end of the current term. contrary to what is often reported, we are not sparing the parliamentary administration either. for example, staff travel allowances have not been revalued since 2007. we are planning further savings over the coming year, particularly in the area of translation, but this is very important without prejudice to the principle of multilingualism, which is very important in this parliament. similar activities - in writing. – decreasing our expenditure is one way to show solidarity with our citizens during these times of financial instability. it is now agreed by most leaders that austerity and cuts alone are insufficient to tackle the crisis, and that more attention should be placed on measures to stimulate growth. in this respect i welcome the 2014 budgetary guidelines, which continue to follow the approach of the previous year, trying to strike a balance between austerity and growth. the report calls on parliament to identify more areas where structural changes can be introduced, making our organisation more efficient and less costly. yet it fails to mention one area where a structural reform could lead to real savings: namely, parliament’s multiple working places. the financial cost of maintaining three places of work is estimated at eur 180 million per year. the additional cost of maintaining the working places in luxembourg and strasbourg is set at eur 148 million. these figures represent potential annual savings that could be reinvested instead in programmes for boosting job creation, expanding research and development, and other schemes to help us overcome the current crisis and restore economic growth in europe.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased to have had the opportunity today to debate two excellent reports on the subject of corporate social responsibility, and i congratulate the two rapporteurs, mr baldassarre and mr howitt, on their work. the adoption of these resolutions is the positive conclusion of a debate which we started more than a year ago with the communication from the european commission. it was october 2011, and it had already been formally accepted by the council. the adoption of the resolutions before this house today will also send a strong signal that the european institutions are on the same page on this important subject: the commission, the council and parliament have one vote. europe needs an ambitious policy in this area, that of social responsibility, because it is in the interests of companies, citizens and investors and also in the interests of the proper functioning of our social market economy. socially responsible enterprises are also the most competitive in the medium and long term, create quality jobs and are more innovative and also generate higher levels of confidence in the economy. i agree with mr baldassarre that the new definition of csr proposed by the commission overcomes the old opposition between voluntary and compulsory action, and brings greater coherence with major policy developments at national, european and global levels. while we recognize the role that certain legislative instruments can and should play in promoting csr in specific cases, we do not believe that legislation is the preferred policy instrument for all aspects of csr. as far as small and mediumsized enterprises are concerned, the commission wishes to avoid any unnecessary increase in administrative burdens. for example, we have rightly avoided proposing a new set of principles at european level, preferring instead to rely on the existing set-up at global level. our policy takes full account of the specificities of small and mediumsized enterprises and the action plan we are putting in place includes specific measures to support the social responsibility of smes. we know that this type of support is most effective when it is provided by those closest to the business. we therefore call on all member states and regional authorities to take full advantage of the opportunities offered by the european structural funds. the commission's communication also reaffirms our commitment and my own commitment to present a legislative proposal on the dissemination of social and environmental information by companies. a clear disclosure obligation at union level is necessary to improve both the quality and the quantity of information disseminated, as is strongly requested by investors and other stakeholders. it is obviously essential to develop a quality proposal, i.e. one which gives companies the flexibility to disclose the information most relevant to their specific situation and one which does not impose new disclosure obligations on small and mediumsized enterprises. i think it is unnecessary to add that the commission will be analysing carefully the ideas that will come out of this debate and which are contained in the two texts that parliament is about to approve. i believe that we have proposed a balanced policy in the interests of business and other social interests. we remain committed to the multilateral approach which is characterised by corporate social responsibility in our union and we want to reaffirm europe's ambition to lead the global debate on this issue, much as we do with regard to environmental policy. at the same time, however, we are keen to ensure that companies have the flexibility to meet their social responsibility obligations in a way that reflects their specific situations. i believe that this debate represents an important step towards the final objective and confirms once again the strength of the link between the european parliament and the commission. this time, fortunately, the council is also in line with our positions, and that gives us hope. it is also a positive message that we are giving to our fellow citizens because when all the institutions speak with one voice, we build confidence in the half a billion citizens who are watching carefully the work we do.
author of the draft opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. - mr president! - what are you doing? i welcome the reports prepared by my colleagues, mr baldassari and mr richard howitt. i am also very pleased with the remarks made by commissioner tajani on corporate social responsibility in response to both the european commission's communication and the un guidelines on business and human rights. i would like to point out first of all that the global economic crisis is also caused by the fact that certain principles of social responsibility have been violated. secondly, the restoration of economic growth - the aim of the europe 2020 strategy - also requires the restoration of mutual trust: public, business, national and european institutions. thirdly, we need to strike a balance between effectively promoting standards and sharing good practices in corporate social responsibility at union level and in relations with third countries, and avoiding new, rigid and excessive burdens, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises. fourthly, it is in the interest of european companies to promote corporate social responsibility internationally, particularly where we are dealing with, for example, violations of human rights, employment standards and also violations of certain international legal orders. fifthly, the european union and the member states can use public procurement, strategic investments, export credits and access to the community market through trade agreements as effective instruments of influence. sixthly, i would like to highlight the role played by the important partners, including national human rights institutions. the next conference with civil rights advocates from the eastern partnership countries will be an example. and finally, mr. chairman, i will say that corporate social responsibility pays off, as exemplified by the respect index on the warsaw stock exchange, which shows that socially responsible companies have higher quotations, higher profits than those that are in the group of the largest companies.
mr. chairman, please! corporate social responsibility is the voluntary, over and above the minimum legal requirements, incorporation of social and environmental issues into business activities and relationships with stakeholders. the basic premise of corporate social responsibility is that business behaves responsibly and ethically towards the social groups it affects, with the greatest possible respect for the environment. that's the definition, and i suggest we stick with that definition. the added value of csr is its flexibility - companies can adapt their plans and ideas in this area to their business strategies, thus making an even more positive impact on the environment in which they operate. i am therefore pleased that the reports we are discussing today are primarily about encouraging the integration of csr into business strategies, highlighting the many ways in which it can be applied and the benefits it brings to both sides. at the same time, i believe that too much legislative intervention in this area would be inappropriate, given the steadily increasing percentage of companies that are themselves interested in this responsibility. let's encourage, not discourage! let's not force it! i also think we have to finally get rid of the assumption that the activities of entrepreneurs, both small and large, are always against the interests of the local community and endanger the environment. we are not demonizing european business. practice shows that entrepreneurs do not need to be persuaded or coerced to conduct their business on the basis of the principles of transparency and sustainability. the principle is that the more trust a business has, the more profits it makes, and the corporate social responsibility strategy is proving to be a very good example of this.
mr. chairman, please! the so-called 'revised european strategy 2011-2014 for corporate social responsibility' published by the commission in 2011 is a step in the right direction to strengthen and rebuild citizens' trust in european economies. the commission's proposed definition of corporate responsibility for its impact on society is balanced and reflects well the relationship between the voluntary and the mandatory approach to the issue. i agree with the rapporteur that a debate on corporate social responsibility is necessary in a broader context, including the discussion on future regulatory measures. citizens are counting on clear and transparent rules of conduct in the business world to revive a declining economy, boost employee engagement and consumer confidence. as a consequence, they may also contribute to the reduction of unemployment in europe. special rules should therefore be developed for smes, which represent over 90% of the european entrepreneurial community, to encourage them to engage more in social responsibility without additional administrative or financial barriers.
mr. chairman, please! the introduction of csr principles deserves respect and support. it is an important factor in the positive actions of enterprises in their social and environmental environments. it should be borne in mind, however, that at the declarative level some of the companies and enterprises may very well use the good practices and standards which we refer to in our declarations, but on the other hand at the practical level they are forgotten. the best example of this is the experience of recent years in poland, when large retail chains with a recognized brand, entering the market, avoided paying taxes through creative accounting, while ruining small and small trade. examples include large pharmaceutical companies that engaged in corrupt practices, even budgeting for corruption, and their sales representatives bribing doctors and hospital directors, with negative consequences. in short, these activities should be encouraged in the area of social responsibility, but also be aware of the legal standards that must accompany them.
