mr president, commissioner, minister, i have to ask you to stop this. the next european council will largely determine the direction the european union will take by the end of 2020. will it be economic growth and job creation, or stagnation and further job decline? president van rompuy proposes that the 2014-2020 budget be a budget of moderation. however, this moderation must not lead to the conservatism and apparent savings that some member states seem to be aiming at. citizens today need positive signals to rebuild trust in the european institutions. the adoption of a multiannual financial framework at a level that will allow the ambitious objectives of the europe 2020 strategy to be achieved and a return to growth can certainly be a signal.
the upcoming european council will focus on the union's 2014-2020 budget. in the face of a crisis, understanding motivates better spending and saving. however, they may not concern strategic and key funds such as the cohesion fund. drastic cuts in this sector would send a clear signal that the older eu member states want to plug the budgetary gap at the expense of the newly joined member states. it is not only countries like poland and hungary that are losing out, but it will also undermine confidence in the european union as a whole and in the principles of solidarity that it has previously adopted. many are already wondering if the european commission's decision in december to withhold funds for road construction in poland is the first step in a strategy that some countries have already planned. if the cohesion fund cuts for the new member states, including poland, were to be seen as a compromise, then they would certainly not see it as a compromise but as a compromise of the union.
in writing. the next european council will be very important for our european future. the financial framework that is the subject of such emotional disputes and treatments is both small and large. yes, it is a paradox. small, because in purely financial terms, they represent only 1% of the european union's gdp. the european council in strasbourg on 14 and 15 december adopted a resolution on the future of the european union, which calls for the european union to be a "common european space". i am optimistic and confident that the leaders will reach a reasonable agreement. the only thing that's troubling is that so many opposition politicians would wish for the summit to fail. they can't see any further than their own short-term and particular political interest. all they care about is the next election and anything they can do to hurt the current government. this is discouraging because it is a betrayal of the very essence of politics - the search for the common good. they are destroying the values that underpin european integration, such as solidarity. i am convinced that the citizens are not blind, and in their wisdom they can see who is looking for the common good and who is looking for cheap applause.
in writing. we have high hopes for the summit on 7 and 8 february. after the failure last november, it is now high time to agree on the eu budget for 2014-2020. this is the budget that all europeans are waiting for. they want to see the eu take action to get back on the path to economic growth. the eu budget, which is over 90% investment-based, is certainly a tool to bring us closer to this. it is particularly important not to reduce the resources for the cohesion policy and the common agricultural policy, which provide a high added value. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the programme. for example, president van rompuy's so-called second proposal last november provided for a cut in the cap pillar ii (i.e. rural development policy) for poland of almost €3 billion, almost 25% of the current allocation! unfortunately, unofficial information suggests that president van rompuy will still propose further cuts, up to €15 billion, compared to his last proposal, which was already €75 billion lower than the european commission's original proposal. the question is, where will the heads of state and government cut? president van rompuy lists research, development and education among his priorities. but it seems he may be lonely.
in writing. our priority is an ambitious budget for europe, especially in the current crisis, because we see such an ambitious budget as an effective instrument to stimulate economic growth in the eu. we must also bear in mind the importance of cohesion policy as an element of this budget, whose funds are essentially investment funds. the cut should not be made at the expense of the new member states, whose development benefits the community as a whole. but first and foremost, we must ensure that the 2014-2020 budget is adopted. of course, not at any price and in accordance with the demands of parliament. failure to reach an agreement would be bad news for a europe in crisis.
in writing. the financial crisis of 2008-2009 began and ended shortly after the start of the implementation of the eu budget for 2007-2013. sadly, few people thought that the crisis would spread to other countries and that the european union would be in for a long time. thus, few experts and politicians have been preoccupied with the impending problems of agreeing on the next financial perspective. the alternative of 'saving or spending public money' is very much on the agenda now, and this is particularly evident before the council meeting. to begin with, the eu budget is not impressive from the point of view of all 27 economies combined. that's just over 1% of the gross national income of the entire community. for comparison, the level of fiscalisation (the ratio of public sector expenditure to gdp) in the eu was close to 50% in 2011. in poland, the rate was 43,6%. but as it turns out, even for such a small sum, the fight can take months, especially in times of crisis and a europe-wide trend towards saving. the amount of the funds awarded will be important, but so will their purpose. experts are increasingly talking about the need to limit subsidies and subsidies to repayable financial instruments such as loans or guarantees. the issue of vat clearance in eu-funded projects, which in polish reality represents a significant part of the costs, also remains unknown.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. the united states remains one of the world's most important producers and a key economic partner of europe. as a result of the enlargement of the customs union following the accession of bulgaria and romania, the commercial rights of this country have been slightly overridden. in line with the international rules of the world trade organisation, of which the union is a member, we are obliged to eliminate disadvantages in foreign trade. the restoration of the united states' trading rights with the new community countries is beneficial to all parties.
in writing. - with the accession of bulgaria and romania to the eu, the customs union had to be extended. in accordance with wto rules, the eu has committed to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights on concessional letters from any of the acceding countries. these negotiations were undertaken with the aim of agreeing a mutually satisfactory countervailing duty to compensate for the increase in the related duty rates and the resulting material injury. such compensation shall be due where the adoption of the eu external tariff system results in an increase in rates above the level to which the acceding country has committed itself under the wto. the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the countries entitled to compensation. negotiations with the united states resulted in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters, which was initialled by the eu on 21 december 2011 and by the us on 17 february 2012. the products covered by the eu-us compensation agreement are mainly poultry and pork meat and food products. the draft resolution could help to improve trade relations with the united states. under this provision, wto members benefit from countries with a higher rate than the eu tariff, while countries with lower rates are compensated by the eu for the difference. i believe that such measures will help to improve trade, which can be one of the factors that positively affect economic growth.
in writing. - i supported the report by mrs pervenche berès on the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. i believe that the development of appropriate labour market policies, with particular emphasis on combating unemployment, is a key challenge for the european union and the member states. the financial crisis, the deterioration of the economy, the alarming level of unemployment, the threat of social exclusion and poverty for millions of europeans are the greatest pains we have to deal with. it is therefore necessary to develop long-term strategies for employment policies, creating new jobs, especially for young people, who have been most affected by the negative economic trends of recent years. it is also necessary to prepare appropriate programmes for other groups at risk of labour market disadvantages, i.e. women, the elderly, the disabled, rural and small town residents. i hope that the efforts made both within the eu and by the member states will contribute to reducing unemployment, promoting a high level of skills and training for workers and combating poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. − in terms of employment policy, member states should focus all their efforts on priority areas, including raising the employment rate and reducing unemployment, especially among young people. i believe that it is worthwhile to improve the efficiency of education and training systems in all areas and to develop national reform programmes and their implementation. that is why i voted in favour of the pervenche berès report on the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states.
in writing. − the european union's development objectives are set out in the europe 2020 strategy, which is based on closer coordination of economic policies, with a particular focus on the key areas for action to boost europe's potential for sustainable growth and competitiveness. these objectives are pursued, inter alia, by the guidelines on employment policy, which are intended to facilitate the coordination of member states' policies. the integration of the guidelines is intended to ensure that policies at national and union level fully contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy objectives. i am positive that the number of guidelines is small. this ensures their consistency and transparency. i highly value the guidelines, as well as the whole europe 2020 strategy. the inclusion of recommendations on combating poverty and social exclusion, reducing structural unemployment and improving the quality of the education system in the guidelines is particularly commendable. i hope that the polish government will follow the above guidelines, which i consider to be of priority importance, when drawing up its national reform programme. we cannot lose sight of the social dimension of the fight against the crisis. in view of the above, i have decided to support the report on the proposal for a council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states.
in writing. - there is no doubt that europe is in crisis. this is evidenced by the unemployment rate, which is the highest in 10 years and currently stands at 9.6%. analyses carried out by the european parliament indicate that the main employment sectors will be services and transport. the new strategies include increasing the employment rate and reducing unemployment, developing a skilled labour force that meets labour market needs, promoting quality employment and lifelong learning, improving the efficiency of education and training systems at all levels and increasing higher education enrolment, and tackling poverty and social exclusion. unfortunately, the common guidelines will not help us to understand the problem of unemployment better and to find effective solutions. i believe that there is no one size fits all approach to the european economy, because each country is different from the others. the fact that the guidelines proposed by brussels may work in spain, for example, does not necessarily mean that they must have the same effect in poland or another member state. member states should therefore pursue their own employment policies and respond as quickly as possible to changes in the labour market. i'm against such regulations.
in writing. - the fight against unemployment in europe is the largest and longest in recent times. i think it should remain a matter for the member states to decide. but the european union also has its own importance and important task. this task is primarily to reduce the recklessly imposed administrative burdens and climate and energy policies leading to the deindustrialisation of europe. analysts estimate that over 250,000 people could lose their jobs in poland alone because of such records.
in writing. − member states have exclusive competence in deciding on the pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products within their public health insurance systems. however, to ensure a proper functioning of the single market, pricing and reimbursement measures must be free of discrimination against imported medicinal products and based on objective and verifiable criteria which are independent from the origin of the products. the existing directive has never been amended since its adoption and its provisions reflect the pharmaceutical market conditions which prevailed more than twenty years ago and which have fundamentally changed, especially with the emergence of generic medicines providing cheaper versions of existing products. in parallel, the constant rise in public expenditure on pharmaceuticals in the last decades has encouraged member states to invent more complex and innovative pricing and reimbursement systems over time. the proposal therefore aims at adapting the directive to the current pharmaceutical environment while preserving its core foundations. for this reason, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − medicines and all other medical products for human use should be subject to appropriate controls, both in terms of their quality and availability. availability is to be understood in a broad sense: physical, i.e. the supply of a sufficient quantity in places that can be reached or reached, or economic. today, we are dealing with affordability, which is transparency in regulating pricing, so that medicines and medical products are affordable to everyone who needs them.
in writing. − union legislation requires that a marketing authorisation be granted by the competent union or national authorities before any medicinal product can be placed on the market. i don't think there's any doubt that life and health are one of the most important values for any human being. any medicinal product authorised in the eu should be available to patients in all member states. the prolongation of the pricing and reimbursement procedures contributes to delays in the placing of medicinal products on the market. this can be particularly detrimental in the case of innovative measures. this may result in loss of life or even a shortened life. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (hereinafter 'the agency') is based on the principle of equal treatment for all medicinal products.
in writing. - the european union should not fix any prices for medicinal products from above. i understand the need for a common market, but the prices of such basic products should be regulated by the market, not by an eu directive. at the same time, the amendments tabled contained many valuable comments which i supported in my vote. those minimum procedural requirements should also ensure legal certainty and transparency for the competent authorities in their decision-making on the pricing of medicinal products and their reimbursement by universal health coverage schemes, an important statement that points to a common problem among member states, namely the compliance with pharmaceutical lobbyists. in my country, corruption and inaccuracies in the procurement of medicines and the list of medicines that are reimbursed have been exposed on many occasions.
in writing. − the european fisheries sector produces around 6.4 million tonnes of fish each year. the fisheries and processing industries employ 350 000 people. this shows the importance of the sector and its impact on other important areas such as the economy, employment and the environment. i voted in favour of the report on the common fisheries policy. we cannot ignore the problems in this sector, but i believe that the measures we are taking are the right step to overcome the difficulties. i hope that the solutions proposed will contribute to the development of this sector, the sustainable exploitation of marine resources, the effective protection of the marine environment, and the security of the food supply.
in writing. - we have adopted an important report on the future of the common fisheries policy. the changes in this area would take effect from the beginning of 2014. the main objective of the regulation is to create the conditions for the recovery of fish stocks by 2020 so that fisheries in europe become a sustainable sector. the measures adopted provide for greater protection of marine resources. the renewed fish stocks will generate more catches, so in the long term the expected trend should lead to the creation of new jobs in the sector.
in writing. - despite the many steps taken in the past to reform the sector, the problems relating to the common fisheries policy have been resolved over the years in a few major blocks. the main complications were the lack of environmental sustainability, due to the problem of 'overfishing', the vulnerability of fishing fleets to 'external shocks' (even if high fuel prices), the inability to achieve relative economic stability, the lack of social sustainability (the sector has ceased to be a source of attractive jobs for potential new generations of fishermen) and the complexity of the legal framework, which in turn closes the loop and makes it difficult to achieve the sustainable natural environment mentioned above. i look forward to the future of this sector as i consider the changes proposed by the project presented. the introduction of precise regulations addressing each of these issues should lead to the comprehensive systematisation of the cfp as from 2017 this date represents a clear sign of hope for this sector, which is still in an internal impasse.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. this report is very important because it sets out the framework of the future cfp policy for the next 10 years, and will have a big effect on fishermen all across europe. i believe that it is critical that we find concrete ways to stop overfishing. there are a few ways that we can help to achieve this goal. eu vessels fishing outside eu waters must meet the same requirements as boats in europe, and fisheries agreements with third countries should only cover fish stocks with a surplus of fish. we also need to find a balanced approach with regards to the number of controls carried out in eu waters. it is absolutely crucial to sustainable fishing that the control system is reformed to take into account specific characteristics and sizes of different european fleets.
in writing. - the common fisheries policy is an important and sensitive issue. important for the food balance and the biological balance of the seas and oceans. it is a sensitive, even delicate issue because it is about access to resources, about limiting access and about being willing to share resources with others. we've received hundreds of emails with suggestions, requests and expectations. i admit that the emails helped us make our decision in the vote. we have adopted a good document which takes account of the requirements of sustainable fishing, rationalization, sustainable fishing methods, and the shaping of fishing effort. other important areas of regulation are research and innovation programmes, fair control of fishermen and fisheries, and territorial and coastal waters. the spirit and the letter of this policy can also serve the baltic fisheries and polish fishermen well.
in writing. - i voted for the reform of the eu's common fisheries policy because overfishing could no longer be tolerated. we see that the current fisheries policy has failed, with the increase in overfished stocks compared to 2002. without a sustainable fisheries policy, we would expose the environment to irreversible, catastrophic consequences, with many fish species reduced to a minimum or even extinct.
in writing. − the common fisheries policy, last substantially reformed in 2002, has largely failed. mis-setting, over-fishing and ineffective mechanisms for the conservation of living marine resources have led to a significant overfishing of mediterranean (80%) and atlantic (40%) stocks and to an unacceptably high rate of discards of healthy fish back into the sea. the alarming state of the environment and the difficult economic situation of fishermen and businesses prompted the commission to start work on reforming the common fisheries policy in 2011. the proposed changes are mainly to introduce sustainable fishing quotas by 2015 to restore fish stocks to sustainable levels by 2020 and to establish a discard ban for all species caught. this will improve the environment and rebuild marine resources, while benefiting fishermen by increasing their profits and consumers by providing them with easier access to cheaper fish. in view of the above, i voted with full conviction in favour of the reform of the common fisheries policy and the amendments to the regulation put forward by the rapporteur for the committee on fisheries, ms ulrika rodust of the s&d group. the next step is for member states' ministers to take a position on the proposed regulations. the european parliament has shown in the negotiations that reform is a priority for it, and has also sent a clear signal to the council that it will have to take its position into account.
in writing. - the current eu common fisheries policy is struggling to address many longstanding problems. the proposal in this regulation, to bring all catches closer to the maximum allowable catch (msy) and to reduce those that are too high, is a good solution. it is also necessary to maintain the landing policy in order to avoid unwanted by-catches. it is also proposed to reduce the commercialisation of 'transferable fishing concessions'. as regards fishing concessions, the rules for their award should be more transparent in order to reduce the risk of discrimination between fishermen. it is also necessary to adapt fishing capacity to the prevailing conditions. as part of the restoration of fish stocks, it is proposed to exclude 10 to 20% of its waters as fishing areas. i think that the appropriate regulations contained in this regulation will contribute to a wise and fair management of the marine fisheries sector.
in writing. - the common fisheries policy needs to be changed. two thirds of the world's marine resources are overfished, which has long caused fish prices and fishing costs to rise. the cost of an irrational marine policy is about €865 million a year, according to biodiversity organisations, and resources have declined by 26% in the last 10 years. i am glad that the european parliament finally has a chance to decide on maritime policy. i hope we made the right decision today. the decision is aimed primarily at strengthening the fisheries sector while restoring the balance of the seas. within a few years, the profitability of the fisheries sector should increase and the sector as a whole should recover and create new jobs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the position taken by mr miroslav ouzkỳ on the noise level of motor vehicles. i believe that the proposed changes, which aim to introduce lower limits on motor vehicle noise and new methods of measuring noise, will improve the quality of life, health and the environment. clear and reliable information on the noise limit should be provided to both car manufacturers and consumers. in addition, the laws of the member states should be harmonised so that the technical requirements concerning the noise level of motor vehicles are applied consistently throughout the european union. there is a need to stimulate the development of innovative, less noisy motor vehicles. however, it should be considered that this may lead to an increase in vehicle prices, which may consequently lead to a decrease in demand.
in writing. − a report on the permissible sound levels of motor vehicles has been drawn up in the environment committee. i congratulate the rapporteur because the subject of the work was primarily technical and the voices of citizens, industry and environmental organisations were included in the discussion. it is good that reason and the arguments in favour of supporting europe's dying automobile industry are finally winning. in poland too, many jobs depend on production decisions in this sector.
in writing. - motor transport is undoubtedly one of the main causes of environmental noise. i am all for reducing noise, which is so bad for our health. reducing noise limits is an important factor, but these values must be both ambitious and achievable. improved methods of testing noise emissions, systematic monitoring of the road surface, which also contributes to vehicle noise, and better information to consumers on vehicle noise levels are certainly needed. better informed consumers will be able to make more informed purchasing decisions based on noise emission data. better information should also help to enable public authorities to put in place appropriate incentives to buy quieter vehicles, so that the noisiest vehicles gradually disappear from our roads. it could also be useful to introduce a vehicle noise level indicator. the union type-approval requirements are also very important, as they should strike a balance between the different objectives and be consistent with the overall approach of striving for quieter, safer and more environmentally friendly vehicles. i am confident that the new legislation will benefit citizens and the environment and will be an important step towards reducing noise.
in writing. − prolonged exposure to high levels of noise can cause significant health problems, leading not only to insomnia and hearing damage, but also to cardiovascular disease and serious mental illness. motorised transport is one of the biggest sources of noise for many europeans. this is why it is so important to have the right legislation and the right use of available technologies to protect the health of citizens as much as possible. the commission proposal should be supplemented, inter alia, by provisions to enable consumers to be informed effectively and clearly of the noise level of a given vehicle, for example by means of an appropriate labelling system used by manufacturers and uniform in all member states. a road classification system that takes into account the impact of the surface on noise levels and limits the entry of heavy goods vehicles, for example into residential areas, at certain times of the day could also be beneficial. it is also necessary to update the current system of vehicle categories and subcategories, which establishes maximum noise emission values, established in 1970 and unchanged since 1985.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the commission proposal for a regulation on the sound level of motor vehicles has as its principal objective the protection of public health and the environment through measures to reduce the sound level of motor vehicles. the proposal would introduce a new testing method for measuring the sound level of motor vehicles and new noise limit values for different categories of light, medium-sized and heavy vehicles. i believe that this is something that will benefit european citizens, but i also think that the eu must give realistic guidelines to the industry for the coming years.
in writing. − the commission’s proposal, supported by commissioner tajani, the envi report and the amendments proposed for plenary set limit values for all new car models. the current vehicle noise standards date back to 1995 and are therefore urgently in need of being updated. around a quarter of cars and a third of trucks tested over the past five years already meet the levels proposed by the committee. however, unfortunately, my vote could not stop the intent of mainly ppe and ecr meps to weaken the balanced proposal in favour of the automobile industry, bringing in much longer phasing-in periods. this clearly shows a lack of ambition in order to create a level-playing field between the modes!
in writing. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety wants new standards to be introduced in the setting of noise standards. the introduction of a new test method is intended to measure the noise level of motor vehicles and to set new noise limits by categorising vehicles into light, medium and heavy. the application should be supplemented by several elements to encourage the purchase of vehicles with a lower noise level. it is also mentioned that not only engines are a source of noise, but also tyres, road surfaces, etc. the present application does not provide information on the noise level of the vehicle. it is therefore necessary to introduce on motor vehicles markings indicating the noise emission characteristic of the vehicle. the commission proposal could also be enriched by a system of classification of roads, taking into account the quality of their surface. from a psychological point of view, noise is a very unpleasant and undesirable sound, causing irritation and fatigue of the whole organism, and in particular of the hearing. it also affects health, as well as the physical condition of a person. therefore, any steps to reduce noise are highly desirable. i'm all for that.
in writing. - the idea of reducing the noise level of motor vehicles is a good one, as it will improve public health and protect the environment. however, it should be noted that this has at least two serious problems. first, it is not enough to improve the quality of the engines themselves. noise also comes from other sources, including tyres and road surfaces. the commission therefore considers that the measures in question are appropriate to address the specific needs of the union industry. the second problem is of a different nature, but it is also one that we must bear in mind. effective noise reduction may mean that some people, especially those with impaired hearing, may be unaware of the approaching vehicle and become its victim. this is particularly relevant for electric or hybrid vehicles. therefore, assuming progress in noise reduction, the introduction of audible warning systems for approaching vehicles should be considered.
in writing. - the new noise directive is an important part of health protection, but i am still wondering what the implications will be for car manufacturers. and what will be the cost to countries like poland, where the state of the cars leaves much to be desired? there is no proper analysis showing these costs. i voted yes, though.

in writing. − due to the economic crisis, some eu member states find themselves in a position where they can no longer pay for their share of eu-funded projects and programmes. these are therefore at risk of being cancelled, with negative effects on the member states’ economies and the objectives of the projects and programmes. this report proposes to approve the commission proposal which allows for increased co-financing rates for projects and programmes under the external borders fund, the european refugee fund, the european return fund and the european integration fund and for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability (e.g. the countries under the various european rescue mechanism, such as greece and ireland). very often, it is better that less money is spent on a project than to cancel it completely. for example, if a project for eur 10 million that would previously have been financed with eur 5 million from the eu and eur 5 million from the member state, this could now be eur 5 million from the eu and only eur 2 million from the ms, bringing the total amount down, but without altogether cancelling the project.

in writing. − the economic crisis has hit public finances in the eu countries hard. some countries have managed to get public finances back on track on their own, but some have had to ask for financial support. the commission has proposed the possibility of increasing the level of co-financing for member states benefiting from the financial support mechanism. the proposal aims to allow an increase of 20 percentage points in the level of union co-financing. this could lead to greater solidarity between member states in the management of migration flows. this could have an impact on improving governance in the eu. it is therefore in the interest of all member states that commitments made in relation to migration are not affected by economic difficulties in the member state concerned. as the members of the recent libe delegation to greece can attest, many of the projects planned require increased levels of co-financing in order to be implemented. this includes repairing detention facilities that are in poor condition or improving the technical equipment necessary for effective border management.

in writing. - we have adopted an important report on the future of the common fisheries policy. the changes in this area would take effect from the beginning of 2014. the main objective of the regulation is to create the conditions for the recovery of fish stocks by 2020 so that fisheries in europe become a sustainable sector. the measures adopted provide for greater protection of marine resources. the renewed fish stocks will generate more catches, so in the long term the expected trend should lead to the creation of new jobs in the sector.
in writing. - the adopted report is a guarantee of a better future for both european and polish fisheries. the reform of the union's common fisheries policy aims to prevent overfishing by introducing sustainable fisheries and creating the conditions for fish stocks to be renewed by 2020. the regionalisation of fisheries management is a very important aspect of the reform. in practice, this will mean that only the main legal framework and principles will be defined at eu level, while the actual implementing decisions will be taken at regional level, allowing the specificities and needs of individual water bodies to be taken into account. such changes will allow the sector to function well and even create additional jobs. of course, the document we have is still in need of improvement, but it is a good starting point for further trilateral talks with the european commission and the council.
in writing. − technical protection measures are the rules that our fishermen throughout the european union must apply every day when they go fishing to ensure that the place and the way they fish guarantee their sustainability. these include, inter alia, the minimum size of the individuals to be landed, the minimum size of the nets. the current commission proposal aims to extend the technical measures for a further transitional period until the adoption of a regionalised technical measures framework under the cfp. since the cap could not be introduced before 1 january 2013, a temporary solution was proposed. it consists in amending the basic act without specifying the expiry dates and thus repealing the 2009 and 2011 regulations. the act also takes into account the measures for reducing discards in the waters of the north-east atlantic agreed with the partner countries. this proposal is unfortunately temporary and does not provide fishermen with a clear legal position, but it does ensure sustainable fishing and allows reproduction in ecosystems.

in writing. − the lower social status of women is the result of centuries of discrimination and negative stereotypes. this is one of the main reasons why violence against women is still such a widespread social phenomenon. the european union's policy is against this and strongly condemns all discriminatory attitudes and violence against women and children. tradition, honour, culture, privacy or religion cannot be an excuse for member states to dispense with preventing and eliminating violence. combating all forms of violence against women and children requires coordinated strategies. action must start at the lowest national level. the approach should be complex and focused on key issues such as prevention, protection, support for victims, as well as prosecution of perpetrators. the commission is therefore proposing to support initiatives which oppose all forms of violence against women.
in writing. - it is a shame that there are still so many cases of violence against women in europe. of particular concern is the fact that a significant proportion of cases of violence are not reported to the police, especially in the case of serious crimes such as rape. no strategy to combat violence against women can be effective if victims do not report the violence to the appropriate authorities. the law must provide a strong response to this, so that victims can regain a sense of justice, while at the same time both victims and society as a whole are protected from similar cases in the future. it is of concern that in several eu countries, including poland, the penalties for sexual offences are very low and, in addition, their enforcement is often suspended. as an example, 40% of the sentences for rape in poland are suspended prison sentences. such lenient sentences are, in effect, a slap in the face to the wronged by courts that have taken a dismissive view of the wrong done. taking violence against women seriously must mean taking the perpetrators of violence to task, to ensure that they are punished fairly for the harm they have done and at the same time to ensure that society is protected for the future.

in writing. - i support the report by ms kartika tamara liotard on active ageing in good health. older people are the fastest growing age group in europe. member states should therefore promote and support all forms of ageing in a dignified manner. despite statistically increasing life expectancy, an increasing proportion of people suffer from serious chronic diseases associated with age. in this context, the provision of better and more reasonable health care, social welfare services and health insurance is particularly important. a very common problem is the lack of physical activity among the elderly. according to the who, lack of it is the fourth most common cause of death. it is therefore important to promote healthy and active lifestyles and to provide information on the risks of an unhealthy lifestyle. i also think it is highly desirable to promote intellectual activity as a way of combating the dementia that is spreading among the elderly. i also support other innovative solutions that would contribute to improving the quality of life and health of older people and would allow them to participate more fully in society.
in writing. − the problem of an ageing population is affecting a growing number of member states. it is estimated that by 2060, the number of europeans aged over 65 will almost double. we must therefore do everything we can to ensure that this group of people enjoys a decent standard of living. the infrastructure has a direct impact on living conditions, both the one closest to the house or apartment and the local one in rural or urban areas. providing adequate access to transport services is particularly important in rural areas, where it is very common for an elderly person to live in a place far from urbanised areas. in this case, the lack of communication means drastically reduces the possibility of access to services, such as health care. we must not forget the phenomenon of social exclusion - lack of employment opportunities, or even volunteering opportunities, and discrimination on grounds of age, health or disability are common causes of isolation of older people from the rest of society. and the ability of an older person to impart knowledge and experience is invaluable. it is also worth using this wisdom in, for example, policy and decision-making processes. support initiatives to improve the living conditions of older people, call on regional and local authorities to act on behalf of this group of citizens and support them to live as long, healthy and active lives as possible.
in writing. - the eu population is ageing rapidly. this makes you think about the idea of active aging and maintaining fitness. since aging affects all of us, this idea is long-lasting and extends to future generations. in this context, it is necessary to examine how the administrative units of the eu member states are adapted to the needs of an ageing population and whether they enable active ageing. the better the adaptation to such active time-spending, the longer the period of independent living of the elderly person. studies have shown that most areas are not well adapted to these changes. so there was a need to adopt a strategy to help make them more welcoming. the strategic implementation plan for the 'european partnership for innovation in active and healthy ageing' can be the first step taken by the european commission towards creating age-friendly places for older people with the aim of creating a society open to all age groups by 2020. standardised data collection, evaluation and monitoring processes will enable stakeholders to target their actions and resources to those groups of people and places most in need of change and adaptation, thereby contributing to the implementation of policies and programmes in a more cost-effective manner.

in writing. - the concept of corporate social responsibility has undergone a major transformation from an idea that is rather foreign to companies to a business card, in a sense, of their reliability. businesses see the real benefits of being socially responsible and we should continue to promote these principles and encourage and motivate businesses to implement them. companies have to do this voluntarily, they have to want to implement these principles. forcing is not the answer here. i fully support the concept of corporate social responsibility and i am glad that companies are also seeing the benefits. from the perspective of international trade, the implementation of the principles of corporate social responsibility in trade policy is a necessary condition for the policy to be consistent with the union's overall objectives. responsible companies also play a key role in trade agreements. there is no doubt that, as a matter of principle, trade should not be detached from other eu policies, internal or external, and should in no way lead to abuses in the areas of working conditions, democratic freedoms or the environment. trade and corporate social responsibility should be more closely linked. i support a new definition that enables businesses to contribute to a social market economy, supported by innovative business models. it is very important not only to create incentives for companies, to remove red tape, but also to ensure that this responsible action also translates into improved profitability and does not impose additional burdens.
in writing. − the resolution adopted today is a strong signal to the european commission, member state governments and businesses themselves to take bold steps to promote csr strategies. a company's active attitude towards its responsibility for the interests of its employees leads to greater social trust and acceptance and thus to a more stable position on the market. we therefore support the commission in its plans to develop appropriate guidelines or legislative initiatives to pursue a coherent eu policy and to implement international standards effectively. at the same time, we believe that any regulatory action should ensure that businesses retain maximum flexibility, as they have the primary responsibility for implementing this strategy, including by mitigating the social impact of the current economic crisis. we are also working to make it easier for businesses of all sizes and structures to access finance.
in writing. − the committee on legal affairs and the committee on employment and social affairs have decided to establish close cooperation to ensure a coherent approach to parliament's position on the renewed eu strategy 2011-2014 on corporate social responsibility during this period. the exclusive competence of each committee was defined based on three key words: people, profit, planet earth. in its new strategy, the european commission proposes a new definition of corporate social responsibility, understood as 'the responsibility of companies for their impact on society'. on the basis of this new definition, the commission proposes a series of specific measures to optimise the impact of csr policy.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the report on the renewal of the eu strategy for corporate social responsibility. we must make sure that csr is not just a marketing slogan, interpreted at will by corporations, but above all that it is in line with the legislation and collective agreements in force. modern, socially responsible companies are not indifferent to such actions as environmental protection and the introduction of special social and protection programmes for employees. today, it is of the utmost importance that efforts, especially in the area of global business, are aligned with environmental, social and human rights standards. we should insist that corporate social responsibility policy at eu level is coherent.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? the positive assessment of european support for global csr initiatives and the increased activity of the commission in the report are certainly valuable. the same applies to the report's objectives of sustaining economic recovery and of drawing attention to the need for the european institutions to step up their efforts to implement the recommendations of the organisation for economic cooperation and development in the field of business. the proposal to oblige the commission to submit an annual report to parliament and the council on this subject is noteworthy. unfortunately, the resolution contains a number of proposals which i cannot support, for example the requirement that companies disclose non-financial information, which is contrary to the rules of competition. i do not agree with the attempt to shift the responsibility for environmental protection measures taken by public authorities to the business community. the european social charter and the charter of fundamental rights also raise doubts as regards companies. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. − promoting corporate social responsibility (csr) avoids harmful trends and tendencies emerging from the crisis in a society functioning in a particular environment. csr must have a positive impact on the sphere of economic benefits and on the building of a better brand image. it is an incentive for businesses to play an active role in creating better living conditions. i support the report by mr richard howit, on corporate social responsibility. i am also convinced of the need to implement and respect the international oecd guidelines on transnational corporations and the principles developed and promoted by the un. corporate social responsibility should be promoted by leading companies. member states should encourage decent work and respect for private and family life. the role of global csr instruments in third countries is also an important factor. i would thus like to express my belief that csr will strike the right balance between the interests of companies and their social responsibility.
in writing. - the concept of csr is an innovative response to various social or environmental problems. therefore, it should be better promoted so that companies actively use it and citizens are aware of it. companies want to implement csr and we need to ensure that we provide the right legal environment, but also promote a general attitude that will motivate companies to voluntarily incorporate csr into their practices. corporate social responsibility should be seen as an opportunity, not a threat, for the competitiveness of enterprises. i welcome the emphasis on european support for global initiatives on corporate social responsibility, the redefinition of the concept and the much more active role of the european commission itself. corporate social responsibility is essential if business confidence is to be restored and the economic recovery to be sustained. in the context of international trade, this responsibility is so crucial that trade is justified if it contributes to economic development, employment and an increase in living standards. only under this condition can the opening of trade be seen as positive. europe, but also the international community, is faced with the need to incorporate real guarantees of sustainable development and social rights into the rules of trade in the name of cohesion. this is very important because it responds to the expectations of a large number of citizens. i supported the report because it makes an important contribution to the debate on the development of this very important concept.
in writing. − corporate social responsibility is essential if confidence in the business of companies and firms is to be restored and if the economic recovery in the european union is to be sustained. we should see it as an opportunity, not a threat, to the competitiveness of these entities. responsible and prosperous businesses should be asked to demonstrate active involvement in the process of mitigating the social impact of the crisis. this action should be to implement the solutions proposed by the rapporteur on corporate social responsibility, namely in the areas of job creation, health at work, pension stability, promotion of minimum wages, elimination of labour exploitation practices in business supply chains, and promotion of new markets for socially useful and environmentally friendly products and services. that is why i voted in favour of the report by mr richard howitt.
in writing. − the european parliament's draft resolution welcomes the new emphasis on european support for global corporate social responsibility initiatives. first of all, the debate on corporate social responsibility is situated in the context of the current economic crisis. it was argued that csr is essential if business confidence is to be restored and the economic recovery to be sustained. short-term thinking in brussels, which focuses solely on the transparency, accountability and accountability of financial markets, would be to repeat the same mistakes that are accused of being the agents responsible for the collapse of banks. another priority of the report is to present concrete concepts that will help to translate the commission's intention into better implementation of global csr initiatives.
in writing. - corporate social responsibility is an important issue. the report prepared by mr howitts is a perfect expression of her spirit. in poland, for some years now, it has been evident that companies and industry are trying to invest a percentage of their resources in socially acceptable purposes. they donate to foundations, build public facilities, and support sports. the latter form in particular has become a popular way of combining a mutual interest company advertising and support for local sport. for example, the most deserving football club in krakow - krakow's wisła, which has been the calling card of polish football for almost 107 years - is supported by a global powerhouse in cable production. the women's basketball section of this great and deserved club for poland, winning laurels of victory on the international arena, is supported by a company from the processing sector, which has located production facilities in lesser poland. i can only encourage such solutions.
in writing. − the commission has proposed a rapid reaction mechanism. it would enable member states to respond more swiftly and effectively to vat fraud. the rapid reaction mechanism would give member states the possibility to introduce certain emergency measures. the proposal provides that member states could apply for one month a 'reverse charge mechanism' under which the recipient, rather than the supplier of goods or services, would be liable for payment of vat. this would significantly increase the chances of effectively combating complex fraud, such as carousel fraud, and of reducing the financial losses that are irreversible in such cases. vat fraud costs the eu and national budgets several billion euros a year. in some serious cases, large sums of money are lost in a short time because of the speed with which fraud mechanisms are developing today.
in writing. − strengthening the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion is crucial to restoring and maintaining the stability and strength of the public finance sector across the union. this is one of the most important amendments to the report, and it reflects the report perfectly. today, vat evasion is a major drain on national budgets. as with drugs, the fight against drugs must be conducted at the pan-national level to be effective, especially in the case of the so-called 'tax carousels'. they came with the disappearance of customs borders. the amendments voted today are therefore important, especially as countries burdened by the costs of the crisis are increasingly faced with the decision of how to defend their own finances. i do not agree with a common vat for all eu countries.
in writing. − the annual growth survey sets out the economic priorities for 2013 and indicates that while the temporary anti-crisis measures are beginning to deliver positive effects in terms of deficit reduction and financial market sentiment, continued reforms are essential to achieve sustainable growth and job creation in the long term. the five priorities identified by the commission as key to overcoming the crisis and restoring growth, namely diversified and smart fiscal consolidation, restoring normal lending to the economy, promoting growth and competitiveness, fighting unemployment and modernising public administration, should be welcomed. the resolution also calls on the commission to present a report to the european council on the implementation of a strategy for sustainable fiscal discipline, with specific proposals to promote private investment, improve the efficiency of tax systems and create jobs. the need for structural labour market reforms to increase the flexibility needed to effectively mitigate shocks and reduce youth unemployment by better matching skills to labour demand has become particularly evident in recent times. in today's resolution we also point to the potential for growth in the single market, which can be realised, for example, by removing the many barriers that still exist in the services sector.
in writing. − the european semester constitutes one of the bases for sustainable functioning of the euro area with the aim of fostering competitiveness and convergence across the european union. parliament, in cooperation with the national parliaments, is actively involved in the process. the text adopted notes the challenges of growth-friendly consolidation which must be addressed to regain stability and recovery in the union. in particular, parliament calls for a proper role to be played by the eu budget to this end, as it constitutes an investment instrument for growth and employment. the commission should properly note its importance, therefore, in the annual growth survey.
in writing. − it should be stressed that the priorities for the current european semester presented by the commission are broadly in line with those of the previous year. although european leaders are already predicting a quick end to the crisis, experience has shown that such declarations should be treated with a certain amount of restraint. nevertheless, it is true that some signs of improvement are already apparent. the euro area countries, which have undergone difficult reforms, are slowly recovering from the crisis their imbalances in economic contacts are decreasing and their competitiveness is increasing. this in turn translates into a slow recovery in financial market confidence and a fall in the cost of debt financing. the euro area and the eu are feeling it the euro is strengthening against the dollar. the next stage of the 2013 european semester will be the assessment and endorsement by the european council at its spring meeting of the priorities contained in the growth analysis. the individual member states will then present national reform programmes corresponding to the priorities adopted by the european council, which, after their assessment, will be used by the european council to formulate formal recommendations, which should then be reflected in the draft national budgets for the following year. as the results of last year's european semester show, the commission is doing increasingly well in coordinating economic governance in the eu. it is to be hoped that the 2013 semester will deliver even better results, marking the end of the era of crisis in europe.
in writing. − we adopted three resolutions on the 2013 annual growth survey, the governance of the single market and employment and social aspects, respectively. the commission's growth analysis for 2013 has won our approval as it assumes fiscal consolidation and appropriate structural reforms to foster growth and long-term competitiveness, which is the key to overcoming the crisis. i am also pleased to note that the draft decision contained in the 'two-pack' supports the economic dialogue and the overall monitoring of the european parliament and national parliaments over the european semester process. since the beginning of the semester, i have advocated this key element of the semester's democratic legitimacy by involving both the ep and national parliaments in the process.

in writing. − since the financial crisis, which began in late 2007 and early 2008, the world has been in recession. it has serious socioeconomic consequences for citizens and businesses in the eu. the crisis has further highlighted the significant inefficiency of the public debt management system in the union. the costs of this failure will be borne by citizens and businesses. as part of the remedial action, the single market is crucial for citizens and businesses. it will be a key driver of growth and jobs. it will restore competitiveness and stimulate growth. given the considerable body of legislation already in place in the form of single market rules, their proper implementation and enforcement is becoming increasingly important. however, statistics showing member states' backlogs in transposing single market legislation raise serious doubts and show that we are still not reaping the full potential benefits of a fully developed single market.

mr. president, i would like to thank you for your service. stereotypes are both the cause and the effect of discrimination. we often don't realize they exist because we've been raised as "nice and kind girls" or "strong and brave boys". we face a strong social penalty for challenging stereotypical behavior. a particularly negative role in gender stereotypes is played by the sexist culture in which we live, which perpetuates the belief in the superiority of men. stereotypes introduce a bipolar division of society: if a trait is attributed to women, then the opposite is attributed to men, e.g. weak versus strong, regardless of personal potential, personality, sensitivity, education. stereotypes in the labour market are particularly dangerous because they perpetuate horizontal and vertical segregation; they are responsible for the glass ceiling that blocks advancement to higher positions, the sticky floor that keeps women in low-price, low-paid jobs, and the glass walls that make it difficult to escape from a position. the key to fighting stereotypes is education and training. thank you, sir.
blue-card question. – where do you see these quotas for management positions in companies? they do not exist; we are fighting for them. we are trying to implement this, but i do not think that there are many quotas in place. perhaps there are isolated cases, but it is not systematic. i do not think that men are being persecuted in that sense.
the economic crisis has unfortunately widened the gap between women and men. this is most evident in the labour market, with increased job insecurity, the forced entry of women into part-time work, and the large number of redundancies in female-dominated sectors - for example in the public sector, where fiscal consolidation is leading to job cuts in both the administration and the public services and public assistance sectors. add to this the fact that women are blocked from advancing and the persisting gender pay gap is exacerbating the situation for women. gender equality therefore remains a challenge for the european union, especially in times of crisis. i believe that the new priorities for equality between women and men set out by the commission will be implemented and will have a positive impact on the improvement of the situation of women in both the public and private spheres.
in writing. – hit by the economic crisis, many governments across the eu have found adjustment measures and cuts to public services and social benefits to be the only way of reducing the fiscal deficit. most of the austerity policies target wages of employees in the public sector, child benefit, healthcare, maternity leave, pensions, education, free school meals, etc. since women are mostly employed in the public sector, and are the main benefactors of social allowances, the applied measures disproportionately affected them and have further contributed to increasing gender inequalities across the eu. on the occasion of international women’s day, on 8 march, we must make a strong commitment and ensure eu employment and economic policies take into account gender equality goals and commitments. some of the ways of achieving this, based on the current report, are investments in education and training – both initial and lifelong – in order to be able to adjust to changes in the labour market. moreover, using the european social fund and other eu programmes would enable greater social integration of women through employment. women have an important role to play in exiting the current crisis. recognizing and promoting their role is not a cost, but an investment.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. i would like to begin by thanking the rapporteur and his shadow rapporteurs for their dedicated, competent and successful work, which also involves the council and the cyprus presidency. they have put together a package that is important for europe's energy strategies in a considerable amount of time. whether you want to optimise security of supply, whether you want to use increasing shares of renewable energy in the electricity sector, whether you want to show solidarity in an emergency, whether you want to strengthen competition and thus the consumer, infrastructure is the necessary basis for this. we have a very good infrastructure in europe with our railways, our motorways and road networks, our european airspace with hubs and regional airports, our sea ports, our inland ports and also in the digital world of information and communication. when you compare the quality and capacity of our roads and railways, our airspace and our digital world with our gas and electricity networks, we are not anywhere near as well positioned for gas and electricity as we are for the transport of goods, goods and citizens in europe. we have an intact oil infrastructure, an intact infrastructure to transport biomass, bioenergy and also coal, and we now have to catch up in gas and electricity with what is possible for all the other goods, goods and services in europe in quality and capacity. firstly, it is a question of transnational planning. the old world, that was the power plant by the river, whether it was coal or nuclear, the cooling by the water, the web into the region like a spider web to the consumer at work and at home. the new world is a transfrontier, pan-european world, which includes the member states, but also countries such as norway, switzerland, the western balkans, ukraine, turkey and other european countries participating in our energy community. we have concrete plans for crossborder infrastructure development in larger regions, whether we mean the north sea countries or the mediterranean countries, central europe or countries on the periphery. secondly, we must work with all those involved to define projects of common interest, projects which are important for more than one member state. the commission will present its list of priorities in the summer, on the basis of which the council and parliament will decide on the priorities for the next few years. every two years we will continue the list, in close cooperation with the regulators, the transmission system operators, the national ministers responsible, the european energy industry, in order to determine in the coming years the order in which gas pipelines, electricity networks and bridges should be developed across the borders of the member states. this is to meet the mandate of completing the single market by the end of 2014 and bringing isolated islands countries not integrated into the european market out of their isolation in 2015 and linking them with their european neighbours, such as malta, cyprus, the baltic states and others. we have two major challenges. first, the planning time until approval, and second, the funding. with what you have just produced, we want to reduce the planning time for the determination of a route, for the determination of the laying of the line up to the official approval of the pipeline or the transmission network from currently - as the rapporteur reports - normally ten, twelve, fifteen years to a maximum of three and a half years. in three and a half years, if you have enough staff, you can make all the trade-offs. the question of environmental and landscape protection, the question of interference with the landscape, the distance requirement for settlements, all these questions can be resolved in three and a half years. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. on the contrary, after 10 to 12 years, acceptance is often much lower than in a coherent and intensive consultation process which takes three and a half years. then there is the financing: we anticipate the necessary investment in energy infrastructure in the european union of some 200 billion euros over the next few years. first of all, the funding must come from the market, which means that the regulators are needed. what interest, what compensation do i give to the person who invests in networks and pipelines? this is always a trade-off between the interests of consumers, who want to have the lowest possible cost of electricity and gas, and the interests of investors. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. investors have offers beyond the energy sector, in real estate, in industry, in other sectors of the economy and in infrastructure outside europe. we are competing with the new airport in istanbul, with a power plant in brazil or with an auto plant in china. we have to be attractive! that is why we need a clear and convincing european plan. the citizens and the investors must be made to understand that this pipeline is a business because it has become part of our european energy strategy. then the connecting europe facility. in recent years we have had experience of co-financing european energy infrastructure. the crisis programme you gave us a few years ago was the basis for some 800 million euros a year of co-financing. we are now building on the fact that there will be more than eur 5 billion available in the next multiannual budgetary framework for connecting europe in the area of energy infrastructure. we want to work with project bonds, we want to use the eib, we want to use national public structural banks as partners, we want to give interest rate subsidies, we want to give guarantees so that co-financing in euros and cents is not the only instrument and a toolbox can be intelligent and provide the right leverage for the individual case. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would like to thank parliament and the rapporteurs in particular once again. a year ago, it was unthinkable that this would work. we have now made great strides towards a pan-european energy infrastructure for electricity and gas with the package which parliament is about to adopt.

author of the draft opinion of the committee on regional development. − european regions must be regarded as equal partners in the process of locating and implementing trans-european energy investments and benefit from them on an equal footing at every stage. only an open and transparent public consultation process can minimise the social and economic costs of an investment. the committee on regional development sees investment in trans-european energy networks as an important opportunity to deepen the economic integration of the european union. however, to achieve this, the role of local and regional authorities in the planning and implementation of individual projects needs to be strengthened and the bureaucratic burden on businesses and other actors who will then implement them reduced. it is also important for us that all forms of eu aid to project promoters be granted on the basis of the expected costs to energy consumers, in order to avoid the socialisation of costs and the commercialisation of profits. finally, the trans-european energy networks should treat the distribution of energy from renewable sources in a non-discriminatory manner.
