rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. − mr president, on the external dimension of energy: the geopolitics of energy are changing, new producers are emerging and resources like shale gas are become more equally distributed, more diversified and the markets more liquid. we may soon see a global democratisation of energy, but we are not there yet, nor is the european union’s energy security guaranteed. the eu must therefore respond to the changing energy landscape in planning its energy policy up to 2050. gas – thanks to global shale evolution – and the increasing role of energy, is likely to play a much more long-term and prominent role in europe’s energy mix than the commission assumes in its energy roadmap, also allowing for greater emission reduction. also, the european commission’s over-optimistic assumptions on achieving globally-negotiated climate targets should be accompanied by a scenario b, in case the outcome is less positive. the eu’s external energy policy must be reinforced. we do have instruments like internal market competition law, the energy community treaty and the enp. it is good that growing external energy competence is happening, but we should go further and think of coordinating energy purchasing from outside the union and even go towards joint purchasing.
author of the draft opinion of the committee on regional development. - first of all, i would like to thank mrs tzaveli very much for her cooperation, for the conversation, for the atmosphere in which this report was prepared. the commissioner said that it was very important to have a long-term perspective. the horizon is important for consumers and investors alike. however, the number of amendments, submissions and scenarios contained in this report leads to a 'sneak' which is, of course, characteristic of many reports in the european parliament. so there's something for everyone there - supporters of nuclear, renewable and coal - and that's good, because that's the energy basket we need in europe. and that's why the decisions we make today will have a huge impact on our future. and so i'm afraid that we're facing challenges today that the document doesn't address, because it can't address them very well. on the one hand, we have the uncontrolled expansion of german renewable energy, which has led to a situation where many gas-fired power plants are simply shut down. common eu rules on the power market, on support for renewable energy, and work on the communityisation of this market are needed to make this future policy also common.
on behalf of the ecr group. the report we are presenting is the result of extremely difficult negotiations and an extremely difficult compromise, which unfortunately has been and is being challenged in this chamber. this is why we cannot agree to the wording of article 91, which means a radical tightening of climate policy, which entails raising the costs for all energy-intensive industries, such as paper, chemicals, fertilisers for agriculture, glass, steel for plants that compete at the same time with similar plants in china, russia, canada or the usa. in the context of free trade talks, this is particularly important, even more important than usual. total decarbonisation, which is mentioned in the report, is one of the european superstitions that has nothing to do with the energy reality - also in our part of the world. analysts estimate that by 2035, more than half of our energy will come from fossil fuels. hence, political discrimination against fossil fuels is not only unrealistic, but also has very negative consequences for our industry, blocks the necessary investment in energy, deprives the market of the necessary stability and is ultimately the main reason why energy in europe is the most expensive in the world.
in writing. the main objective of the proposed regulation is decarbonisation. the question is: does the economy need this, and is it better that efficiency gains - as the main goal - lead to decarbonisation? the claim that renewables will account for 75 to 97% of energy in 2050 and that co2 emissions will be reduced accordingly is unfounded. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market if it is granted through state resources. there is also no energy infrastructure project, and the legislation itself does not prohibit it. the second objective (after efficiency) should be energy security, which has been declining in recent years, not decarbonisation. in addition, the ets should be improved by means of a co2 absorption premium, e.g. for agriculture and forestry. i also think we need to pay more attention to geothermal energy. the eu cannot create an energy sector which is already uncompetitive on a global scale and reduces our overall competitiveness.
in writing. for me, as a miner and a member of parliament, the most worrying thing is the short-sighted approach. i believe that the role of fossil fuels in ensuring the european union's energy security should no longer be marginalized. coal should not be treated as a 'dirty fuel' but as a common good for citizens, and we should work together to optimise existing technologies and develop new ones that reduce the burden on the environment. the european commission's approach also fails to recognise that the key pillar of energy security is the reliance on and easy access to energy resources in the eu member states. it is therefore most rational from this point of view for countries to develop those energy technologies in which they have the greatest potential and experience. and those that guarantee a continuous supply of stable and cheap energy. i thank the rapporteur for reminding the european commission that it is up to the member states to define their own energy mix.
in writing. it is worth repeating with commissioner tajani: europe needs reindustrialisation today. it needs new jobs and a lasting economic recovery. the key factor determining the economic competitiveness and investment attractiveness of individual countries for industry is first and foremost the price of electricity, which largely determines the cost of production. the dynamics of global economic change and the economic competitiveness of individual countries are thus linked to current and expected electricity costs. so if we want to catch up with asia and america today, we need to focus more on actions to bring down prices. the key is to abandon the blind and ineffective energy and climate policy aimed at further reducing co2 emissions. that is why we cannot agree with many of the points made in the report by mrs tzaveli.
on behalf of the ppe group. i think that this action of testing extreme conditions, which will lead to the preparation of the directive and guide the further work of the european commission, is a great example of joint action for the safety of citizens, joint action of many countries and harmonisation of this work by the commission. that is why we should support them, even if some countries claim that this is their own competence. i believe that the safety of our citizens is our common good. what the commission is doing on this issue, these results of the tests under extreme conditions, are also important for countries that are just starting to build nuclear power stations, because in every country there are certain concerns, there is opposition, and in this situation we will be able to show that we care, we work, that certain nium standards are guaranteed in this matter. i would therefore ask the commission to put more emphasis on contacts with the countries neighbouring the european union. the commissioner mentioned that there were extreme conditions tests in ukraine. besides ukraine, there are other countries that are currently planning and building power plants. the cost issue can be a barrier to them. so they may want to take shortcuts, build in cheaper ways, hence the call for collaboration.
in writing. the draft resolution we are discussing today is a summary of the eu's grand project of putting european nuclear power plants through stress tests, i.e. tests of their resilience to extreme risks such as earthquakes, tsunamis, power cuts and core meltdowns. the safety inspections of 147 nuclear reactors in 15 member states, switzerland and ukraine are already a major success. the endurance testing procedure itself, consisting of a three-stage test process, has allowed to achieve verifiable data reflecting the actual safety level of the facility. the results of the tests were not as bad as those opposed to nuclear power had predicted. no closure of any power plant was requested and the recommendations made by the control authorities were mostly limited to making certain modifications, installing external power generators and training staff in emergency procedures. it is commendable that the resolution states that these tests were only for extreme situations and cannot replace the detailed safety checks carried out in such establishments. it is also very appropriate to call on the community to take all possible measures to prevent radioactive waste from being deposited in areas where there is a high risk of natural disasters. the concept of sharing and implementing good practices in the field of renewable energy generation should also be supported. in conclusion, i would say that this is a very good document and one that deserves our support.
member of the commission. − mr president, first of all let me express my sincere appreciation to the two rapporteurs, kriton arsenis and bas eickhout, the secretariat and the many shadow rapporteurs for their hard work on these two legislative proposals. thanks to what i believe has been excellent and efficient cooperation between the three institutions, including the very committed work done by the cypriot presidency, we are able to conclude the legislative procedure with first-reading agreement on both files. on lulucf, we have, overall, been able to secure an outcome that is an important step forward in meeting our international commitments and in developing our climate policy. the compromise meets the main objectives of the commission proposal: it is in line with the respective decision taken in the international climate talks in durban and ensures the full implementation of the international requirements under the unfccc and the kyoto protocol both now and towards 2020. it will allow harmonised accounting for the greenhouse gas emissions and removals from the lulucf sector. including this sector in the national accounts of the member states closes an important gap and ensures that in the future all sectors can contribute to the mitigation of climate change. the outcome strikes a good balance, as it reflects and safeguards concerns of landowners while confirming the high level of ambition desired by the commission and interested parties. on the two most important political aspects of the commission’s proposal, the compromise firstly ensures full mandatory accounting for agricultural activities, starting with the period from 2020 onwards, but already sets in place a more gradual approach for accounting for these activities during the period up to 2020. this should be seen as a first step and as part of the greater effort needed to collect data on agricultural land. secondly, it ensures the framework for shedding light on member states’ lulucf actions in order to enhance best practices and to collect information which could feed into further steps for regulating the lulucf sector in the future. this decision is also a central piece of legislation for a sustainable bioeconomy. by including greenhouse gas accounting from the lulucf sector into eu law and setting out a roadmap to advance the methodologies and systems to track greenhouse gases related to agricultural soils, we are making sure that emissions and removal related to biomass use and carbon sequestration are fully reflected in the eu’s accounts. as regards the next steps, swift implementation of the decision will be important to enhance our knowledge of this sector. my services will of course be in close contact with the member states to discuss what needs to be done and when it needs to be done. furthermore, let me highlight that the first article of the lulucf decision points out that this is only a first step. the next step is related to the question the rapporteur. - thank you very much, madam president! commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your kind words. i am very pleased to present to you the final result of almost a year's work on the resolution of consumer disputes. the regulation and directive which i am sure the european parliament will adopt today will be the cure for many of the problems that polish, danish and cypriot presidencies (also thank you) is truly european. we want both consumers and businesses - 500 million citizens - to benefit from the entire european market, from the huge range of goods from 27 countries. in the last 12 months, only 10% of consumers have bought any goods or services online from abroad. one of the main reasons for this is a lack of trust, but with the odr platform, consumers will no longer have to worry about buying goods and services on foreign websites, because even if something goes wrong, we can be sure that we will resolve the matter in their own language. after all, there is no well-functioning market without consumer trust in entrepreneurs and vice versa. this trust, especially in cross-border transactions, will gradually grow. the fair settlement of consumer disputes, or adr, which was developed by my colleague mr louis grech - whom i also thank very much for his cooperation - is being built on the existing parts of the arbitration, mediation and conciliation systems in the member states. the directive will complement these systems in all sectors, improve their quality and speed up the resolution of disputes, which will be a major challenge to the judicial systems in the member states. today, in europe, the average time for a court to decide a commercial dispute is about 450 days, whereas under the new system it will take at most 90 days. the advantage of non-judicial systems over traditional ones is, among other things, their amicable nature, since after a settlement has been reached, the parties can return to commercial relations and there are no winners and losers, as is often the case in court. i am very pleased that we have succeeded in making this initiative more federal and more european than the commission had proposed. the platform will not only handle cross-border disputes but also domestic disputes. this will make the platform more compatible with the virtual reality, where there are no physical boundaries. not only consumers but also businesses will be able to benefit from it. it was absolutely crucial for me to simplify the platform for consumers and make it more understandable and easier to use. we will see how well it has worked in a couple of months, but i am glad we agreed that before citizens can use it, the commission has a duty to test it with business and consumer organisations and to report to the european parliament. i hope that together we can ensure that the tool that citizens will be able to use is fully in line with their expectations. and finally, for this project to succeed, information for consumers is essential. our citizens need to know where to find information about online dispute resolution. we all need to be involved in this process: the internet service providers, us members of parliament, the european commission your europe website, so that citizens can really benefit from this new instrument. thank you, and i look forward to an interesting debate.

in writing. − the commission proposal for a directive on alternative dispute resolution (adr) for consumer disputes aims to provide a simple, useful and inexpensive way of resolving disputes concerning the sale of goods and the provision of services in the european union. once implemented, this directive will enable all consumers residing in the eu to have access to a high-quality adr entity. despite the improvements in consumer protection since the launch of the single market, gaps still exist which make life difficult for citizens, and consumers in particular. both the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union contain provisions requiring the eu to ensure a high level of consumer protection. furthermore, the tfeu provides that the internal market is to comprise an area without internal frontiers in which the free movement of goods and services is ensured. the directive's main objective is to address the three most important and persistent barriers to access to alternative dispute resolution by consumers and businesses. first, the scope of adr remains heterogeneous both in sectoral and geographical terms. secondly, many consumers and traders are simply not aware of the benefits of using alternative dispute resolution mechanisms or are not sufficiently informed about them. i hope that the measures taken will lead to a solution of these problems in the future.

in writing. − it is currently estimated that 60% of businesses and up to 90% of consumers in the european union do not make the right choice when selling or buying cross-border. for both, the main reason for the lack of confidence in this type of transaction is the complexity of the procedures and the higher potential costs of handling complaints and resolving disputes. alternative dispute resolution methods are fast, cheap, do not require the use of a specialist lawyer and offer much more flexibility than court proceedings. these extrajudicial mechanisms are already known throughout the eu, but have been developed in a very heterogeneous way. in some countries, they may be the result of public initiatives, both at central and local level, while in others they must be privately initiated. it is precisely because of this diversity that the status of decisions adopted by the competent authorities may also vary. the new law requires member states to make available and monitor the functioning of non-judicial dispute settlement systems in all sectors. in addition, the relevant national authorities will receive consumer complaints from across the eu. i believe that mechanisms that effectively protect citizens, providing cheap and quick redress, are not only essential for the development of e-commerce, but also offer an opportunity to relieve the burden on the judicial system. that is why i fully support today's directive.

in writing. − the regulation on common rules for monitoring and evaluating preliminary draft budgetary plans and ensuring the correction of excessive deficits in euro area member states, together with the regulation on the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance of euro area member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability, commonly referred to as the 'two-pack', are the next steps in the process of renewing economic governance in the european union that we have initiated with the so-called 'six-pack'. these acts improve economic and budgetary coordination in the euro area, while maintaining the appropriate balance between the powers of the european commission and the scope of democratic legitimacy and responsibility of national parliaments. the introduction of a common budgetary timetable complements the european semester procedure for the euro area, thereby achieving greater coherence between national budgets and recommendations made at community level. the amendments drawn up by the committee on economic and monetary affairs, which introduce additional elements to the regulation, such as the obligation to establish national fiscal councils to assess budgetary plans, a broader scope of information requirements for the commission on the macroeconomic models used and the preventive financial assistance granted, the right of parliament to call representatives of the troika to meet and the increased automation of the decision-making process by extending the scope of the reverse qualified majority mechanism, should also be welcomed.

in writing. − venture capital funds still play a small role in the development of business projects. the blame must be placed on both sides, both on the part of potential investors and on the part of companies seeking financing for their projects. entrepreneurs lack not only the preparation to present their idea properly, but also a strategy for the development of their company that would attract investors. venture capital funds are a common form of financing for innovation projects around the world. a potential investor who is interested in a business venture contributes equity to the company, thus taking a certain number of shares. he becomes a co-owner of the company. this form of investment carries a high risk of failure on the one hand and can generate a high rate of return on the other. entrepreneurs who are just trying to get to the market, often with an innovative, unique solution or project, complain about the lack of funding sources and little interest from potential investors. market representatives, i.e. venture capital fund managers, argue that there are not enough projects worth mentioning in poland. few, they feel, have the chance to make the desired profits in the future. i believe that in these difficult times of economic crisis, everything must be done to facilitate the operation of these funds, as this can contribute to the creation of new jobs.
i fully supported this regulation of the parliament and the council on european social entrepreneurship funds. this business is a new and growing investment segment in europe, although the situation varies widely from country to country. it is worth mentioning here that in each country this enterprise today employs between 3 and 8% of the total workforce. the aim of these companies is not only to generate financial profits but also to carry out important social missions. however, entrepreneurship still faces a number of barriers to its development. the proposed solutions will overcome at least part of these difficulties, in particular facilitating the raising of capital. i therefore think that this regulation should be supported.

rapporteur. − mr president, that was not easy as a report – i mean, boy! especially for some of the members from the smaller and medium-sized member states, who are personally influenced by the proposals that we put on the table. i mean, this is one of those rare occasions when the european parliament has the right of initiative, and i think that the most important thing is that we cannot shy away from that responsibility. we decided with roberto to choose a pragmatic solution. what were the other options? asking for more seats? i think that would be the worst possible signal in today’s crisis and, seriously, could we think of ourselves asking for more seats? that would be the only posture coming from the european parliament. i do not think that that is the way forward. the other option was to ask for a radical overhaul of the system. it is true that if we wanted to have a smooth progression from the smallest to the biggest state when it comes to the number of citizens represented by a single member of this house, with the bigger the member state the more citizens a given member of this house represents, we would have to have a more radical solution, where some member states would gain seats and some would lose more than one. but could we realistically see a radical solution accepted either by this house or by the council? we decided that for the moment no state should lose more than one seat and that no state should gain seats. such a profound change can only be made when other institutional questions are up for review, because our institutional set-up is based on the balance between what happens in the european parliament and what happens in the council. my view is that we can only have a radical solution in conjunction with other institutional reforms; most importantly, with the weighting of votes in the council, which is not now up for discussion. we will however – and i can promise you that – come back to that issue in the near future, when maybe we can have a system which is a little bit more far-reaching. our system in this house, when it comes to seats, is that of digressive proportionality. we always, however, have a dilemma: how digressive and how proportional should the system be? we looked at the historical development when it was the biggest states which were progressively losing seats. the system is skewed to their disadvantage. that is why we decided to remedy that. our point of reference consisted of the severin/lamassoure report, primarily, not because it was the best, but because it was voted by this house in the previous legislature. no wonder that we used it as a point of reference. that is why we care very much about the relationship between representativeness on the one hand and demography on the other. that is why we proposed what we proposed. in our system the medium and smaller states are still over-represented, as the purely proportional system taking into account what we have in the council, constitutionally, would not make much sense. although i understand why some of you have submitted amendments, we as rapporteurs cannot support amendments which question either the rationale or the main principles of our thinking and of our report. in that respect, i feel bound by the vote that we had in the committee on constitutional affairs. for us to be effective, for our proposal to carry the day in the council, we need a strong majority in this house backing our report and, therefore, even though i know that for some of you it will not be easy, i ask you to support our compromise. not because this is the best compromise in the ideal world, but i think that there is simply no other solution visible on the short-term horizon. thank you very much for your support and i hope that we can tackle the issue at least for the moment.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on regional development. − mr president, for years there has been no progress in the system of national and regional accounts with regard to the regional level, while the budgetary responsibility of regional governments has increased substantially. more than one third of total public expenditure in the union is now managed by levels of government other than the central level, exceeding 50 % by far in some member states. indeed, collecting regional government statistics is key to understanding public spending choices and the reasons for regional disparities, for establishing coherence and complementarity between interventions and different governance levels, for informing future investment decisions and improving the efficiency of scarce public resources, as well as for assessing the impact of policy intervention, which is particularly important in the case of cohesion policy. the reporting of data following the cofog classification of expenditure should be compulsory in order to allow the commission and stakeholders in general to analyse and understand the patterns of regional public expenditure in its functional breakdown, as well as in its ultimate efficiency and impact.
we shall be voting on this report tomorrow, and it is really high time. the current methods were regulated over 17 years ago, and the world - and even more so the european economies - no longer looks the same today as it did then. let's describe our economic development using current methods that correspond to today's reality. statistics are essential for the informed and responsible formulation of european policies. this system must therefore be precise and timely. this will increase the reality and transparency of the entities we're describing, which in this case is the public sector. the citizen, the citizen, will be the main beneficiary of these new regulations, because he will be able to receive reliable and up-to-date information about the economy of the chosen region. this will also benefit the entire administration of the member states, which often bases its work and decisions on statistical data. we need to encourage further development of methodological research, as this will help us to better understand the economic situation in our region. we're in a crisis, people are talking about it all the time. this crisis has just shown how important it is to understand the present situation in the context of the recent past. consistent, consistent and reliable data gives us the ability to better visualize economic phenomena. these statistics are not only used to describe what has happened, but also to inform public decisions about the future, and without them, policy has no relevance to the reality it wants to influence. we therefore support this important and timely report.

recognition of the legal form of mutual societies in most member states, their effective functioning within the internal market continues to be hampered. the current legal rules differ on such basic issues as the formalities for the formation, operation and winding-up of a company. the range of specific services they may offer is also regulated in very different ways. the main objective of the in writing. − since the end of 2010, a wave of protests and demonstrations has swept across north africa and the middle east, changing the region's internal structure and character. regardless of their position in the region, women participated in these events as demonstrators, organizers and leaders, playing key roles alongside their male counterparts. today, they continue to fight for representation in the newly formed assemblies and governments, and for equal rights in the new constitutions. the results of these revolutionary movements, known as the arab spring, vary from country to country for many reasons. this report focuses on four north african countries egypt, libya, morocco and tunisia and i think that narrows the subject down too much. women in tunisia, and to some extent also in egypt, morocco and libya, have gained quite advanced legislation to protect their rights. however, in practice, the achievement of effective equality is still limited, often due to, for example, the lack of effective law enforcement and traditional perceptions of the role of women.
in writing. − the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states and the european community and its member states, signed in cotonou on 23 june 2000 (the cotonou agreement), provides the basis for cooperation with the acp states. part iv of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the overseas association decision of 27 november 2001 concerning the association between the eu (formerly the ec) and a number of overseas countries and territories (octs) constitute the legal basis for the association with the octs. the commission communication of 7 december 2011 entitled 'preparation of the multiannual financial framework for the financing of eu cooperation in favour of the african, caribbean and pacific states and the overseas countries and territories for the period 2014-2020 (11th european development fund) ' is the background document for this report. it is therefore necessary to maintain a significant role for budget support, while strengthening the human rights dialogue with the beneficiary countries. at the same time, it is important to bear in mind the importance of article 96 of the cotonou agreement, which allows for the suspension of access to aid in the event of a flagrant breach of the rules of the agreement by the state concerned. this conditional clause should be accompanied by a common eu framework. the eu must continue to support regional integration processes, especially through regional edf programmes. many acp countries are small economies and therefore it is very important for them to have access to infrastructure (energy, roads, warehouses, etc.) that allows the development of genuine regional markets.
in writing. − the mff deal agreed by the council in the last meeting of 7-8 february produced an outdated agreement which priorities fall short of eu’s current and future needs. the deal decreases for the first time eu’s budget for 2014-20 by 3 %, making the levels of payments similar to those in 1988-1989. additionally, the deal overlooks ep’s position on the mff, as also expressed in the resolution adopted on 23 october 2012. acting this way, the council completely disregards ep’s competences set out by the lisbon treaty. the current resolution makes it clear to the council that the ep will reject the mff deal in the present form. yet the resolution also expresses our readiness to enter negotiations with the council with the aim of improving the agreement. our demands are reasonable. we want a modern long-term budget with greater flexibility and transparency. we ask for an agreement that invests in areas which are essential for job creation and promotion of growth, for instance: research, education and cross-border infrastructure. taking into consideration that the ep’s position could produce an agreement that meets the needs of our citizens in these times of financial difficulties, we are keen to begin serious negotiations with the council.
in writing. − together with the ecr group, i voted against the changes proposed by parliament to the new eu financial perspective for 2014-2020. the compromise on the eu budget negotiated in february envisaged a focus on cohesion policy, while parliament is calling for a shift to research, climate and innovation, which will mean a reduction in funding for poland and other eastern european countries. the ep also wants to introduce a financial transaction tax, which my group strongly opposes.
in writing. - due to a voting machine failure, which i had reported to the services, i was unable to support the ecr group's amendment 1 to the resolution on the multiannual financial framework. however, i have entered my vote in favour of this amendment in the minutes of the meeting of 13 march 2013.
in writing. - we believe that the european parliament must negotiate (the eu budget) first and foremost, and we support most of the demands of the parliament, which should be taken seriously. we do not agree with the wording that rejects the budget agreement. so we like the substance of the resolution, but not the rhetoric.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, like many of you, i disagree with the budget negotiated at the council summit. however, i believe that this compromise, which is a rotten compromise in poland's case, is better than the provisional budget. that's why i've supported all the bills that call for the budget to be passed.
in writing. − this regulation lays down the principles to be followed in the compilation and publication of basic macroeconomic data in the eu. in practice, the commission proposal is a broad and more detailed review of the european system of national and regional accounts (esa), based on the latest revision of the united nations system of national accounts (sna) adopted in 2008. statistics are at the heart of the public debate: independent, reliable, comparable and up-to-date data are essential for policy-makers and for economic operators and citizens to measure, assess and monitor the economic situation and its changes. every effort should be made to ensure that the esa review provides eu citizens with the highest quality macroeconomic statistics based on a sound methodology and in accordance with a precise timetable.
in writing. − in practice, the commission proposal is a broad and more detailed review of the european system of national and regional accounts (esa), based on the latest revision of the united nations system of national accounts (sna) adopted in 2008. statistics are at the heart of the public debate: independent, reliable, comparable and up-to-date data are essential for policy-makers and for economic operators and citizens to measure, assess and monitor the economic situation and its changes. every effort should be made to ensure that the esa review provides eu citizens with the highest quality macroeconomic statistics based on a sound methodology and in accordance with a precise timetable.
in writing. − the flag state control aspects of the 2006 maritime labour convention need to be transposed into eu law in a more detailed and concrete way. the main benefit of incorporating the convention into eu law is that it will allow for more effective enforcement of the provisions of the convention in the eu, for example through eu infringement procedures, which will also have a positive impact on compliance. the eu flag state rules should reflect much more the specific and unambiguous requirements of the convention in order to avoid divergent interpretations in the member states which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. the proposal for a directive is part of a wider set of european legal measures introduced to apply certain standards of the maritime labour convention (mlc) adopted by the international labour organisation (ilo) on 23 february 2006 in geneva. at this stage, the mlc has been ratified by 30 countries representing more than 59% of the world fleet tonnage, and the condition for entry into force of the convention, i.e. the requirement of ratification by 30 countries representing 33% of the world gross tonnage, is therefore fulfilled.
in writing. − while not all of the solutions in the anna jensen report are worthy of support, the budgetary priorities set for 2014 fully reflect my convictions: promoting growth, employment and competitiveness and focusing on tackling unemployment, especially among young people. in many countries, the labour market situation for young people is dramatic and without support from the eu budget, public funding for activation programmes would be minimal in the current economic climate.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the anne jensen report on the 2014 budgetary guidelines, as it rightly points out that the budget must provide for adequate payment appropriations and that unjustified cuts must be avoided. the union budget is an investment budget which, when properly composed, can be an effective tool for overcoming the crisis. these requirements must be reflected in the 2014 budget. the union budget must support economic growth and competitiveness and increase employment, especially among young people. the council has already made concrete commitments in this regard, inter alia, in the form of the growth and jobs pact and the youth guarantee. these commitments cannot be met without adequate means. nor can the credibility of the union be undermined by a continuous increase in outstanding liabilities, which have already reached eur 217 billion and are still rising.
in writing. - the european parliament is an institution close to the citizens. europeans directly elect their representatives to the european parliament, they can petition the parliament, they can indirectly initiate the legislative process through a european citizens' initiative, and they can participate in the many public consultations conducted by individual members and the european commission. yet the voter turnout is quite low. in 2009, only 43% of the population went to the polls, and we should change that. citizens should be able to take an active part in the work of the union, and this is possible through elections in which europeans directly elect their representatives. the key issue here, however, is the allocation of mandates between the individual member states. i supported today's resolution because the distribution of seats has a direct impact on the representation of the citizens of the member states in the european parliament. the principle that a member from a larger member state should represent a greater number of citizens than a member from a smaller member state and vice versa, and the fact that the larger the population of a member state, the more seats it is entitled to, are important provisions to ensure adequate representation of all europeans.
in writing. − the report on the composition of the european parliament after the 2014 elections, adopted today, is far from ideal, but it is the only compromise solution currently possible. it guarantees that no country will lose or gain more than one seat, with the exception of germany, which has to lose three under the lisbon treaty. a radical redistribution of ep seats could only be carried out while taking into account other institutional issues, such as the voting system in the council. however, a moderate reform of the composition of the ep after the 2014 elections is inevitable due to the need to find seats for croatian meps and the implementation of the treaty provisions. the provisional, pragmatic solution voted on today, however, provides a good starting point for establishing a new, durable and transparent system for the distribution of seats in the ep before the start of the 2019-2024 parliamentary term. that new system should allow for the automatic redistribution of seats between member states on the basis of an objective criterion, the principle of degressive proportionality and any demographic changes in the member states.
in writing. − the proposal for a number of smaller eu member states, including latvia, to reduce their number of meps cannot be supported. i believe that every eu member state should be represented in all the european parliament's committees in order to ensure that the interests of all eu citizens are fully represented in the most important european policy areas. even at this european parliament's session, smaller member states are not represented in all committees, while large eu member states germany, france, italy, etc. are represented by several meps in each committee. latvia, which has already lost 10% of its population in recent years, will have even less influence in european decision-making processes. i therefore do not support this report which proposes to reduce the number of latvian meps from nine to eight.
in writing. − the rapporteur members have done a great deal of work to balance the member states' demands with the necessary legal changes. i personally think the changes should be even deeper. we should be voting today on a further reduction in the number of meps and a more profound change in the proportions between member states. it must not be forgotten that the new member states are the ones who lose the most from the changes being introduced. the report also lacks any changes to the vote counting systems. i supported the amendment to deepen proportionality in elections so as to increase the presence of small parties in the new parliamentary term. i hope the council will accept the changes i have proposed.
in writing. - vodka is one of poland's most important export products. poland is the largest producer of vodka in the european union: it produces about 290 million litres, of which more than 50 million litres are exported. recently, the polish sejm took steps to safeguard the interests of polish vodka producers. on 13 january 2013, an amendment to the law on the production of spirit drinks, which was adopted in may last year, entered into force. by definition, polish vodka is an alcoholic beverage produced in poland, obtained exclusively from rye, wheat, oats, barley or potatoes grown in our country. the geographical indication 'polska wódka/polish vodka' will benefit financially both farmers and producers and the state budget. i am convinced that the new geographical indication will contribute to further increasing the export of polish vodka. the european commission implementing regulation amending annexes ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on the definition, description, presentation, labelling and the protection of geographical indications of spirit drinks safeguards the interests of polish producers of spirit drinks. that is why i support the above regulation. in the light of the above, i have decided to vote against the motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation amending annexes ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on the definition, description, presentation, labelling and the protection of geographical indications of spirit drinks.
in writing. - today, one of the most important votes of this term of office took place in the european parliament. for countries that joined the union in 2004, such as poland, the discrimination experienced by farmers benefiting from direct payments is a very important issue that remains to be resolved. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. we therefore welcome the report by mr capoulas santos, in which the appropriations for the polish countryside are much higher than the amounts negotiated at the last summit of heads of state or government.
in writing. - the proposed reform of the common agricultural policy contains more elements of continuation than of change. there was no concept for proposing objective criteria for the allocation of funds. the solutions proposed in the current reform, while closing some of the gaps, do not eliminate them. the biggest beneficiaries are those who have had the least - the baltic states. the countries with the highest subsidies lose a little bit, but it's a small amount because the countries that benefit are small. the 'middle countries', which include poland, receive little more. to this must be added a reduction of eur 44 billion in the common agricultural policy (cap) from the current financial perspective for the period 2014-2020. the changes proposed by the committee on agriculture and rural development in the european parliament's plenary session have had the effect of 'de-normalising' and making the cap more farmer-friendly than what the european commission proposed. when we started the discussions on cap reform, we said we needed a strong cap backed by the right budget. however, the eu budget has been reduced. as i said, the cap is 44 billion less, so it is difficult to implement a reform that should help to raise the income of farmers who are still at an unsatisfactory level, as is the case with only 7% of farmers under 40.
in writing. − to ensure that the cap is fully effective and unleashes its development potential, direct payments must be equalised. i fully support all amendments that implement this principle. in view of the chaos of the vote and the constant attempts to interrupt it, i believe that there may have been a mistake in the vote on some amendments, including the one mentioned above. of course i'll adjust my vote according to the national interest of the poles.
in writing. − rural development programmes are, in addition to direct payments, a key source of funding for agricultural regions from eu funds. such a region is poland's mazowsze, where nearly 70 percent of the province's land is used for agriculture. the motion for a resolution which i voted for contains a number of important points. for example, it draws attention to the issue of organic farming, which is highly desirable in the face of the threat of gmo crops. it proposes to continue the current allocation of funds between member states and to extend the agricultural advisory service. the rural development programmes cover forestry. the provisions on the criteria for less-favoured areas are relevant. the scheme also aims to pay farmers who have left farming and transferred their holdings to others. agricultural policy must remain a priority for the european commission, and the solutions implemented through support programmes should in particular help to stimulate innovation and strengthen cooperation mechanisms.
in writing. - by voting in favour of the adoption of the regulation as it stands, i agree to the opening of negotiations with the council. the committee on agriculture has taken note of a number of important changes. for example, penalties for greening have been limited to greening payments rather than single farm payments. more flexibility and a risk-based approach to control and inspection are also called for. a provision has been introduced for the publication of the names of the beneficiaries of the common agricultural policy. the proposal by my group on the exchange rate for payments, which was adopted by the members of the committee, also deserves attention. it will be calculated on the basis of the average monthly exchange rate, not the exchange rate on a specific day. this solution is more favourable to polish farmers. the solutions provided for in the regulation should simplify the rules for the financing and management of the union's agricultural policy.
in writing. − the new cap should take account of the following priorities: transparency, environmental protection and simplification. first, there is transparency. the names of all farmers receiving payments should be made public. there is a need for greater openness in public life, especially when it comes to spending public money. second, the protection of the environment. greening should be a necessary condition for farmers to receive payments. at the same time, the greening model must be adapted to local conditions. for example, the agricultural situation in france and poland is so different that it is difficult to apply identical solutions without harming farmers. in addition, farmers should respect the principles of cross compliance, such as soil and water protection, the control of animal and plant diseases, food safety, and the protection of biodiversity. and third, simplify. small farmers should be exempted from the obligation to comply with the cross-compliance rules. this will make life easier for small farms, which are the most likely to produce organic food. the second important requirement is the introduction of multiannual payment applications: this will reduce bureaucratic burdens. the cap thus designed should serve european farmers and food consumers well. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of a negotiating mandate on the shape of the new common agricultural policy.
in writing. - europe needs to re-industrialize today. it needs new jobs and a lasting economic recovery. the key factor determining the economic competitiveness and investment attractiveness of individual countries for industry is first and foremost the price of electricity, which largely determines the cost of production. the dynamics of global economic change and the economic competitiveness of individual countries are thus linked to current and expected electricity costs. so if we want to catch up with asia and america today, we need to focus more on actions to bring down prices. the key is to abandon the blind and ineffective energy and climate policy aimed at further reducing co2 emissions. that is why we cannot agree with many of the points made in the report by mrs tzaveli.
in writing. - action towards a low-carbon economy must be based on real conditions, not on the ambitions of euro-bureaucrats and declarations forced on us by lobby groups. this resolution is a typical example of such negative activity. it is one thing to push for renewable energy, which i support, but it is another to push for clean and safe nuclear energy, which i support. however, it is naive and frivolous to talk about a low- or zero-carbon economy without any economic vision for the eu countries in the perspective of 2050, and without any vision for how to use available and cheap alternative energy sources, and without any vision for the future consumption pattern. i propose that the commission should employ science fiction writers for this purpose, not the european parliament. this ridiculous project has no practical future unless it takes full account of climate justice, i.e. the distribution of the global and eu climate burden based on per capita co2 emissions. because it's not, i voted for it.
in writing. - i voted today to adopt the report by mrs tzaveli on the future energy policy of the european union. the report sets targets for 2050 for greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy, energy efficiency and indicates the benefits that can be achieved by investing in and developing these energy policy areas. we need a clean and sustainable energy system that will lead to equal competitiveness and independence in the energy market in the future. the development of these areas is of great importance in view of the ever-increasing demand for energy. i also welcomed the fact that the report does not ignore the issue of environmental protection. i am glad that the european parliament is taking a specific position on this matter and i believe that we are able to achieve the objectives set out in this report.
in writing. − the 2050 energy action plan is an important document because long-term policy strategies are essential when planning for costly energy investments. the rejection of some of the most radical demands, such as the eu's commitment to green energy and the discrimination against shale gas, should be welcomed. the resolution adopted by parliament today is not without its very serious flaws. this includes underestimating the role of shale gas in building the eu's energy capacity, building an energy strategy on the assumption of a global climate agreement, lacking plans to coordinate energy purchases outside the union and lacking a credible cost analysis for ambitious energy and climate targets. first of all, however, it is unacceptable to call for a change in the rules of the european carbon trading system by suspending emission allowances (backloading) when the price of the allowances falls. in my view, changing the previously agreed legal framework of the scheme to manipulate emissions prices violates the principles of the eu ets as a market instrument, reduces its credibility and distorts sustainable and competitive access to energy.
in writing. − energy security and climate change prevention are of paramount importance. the decisions we make now will affect not only our future but also the future of future generations. therefore, all these matters must be carefully considered. energy efficiency and reducing pollution in europe are important. but what is the real effect of the union spending vast sums of money on this purpose when the rest of the world does not follow the basic principles? is there a real chance of influencing the biggest emitters of greenhouse gases like china, india, brazil or the united states to reduce emissions and how to do that? the decarbonisation process should be gradual. companies must be given sufficient time to adapt to the proposed changes. the effects of this could be negative for the economy. some companies will slow down or raise prices, and some will move capital outside the eu, where they will not have to pay fines. in conclusion, i would like to stress the importance of the decisions we will take in this area. all the tools to prevent global warming and its negative consequences should be developed for the benefit of future generations. therefore, every effort should be made to develop an action plan in this regard.
in writing. − unfortunately, the report was not acceptable because of the clause calling for reform of the european co2 emissions trading system.
in writing. − in december 2011, the european commission (ec) adopted the energy action plan 2050, a long-term strategy that takes into account the opportunities and challenges associated with achieving the european union's (eu) 2050 emissions reduction target while ensuring the security of energy supply and europe's competitiveness. the energy sector generates about 80% of total emissions in the eu. the 2050 target is therefore a test for existing energy systems. in particular, paragraph 91 which talks about tightening climate policy goes far beyond the previously included compromise on so-called back-loading (this is about faster extinguishing of allowances during ets stage iii). i believe that these regulations will be detrimental to our industry, which in turn could lead to a reduction in jobs in the energy and mining sectors and an increase in the already high unemployment rate. that's why i'm voting against it.
in writing. - the tzaveli report contains many very good solutions: it calls for diversification of hydrocarbon suppliers, greater energy solidarity and increased energy expenditure in the eu. these are important considerations, given that the eu today produces only 7% of the world's energy, with ever-increasing demand. however, the itre committee has already succeeded in 'squeezing' in unrelated elements to the report: amendments that distort its composition and the main idea of the honourable member. among them is the 91st amendment. it provides for a very damaging non-market solution for the european economy, namely the withdrawal of part of the oco2 emission allowances. they are contrary to the decisions taken so far and are disrupting the european economy. so are the amendments on shale gas and green energy. i was unable to support such negative solutions, which is why i voted against the report.
in writing. − solidarny poland, which i represent in the european parliament, is in favour of basing european energy on coal and gas - natural resources that provide a significant number of jobs and are currently the basis of the eu's energy basket. we are opposed to the development of nuclear energy, but we leave the final decision to the member states. we believe that any 'yes' to the atom must be backed up by a significant amount of regulation to protect the environment and people from the negative impacts of nuclear power plants.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament’s resolution on strengthening the fight against racism and xenophobia. this resolution is vital to improving our union by way of tolerance and understanding of others. we must not forget that ours is a union developed of 27 differing countries with multiple religions, cultures, and ethnicities. these facts should indicate that ‘united in diversity’ is not only a slogan but a realistic aspect of the eu. the noticeable increase in hate crimes is also quite startling, many of which were based on ethnicity. as we all know, the european union was built on the idea of preventing war and moving forward together, which includes our tolerance of other ethnicities. furthermore, the european union is based on the common values of respect for human rights and the rule of law and is underpinned by the promotion of tolerance. thus, i strongly support the recommendation for member states to further their efforts in educating their respective societies/citizens on the importance of tolerance for others. i feel that more can be achieved to better our states and our union if we all work together in harmony, than if we continue down this road of racism and prejudice.
in writing. − the report raises too many doubts to support it in its present form. in this context, it is also worth noting the controversy surrounding the mandate given to the european food safety authority to prepare a report on substances affecting the endocrine system in humans. unfortunately, questions have been raised again about the independence of the group of experts appointed to this task. conflicts of interest have been identified on a number of occasions in the work of the agency.
in writing. − the increase in the number of cases of hormonal disorders and diseases in humans in recent years should be taken very seriously. the endocrine system regulates many of the body's functions, including reproduction, metabolism, growth, water and mineral metabolism, and heart function. there are worrying developments, especially in relation to reproduction, with which endocrine disruptors appear to be strongly associated. the precautionary principle is and should remain the guiding principle of the union's chemicals policy. lack of complete knowledge cannot be an excuse for passivity. the risk of irreversible changes in the environment and the human body is simply too high. there are currently around 27 000 scientific reports on endocrine disruptors and their effects on humans and animals. the incidence and detection of a number of diseases are skyrocketing worldwide. the increasing incidence of potentially reproductive disorders is particularly noteworthy, but there is also an increase in foetal damage, cancer and diabetes, and an increase in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and adhd. as you can see, the problem is so important that it cannot be ignored.
in writing. - the european union is at a turning point in its labour market policy, with a shrinking working age population. without more immigration, it will fall by another 14 million people in the next 10 years. this phenomenon not only affects the long-term balance of european pension systems, but also leads to a shortage of skilled workers in the short to medium term. a key way of solving this dual dilemma of a declining working age population and a shortage of skilled workers is skilled immigration. european citizens have already understood this, and eurobarometer surveys show that 70% of them consider immigrants to be essential to the european economy. however, it is equally clear that immigration without a strategy is a source of problems and a threat to the eu's competitiveness. member states should aim at a qualitative rather than a quantitative migration policy. the challenge of attracting highly skilled workers is already clear. it is already clear that the integration of citizens of other eu and third countries with migrant backgrounds is becoming a major social issue of our time.
in writing. − recognising the high harmfulness of asbestos materials, we should make every effort to eliminate asbestos and all its derivatives from our environment as quickly as possible. this is a necessary step, but it is nevertheless a relatively expensive one. in view of the above, poland has set the end date of the asbestos removal programme as 2032. the date indicated will allow for a gradual changeover without the need to incur the very high one-off and sudden costs of replacing asbestos roofing with harmless panels. in my view, setting a time frame for the elimination of all asbestos residues seems to be a good step in the interests of public health.
in writing. − the report of the committee on employment and social affairs touches on an important public health aspect of the removal of all asbestos-containing products from the environment. local communities, for example in rural areas, are not always fully aware of the risks of exposure to hazardous material. asbestos landfills, often located in rural areas and having a negative impact on groundwater, also require adequate protection.
in writing. - the problems caused by the presence of asbestos-containing products in our environment are undeniable. each year, tens of thousands of people are diagnosed with diseases caused by exposure to asbestos fibres. we must do our utmost to reduce, in a skilful and intelligent manner, the risks to human health posed by asbestos in the immediate environment. particular attention should be paid to rural areas, where there is a much higher incidence of asbestos in various forms being used on farms. systemic, regular actions are needed to increase the effectiveness of local asbestos removal programmes. local communities living in rural areas should be aware of the health risks associated with asbestos. further intensive and wide-ranging information campaigns on this issue are essential. asbestos landfills very often located in rural areas are another problem, with negative effects on groundwater and air. asbestos fibres are durable, and the problems associated with its storage will be borne by future generations. we need to improve the system for locating and monitoring illegal asbestos deposits and the process itself for the safe disposal of asbestos-containing materials. i welcome all such initiatives to improve the health of citizens.
in writing. − the main objective is the safe disposal of asbestos-containing products and waste from the european union area. this will be achieved by: increasing the knowledge of the population about asbestos, its safe use and disposal (eliminating the social acceptance of illegal behaviour related to asbestos, unauthorised dismantling and dumping of waste, including into forests, eliminating the creation of 'wild landfills'); creating the right conditions for the implementation of the applicable legislation and good practices related to asbestos products; creating favourable conditions for the disposal of asbestos products throughout the programme period; monitoring the generation and proper management of asbestos waste; organising the collection and disposal of asbestos waste.
in writing. - the tuws' share of the european market, which is close to 30%, has been built up over several decades. at the same time, this growth, though slower, is also safer. this also serves as a reminder of the importance of legislative issues for the development of mutual institutions. we are working with the european commission, including amice, to develop specific rules to take account of the different nature of the octs and, while respecting the principle of proportionality, to allow them to maintain their distinctiveness. reinsurers influence what happens in the economy, inter alia, by acting as a counterweight to the policies of commercial listed companies. it is also particularly important, especially from the point of view of a socially responsible market, that the existing rules take into account the particular importance of sgeis. the ongoing work on this project should have a positive impact on the development and transparency of the sector.

in writing. - the situation in egypt, following the changes brought about by the arab spring, is still very difficult. although free presidential elections were held in 2012, the situation in the country remains very tense. the judiciary is under constant pressure from various political forces, the drafting of a new constitution has deepened the internal divisions in egyptian society, 42 people have been killed in clashes with the police in recent riots, and a state of emergency is in place. persecution of religious minorities, including coptic christians, who make up about 10% of the country's population, continues. the resolution adopted today also addresses this issue, calling for every effort to be made to stem the tide of christian emigration from egypt. it also calls for comprehensive reforms leading to democracy, the rule of law and social justice, which would contribute to stability not only in the country but also in the region.
in writing. - the events in tahrir square in january two years ago marked the beginning of the transformation in egypt that led to the ousting of president hosni mubarak. more than 60 years of dictatorships came to an end. the protests against mubarak have united citizens with different political views and visions of the state. the protesters demanded free elections, an end to corruption and the introduction of freedom of speech. the unity that united the protesters has long since been forgotten, replaced by conflict and political polarization. in december of that year, a new constitution was approved in a referendum with 64% voting yes, but less than a third of those eligible voted. the constitution was firmly based on sharia law. it also gives more power to the president and more power to the islamist-dominated upper house of parliament. the new constitution introduces restrictions on many human rights issues. it diminishes the rights of the christian minority and may lead to greater discrimination against women. the opposition fears that this will open the way for further islamization of the country. in the recent period, egypt's economy has declined. income from tourism and foreign investment declined. the rising unemployment rate shows the need for economic reform. the european union should encourage egypt to democratize and respect human rights. it is also important to develop civil society, which is a prerequisite for democracy. the current situation is far from the ideals that egyptians fought for two years ago when they overthrew the mubarak dictatorship.
in writing. - the developments in egypt seem to indicate that the policy that mrs ashton has adopted has reached a dead end. unfortunately, as some have pointed out, radical islamic circles stole the revolution that toppled mubarak. this is the dark scenario we see almost every day, and the entire opposition in egypt is sounding the alarm, pointing out that president morsi's actions go beyond what we are used to from egypt's previous dictator, mubarak. in this situation, a shock is necessary, changes are necessary and a radical and clear position of the european union is necessary in the face of the disturbing signals that reach us every day from egypt. shocking are the acts of aggression against the copts and the complete breakdown of the judiciary. it's not just democracy that's at stake there, but the very foundations of the rule of law, and we have to defend them.

in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the proposed amendment to the directive gives the european commission virtually an unlimited mandate to change the auction calendar, or de facto market. in accordance with the directive in force, the auction process should be predictable, in particular with regard to the timing and the course of the auction and the estimated volumes of allowances to be made available. proposals for intervention in the ets market by its regulator can in fact be taken as a clear signal of the instability of this market. the proposed amendment to the directive appears to be contrary to article 290 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, according to which the power to adopt a delegated act cannot be delegated to cover the essential elements of a field, since such matters should be regulated by a legislative act. the temporary withdrawal of allowances amends an essential element of the ets directive as it violates the accepted principle of an annual reduction of the market allowance pool by 1,74% and therefore cannot be resolved by means of a delegated act. consequently, by periodically reducing the prices of the allowances marketed, the commission could have increased their price. it therefore appears that the european commission's actions do not lead to emission reductions at the lowest cost, but only affect the price of allowances. i would like to note that the results of the public consultation clearly show that the voice coming from poland is being ignored. that is why i am strongly opposed to this type of regulation.
in writing. the commission's proposal to change the timetable for the european emissions trading system's co2 auction, which aims to increase the price of co2 allowances, is a bad project because it upsets the balance between climate policy and the economic objectives of the member states. it is incomprehensible that in a situation of economic slowdown and the restoration of the competitiveness of european industry, we want to inflate energy prices and weaken the pace of recovery. the ets was designed as a market instrument that naturally adapts to supply and demand. a decline in prices is a normal symptom of an economic slowdown. the system remains fluid, so climate targets can simply be achieved at a lower cost to the economy. administrative interference is a market-distorting tactic. the proposal is a temporary solution which prevents european businesses from planning for the long term. this action will not change the face of the system but will contribute to increasing price volatility in the energy market. the need for reform of emissions trading is justified and the design of the instrument itself needs to be reconsidered. i think green growth is possible, but we have to define balance differently. we cannot allow climate policy to be over-ambitious at the expense of the economy. the eu's co2 emissions are about 11% of the world's. without china, brazil or the us convinced of the merits of the eu's climate change approach, there is no chance of achieving significant emissions reductions.
in writing. european climate policy is designed to adapt the european economy to the reality of climate change. its tool is the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions achieved through initiatives such as the ets. emissions trading has so far been a way of curbing emissions, which has also been greatly helped by the weakening of the european economy as a result of the global crisis. however, it should be noted that the ets must not only be effective but also fair. it cannot impose the same requirements on all eu countries without taking into account the national characteristics of their economies. just as the economies of western europe have long since begun to shift towards renewable energy sources, the economies of the new member states have for decades been dictated by central planning, which has perpetuated their inefficient and unsustainable energy consumption. you can't make a simple comparison here. on the one hand, ambitious emission reduction targets should be set, but the level of ambition should remain commensurate with the level of capacity available to individual countries. we cannot subordinate economic growth and thus energy and consumer goods prices to a climate policy that is overriding, because this could lead to a decline in living standards and a deepening of the very unfavourable energy poverty. we therefore expect the european commission to prepare a proposal for the functioning of the ets that effectively balances these objectives.
in writing. the european commission has decided to take a very dangerous step, which is to interfere with previously established market rules. backloading is not only a futile tool, it's also a dangerous game that tends to discourage investors. many investments have already been put on hold due to the uncertainty created by successive commission decisions. it should be borne in mind that the adoption of the provisions in question will lead to a further increase in electricity prices and thus to a reduction in competitiveness. electricity prices in the eu for industrial customers have already increased by 45% over the last decade. europe in crisis cannot afford to do this. the more so as the carbon market is functioning well. it does not need to be regulated by successive administrative decisions, especially in times of crisis. the industry needs predictability and clear rules of conduct. in our industry, it takes about 15 years between the decision to build a plant and the decision to rebuild it. chaotic market intervention reduces predictability and holds back investment in energy-intensive industries. it is sufficient to mention the many cases of power plant expansion in poland, among others in opole or rybnik. moreover, backloading appears to be the first step towards raising the 2020 greenhouse gas emission reduction target. this could happen, as agreed by the council and parliament, if the next global climate agreement is reached.
mr. chairman, please! i am very much of the opinion that the increase in reduction targets for europe should only be made in situations where a global climate agreement is reached. the aviation solution we're discussing today is worthy of support. it is based on the idea that a global agreement on emission reductions in this sector must be reached first before an emissions tax is introduced at eu level. so we're suspending the intercontinental flight fee for one year. however, the european commission was forced to do so and to abandon its original ambitions and aspirations due to international protests and even trade wars by partners such as the united states, india and china. it's spectacular. i regret that a similar reflection has not taken place in the european union on the functioning of the climate package, which is very damaging to our economies. i also think that the problem is the competitiveness of european companies, both in terms of the climate package and the issue we are discussing right now.
