prime minister of finland. − mr president, honourable members, thank you very much for your comments. the issue of the diversity of the union reminds me of the debate within my own six-party coalition. almost all opinions are contained in one government, and i have got used to finding a compromise on the different values and different opinions and to trying to find a way forward. (interruption from the floor)yes, we only have one prime minister, and that is a difference. ladies and gentlemen, i enjoyed many of your quotes from margaret thatcher, and i would also like to quote her when she once said that pennies do not drop from the sky and we have to earn them down here on earth. that is very true, and i think we can all agree with her on this. i would like to comment on some larger entities, like a rule-based union and the rule of law. just because i am a fan of a strong rule-based union does not mean that it would represent a hardline school of thinking on europe. on the contrary, i believe the rule of law – a good, strict rule base and living according to rules – is the very essence of democracy. it is like having a soccer team and playing soccer without a common rule base; it does not make any sense. so at once the eu is a union of values and also a union of democracy. we have to underline that we have to live according to our common rules and respect the rule of law – otherwise we do not have anything; we are just a team with nice words but without a common commitment. so that is why a rule base and the rule of law are so important to my mind. many of you are worried – as we all are – about the future of the welfare society, and whether the austerity policy or consolidation of the budget will hit the welfare society too hard. our interpretation of the welfare society is that, first of all, we have to be competitive enough to earn enough money for it. and the other way round: the welfare society is a precondition for equal opportunities for all. my country is very dependent on external trade. nearly 50% of our income comes from foreign trade, which means that in order to run a very generous welfare society we must be competitive not only in europe and not only with the northern countries, but on a global scale. this is because the welfare society needs such a lot of money that we cannot afford to run it with finnish taxpayers’ money alone; we need money from outside. that is why competitiveness and all the reforms which we need to make in order to improve competitiveness every single year are essential in order to strengthen the welfare society, which gives equal opportunities to everybody. that is one of the reasons why we have cut our budget and raised taxes by approximately 3% of gdp during the last two years. we have done this in order to safeguard the welfare society. we also lowered the corporate tax rate in order to make our country more competitive on a global scale, because we have very good education in finland, we have such good surroundings for innovation and we have invested in the welfare society for decades and now we want to profit from those assets such as the welfare society, education and our innovation system. so fiscal discipline is the best friend of the welfare society. it is not a theory; it is just plain common sense. a second thing: there were a few colleagues who mentioned mutual debt. i am quite hesitant about this because i can see that we have already had a eurobond and we have seen the result. during the first decade of the existence of the euro, all the countries belonging to the euro received money at the same value, and this is part of the problem at the moment. i know that there are different opinions on this issue, but i am not that sure that a common debt would be a solution to our current problems. moreover, it would mean some kind of treaty change. we should not mix the current short-term challenges and difficulties with long-term solutions. if we wanted to create a eurobond, which would be joint and several, to me it would be like creating religion without the devil. even though we do not like the market forces right now – especially in the current situation where some countries are under heavy pressure from the market side – if we allow the market forces of the financial market to make the same mistake they made during the first decade of the existence of the euro, then it will not help us in the long run. by the way, the financial market did not differentiate between the member states, and that does not make any sense. in a market economy you have to know in which country or in which company you are investing your money, and there are several risks, or the level of risk varies from country to country or from company to company. that is why i would pay more attention to competitiveness (which is the best way to stimulate the economy) and to consolidate our budgets. this is what, for instance, ireland and portugal are, quite rightly, doing at the moment. we can already see some results. i was in portugal, where i met ordinary citizens. i got the impression that many citizens in portugal are very close to losing all hope. i understand that situation, because this time is probably the most difficult for the portuguese and irish people. the citizens have already taken the bad-tasting medicine and the fever has come down, but the disease is still there. but, as we can see from the reactions of the financial market and the export and external balance figures in portugal, we can already see some results. we just have to be patient. i am not asking the ordinary citizens to be patient, because they are suffering every single day. they are suffering. but what is the alternative? if these countries stopped consolidating their budgets, who would lend them money? i do not know of anybody. so we have to show solidarity in order to help these countries. we have to make sure that we stand by them, but the countries in trouble must also do their share in order to get good results. very briefly, i would just like to say to mr callanan that europe has been a great opportunity for finland. during its membership of the european union, we have gone from thirtieth to third position in a competitiveness study. we have to struggle every single day and every single year in order to improve or maintain our good position. it has also improved our foreign trade and strengthened our welfare state. i very much agree with what mr verhofstadt said and with his attitude about the importance of europe. i do not see any reason to even speculate about the fall of europe. it does not make our life any easier. we just have to correct the mistakes or weaknesses that we have in the currency union. we have basically already done that, and i believe that after a couple of years the euro area and europe as a whole will be stronger than ever before. there were some questions concerning federalism. i tried to talk in straight terms about the facts and issues, not raising the debate in abstract terms like federalism. when somebody asks whether i am in favour of federalism or not, i have to ask whether that is the united states type of federalism or the german type of federalism, or even the uk type of federalism. which federalism are we talking about? in this speech and in several previous speeches i have tried to assess what we need to do for europe in order to make it more competitive, stronger and more united. let us have this debate through the issues. what do we have to reform? what are we satisfied with and what are the biggest challenges ahead of us? regarding a transaction tax, i understand the logic behind it. in principle i do not have anything against it, but if we had taken it to finland, knowing that sweden will never take it and that estonia does not have it, we would have lost money and it would have harmed our own economy. i did not want to do that. regarding tax evasion, i appreciate european parliamentarians actively fighting against tax evasion because it is a cancer of the market economy. we cannot afford to see a situation in which we have lived for so long. this is one part of making europe more competitive, namely finding concrete solutions to tax evasion. i am very happy that the commission has been so active on this issue and i appreciate parliament’s activity in this. no matter what ideologies we are representing, i think we all – or at least the majority of us – are in favour of a fair and transparent market economy because it is the best way to create and generate welfare for our citizens. thank you very much for this debate.
in writing. competitiveness is a key element in ensuring the effective functioning of a market economy. the existence of competition provides benefits to consumers by keeping prices low while maintaining good quality. the combination of these two factors motivates producers to seek innovation, which contributes to the development of the whole economy. this is why the commission's efforts to maintain competitiveness in european goods and services markets are so important. the communication presented on the commission's activities in 2011 shows that the commission's activities addressed priority issues and were carried out effectively. the commission's contribution to the regulation of the financial sector was particularly important, as it is a sector on which the activities of firms in other sectors depend to a large extent. it is important that not only the symptoms but also the causes of problems are eliminated and that banks are required to make changes to their business models. the banks were encouraged to focus on their core business. the crisis and the economic slowdown have led many sectors of the economy to benefit from state aid. it is therefore an important task for the commission to monitor that the fight against the effects of the crisis does not lead to long-term distortions of competitiveness. equally important are the commission's actions to promote competitiveness in those markets where there is an imbalance of power. this is the case in the food market, where attempts are made to strengthen the bargaining power of agricultural producers. interventions are also needed in markets where there are no adequate incentives to lower prices as a result of high barriers to entry.

in writing. − the digital world is developing very rapidly and is an essential part of the lives of europeans. this fact presents new challenges. more and more activities are taking place online, which requires the continuous improvement and maintenance of cybersecurity. consumers are exposed to a variety of dangers, including financial fraud and identity theft. that is why i strongly support the work of the european network and information security agency (enisa), which aims to increase the capacity of the european union, the member states and the business sector to protect and respond to network and information security issues. enisa also offers assistance and advice to the commission and eu countries. in order to achieve even greater effectiveness of the agency's activities, cross-border cooperation between member states and the systematic involvement of third countries is also necessary.
in writing. − i support the initiative to strengthen and modernise the european network and information security agency (enisa) and to give it a new mandate for a further 5 years. the agency has been in existence since 2004 and it is time to adapt its activities and capabilities to the challenges of the rapidly evolving digital world. the extension of the agency's mandate, the clarification of its role and objectives in the regulation and the increase of the budget for operational activities seem to be reasonable recommendations for the creation of a more efficient body. while the cost of the new tasks of the agency is estimated to be an additional cost of eur 1 to 1,5 million, it is necessary for the agency to be operational and to address the network and information security aspects of today's cybercrime threats. enisa should also establish closer relations with the national authorities responsible for the protection of personal data in order to ensure an adequate level of protection for citizens throughout the community. in addition, the agency should be empowered to engage in dialogue and cooperation with third countries and international organisations in order to adopt a common approach to potential threats. i also agree with the proposal to move enisa's headquarters from heraklion to brussels, which will increase its visibility, allow for better contact with the eu institutions and - importantly - reduce its running costs.
in writing. − computing and networks have become an essential part of the daily lives of european citizens. the rapid development of communications networks and information systems inevitably raises the issue of their security, which raises increasing concerns in society. the increasing number of security breaches has caused significant financial losses, weakened user confidence and harmed the development of e-commerce. an attack on key information systems could have a serious impact on the provision of services essential to the well-being of european citizens. the rapid growth of internet connections and the expansion of networks make security requirements even more urgent. individuals, public administrations and businesses have introduced security technologies and security management procedures. however, apart from some administrative networks, there is no systematic crossborder cooperation between eu countries on this issue. the european network and information security agency (enisa) aims to enhance the capacity of the european union (eu), the member states and the business sector to protect, identify and respond to network and information security issues. in addition, enisa offers assistance and advice to the commission and eu countries. at the request of the commission, enisa shall assist the commission in technical preparatory work on the updating and development of eu legislation. furthermore, enisa facilitates and extends cooperation between the various actors in the public and private sectors in order to achieve an adequate level of security in the eu countries. that's why i'm in.

in writing. − in the context of the vote on the report on the greenhouse gas auction timetable, i supported amendment 20, which rejected the ec's proposal to expect the suspension of 900 million co2 allowances from 2013. in my view, the current emissions trading system is a well-functioning market mechanism for achieving the climate targets set. last year, greenhouse gas emissions in poland fell by a further 3.2%, and in the eu by 1.4%. the 2008 climate package is being effectively implemented by eu countries. therefore, the commission's intervention in the greenhouse gas auction schedule, the so-called backloading, aimed at artificially increasing the price of co2 emission allowances, is an unjustified proposal for me, especially in times of economic crisis. high prices for allowances can directly translate into higher electricity prices for households and industry, thus reducing their competitiveness on the global market. on the other hand, the agreement reached in the climate package makes it conditional on the modification of the targets set therein from the acceptance of binding commitments by other countries, including china, india, russia, brazil or the usa, to a similar level of reduction. if that is not the case, i see no reason to discuss changing the objectives for europe, especially since the eu is realistically and ambitiously pursuing them.
in writing. − in the vote on the report on the timetable for the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances, i was in favour of rejecting this project, although i agree with the general idea of reducing co2 emissions and moving towards a green economy. the introduction of backloading, i.e. partial postponement of the auctioning of allowances in order to raise the price of those allowances in later years, would be too drastic an intervention by the european commission in the emission allowances market. in addition, the commission proposal derogates from the treaty provisions because the member states were omitted from the consultation process, using as legal basis article 192 (1) tfeu, which is not relevant for the amendment of this directive. the proposed provisions are not exclusively environmental in nature but also have an impact on the diversification of the energy structure. the appropriate legal basis should therefore be article 192 (2) (c), which provides for unanimous consent to the special legislative procedure and after consulting the ep, so that eu countries would have the possibility of opposing any changes in the directive that threaten their economies. the proposed rules give the commission too much discretion in determining the appropriateness of such intervention and thus the possibility of artificially and arbitrarily regulating the emission allowance market on the basis of unverifiable premises. this would have a negative impact on revenues to the budgets of countries applying for the possibility to allocate free allowances under the derogation, i.e. for poland, which could lose up to around eur 1 042 million between 2017 and 2020. as a result, citizens would bear the costs of increasing energy prices and thus final goods and services.
in writing. − balance problems have arisen in the eu ets. the economic crisis, together with the implementing rules for the next accounting period, has led to an excess of allowances. according to this proposal, by the end of 2011 the surplus was 955 million and this figure will increase as the supply of allowances exceeds the demand, the carbon prices have fallen from eur 30 per tonne of co2 to around eur 7 per tonne of co2. in order to stimulate the economy, encourage investment in low-carbon technologies and decarbonise the european union from high-carbon infrastructure, the proposal proposes that the commission may adjust the auction schedule if necessary. such action would be limited to exceptional circumstances, such as the current eu ets situation. it should be stressed that the proposed solution is short-term and does not guarantee the long-term stability of the eu ets. businesses will have one more variable to consider, beyond market mechanisms, administrative decisions by the ec. moreover, the increase in ets prices will have a negative impact on costs for manufacturing industry, contributing to a decline in the eu's competitiveness on the international market. this will result in closures of workplaces, redundancies and the relocation of investments outside the union. instead of focusing on a short-term panacea, action should be taken to create long-term conditions for economic growth, including reforms of the eu ets after 2020.
in writing. − the european greenhouse gas emissions trading scheme (ets) is a highly exciting issue. no one denies the need to fight global warming. on the other hand, it is also clear that different countries have different carbon emissions from their energy systems. these differences are not usually the result of a conscious political decision but are the result of historical circumstances. poland's energy sector is still largely based on hard and brown coal. as a result, poland is one of the countries whose competitiveness is most likely to be weakened by the ets. the european commission's proposals to freeze part of the greenhouse gas emission allowances have therefore caused considerable excitement in poland. the authors of this proposal made it clear that they intended to increase the price of emission allowances. this would directly affect the competitiveness of the polish economy. the need for electricity producers to purchase additional allowances at a higher price would also have an impact on the budgets of polish households, as this cost would inevitably be reflected in the amount of electricity bills. there are also arguments that the freezing of part of the allowances could undermine confidence in the whole system. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report on the timetable for the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances and, within that framework, against the commission's proposal.
in writing. - this is good news for poland. we have defended our position and convinced the majority of the european parliament to adopt a sensible climate policy. the european union is on the path to reducing co2 emissions and there is no need to artificially interfere with the emissions market, as we have proved today in the vote.
in writing. - at today's plenary session in strasbourg, the european parliament rejected by 334 votes to 315 the european commission's proposal on 'backloading'. the european parliament's decision on directive 2003/87/ec on the emissions trading system means that it does not agree to unacceptable interference with the originally adopted market pricing mechanism for co2 emission allowances. meps' rejection of the commission's initiative may also have been influenced by europe's 'isolation' in its efforts to reach a global climate agreement. the absence of such an agreement means that the adoption of further, very costly climate initiatives is not delivering the expected global impact and is undermining the already reduced competitiveness of european economies. today we have given a clear signal of opposition to the continuation of the costly and irrational so-called green policy.
mr. chairman, please! unilaterally imposed environmental taxes are proving to be a major obstacle to the operations of air carriers, increasing the cost of connections. they therefore reduce the global competitiveness of european airlines. attempts to apply these solutions to non-community carriers have failed. the us authorities will certainly take all possible measures to prevent any damage to domestic enterprises. they already banned the eu ets in december. the imposition of obligations on chinese carriers threatens to withdraw orders for airbus aircraft from beijing. the community's approach has also been particularly strongly criticised in canada and india. it is therefore necessary to speed up the talks within the international civil aviation organisation. i am in favour of the implementation of the so-called stop-clock proposal for aviation emissions trading, without any additional restrictions, as some members of the environment committee have advocated. unjustified fighting with economically strong partners in europe simply doesn't pay off.
in writing. − i support and support the positive trend from the last meeting of the council of the international civil aviation organisation (icao) as it offers a chance to reach a final agreement in september on the enforcement of the obligations of aircraft operators for flights to and from the eu under the emissions trading system (ets). however, a decision to suspend the system is not, in my view, a good solution to ensure that 'global' decisions are taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from aviation. although the emissions of these gases under the kyoto protocol have increased by around 100% since 1990, the reference year, the aviation industry is only obliged to reduce emissions by 5% by 2020, while other industries must reduce emissions by 21%. it is incomprehensible to introduce exceptions only for this business sector, and moreover to apply different criteria for individual market 'players'. the exemption should cover all flights within the eu and to and from the eu, due to the need for non-discriminatory treatment of european carriers. the international agreement on aviation emission reductions should aim to create a system ensuring a level playing field for all aviation operators. the european commission's action on the temporary suspension of the eu-ets, on the other hand, introduces exceptions and privileges at the very beginning of this path. as the commission proposal does not treat all air operators involved equally, i did not support the proposal in the final vote, but only abstained.
in writing. − under the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc) and the kyoto protocol, the parties, including the then 15 ec member states, committed themselves to reducing greenhouse gas emissions into the air. the reduction target for the ec was set at the level of emission reductions for all then ec member states and was 8%. member states chose to use the option provided for in article 4 (1) of the kyoto protocol, which allowed states parties to conclude an agreement on the joint fulfilment of reduction commitments. the european union has set up a system of trading co2 emission allowances to meet its reduction target. the legal framework of the scheme was established by directive 2003/87/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 13 october 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the community and amending council directive 96/61/ec. the trading system was intended to enable the eu and its member states to meet their greenhouse gas emission reduction commitments by trading greenhouse gas emission allowances within the union in a cost-effective and economically efficient manner. directive 2003/87/ec was transposed into polish law by the act of 22 december 2004 on greenhouse gas and other substances emissions trading.
in writing. - we've all felt the rise in airfare recently. one of the reasons was the imposition of an additional charge on the airlines. for some time now, they have had to pay a carbon tax on their flights. will drivers in the european union soon be charged similar fees for driving? where does the european commission's ingenuity in imposing further charges end? the document to be voted on today concerns the kyoto protocol. it is an important agreement and it is a pity that it is only respected and implemented by the eu countries. unfortunately, its provisions are a serious blow to europe's competitiveness as a community. in times of crisis, can we afford to pay higher energy prices, higher air fares and higher living costs? no, i'm not going. that's why i voted against it. i think it's time to think about the future direction of the climate commission.

in writing. − additional equity buffers are intended to strengthen the resilience of the banking system to losses and to adapt lending to business cycles. the introduction of minimum levels of penalties is intended to ensure compliance. the importance of external credit ratings will be reduced. the parties concerned by this directive are credit institutions, investment firms and supervisory authorities. the benefit of such action is the creation of a capital buffer that will strengthen the institution's ability to cope with losses without recourse to state aid. the countercyclical capital buffer is questionable in many respects. the introduction of minimum penalty rates does not guarantee that supervision will be adequate to do so, the eba should be given more powers. replacing external ratings with internal ratings will not necessarily lead to a better risk assessment, and the implementation of basel iii only in the european union will not strengthen the stability of the financial system and will have a negative impact on the attractiveness of europe as an investment location.
in writing. − a higher quality of ground handling at european airports is not only important from a transport perspective but also from a single market perspective. consumers, passengers travelling in the single market, have often encountered problems such as lost luggage or flight delays caused by the quality of ground handling. the number of passengers is increasing year by year, which is also a consequence of the increasing and so important mobility for the single market. i voted for the report because we need such minimum standards which will greatly improve the quality of ground handling, because these standards will have to be respected by companies dealing with passenger and aircraft handling. the companies in question are responsible for transporting passengers from the terminal to the aircraft, unloading and loading luggage or unloading aircraft. the provisions concerning the maximum waiting time for baggage, the minimum number of persons to receive baggage and the appropriate amount of defrosting liquid in airport tanks are particularly important for passengers from a practical point of view. another important aspect is the legislation aimed at opening up the ground handling market, which will require the number of ground handling companies to increase from two to three at airports with more than 15 million passengers a year.
in writing. − the last decade has seen an unprecedented increase in the number of people travelling by air. europe was, in a sense, united only when the average person could afford to fly across the continent. this has not only helped to strengthen the single market based on the free movement of people, but has also allowed union citizens to get to know each other. it is not conceivable that this was made possible to a large extent by the previous directive liberalising the market for groundhandling services at airports. since its entry into force, the cost of passenger services has fallen dramatically, which has affected air ticket prices. it can therefore be hoped that the adoption of the proposed regulation will improve efficiency and the overall quality of service at airports. there are voices that this may contribute to worsening working conditions for those employed in this sector. i think the opposite is true, and the added value will be to focus more on passengers and to improve the standard of their service. therefore, together with the liberalisation of access to this market, minimum requirements should be introduced to improve the quality of service and the functioning of airports. however, it is important that those conditions not only respect the safety rules and arrangements and the airport safety management systems, but also maintain relative stability in this market area. i therefore voted in favour of the rules' rapporteur's report.
in writing. − many eu citizens have experienced problems on a number of occasions when travelling by air delayed flights, lost luggage, check-in queues are just some of the difficulties that travellers have to face. that is why, in the european parliament, where we represent the interests of our constituents, we are working on rules that will help to remove the biggest constraints and simplify procedures so that europeans can reach their destinations freely and safely. the report on ground handling at european airports aims to introduce minimum quality standards for passenger handling companies, increase the number of companies allowed to handle passengers, thereby increasing competition and reducing prices, and harmonise certification rules, so that a company that has been approved to handle passengers in one country can provide services at airports across the eu. this initiative will certainly contribute to raising standards of passenger service and make it easier for all of us to use european airports.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by the member of the rules committee on groundhandling services at european airports because i want to support the proposal put forward to further liberalise the market, inter alia by increasing the number of companies providing groundhandling services at airports above 15 million passengers in order to ensure healthy competition and lower prices for services. i also think that the provisions in the report which provide for the so-called minimum standards which passenger and aircraft operators will be required to respect are important. the document also guarantees, among other things, a maximum waiting time for luggage or a minimum number of persons accepting suitcases. this will probably help to improve the handling conditions at european airports considerably.
in writing. − the regulation on groundhandling services at airports is a major step towards improving minimum standards and increasing the competitiveness of european airports on a global scale. the new rules will contribute to improving the quality of services and working conditions of staff. the new rules include a maximum waiting time for luggage and a minimum number of people to accept suitcases, which will greatly improve travel comfort. the document also regulates the number of companies dealing with passenger and aircraft handling. the number of such airports will increase from two to three at airports handling more than 15 million passengers per year. it is worth noting that an increase in the number of service providers will not only improve quality but also lower prices for the services they provide. the regulation forms part of the so-called 'airport package', which, in addition to the ground handling aspect, also regulates the allocation of take-off and landing times, the permissible noise level of take-off and landing aircraft and the standardisation of approval procedures for companies providing services at airports. this procedure allows, for example, a polish ground handling company to provide services at any other eu airport. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on groundhandling services at union airports and repealing council directive 96/67/ec (com(2011)0824 – c7-0457/2011 – 2011/0397(cod)). this piece of legislation was crafted for the citizens in that it sets the standards for customer service at a high level while at the same time increasing safety and efficiency. far too often the airports are unprepared and unknowing of the situations that may arise, thus the new groundhandling liberalises the airports to be better prepared for any or all situations and provides the needed services for the customer. the further liberalisation of groundhandling will further induce competition, which will in turn improve the quality standards. we all can agree that competition plays a vital role in a market economy such as ours and these types of legislation allow for growth and improvements across the board.

the next item is the preliminary report by mrs danuta maria hübner, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy, on the proposal for a council regulation establishing an instrument for financial assistance to member states whose currency is not the euro (com (2012) 0336 - c7-0129/2013 -
rapporteur. − mr president, the focus of crisis-driven reforms has been mainly on the euro area and rightly so, due to the need to rethink the original architecture of the single currency. however, as we move forward with reforms, we must not forget to keep the eu united and to preserve the integrity of the single market. with these thoughts at heart, the revision of the balance of payments (bop) facility stresses the need to also take non-euro member states on board when it comes to the provision of financial assistance for macroeconomic difficulties. in an attempt to contribute to the catching-up process, the revision of the bop will allow non-euro member states to also have access to the precautionary and enhanced conditions credit lines. these instruments will ensure that risks are addressed early along the road and potential difficulties tackled before they become fully-fledged threats to financial stability which, as the experience of the crisis has shown, can produce contagion effects. the bop revision does not merely grant further financial assistance rights to non-euro members, it also puts forward corresponding obligations through a toughening of surveillance measures during and after the granting of financial assistance. the bop revision spells out the guidelines which debt-sustainability analysis and the macroeconomic adjustment programme should follow, stresses the importance of realistic forecasts and enhances the transparency of this process by promoting an interinstitutional dialogue on financial assistance. the afore-mentioned requirements which non-euro members will be subject to are modelled on the two-pack, the legislative duo dealing with budgetary matters and financial assistance in the case of the euro area, and they thus constitute an eu harmonisation effort with the single market at heart. the need to have an enhanced bop is justified, especially in the context of the ongoing debates on a european banking union. if the banking union is to succeed, its members will need to be treated in a fair and equal manner. this is why non-euro member states, which will opt in to the single supervision mechanism, will need to be provided with an appropriate set of rights and duties. a key issue in this context is offering non-euro members a fiscal backstop, since supervisory decisions taken by the ssm may have harsh fiscal implications and elicit a need for bank recapitalisation. european leaders announced that once the ssm is up and running, the esm would be able to directly recapitalise banks. my proposal in the context of the revised bop proposal is to put forward an indirect bank recapitalisation instrument for non-euro member states participating in the upcoming ssm. under this label the governments of these non-euro member states would be able to take out loans for the purpose of recapitalising the financial institution. as the european financial stabilisation mechanism (the efsm), which replicates the bop for the eu 27, will soon be discontinued, its unused lending capacity worth eur 10 billion could be transferred to the bop. in the long run, should the revision of the esm treaty be discussed, we could then consider the option of allowing non-euro members participating in the ssm to contribute to the bank recapitalisation instrument of the mechanism, with a view to potentially also benefiting from it. to conclude, the revision of the bop sends out an important message which goes beyond the issue of financial assistance, namely that a greater harmonisation of reforms across the union is ultimately beneficial to euro and non-euro member states alike and, above all, is in the interests of the single market.
rapporteur. − mr president, i shall be very brief. i would like to react to the comments made by my epp colleague mr ferber on his worries about bank recapitalisation and access of non-euro member states of the european union to a bank recapitalisation fund. i would like to say that this parliament endorsed not so long ago the ‘opt-in’ mechanism for non-euro member states to the single supervisory mechanism. we all know that, within the single supervisory mechanism, there might be situations in which the supervisor will impose recommendations or requirements on national financial sectors that might lead to the recapitalisation of the banks. i therefore think that our responsibility should go beyond the ssm, and we should see how we can help those member states to have access to recapitalisation funding based on loans. secondly, when we talk about the transfer from the efsm (which will soon be discontinued, when the esm enters into force), this is not the transfer of remaining funds but of lending capacity. therefore, i think that there is also a difference in this context. finally, i would like to thank everybody with whom i had the pleasure of discussing this report over the last two or three months: all the rapporteurs and all those who participated in this extremely edifying debate today.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday, 17 april 2013. written statements (rule 149)
the next item is the debate on the oral question to the commission on regional state aid by danuta maria hübner, on behalf of the committee on regional development (o-000017/2013 – b-70115/2013).
author. − i would like to start by reminding you that, in its resolution of 17 january of this year on state aid modernisation, the european parliament asked to be associated with the preparation of the proposals for state aid modernisation. i will be brief, because the oral question is well known to the commission and to commissioner almunia in particular, and i will focus on what we are worrying about here in the european parliament and especially in the committees involved. as we are now negotiating the regulatory framework for 2014-20 on regional policy, we see that some of the provisions of those regulations lose their rationale when regional aid guidelines (rags) come in, and we need maximum consistency between the regional policy – its investment in growth, jobs and competitiveness – and the state aid rules. we are worrying about these new rules – wondering whether this is really the best moment politically, economically and socially for actions leading to lower population coverage, reduced state aid and state aid intensity. we worry about the restrictive impact of the new rules on investment and growth in regions which graduate from the less-developed category and move to the more-developed one. we also expect the commission to take into account the situation in economies which are particularly strongly hit by the crisis. for them, public funding provided by regional policy might be the only source of investment, and these are member states where the worsening of the economic situation is not reflected by the data for the period 2008-2010 which will be used by the commission as the basis for eligibility. in this context a mid-term review clause would allow the new situation to be taken into account. that being so, my original question is: why has the commission not proposed a fixed date for the mid-term review (as is the case today) but instead has left this option open? we are worried about the commission’s rag approach to the internal diversity of regions, where growth is mostly driven by metropolitan areas with many nuts 3 areas lagging behind. we believe that well-balanced transitional arrangements are needed. in the current legal and political context in which the committee on regional development is involved in this ordinary legislative procedure on the cohesion policy legislative framework, it is important that the commission continues its dialogue with us in order to clarify all the relevant points and also to reduce the risk of undesirable effects of the guidelines. while hoping for this further collaboration, i would also like to emphasise the importance of close cooperation between all commissioners, especially commissioner johannes hahn and commissioner joaquín almunia, because we believe this cooperation might make the rules an undertaking that would allow us to make better use of all the potential of the regional policy in the context of the post-crisis situation and europe’s dramatic hunger for growth and job creation and with a view to a more competitive european economy.
mr. chairman, please! the main challenge in the current debate is the complementarity of european policies and therefore the coherence of action between the different forms of support for the different actors. i would like to make it clear that when we as parliament negotiate regulations in cohesion policy, it is not very important for us whether we are negotiating with a specific directorate, for us these negotiations are being conducted with the european commission. if we are negotiating with the european commission, it means that we assume that there is internal consistency in the approach to regional aid between the different directorates, between the different commissioners. we are in the process of finalising the negotiations on the european regional development fund. one of the most difficult points is support for large enterprises. after many very difficult discussions with the council, we have come to the conclusion that support should be allowed, particularly where innovation is concerned and where cooperation between large and small enterprises is concerned. the point is to ensure consistency in the approach here, because if we agree that it is possible in one place and it will be limited in another, there will be a discrepancy. i think if the commissioner were at our committee meeting, we could clear this up. this is really urgent.
i'm closing the debate.

in writing. − voting to grant parliament discharge in the financial year 2011 shows that eu funds were correctly controlled and managed by our institution. while 2011 was a challenging year, amid the financial crisis, parliament was able to implement its budget in accordance with the principles of good financial running. thanks to a number of smart reforms, parliament managed to save almost eur 40 million in 2011, a sum subsequently incorporated into the 2012 ep budget. yet, real and serious savings can be achieved elsewhere. based on the estimates of the ep bureau in 2002, over eur 200 million, equal to 20 % of the ep’s budget, could be saved annually by having one working place for the ep. while parliament is still bound by the eu treaty to work from three places, i am encouraged that the adopted text asks member states to revise parliament’s working places in the next revision of the treaty by amending protocol 6. i also welcome the repeated request for a road map on the multiple seats of parliament, to be presented by june 2013. now more than ever we must find ways to improve the efficiency of our work, demonstrating to eu citizens our commitment and financial responsibility.
2011 was the first year of operation of the european external action service and therefore the absence of flagrant errors in the implementation of the budget of this institution is certainly noteworthy. only the fact of the documentation of incorrect payments to some employees and the complicated legal situation of temporary workers can cause concern. irregularities revealed in the procurement and tendering procedures require immediate clarification. the most significant problem, however, is the continued geographical imbalance in recruitment and appointment. the share of workers from the new member states is dramatically lower than in the old 15. i cannot agree with such a ruthless discrimination against the representatives of poland and other countries which have joined the community in the past decade and which have excellent, extensive organisational and scientific facilities. i expect urgent action to be taken to improve this situation. i therefore think that the question of discharge for european diplomacy should be postponed.
in writing. - the european external action service is poorly organised and therefore very expensive. when it was established in 2010, i submitted amendments to introduce national quotas for the filling of posts in the eeas. this would allow for better use of the potential of the workforce and reduce personnel costs. all the opinion-makers in the report underlined the shortcomings of poor human resources management and the lack of national quotas. it's time to change that.
i would like to refer to the report on parliament's preliminary draft revenue and expenditure for 2014. it is worth recalling that in 2014 the european union plans total expenditure at eur 130 billion, including eur 1.7 billion for the european parliament. this will be a budget lower than in previous years. in times of crisis, you have to look for savings everywhere. we should also look for them in parliament. in our case, this should be a real dimension, showing also to all the other eu institutions that the savings should be applied to absolutely everyone without exception. i think we can find such savings in parliament's budget by saving on the rental of buildings, saving on travel, and also by striving to reduce the number of parliament staff. i am in favour of parliament's budget being smaller than it has been up to now.
in writing. − this year’s report on estimated revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2014 is particularly important. next year is the first financial year of the eu’s mff 2014-2020. moreover, 2014 will see the next european parliamentary elections. the adopted resolution confirms a net increase of 3.29% in parliament’s budget for 2014. this rate is lower than the initially-proposed 3.58% increase, and it is linked to expected expenditures of the 2014 european elections. being the only directly-elected institution in the eu, the ep must ensure that taxpayers’ money is spent in a responsible way. therefore we must continue identifying areas where savings can be made in order to make our institution more efficient and resourceful. one such area is the ep’s multiple seats. significant savings estimated at eur 200 million a year could be achieved if the parliament were to work in one place. in this context i am pleased that the adopted resolution includes a reference to the seat arrangements by urging the budgetary authorities to include the issue in the ongoing negotiations on the mff 2014-2020. in times of difficult economic conditions we must show our financial responsibility by delivering results in areas that are important to our citizens.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the preliminary report by mrs danuta hübner on the proposal for a council regulation establishing a financial assistance instrument for member states whose currency is not the euro. this document modifies to a large extent the provisions of the previous legislative act of february 2002. the need to update it was linked to the need to keep pace with developments in the euro area, where a number of measures were taken to prevent possible future debt crises. i am pleased that both euro-area and non-euro-area eu member states facing balance of payments difficulties will be able to benefit from similar financial assistance instruments, including loans and credit lines. the hübner report also considered the development of an instrument comparable to the european stability mechanism (esm) that would allow banks to be recapitalised for non-euro area countries participating in the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). i would like to thank the honourable member for her work and congratulate her on the outcome of today's vote.
in writing. - contrary to the recent statements of the uk prime minister david cameron, the euro is the currency of the european union. this is clearly stated in the treaties and will not change with the increasingly eurosceptic policies of london. therefore, when adopting further measures to stabilise the situation in the euro area, it is necessary to take account of those member states outside the euro area which will sooner or later adopt the single currency. this awareness was apparently lacking in the commission when it prepared the regulation in question. the lack of a recapitalisation facility for banks in non-euro area member states in the financial assistance toolbox is a major mistake. if we are to create a banking union open to all countries, we must also create mechanisms to take account of different scenarios. the commission apparently only foresaw the collapse of the banks in these countries, without the possibility of rescuing them by recapitalisation. the rapporteur rightly points out that in order to prevent problems, rather than simply to solve them on an ongoing basis, the tools for recapitalising banks in difficulty are needed. this is a much simpler mechanism than the process of restructuring and orderly liquidation. the rapporteur has proposed specific solutions to this problem which could form the basis for the development of specific mechanisms. however, this requires the goodwill of the commission, which was apparently lacking in the absence of appropriate consultation. that is why i voted in favour of mr hübner's report.
in writing. − 2011 was a challenging year, with the increase in inflation compared to 2010 mainly due to rising fuel and energy prices and, to a lesser extent, food and other commodity prices. moreover, the decline in the level of loans to enterprises and households has further constrained the economic growth of these entities. the main objectives of the european central bank are, first and foremost, to maintain price stability and to support economic policy. i would like to point out the difficulties faced by the european central bank in 2011, which were the result of the ongoing economic crisis. maintaining the flow of credit to smes has been and remains a particularly important issue, and while there is a possibility of exceptional support to the financial system by the european central bank, further such action will prove ineffective without obliging institutions that benefit from such support to increase their level of lending to such entities. to sum up, i would like to stress that the above problems, which arose in 2011, can only be reduced if a comprehensive and far-reaching solution to the euro area crisis is implemented, based on an approach combining solidarity and responsibility. according to eurostat statistics, unemployment in the euro area reached a historic high of 12% in february this year. policies to stimulate growth and create jobs must therefore be a priority for the union to be taken into account in the future work of the european central bank.
in writing. − the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance is an important instrument for citizens, as it establishes a mechanism under which it is possible to enforce obligations, in particular maintenance obligations, relating to children. the report by mr lopez isturiz, which was voted on today, is a formal endorsement of this convention, which is a condition for its application in the european union. although this is a procedural step, it is a necessary element for the smooth functioning of the convention system, as the changes introduced by today's report will allow the entry into force of this document in the union as soon as possible. it is not necessary to recall here that the provisions of the hague convention will certainly contribute to the quicker recovery of maintenance payments, which are currently extremely difficult to enforce in cross-border cases.

in writing. the european citizens' initiative, launched a year ago, which allows citizens of the european union to submit legislative proposals, is undoubtedly playing an important role in shaping democracy at community level. last year, the european commission received 25 such proposals, of which 14 initiatives are currently registered. this is a testament to the success of the instrument and to the willingness of citizens to participate in the decision-making process of the eu institutions. the european citizens' initiative is a response to the crisis of democracy and plays an important role in times of economic uncertainty. it is guided by two fundamental principles: indirectness and representativeness. its main and most important task is to bring citizens closer to the eu. the initiative gives them a direct say in shaping european policy. it is an instrument through which citizens of the member states can influence eu law and submit their proposals for new legislation. the initiative has the added advantage of a wide range of areas to which it relates, i.e. those in which the european commission has the power to submit a legislative proposal. in addition to petitions and the opportunity to vote in elections, it is an additional form of expression of citizens' expectations. i hope that the citizens of the union will use this instrument more and more.
in writing. the european year of citizens is undoubtedly the best opportunity to remind ourselves who we really serve. the european union is often accused of not having direct contact with its citizens, as my constituents remind me, and of having little or no influence on what brussels does. the european citizens' initiative was supposed to fix that. i am far from saying that the first year of operation is a complete failure, because it is not. we're seeing a lot of interest in this instrument, and that's very gratifying to me personally. but we must be careful not to disappoint those who have been awakened to hope. the impact of the eio is limited. additional obstacles of a purely technical nature are therefore simply unacceptable, as is the lack of political will on the part of some countries to commit themselves more to the success of this instrument. we therefore call on the commission and the council to resolve the problems immediately.

in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to clarify the issue of harmonisation of population data in the member states. the amendments include the establishment of a common framework for the systematic production of european statistics in the field of demography, which governs the collection, processing and transmission of population statistics by the member states. the proposal therefore introduces new rules and new definitions to create a unified pan-european statistics in the field of demography. this will allow comparison of demographic data from local, regional and national databases, to assess data across europe and to promote the exchange of good practice between eu members. this harmonisation proposal is a good idea for the european union, as it will improve the quality of information received by the european commission. because of the different methodologies used in the collection of this type of data in the different member states, the ec has received information that has sometimes been difficult to compare. this proposal will solve that problem.
in writing. - demography is a major challenge for the eu in times of crisis. this is particularly evident in the commission communication 'europe's demographic future: turning challenges into opportunities'. although the message is several years old, it is still relevant today. experts predict that the working-age population will begin to decline in the coming decade as a large number of baby boomers retire. they stress that the increase in the number of older people is primarily the result of major economic, social and medical advances, which enable europeans to live longer in conditions of comfort and safety unprecedented in the past. the ageing of the eu population must be seen in the context of the global increase in the world's population. after increasing from 2 billion in 1950 to 6.5 billion today, the un forecasts a further, albeit slower, growth trend, with the world population reaching 9.1 billion by 2050. about 95% of the overall population increase will occur in developing countries, bypassing europe. as a consequence, the share of the eu-25 in the world population will decline. that is why i welcome the changes proposed and supported them in today's vote.
in writing. − the ship recycling regulation is designed to ensure that european ships are recycled in facilities that are safe for workers and environmentally friendly, and that have the necessary means to neutralise hazardous materials contained in decommissioned ships. the amendments proposed by the committee, however, introduce measures which are too stringent to achieve the objective of the regulation. the amendments proposed include the creation of a european ship recycling fund, which would be financed by fees charged to ships using eu ports, regardless of their flag. i think that this proposal is damaging to the competitiveness of european ports. the need to pay additional port charges will limit their development prospects, as it puts ports in the eu's neighbouring countries in a better position. these proposals carry the risk of changing existing trade routes and the high probability of increased red tape. it should also be added that these additional charges will reduce the competitiveness of maritime transport compared to rail and road transport, which are much less environmentally friendly. for the reasons mentioned above, i voted against the amendments of the parliamentary committee and supported amendment no 120 which calls for a postponement of the decision on the recycling fund until 2015 and calls on the european commission to prepare an appropriate impact assessment of the regulation.

in writing. the european parliament's proposed resolution opens a discussion on the future policy framework for the development of renewable energy after 2020 and further promoting the integration of renewable energy in the eu's internal energy market. currently, with the increasing share of wind and solar energy, which are highly volatile energy sources, renewable energy sources (res) only supplement the eu's energy balance and at the current level of development of these technologies, it is necessary to maintain reserve capacity based on conventional energy. i believe that in the process of making renewable energy competitive, a strong emphasis should be placed on reducing its costs, rather than artificially raising the price of conventional energy through energy taxes or modification of the ets. such actions by the european commission may lead to a deterioration in energy security in countries currently relying on fossil fuels. the european commission should take into account the diverse potential of member states in the field of res and the development of energy infrastructure. it is therefore necessary to prepare appropriate analyses of both the potential of res in individual countries and the impact of an increase in the share of res in the energy mix on their economies. the 2030 renewable energy targets res share of 40-45% should be set after global agreement, while res support schemes should remain the responsibility of member states.
in writing. the european union is faced with the choice of an energy model that responds to the needs of a european economy operating in a globalised world. renewable energy should be an integral part of this model, and we need to systematically increase its share to meet the real challenges of climate change. however, a policy to promote renewable energy sources cannot be driven solely by a climate perspective, but must take into account a number of other dimensions. first, investments in renewable energy must be subordinated to global investments in european competitiveness. following the example of the us, the union should boldly pursue a deep transformation of its economy towards renewable or low-carbon sources based on the highest innovative technologies. secondly, it is necessary to ensure that the use of renewable energy does not contribute to the increase in energy prices and thus to the deepening of the energy poverty of the population. third, union policy should aim to strike a balance between all types of support to both small and large renewable energy producers, while appealing to the principles of global competitiveness, energy efficiency, promotion of local initiatives and equal opportunities. only through such a comprehensive approach can the eu's energy policy have a chance to deliver added value.
