in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation because it effectively underlined the inconsistencies between the law of the union and the present bilateral air service agreements, and it explained the benefits that will result. i believe that this is a right step towards the elimination of the errors that are associated with the eu laws. also, i trust that this will make air transportation more efficient within the eu. the eu carriers will be able to benefit from their right of establishment and will not encounter the problems that were created by the old delegatory clause.
in writing. − traditionally, international aviation relations between member states and third countries have been governed by bilateral air service agreements. they include a 'designation clause' which allows third countries to refuse, withdraw or suspend the authorisation or the authorisation granted to an air carrier. the 2002 ecj ruling found that the clause in article 49 tfeu was incompatible. the solution is horizontal agreements to replace the designation clause, so that eu aircraft can benefit from the right of registration and have access to connections between the eu and third countries on a non-discriminatory basis. in accordance with rule 81 of its rules of procedure, parliament shall give its consent to the conclusion of international agreements by means of a single vote. no amendments are reported. the rapporteur recommends that the committee on transport and tourism approve the conclusion of the contract.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? the european aviation safety agency is the key institution for the efficient management of air traffic in europe. it therefore acts as a sort of network manager for the air connections on the continent. in the context of an increasingly dynamic aviation market, appropriate oversight and regulation is desirable and in the interest of citizens. the implementation of the single airspace area should make air transport considerably easier, especially in the community countries. i therefore welcome the efforts to strengthen cooperation between the union and eurocontrol, which will ensure that this objective is achieved. this agreement shall specify the principles and mechanisms of such cooperation, while strengthening eurocontrol's role in the union's system of enforcement agendas, and focusing on safety and environmental issues.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's consent to the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation (eurocontrol) establishing a general framework for enhanced cooperation. eurocontrol is the eu's technical and operational body for the development and implementation of the single european sky and plays a key role in air traffic management in europe. i hope that the conclusion of the enhanced cooperation agreement will contribute to the development of a single european airspace and will also allow for more effective and coherent cooperation with the european aviation safety agency (easa), which will in turn contribute to the improvement of air traffic management in europe.
in writing. − the enhanced cooperation between the eu and eurocontrol will effectively contribute to the implementation of the single european sky. this recommendation will decrease the separation and strengthen the communication between the two entities. i believe that this change will make air-traffic management within the eu more effective. moreover, this recommendation effectively shows the terms and conditions of the cooperation between the two entities. this ensures the concreteness of this new collaboration. thus, i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation since i welcome the further implementation of the single european sky. giving consent to the conclusion of the agreement will make sure that all airspace users can use safe and efficient airspace. furthermore it will improve the air-traffic management system not only in poland, but also in the eu and beyond.
in writing. − the council voted in favour of the signing of the agreement establishing a general framework for closer cooperation between the european union and the european aviation safety organisation. the agreement confirms the regulatory role of the european union, while eurocontrol is to be responsible for the operational and technical tasks related to the implementation of the single european sky (ses). the european union points out that the best solution would be to introduce a global aviation emissions trading system based on the principle of non-discrimination. the commission has called on eu member states to work together to tackle issues such as the charging of trans-siberian air fares. the commission has entrusted eurocontrol with the function of verifying the effectiveness of the functioning of the single european sky (in 2010) and with the function of network manager in the implementation of network functions in the framework of air traffic management (in 2011). it was proposed to set up a joint committee responsible for the management and operation of the contract. the joint committee would be empowered to adopt and amend annexes falling within the scope of the agreement.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the report by mr kohlíčka. since the 1990s, we have seen a marked increase in air traffic over europe. over the past two decades, it has doubled there are some 26 000 passenger flights over the community every day. experts estimate that by 2030, that number will double again. unfortunately, the development of modern air traffic management systems does not directly translate into its efficiency. the reason is clear: fragmentation of airspace over the european union. the commission has also received comments from interested parties. the single european sky project tripling airspace capacity, improving safety by a factor of ten, reducing the environmental impact of aviation by 10% and reducing air traffic management costs by 50%. i believe that the agreement adopted today will strengthen cooperation between the eu and eurocontrol to enable eurocontrol to support the eu in implementing the long-delayed single european sky project.
in writing. − i support the proposal for a regulation on the deposit of historical archival material of the eu institutions at the european university institute in florence (eui). the proposal aims to give the european parliament its consent to the council of the eu amending the existing regulation. the main changes include clarifying the legal and financial rules for cooperation between the eu and the eui, increasing the role of the eui in managing the archival material of the eu institutions, protecting personal data contained in archives, and making archives available in electronic form where possible. these materials are a very important source of information on the european integration process, and it is therefore very important to ensure their adequate archiving, to guarantee their universal access and to support scientific research on the european integration process.
in writing. − the historical archives of the eu institutions are an important source of information on the history and heritage of the european union. the commission is identifying measures that will ensure universal access to archives and protection of information on the eu institutions, and support research into the history of european integration. the commission mentions, inter alia, the institution's obligation to deposit historical archival material with the eiu, and points to the right of the depositing institution to obtain information on the management of its archival material and to carry out inspections. the commission shall, on behalf of the depositing institutions, undertake to conclude a framework partnership agreement with the eiu to establish detailed rules governing the respective competences and tasks of the union institutions and the eiu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr carlo casini on the timing of the next elections to the european parliament. this document expressed support for the draft decision of the eu council on the change of the date for the election of members of the european parliament. the original proposed date for the elections coincides with the so-called long weekend in many eu countries, which could have a negative impact on voter turnout. in view of this, i consider it appropriate to postpone the elections to 22-25 may 2014. i believe that this will be beneficial and will contribute to the active participation of eu citizens in the elections to the european parliament.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i fully support the decision to move the elections to the period from 22 to 25 may 2014. the whitsun bank holiday weekend that is celebrated by many of the member states clearly interferes with the election dates that would have ordinarily been held. the holiday pertains to many people and, in my opinion, takes away a big number of potential voters. i believe that this will enhance voter turnout for the 2014 elections.
in writing. - the change of the date of the european parliament elections provides an opportunity to increase voter turnout. parliament itself has been pushing for this change for years.
in writing. − the council requested an opinion on the draft decision amending the date of the elections. this would cover the period from thursday 5 june to sunday 8 june 2014, by analogy with the date on which the first direct elections were held (from thursday 9 june to sunday 12 june 1979). as the election deadline that would apply in most member states would correspond to the long green christmas weekend, the council considered that it would be better to expedite the elections and proposed to set them for 22-25 may (thursday sunday) 2014. in order to give member states sufficient time to take the necessary measures to organise those elections, a decision on the new date should be taken as soon as possible. this justifies the application of the simplified procedure provided for in rule 46 (1). the draft council decision is rejected.
in writing. - the application of gabriele albertini of 25 april 2006 for immunity in connection with the criminal proceedings against him before the milan court was rejected. since he took up his seat as a senator in the italian senate on 15 march 2013, article 9 of the protocol no longer applies to him, since the position of senator in the italian senate cannot be combined with the function of member of the european parliament in accordance with article 7 (2) of the 1976 act on direct elections.
in writing. − at the meeting of 6 february 2013, the chairman submitted a request for the waiver of the immunity of mr spyros danellis. he was charged with inciting a third party to commit an offence and with knowingly making false statements about that third party which could damage that third party's reputation and good name. the alleged false statements and the charges relate to the activities of mr danellis in his previous capacity as mayor of chersonisos and have no connection with his mandate as member of the european parliament. mr danellis has had the opportunity to comment on this matter and there is no reason to suspect that this is a case of fumus persecutionis. on the basis of the above circumstances and after examining the arguments for and against the waiver of the member's immunity, the rapporteur has decided to waive the immunity.
in writing. − merger and acquisition operations often require complex financial support. the commission's action plan on eu company law is expected to be adopted by the ep. the ep stresses that the mandatory takeover bid provision is the main provision governing the protection of minority shareholders and allows for derogations from this provision to protect the interests of shareholders' control. the ep also stressed that the mandatory takeover bid provision allows minority shareholders to receive a premium paid for the controlling stake in the event of a change of control. the directive abolishes the obligation to submit a mandatory takeover bid if, after an initial voluntary offer, the threshold of control is reached in such a way that the bidder can then increase its holding in the company being acquired by simply acquiring shares. the rapporteur believes that information flows should be ensured for workers and that all workers should have access to transitional support, regardless of their status. it is considered important to maintain the rights, obligations and working conditions set out in the current employment contracts and to prohibit dismissals in connection with the activities carried out during the acquisition. the rapporteur raised the issue of establishing an effective system of penalties and controls to protect against violations of workers' rights.
mr. chairman, please! we must remember that the economic slowdown has weakened not only entire countries but also the potential of individual regions, even those that have been prosperous. i fully agree with the need to develop strategies to revive them. we are in the process of planning the eu budget for the next few years. it is therefore worth considering a chapter on the funds which will be used to support regional economies and will also allow the balance of capital between weaker regions and stronger ones. it is fully in line with the recommendations to create favourable conditions for the development of new enterprises. this will generate much higher profits than the current preference for large national centres. it will also be a driver of innovation in the economy and a catalyst for the often frustrated young people who are looking for their own way into business. this is the best way to stimulate job growth. in poland too, there are many regions with very poor industrial infrastructure. the development of future industries and the location of new investments in these regions would be a desirable direction for their development.
mr. chairman, please! the problem is undoubtedly very serious. we have a number of industrial centres in europe which, for various reasons, have been in a dramatic crisis. many redundancies are taking place or are already foreseen. this can lead to serious social problems. in this situation, the european union should prepare a strategy to support especially such industrial centres that have a development perspective. in poland, we see these problems, for example, in the upper silesian industrial centre, where cities such as katowice, chorzów and bytom need support to find new ways of industrialisation and modern technologies that will guarantee new jobs. i hope that this kind of coherent strategy will emerge, because the european union is in dire need of it.
in writing. - i support the report by mr jens geier on regional strategies for industrial centres in the european union. industry has always been one of the most important sectors of the economy, contributing to job creation and economic growth. in recent years, we have seen the collapse of many traditional industries, such as mining, metallurgy, textiles and machinery. as a result, many eu regions are facing challenges linked to structural transformation processes. the measures available under cohesion policy could be very helpful in countering the negative effects of post-industrial areas. it is very important that these funds support actions to stimulate industrial policy in formerly industrialised areas, inter alia by improving the conditions for new investments, supporting the modernisation of the industrial sector and the transfer of new technologies, and promoting new industries of the future. the development of regional strategies for former industrial areas is also very important. i believe that this will help to overcome the difficulties faced by the industrial sector in many regions of the eu.
in writing. − the industrial sector in the eu has been declining in the last 50 years and requires some major structural transformation. the old industrialised regions are the ones that are in most need and are the ones that have to receive the most focus because of the regional disparity that has occurred due to the enlargement of the eu. today’s civilisation focuses more on the new industry that consists of technology and contemporary innovations rather than ones that include coal, machinery, etc. the restoration of old industry is very costly. technology and any type of advancements do require funding, and european public funding has to play a large role in it. i believe that the cohesion policy brings essential restructuring in the industrial areas in the european union. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on regional strategies for industrial areas in the european union, as it contains ideas on how cohesion policy can best support the regeneration and reorganisation of these areas and contribute to the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. the key recommendations of the report include the development of effective policies in areas such as cohesion policy, economic governance and competitiveness, innovation, research, the digital agenda, sustainable development, the creative and cultural industries, new skills and jobs. developing smart specialisation strategies is also important, and the success of regions depends on sustainable development strategies that are tailored to their needs. the development of entrepreneurship among young people should also be further promoted.
in writing. − eu cohesion policy funding should complement national funding and contribute to the faster implementation of eu legislation on renewable energy and energy efficiency. it is important to promote rational, long-term and cost-efficient strategies for energy and resources and a green economy. local and regional authorities in industrial centres should seek to exploit the synergies between national and union public funding and private investment in energy and infrastructure projects to support innovation, research and development. the need for the eu to mobilise all the policies and instruments available at european level to support job creation was highlighted. it was recognised that planned strategies should aim to protect and respect the environment and physical space, while at the same time being more efficient and environmentally sustainable.
certainly, actions to protect the environment in connection with the extraction and exploitation of natural resources such as gas and oil are important. this is demonstrated by the various cases of major disasters which have had a very negative impact on the quality of the environment and, moreover, have subsequently entailed serious costs associated with restoring the environment to its previous state. but there is no doubt that not only the extraction but also the transport of these raw materials can pose such a threat to ecosystems. the agreement to build the nordstream pipeline under the baltic sea from russia to europe, mainly to germany, is an example of a certain inconsistency between the european parliament and the european union in general. this pipeline carries a real threat. the european parliament passed a resolution in the previous term of office that was critical of the construction of this pipeline for environmental reasons, and then it was approved as if the resolution had never been passed. so why all the fuss when the interests will prevail anyway and the case will be carried out against the objections of the environmentalists and the position of the european parliament?

in writing. − the plan for the safety of offshore oil and gas activities has the right approach toward the attempt to prevent the repetition of the gulf of mexico tragedy in 2010. i believe that the change in the proposed legislation from a regulation to a directive was appropriate. it saves a significant amount of time and cost and gives the possibility of creating a strong legal framework within the directive. additionally, i agree with the proposed transparency of the eu authorities group. this can be used as a forum for the member states to exchange information on experiences with their accident prevention. i believe that this type of information sharing will improve the safety precautions within many of the regimes. it will reduce the need for any type of safety trial and error testing. the proposed directive has effectively thought out the most effective ways to increase the safety of offshore oil and gas activities. therefore, i vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − the deepwater horizon explosion has prompted a review of eu policies. the european commission has launched a safety assessment of offshore oil and gas activities in european waters. further action was identified as necessary to ensure the dissemination in the union of proven solutions establishing a clear and modern framework at union level. the european commission proposal focuses on measures to prevent general disparities and fragmentation of practices and on member states' legislation on the extraction of oil and natural gas from offshore deposits. this was sufficient reason for the rapporteur to accept the commission's proposal. it should more explicitly require operators to have the financial guarantees necessary to cover the costs of clean-up and compensation in the event of a major accident.

i voted against this report. however, in appreciating the value of energy from different sources, including renewable energy, many of those working on the report overlook the fact that renewable energy is twice as expensive as coal-fired energy. it so happens that the whole world is basing its production on the cheapest energy and therefore competing with european industry. we cannot turn a blind eye to these obvious facts. if this energy costs much more, we should be able to allow countries to use it more flexibly, rather than rigidly, with very serious economic and social consequences. often it is the 3 million new jobs that will be created by green energy, but to this we must add the other side namely 6 and perhaps 10 million jobs that europe will lose in the years ahead precisely because of this irrational, unwise policy that turns a blind eye to the much higher prices of renewable energy than traditional energy.
in writing. − renewable energy is one of the european union's main areas of interest, as it is of strategic importance for the development of the community as a whole and of individual countries. there is no doubt that the supply of stable energy at competitive prices is crucial for the rapid development of the industry. moreover, the development of biofuel, wind and biogas technologies will have a significant impact on the development of rural areas, which in many community countries cover a significant part of the territory. to prevent the negative effects of regulation on renewable energy in rural areas, the european union should define a clear and predictable framework that does not negatively impact food production and does not increase the cost of energy. the situation of the internal energy market in the european union must change if the economies of the community countries are to remain competitive. it is therefore necessary to introduce both a new perspective on renewable energy and projects currently under discussion such as iluc.
in writing. − regulation of renewable energy in the european energy market is undoubtedly important, but it also requires a lot of thought. the question is not whether we should use renewable energy at all, but how quickly we can develop this form of energy, especially in times of crisis and with no clear prospects for getting out of it. i voted against the first amendment, specifically against the provision that would suggest renewable energy at 40 to 45 percent by 2030. this objective seems unrealistic, especially in the polish economy. you can try to achieve that goal, but you can't be embarrassed by the record. after rejecting this amendment, i voted in favour of the whole report.
in writing. - renewable energy has been and continues to be a source of great hope, but also of great controversy. its production must be dictated by economic calculation, like any other activity. this does not mean that the production of such energy should not be financially supported. however, such subsidies must be deliberate and coordinated so as not to hamper the competitiveness of the economy. the european commission estimates that investments in renewable energy can create an additional 3 million jobs. but we have to ask ourselves, will more people lose their jobs as a result of the decline in competitiveness of the low-carbon economy? energy production is a long-term investment, so we must set realistic targets, and i repeat: realistic targets! in addition, stable conditions for development over many years are needed. the key will be the planned completion of the internal energy market by 2014. this would allow for more efficient deliveries and lead to lower prices. the production potential of energy, in particular renewable energy, should take into account the local conditions of each country. finally, i would like to say that in the context of renewable energy policy, it sounds strange to announce the decommissioning of 5-7% of agricultural land as part of the cap reform between 2014 and 2020, with the simultaneous intention of reducing the production of first generation biofuels.

in writing. - i supported the report on women's rights in the balkan countries applying for eu membership. the report provides general guidance and detailed country-specific recommendations. the main problems are: 1. effective implementation of the gender equality legislation. in the western balkan countries, legislation in this area, although adopted, is not effectively applied. for example, the constitution of albania prohibits discrimination on grounds of sex, but in practice women are discriminated against, including as a result of the return to the traditional legal code of the kanun, which reinforces the division of gender roles and status in society. there are many similar examples, and the overriding requirement for the balkan countries should be to effectively comply with the eu acquis on gender equality. this also includes the need to promote gender equality and women's rights and to work against gender stereotypes. 2.equal rights and equal access to the labour market as a necessary condition for ensuring women's economic independence. in the balkan countries, unemployment is more common among women. the primary role of women is to care for the children and to care for the home. they are much more likely to live in poverty because of reduced family benefits and other benefits. governments should ensure that gender equality legislation is implemented and respected, guaranteeing equal opportunities for both women and men in accessing the labour market.

in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? the ageing of european societies means that strategic measures must be taken to provide financial security for retired workers, pensioners and students alike. it is important to build on the forecasts and develop solutions now to prevent these negative social trends from escalating. however, not all proposals are conducive to achieving these objectives. the principle of equal retirement ages for men and women is certainly not serving this purpose. in the face of dramatically low birth rates in many member states, it will be more urgent and effective to support pro-family policies, in particular by facilitating the encouragement of young people to take up the challenge of raising children. increasing the birth rate is a natural way to redress the imbalance between the proportion of people in work and those on benefits. the systematic expansion of the labour market to mobilise the ever-growing number of young people who are unemployed and often without any means of subsistence should be an equally important priority.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the plan for adequate, secure and stable pensions by ms ria oomen-ruijten. the ageing of the population and the current economic crisis pose a number of challenges in ensuring the stability of pension systems and guaranteeing social security for eu citizens. in this context, member states should be encouraged to undertake such pension reform measures as would ensure stability and social security. it should also be borne in mind that the increasing mobility of europeans requires the creation of pension systems that guarantee that pension rights acquired in the member state of origin or in another member state are not lost. it is also crucial to agree on minimum standards for the acquisition and retention of pension rights and to encourage the generation of supplementary private pension savings. in addition, i believe it is appropriate to put in place a process of coordination at eu level to help member states to develop sustainable and secure pension systems.
in writing. - i voted today in favour of the resolution on adequate, secure and stable pensions because the financial and economic crisis, the second wave of which we are currently experiencing, has shown very clearly the fragility of the existing pension systems. it turned out that none of the models guaranteed stable and adequate pensions. moreover, they all contribute to the deterioration of the financial situation of the state. in this debate, pension schemes are often seen as a burden on public finances, but they are also seen as a tool to combat the poverty of older people and thus stimulate the economy. furthermore, as the examples of spain and portugal show, pension benefits can also be used to support the whole family when they are the only stable and certain income of one of its members. in view of all these problems, i fully agree with the rapporteur that we must build a system that is most resilient to economic shocks. it seems a good idea to pursue a multi-tiered pension system that would skillfully combine all models. nevertheless, it seems to me that the main challenge facing both the union and the member states today is youth unemployment. no pension system will function effectively if a large proportion of the population is outside the labour market or does not contribute to it.
in writing. − in an era of adverse demographic change in the eu and economic crisis, pension reforms are an essential element in improving the financial situation of citizens. the resolution we adopted calls for the income of older people to be diversified so that public schemes (alongside employee and private forms) are the most important sources of funding. another step to improve the situation is to increase the retirement age and encourage employers to hire older people. in order to increase coordination of systems at european level, we also called for the possibility of transferring pension rights between member states, which could prove extremely useful in the event of a change of residence. pensions are very often the only means of support for older people, leading to a life on the poverty line. this is particularly important for people living in rural areas where access to additional income is limited. guaranteed pension benefits are therefore necessary and should be introduced and reformed with due diligence.
in writing. − the report by ms oomen-ruijten on safe and adequate pensions contains several particularly important elements, namely the reference to the situation of national budgets, changes in the life expectancy of citizens, the ratio of the number of pensioners to the number of persons in employment, the maintenance of several pillars of the pension fund, the partnership of trade unions and ngos. there is no doubt about it: governments are responsible for guaranteeing pensions. i supported the report because it deserves to be supported. the only downside is that the economic crisis, high unemployment, especially among young people, can leave countries without the means to fund their pensions.
in writing. on an important issue such as pensions, it is important to bear in mind all the economic and demographic data which relate to it. the report by my colleague, mrs ria oomen-ruijten, has done that. this report takes into account the increase in life expectancy in the eu and its necessary alignment with the retirement age, the restriction of early retirement schemes to keep older people in employment and the standardisation of the working careers of men and women to eventually eliminate the glaring difference between men's and women's pensions. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
in writing. − the issue of pensions is a matter of great public concern in most eu countries. they are affected by the same problems - albeit to varying degrees - the demographic crisis, the increasing instability of employment (including the 'junk' contracts) and unemployment. all these factors will translate into the amount of pensions paid. according to a 2012 report by the european commission, in 2060 the total pension in poland is to be 22% of the last salary. under the old system, the ratio was 47% in 2010 and was even higher, above 60%, before that. many countries are raising the retirement age, which is causing a huge social uproar. it is understandable if we compare the increase in the retirement age with the state's inaction in the face of the proliferation of junk contracts that mostly devastate the pension system. the compulsory capital system is causing great excitement in many countries, including poland. the authors of the report highlight important issues such as equal pension benefits for women and men, the right to information on future retirement and the pension future of people working in different member states. all these factors have led me to support this report. regardless of the above, it should be borne in mind that the state is the ultimate guarantor of pensions.
in writing. − the green paper on european pension systems published by the european commission aims to launch a debate on the main challenges in this area and how the eu can support member states. the aim of the support will be to ensure adequate and stable pensions. a document analysing the possibility of modernising pension policies in eu countries addresses considerations on the gradual raising of the retirement age and the increase in pension contributions. i believe that the legal framework should be designed to encourage eu countries to carry out reforms that take account of demographic changes in europe (increasing life expectancy) and the need to link these issues to the moment of retirement.
in writing. - i welcome the outcome of today's vote. the resolution adopted today sends a clear signal to member states not to delay pension reforms. the ageing of the population is a pan-european phenomenon. in addition, the negative effects of the demographic crisis are exacerbated by the economic crisis. the european parliament today confirmed that public first pillar pension schemes should remain the main source of income for pensioners, but that governments have a responsibility to seek and promote alternative instruments that can provide funding for the provision of benefits to older people. that is a very clear and unambiguous position of parliament.
mr. chairman, please! the regulation conferring specific supervisory powers on the european central bank provides for a completely new quality of banking supervision. for the first time in history, the supervision of europe's major banks will be transferred to a single international institution. this operation aims to restore market confidence, rebuild the crossborder credit market and harmonise and reduce the cost of refinancing for euro area peripheral banks. the new rules aim to create an effective and coherent banking supervision system that is more pragmatic, efficient and independent of local conditions than national regulators. the new supervision is designed to detect and respond to irregularities in national banking sectors before they become a threat to the stability of the euro area as a whole. in my speech, i would like to draw attention to the non-euro area countries. due to the legal basis adopted by the european commission for the creation of the single supervisory mechanism, it was not possible to grant non-euro area countries full rights under the new system. nevertheless, parliament and the council have reached a good compromise, the provisions of which bear the asymmetric relationship between the obligations and rights of the states with a temporary derogation. recognising the legal and systemic constraints, such as the lack of access to the ecb's liquidity operations, we have developed a formula that is a fair offer for non-euro area countries. non-euro area countries have an influence on the wording of the final decisions of the supervisory board and may terminate or suspend their membership in justified circumstances. as a non-euro-area mep, i would like to stress that these regulations strengthen the euro area, but we do not forget our great achievement, the single financial market. we have been able to create an instrument which deepens economic and monetary union, but which does not discriminate against countries which are only on the way to a common currency. i do not agree with the increasingly loud opinions that we should be content with joint supervision and postpone the next elements of the banking union. it is doubtful mr president, i would like to raise two points. my first point is on the need to look at the single supervisory mechanism and the single resolution mechanism together. they are two sides of the same coin. to ensure an effective functioning of the ssm, there needs to be a transition from a system of national bank recovery and resolution regimes to a single european framework. being part of the same banking union framework, the srm will need to be consistent with the ssm. moreover, the srm will need to have an opt-in system for non-euro members that is compatible with the opt-in system of the ssm. my second point is about the risks related to the functioning of a european banking union. firstly, there is a risk that the ecb’s broad scope in terms of the number of banks supervised, and its dual supervision/monetary policy mandate, may put the reputation of the central bank under pressure, so any related risks should be mitigated as far as possible. secondly, there is also a risk that practical problems and political reluctance will delay the set-up of a direct recapitalisation tool via the esm. existing political worries need to be addressed and steps taken towards its implementation as soon as possible. lastly, it is as yet unclear whether a common resolution mechanism can be designed within the current treaties. there is a risk of following the fiscal compact path of an intergovernmental agreement again. this would be one more reform that would move us further away from the community method and increase concerns about the direction in which europe is heading.

madam president! the facilitation of the free movement of persons guaranteed by article 3 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union has led to an increasing number of people travelling or moving abroad. this requires common, harmonised legal measures to guarantee citizens the protection and security they enjoy in their own country throughout the union. the commission's initiative on a regulation on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters will complement the european protection order directive guaranteeing mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters and thus help to guarantee the rights of victims across the eu. the combined application of these two instruments criminal and civil will allow persons who have been granted a protection order in one member state to maintain it while travelling or moving to another member state without having to undergo time-consuming procedures. the proposed standardised, multilingual certificate, containing all the relevant information necessary for recognition of protection, will be a great help to all victims. the proposed proposal is an excellent example of simplifying and creating european law that is understandable to citizens, fast and effective throughout the community.
madam president! in the debate on the crisis so far, the social dimension of european integration has very often been overlooked because of the urgent need to restore stability to public finances. but the focus on precautionary measures has led to social crises, as in greece and spain. in the present situation, monetary and monetary union must be complemented by more unified social policies and social investment. this is strategically important for two reasons. first, to restore sustained economic growth in europe, short-term precautionary measures must be complemented by a european strategy for social investment. in addition, it is necessary to create social surveillance in the form of economic surveillance, which will allow better monitoring of the actions taken by the member states. secondly, we will never achieve true economic union without social convergence. we are already seeing that what has hitherto been the competitive advantage of the member states is now, in times of crisis, being called social dumping and leading to protectionist measures. if we want to promote mobility in the european union, we need to create the instruments and conditions for the development of the member states, which will lead to better social convergence in the long term.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the report by mrs kleva kekuš on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. in times of financial crisis, the tolerance of these practices should be particularly strongly condemned and eu countries should be consistently forced to take decisive action to prevent the continuation of such practices. the losses are estimated at over eur 1 trillion per year. this has a negative impact on investment, growth and employment. the absence of a centralised union tax policy leads to increased costs and administrative burdens for citizens and businesses, and has a negative impact on consumer sentiment and trust in the tax system in the member states of the european union. the european commission has developed an action plan to reduce the tax gap by half by 2020 in order to put an end to tax fraud. as regards tax fraud and tax evasion, the commission considers that member states should allocate adequate resources to national tax administrations and control staff. the commission believes that eu member states should also withdraw banking licences from financial institutions that facilitate tax fraud. in the case of tax havens, the commission is working to harmonise their definition and to establish a blacklist of member states that have concluded agreements with countries identified as tax havens.

in writing. - in voting on the report by mr peter šťastný, i supported the preliminary draft agreement between the european union and canada. increasing globalisation, the radicalisation of social attitudes in third world countries, global terrorism and cyber threats are increasingly affecting the functioning of the european union. these factors have a negative impact on the intensification of trade with partners outside the union, including canada. the two partners are bound by the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement of 1998. to the satisfaction of the european union, canada has demonstrated a willingness to cooperate more closely on supply chain security and risk management. the focus of the amendment is to systematise the customs aspects of the security of the logistics chain in international trade. in addition, the amendment guarantees closer cooperation between the partners on standards and risk management, security, information and data exchange, strategic cooperation on cargo inspection, as well as cooperation in multilateral fora, including the world customs organization. the contract design is further enhanced by the fact that it is based on the latest standards of the world customs organisation's framework of security standards. i therefore believe that cooperative trade relations to minimise risk and promote international standards without unnecessary burdens on authorities and economic operators will bring tangible and long-term benefits to both partners.
in writing. − safety is an important element of effective trade. this is essential for the smooth running of businesses, regardless of the sector in which they operate. this also undoubtedly has an impact on the quality of the services provided. in the era of globalisation, supply chain security is becoming an even more important element of trade. the eu bases its international cooperation on the promotion of global security standards, in particular the world customs organization security standards framework, the exchange of information and data and the mutual recognition of credible economic operators. in a globalised world, no country can ensure the security of its supply chain on its own. international cooperation and standards are therefore crucial. i voted in favour of the recommendation because the future conclusion of an agreement between the european union and canada is part of a broader process and of the more active actions taken in the last decade in the field of supply chain security and risk management. the new agreement aims to strengthen the customs aspects of the security of the international trade logistics chain, including container security, while facilitating legitimate trade. the eu has already concluded negotiations and reached an agreement on mutual recognition of the aeo with japan and the united states. the eu-canada supply chain security agreement will allow for negotiations on such an agreement with canada as well
in writing. − in a globalised world, it is impossible for a country to conduct supply chain security alone. there is a need for international cooperation in order to have confidence in the legitimacy of the trade. i believe that this is a right step towards ensuring that the international trade between the eu and canada will be secure and admissible. moreover, i think that the increased effectiveness in the security is going to eliminate any type of delays that could have been encountered in the old agreement of 1998. it will make the process flow more smoothly. the recommendation successfully highlights the security measures that are going to be appointed and the benefits that will result. i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. − i believe that international cooperation between the union and canada is essential to ensure the security of the supply chain and to facilitate legitimate trade. the eu-canada supply chain security agreement will allow for negotiations on mutual recognition of authorised economic operators (aeos) with canada. the agreement will be managed by the eu-canada joint customs cooperation committee, which will have the power to take implementing decisions, including on mutual recognition. the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement (cmaa) of 1998 will remain the general basis for customs cooperation between the eu and canada. the new agreement will build on key elements of the world customs organization's security standards framework to secure and facilitate global trade.
in writing. − the establishment of clear and transparent criteria for banking supervision is one of the major challenges facing the european union. negligence in the financial sector, which is not properly controlled, can lead to unforeseen consequences, which we experienced during the current crisis. the stable economic development of the community countries thus depends to a large extent on the establishment of a european banking authority. in accordance with the opinion of the parliamentary committee on budgets, in order to preserve the financial independence of the european central bank, the newly created office should be financed from the union budget. we must not forget to create the appropriate tools and criteria to enable the eba to supervise all financial institutions in a transparent, reliable and uniform manner.
in writing. - i believe that the unification of the supervisory mechanism will make it possible to create a fully developed banking union, which will be able to solve the problem of private and public debt. fragmenting regulatory systems will not help in fighting the financial crisis or in fighting debt. there is a need to further strengthen the european banking authority so that there is an opportunity to deepen the internal market and to avoid a division between euro area and non-euro area members.
in writing. − we have adopted today two reports establishing a preliminary common european surveillance for the euro area countries. as a result, it will be possible to control the cross-border banking groups that have dominated the european financial market. strict supervision of the big banks will help us to prevent crises like the one that hit the world economy in 2008, and the effects of which are still being felt in europe. a common european banking supervision is only the first step in building a banking union. as a result of its creation, the competences of the national supervisory authorities in the euro area will be transferred to the european level. the european central bank (ecb) has been given the status of european supervisor, with supervisory powers over the 150 largest european banks. the ecb will be able, inter alia, to require these banks to maintain an appropriate level of reserves and to grant licences. however, it is important to ensure the separation of the ecb's monetary and supervisory policies. there is still a great deal of uncertainty as to the division of competences between the various supervisory authorities. there is no doubt that economic coordination and fiscal policy harmonisation at european level need to be further strengthened.
in writing. − the fragmentation of the financial sector is a threat to the integrity of the single currency and the single market. the harmonisation of the supervisory mechanism is essential. to this end, it is necessary to establish a european banking union comprising a single supervisory mechanism and a common framework for deposit guarantee, resolution and winding-up. the banking union should include both euro area members and candidate countries. the ecb is the competent institution for the exercise of the supervisory tasks over credit institutions in the participating member states, due to its expertise and credibility.
in writing. - pyrotechnic articles are specific articles which are widely available and which, if used improperly, can pose a direct threat to the health or even the life of citizens. the safety of products in community trade is also a necessary condition for the construction of the single market. in this respect, the coherence of the rules is of the utmost importance. the current loose interpretation, on the other hand, allows for often unequal competition and trade in goods that may be considered dangerous or harmful. the report by mrs roithová makes a number of amendments to the commission proposal to improve consumer protection. for example, it is necessary to provide clear and comprehensible instructions and information on labels, which is of particular importance for the safety of children. it also requires states to monitor and address mislabelling of pyrotechnic products. in order to reduce administrative formalities, manufacturers were also allowed to provide the required declarations of conformity electronically.
in writing. − to ensure consumer safety in the internal market, comprehensive action is needed in a number of areas. one such area is the issue of the placing on the market of pyrotechnic articles. we already have legislation which sets out the essential requirements that must be met before these products are placed on the market, but there is a need to harmonise the legislation of the member states in this area. the directives in question should be adapted to the new legal framework adopted as a 'package of goods' as early as 2008. the sectors covered by these directives are very important industrial sectors, subject to strong international competition, and will benefit from simplification and a level playing field for european businesses. i voted in favour of the report because the alignment of the directives in question with the legal framework of the commodity package is an important step towards the completion of the single market. that legal framework introduces a simplified regulatory environment for products and allows for a more consistent application of technical standards, which will help to improve the functioning of the single market by ensuring equal treatment of non-compliant products and economic operators, as well as equal assessment of notified bodies within the eu market, and reduce the number of non-compliant and dangerous products on the market. i also find it very important that the commission based its conclusions in the adjustment package on extensive consultations, especially with smes, which allowed companies to share directly their experience with the 'commodity package'.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the aligning of the nine product directives to the new legislative framework is an essential step to the completion of the eu single market. consistent implementation and enforcement are necessary to establish fair competition and safe products, and manifest the characteristics of a strong single market. additionally, i agree with the recommended changes to directive 2007/23/ec on pyrotechnic articles. they have been clearly outlined and effectively argued.
in writing. − firms manufacturing and placing pyrotechnic articles on the market will have to ensure that they meet certain requirements and confirm this by means of the ce marking. the new regulations on explosives for civilian use prepared by the ministry of economy will improve the safety of their use and disposal. the draft law was adopted by the government on 23 february. firms manufacturing or placing pyrotechnic articles on the market will determine the class of the product according to the degree of danger in use, the intensity of the sound and the availability of the product to users. they will also be required to display information labels in polish, including the name and address of the manufacturer or importer, the name and type of the product, the class of the product, the authorised place of use, etc. the rules adopted concern so-called spectacular pyrotechnic articles, as well as articles intended for theatrical use and for technical applications, e.g. in car airbags.
in writing. −i am in favour of the adoption of a directive regulating the trade in pyrotechnic articles. i consider it particularly important to improve the level of protection of consumers, who are frequent users of pyrotechnic articles without being professionals. i believe that the placing on the market of a pyrotechnic article should be subject to the affixing of the name and the contact address of the manufacturer so that the manufacturer can be identified. it seems to me appropriate that, in the case of imported products, the name and address of the importer should be given in addition. the safety of children, the elderly and the disabled must be particularly enhanced. i believe that these measures could reduce the number of accidents and human suffering associated with the misuse of pyrotechnic substances

rapporteur. − mr president, tomorrow we will vote on one of the most crucial reports of this term – one which falls within the scope of eu trade and investment policy. with this report we are taking the final step towards establishing a consistent and comprehensive common foreign eu trade policy. we have managed to set up a framework that will allow the eu to manage its financial responsibilities resulting from investor state dispute settlements (isds). as we know, various eu countries were – often, and with increasing frequency in recent years – subject to dispute settlements held at various tribunals. now, after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, it is the eu that has exclusive competence over foreign direct investment. it also takes responsibility for financial commitments resulting from lost civil cases. the core issue in this file was obviously the right apportionment of the obligation to pay awards to an investor. in other words, the decision concerns when and under what conditions the eu pays the awarded sum, and when it is the obligation of the member state concerned to do so. i believe, along with other shadow rapporteurs here whom i would like to thank for author. − madam president, i speak as the chair of the committee which has tabled this oral question and the resolution. let me start by saying that the alps have a very long, strong tradition of cooperation between member states’ regions and local communities and people. this cooperation has been overwhelmingly focused on tangible concrete projects with high added value. in recent years we have witnessed efforts in this part of europe to intensify cooperation. we have seen a growing political commitment to working together and major improvements in governance. this is the reason why, after many years of this strong tradition of cooperation, the regions decided, during the 2012 conference of the alpine regions, to embark on a more institutionalised framework for cooperation via a macro-regional strategy for the alps. they promoted this approach as a key instrument to fully exploit the enormous development potential of this part of europe and to cope more efficiently with challenges that do not respect administrative or political borders. this bottom-up initiative by the alpine regions has been maturing for many years. specific areas of cooperation have already been identified. the alps cooperation has already proved to be effective, and for this reason, upgrading it to eu level through a macro-regional strategy framework constitutes an obvious step forward, reinforcing european territorial cooperation in those regions. we need more cooperation in europe. it is therefore quite natural that the committee on regional development (regi), which i chair, when reflecting on the added value of macro-regional strategies has decided to support the ambition of the regions to develop a macro-regional strategy for the alps. the regi committee has tabled this oral question to the council and to the commission, accompanied by a resolution, formulating explicitly the request that an eu macro-regional strategy for the alps be elaborated and implemented.
i am very pleased that the european parliament is finally taking up the european mountain areas, which are so important for the future territorial development of the european union. the union has long been reluctant to give mountain regions their proper place in regional development policy. it is good that we are thinking of creating a macro-regional strategy for the alpine region, but at the same time i would urge that we also look at the second largest mountain range in europe, which is larger than the alps, the carpathians, which in a unique way fulfils the criteria of the macro-regional strategies described by the european commission. it is a region of great geopolitical importance, rich in culture, nature and society, linking european countries with a tripartite status member states, accession countries and those covered by the eastern partnership. however, it is also the least competitive region, comprising the weakest, poorest areas of the european union. however, the carpathians are not included in any multilateral cooperation under the european union's macro-regional programmes. the carpathian region needs immediate transport, infrastructure, environmental and support for local entrepreneurship. taking advantage of the alps' experience, the carpathians require a separate european programme. i hope that today's debate will pave the way for the development of a macro-regional strategy for both the alps and the carpathians.
madam president! i am a strong supporter of macro-regional strategies, as they bring many benefits and opportunities to the area, allowing for better use of the potential of individual regions and allowing for a comprehensive solution to many problems. cooperation between countries in setting objectives, aligning funds and tackling common challenges can contribute to improving spatial integration and thus to increasing the competitiveness of the regional economy. in addition, macro-regional strategies open up new perspectives for territorial cooperation projects and can ensure more fruitful cooperation between regional programmes and the europe 2020 objectives. territorial and social cohesion is one of the fundamental objectives of the member states, and we should therefore support concrete proposals and ideas for action, and such action is the development of macro-regional strategies that will allow for more coordinated, comprehensive and coherent action to address the challenges and problems of the regions of the european union. for many years in my region, the subcarpathian region, we have been working on a macro-regional strategy for the carpathians, which has strong social support. i have repeatedly stressed the need for this, both at the meetings of the regional development committee and at other meetings. the work on the subsequent macro-regional strategies raises a question which i would like to put to the commissioner: is there a chance of creating a macro-regional strategy for the carpathians? a region which meets all the conditions of a macro-region, which also has a great potential that can be exploited more effectively and better protected? a macro-regional strategy for the carpathians would address many of the problems facing the region, such as poor infrastructure, marked socio-economic disparities, population migration and the protection of its rich fauna and flora. such a strategy would be a more effective continuation of the current activities and the extensive cooperation that has been in place for many years in this particular region.

mr. chairman, please! the application of trade preferences to the least developed countries is an effective mechanism to support their economic growth. access to european markets is often a key stabilising factor for them. burma is a country where there have been and continue to be egregious practices of discrimination against citizens and human rights violations. the authorities' progress in this area is not satisfactory, but the international labour organisation has lifted the restrictions imposed, considering that the violations of workers' rights are no longer serious. it's certainly a good prognosticator. the fact is that the burmese government has taken serious steps to eliminate forced labour, following the un recommendations. while restoring the tariff preferences, the union must closely monitor the actions of the burmese authorities, and in particular the military, which still uses forced labour in some regions. furthermore, religious conflicts are intensifying in that country, and the international community cannot afford to remain silent.
in writing. − under the generalised system of preferences, the european union grants trade preferences to developing countries. the scheme is designed to contribute to the economic development of these countries. however, in certain situations, in particular serious and systematic breaches of the rules by a country to which preferences have been granted, they may be temporarily withdrawn. this is what happened in burma. these preferences, in the light of the efforts of burma, should be restored, although there are still open issues on which europe must demand progress from burma, such as further democratisation of the country, further peace talks with ethnic groups denied citizenship, the release of remaining political prisoners, etc.
in writing. − the introduction of trade restrictions on myanmar/burma by the european union in 1997 was justified. but since then, much has changed in this country. progress has been made in respecting human rights, and many political prisoners have been released, including nobel peace prize laureate aung san suu kyi, who spent 20 years under house arrest. the main opposition party, the national league for democracy, has been re-legalised. today, aung san suu kyi herself is advocating for the lifting of international sanctions. it is also important to realize that the continued economic sanctions are contributing to the strengthening of chinese influence in the country. because of its access to the indian ocean, myanmar/burma remains an important trade partner and freight route for china. however, the union should not ignore the fact that not all political prisoners have been released and that ethnic and religious problems are flaring up. the return of myanmar/burma to the gsp will benefit its economy and citizens, as well as eu investors. however, attention must still be paid to whether the democratization of the country is not being hampered and whether workers' rights are being respected. the eu should support developing countries, but this can only happen if they respect human rights.
in writing. − in accordance with a council regulation, myanmar/burma's access to gsp tariff preferences was temporarily withdrawn in 1997 due to the systematic and widespread practice of forced labour. since 2011, myanmar/burma has undertaken a number of reforms to comply with the principles of the convention. the international labour conference therefore lifted the restrictions on myanmar/burma, which restored its access to the gsp.

in writing. − the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has made it necessary to review the existing rules on health requirements for domestic animals in transport. the modernisation of the rules is intended to make it easier for owners to accompany their animals when travelling within the union and to third countries, while taking into account animal health safety and public health and safety.
in writing. - in today's vote i voted in favour of the report by mr horst schnellhardt on the amendment of the requirements for the importation into the european union of dogs, cats and ferrets and the trade in these animals. the european commission's proposal does not introduce any radical changes, but only extends the period during which animals must undergo a clinical examination before travel by a veterinarian authorised by the competent authority to confirm that they are fit for transport on the intended route. the commission plans to align the 24-hour period with the recommendations of the world organisation for animal health, which provides for, inter alia, a 48-hour period. the rapporteur's intention is to facilitate the travel of both people and animals and to ensure the highest level of health safety.

the question of the blue card. thank you, mr. ambassador, for accepting your "blue card". you're right to say that there is no empirical evidence that the death penalty is the most deterrent or not, because there are no laboratory conditions in which we can say that. but would you agree with the logical conclusion that a greater punishment is more deterrent than a lesser punishment? and if so, would you agree that the ultimate punishment, the death penalty, is the most deterrent? would you agree with that logical sequence of statements?

in writing. organised crime remains a major problem in europe. its global nature and scope require global measures. one of them was the creation of the crim committee. its mandate should also be extended for the next term of office, this time as a standing committee. this is all the more so as, according to socta, there were 3600 organised crime groups operating in europe in 2012. in discussing the problem of organized crime, i'd like to focus today on three key issues. firstly, the fight against trafficking in human beings and trafficking in organs. the numbers are staggering. this phenomenon brings in profits of 25 billion euros. from the eastern border of the union to the atlantic, all the countries of the european community are affected by this nightmare. 264,000 people become victims of sexual abuse every year. in times of crisis, the industrial use of free labour is growing rapidly. combating these phenomena requires a joint effort and increased investment. another important element is drug crime. it provides the biggest profits to organized crime groups. this is an international procedure. to stop it, we need stronger border controls and common eu drug laws. it is particularly important to stop smuggling and to monitor closely the trade in drug precursors. in the last paragraph of my speech, i would like to focus on the fight against organized economic crime. the trade in counterfeit goods, fraud, money laundering are the nightmare of today's markets. their actions cost businesses over $870 billion a year.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i would like first to thank the committee on the internal market and consumer protection (imco) and in particular the rapporteur mr house. innovation and creativity are the engines of our economy. it is important to give rights owners the certainty that the fruits of their inventions will be protected. customs play a crucial role in stopping goods which infringe ipr from reaching the eu market. i am very happy that parliament, the council and the commission have reached agreement on a new regulation on the customs enforcement of ipr. let me recall the main benefit that this regulation will bring. firstly, we are extending the scope of intellectual property rights to be enforced at the borders. for example, counterfeit goods sent in small consignments to private persons are now covered. this is very important if we consider the huge rise in postal traffic due to internet sales. fake products carrying the sign of a well-known trade mark will also be blocked. this will keep the eu at the forefront of ipr protection at its borders. secondly, the regulation clarifies procedures, for instance by introducing a single request that will cover the whole of the eu. it simplifies the work of customs while respecting the rights of traders and of right-holders by streamlining notifications and communication with the various people involved. these changes, coupled with the new tools created to deal with requests from right-holders, such as the creation of a central electronic database, will make customs more efficient in the fight against counterfeiting. finally, the regulation addresses the specific problems we encountered in the past with regard to access to medicines. this has been a particularly sensitive matter, but i am confident that it is now definitely settled. to conclude, today’s agreement will strengthen the legal framework and simplify administrative procedures for the vital work that customs does to protect intellectual property rights. in doing so, it will help safeguard the interests of our legitimate traders and protect the competitiveness of our economy, which relies more and more on innovation and intellectual property. this new regulation is not just good for customs, it is good for our businesses and for our citizens.

the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i'm not going to let you get away with this. the starting point for my own-initiative report on legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial matters was the report presented last year by the european commission on the implementation and application of the 2003 directive. ten years have passed since the entry into force of this document and the transposition of the directive into national systems seems to have been successful. of course, each member state has adopted slightly different solutions, but in principle the right to legal aid is now guaranteed. however, only 12% of eu citizens are aware that they are entitled to free legal aid in the event of a legal dispute in another country. if citizens and, even worse, practitioners are not aware that it is possible to apply for legal aid in a member state other than the country of nationality, then the provisions of this directive are just a slogan that looks good on paper. it is natural that the increasing mobility and harmonisation of the european market should also be reflected in an increasing number of crossborder cases. however, the number of citizens applying for legal aid under the provisions of the directive is still low, as they are not aware that they can receive free pre-trial and in-trial assistance and, due to their ignorance, waive their claims. that is why i have placed the main emphasis in my report on increasing the involvement of the european commission and the member states in a more effective information campaign. i also point out the opportunities offered by modern technologies in the area of communication and awareness-raising of the right to legal aid in cross-border disputes. i also stress the importance of the internet and portals such as ejustice in the process of providing legal aid itself. another issue i have highlighted is that i believe it is extremely important to provide comprehensive legal support to citizens. specific cases. remember, sometimes bad advice is simply worse and more costly in its effects than no advice at all. in the following sections, i outline the steps that should be taken to facilitate procedures and improve access to legal aid. i also encourage member states to create more effective cooperation systems between public authorities and ngos to ensure citizens have wider access to legal aid and legal advice. in my view, good practice in the field of free legal advice such as university legal clinics or pro bono agencies should be widely disseminated and supported through an organised legal aid network. it is also worth highlighting the importance of member states providing access to pre-litigation assistance, including advice on alternative dispute resolution, in times of crisis and austerity. they are often less costly and more effective in civil and commercial matters. finally, i would like to express my deep concern at the trend i have observed towards a
