madam president! while supporting all constructive action in the field of consumer protection, i welcome the commission's proposals for the continuation of the consumer strategy in the coming years. it is based on the need to ensure the safety of food, health, digital and many other products that are essential to everyday life. the essential condition for effective protection remains unhindered access to transparent, comprehensive and expert product information. this applies to all consumers, but is particularly relevant for older people who are more vulnerable. the key to this is to promote consumer rights at the same time. independent price comparison websites are a very good idea, but they need consistent support. i look forward to the timely and consistent implementation of these directives in the individual member states and to the commission's continuous monitoring of the effectiveness of the extension of consumer protection. it would also be useful to propose the development of a green paper for consumers to make it easier for the relevant organisations, institutions and citizens to enforce their rights.
in writing. − as a member of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, i pay close attention to consumer protection and safety. i am pleased that the european commission has taken a very ambitious approach to this issue and has already prepared a 'european consumer agenda' in may 2012 as part of a wider consumer policy. consumers are an important part of the internal market and, with consumer spending reaching 56% of gdp in the eu, they are, alongside small and medium-sized enterprises, the engine of the european economy. the economic crisis has eroded consumer confidence in the internal market and restoring that confidence is now one of the key objectives. we should also seek to increase consumer participation in the market, to increase consumer safety, to increase consumer awareness and to guarantee the possibility of claiming rights. i supported the report because consumers should be given due consideration. in particular, greater protection is needed in the area of food safety, as well as in the area of financial services. it is also necessary to think about particularly vulnerable consumers, such as children, and to protect them from the harmful effects of advertising promoting, for example, unhealthy food. i also believe that closer cooperation between european and national authorities and consumer organisations is necessary. the development of european consumer centres is an important task for the future. the report calls for these measures to be taken, among others, and is therefore a further step towards developing consumer policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the report effectively outlines the necessity for the reform in the european consumer policy and aligns with the treaty of the european union. this new agenda brings up to date the ecp that was out of pace with today’s society. it considers the changes that have occurred over time which include the globalisation of the market, aging population, etc. additionally, it heeds the well-being of the consumers in the eu. it aims to give more knowledge to the consumers about the products that they are purchasing so that they can make informed decision. consumer awareness and protection from the products with dangerous chemicals is essential to maintain good health among the european citizens. other entities of this report that i strongly agree with are: the importance of equality among consumers, battling food wastage, and the importance of e-commerce in terms of consumers’ access to goods.
in writing. - for decades, the protection of workers' rights has been a central political issue. in recent years, consumer protection has also gained a similar status. the report on the new european consumer programme is a multi-faceted document. of particular interest is the report's call for the creation of a financial inspectorate which would act ex officio or at the individual or collective request of consumers record infringements and be able to impose penalties on those who breach the applicable rules. in the context of the housing crisis, it is also worth noting and supporting the requirement to suspend eviction or foreclosure of encumbered property if the delay in payment is due to reasons beyond the control of the consumer, such as unemployment and the application of a moratorium on monthly payments until the consumer finds a job. it is also pleased that the report pays considerable attention to food and food waste issues. this is a serious problem that deserves to be highlighted. the report's demands to ensure the safety of the entire food chain from production to consumption should be considered reasonable. other food safety claims also merit a similar assessment. in view of the above, i have decided to support the report on the new european consumer programme.
in writing. − effective consumer protection has been a priority of european integration for many years. the eu is currently planning to adopt a new consumer strategy for 2013-2020. this issue, as well as consumer claims and consumer law issues, will be discussed by the participants. the risks to consumer interests in the electronic environment are a very topical issue. in the age of global digitalisation, this is a major problem, especially in the context of the lack of respect for the rights of consumers when they make cross-border online purchases. today, such transactions are very disadvantageous to consumers, since the goods are often not as described and contact with the seller is difficult. i am in favour of stronger enforcement of consumer rights in this area by means of consultation with the national authorities.
in writing. − this programme is of particular importance for the future of the eu economy, given the important role consumers play in the eu economy and the economic importance of consumption as a driver of economic growth in the eu countries. in particular, consumer awareness is essential, as the aim of avoiding information overload, while reducing consumer ignorance and raising consumer awareness, can have a positive impact on enforcing consumer rights and reducing the risks consumers face, inter alia, in relation to counterfeit and dangerous products. the risks associated with banking services, in particular short-term loans and investment instruments, are also an important issue. the amber gold case in poland reinforces my belief that there is a need for proper education of the public on consumer rights in the banking sector. moreover, from an economic point of view, the need to educate the staff of small and medium-sized enterprises is particularly important, so that the extent to which consumers can exercise their rights is not distorted by the ignorance of the employees of the enterprises.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr zwiefka on legal aid in civil and commercial disputes. the issue is already covered by a 2003 council directive, but it was only last year that the european commission presented its first report on its effectiveness. the problems identified were the selective application of its provisions by some member states and the low awareness among eu citizens of the legal tools available under it, and thus the lack of knowledge of their rights in the event of a dispute. i fully support the proposals to improve the system, including actions to ensure that lawyers involved in the resolution of crossborder disputes are well-versed in the language and legal system of the country in which the conflict is concerned. i also consider it appropriate to leave the party concerned the choice between the legal system applicable in the country of residence or the country of domicile. i also join the call for those states which have not yet done so to accede to the hague convention, as this would allow their citizens to benefit from legal aid in certain third countries. i therefore welcome the text of the document on legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial disputes adopted today.
in writing. − as co-rapporteur on the report on legal aid in civil and commercial litigation, i strongly support the initiative to improve council directive 2003/8/ec, which has been in force since 2004. however, i regret that the commission did not revise the directive until 2010 and sent its conclusions to parliament two years later. this means that the weaknesses of the regulation will only be analysed 10 years after its transposition. such cases of late legislative analysis should not take place in community procedures. improving access to justice in cross-border disputes by introducing a minimum of harmonisation at eu level is a very important aspect for citizens, especially those less well off, who have access to justice in other member states. however, the regulation will not have the desired effect if citizens are not properly informed about it. the commission's analysis shows that only 12% of citizens are aware of the existence of crossborder legal aid and sometimes even the judiciary is not informed. it is therefore very important to promote the project through information campaigns, training of judges and lawyers and through internet portals. the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters currently provides information on legal aid which has not been updated since july 2007. i therefore support the idea of creating an up-to-date and easy-to-use eu-wide legal aid database where citizens could search for lawyers who can deal with their cases in their own language. the commission, in cooperation with the member states, should also be responsible for promoting and organising specific training for lawyers providing legal aid services. i congratulate the rapporteur and call on the commission to continue its work to improve the eu rules in the crossborder judicial system.
in writing. − i believe that raising awareness of council directive 2003/8/ec of 27 january 2003 is a right step towards increasing the effectiveness of its implementation. i support the general aim of this report and agree with many of the initiatives that it presents. eu citizens have to be more aware of their rights and the legal aid that they can receive. they need to be informed about the policies that can help them in difficult situations. one initiative that i fully support is the effort to provide more information on internet portal websites covering access to justice. this strategy is cost-effective and aligns with the needs of today’s society. the internet has become a major factor in the lives of eu citizens and i believe that using it to increase awareness of their rights will make this directive even more successful. therefore, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − since 2003, a regulation has been in place in the european union's legal order providing free legal aid to entrepreneurs in the event of a legal dispute arising in another country. yet, only 12 percent of the european union's population are aware of this fact. the opening of internal borders has increased cross-border trade in goods. this economically advantageous feature can be hindered by disputes between traders who are not familiar with the legal systems of other eu countries. the natural conclusion is to oblige member states to intensify information campaigns on this subject so that traders are aware of the assistance they receive both before and during the proceedings. however, particular attention should be paid to simplifying the rules for access to that aid as much as possible. as integration progresses and trade within the community increases, there is a need to train lawyers to represent their clients in cross-border disputes. the document provides for the creation of databases of lawyers with the necessary skills in comparative law and language skills. in view of the objectives and assumptions of this legislation, i have decided to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. −the existing directive on ensuring access to justice for citizens who are parties to crossborder disputes, which lays down the conditions for the provision of crossborder legal aid, in particular financial aid, is not sufficiently known and therefore does not fully fulfil its task of helping eu citizens. the rapporteur supports the idea of improving the system for providing access to justice, including by creating databases of lawyers, and revising the ceilings and guidelines for the granting of legal aid.
in writing. − having regard to council directive 2003/8/ec of 27 january 2003 to facilitate access to justice in crossborder disputes by establishing minimum common rules relating to legal aid in such disputes, i support the draft in question, but would like to point out the problematic aspects of its operation. the need to raise awareness among citizens of the european union of the right to cross-border legal aid should be emphasised. information campaigns in the member states are necessary to reach lawyers and potential beneficiaries. there are also other technical issues, such as the storage of forms, the creation of a single database on the e-justice portal and, above all, the regulation of language issues. in order to ensure an adequate level of service and to verify linguistic competence, a database of lawyers with knowledge of comparative law and appropriate language skills should be created to enable the provision of cross-border legal aid (such as the find-a-lawyer platform) and linked to the e-justice portal.' in order to ensure the proper functioning of the cross-border legal aid system, it is also necessary to set up a system of language and comparative legal training, which should be co-financed by union funds. despite these aspects, the project is of great importance for the european judiciary.
in writing. - the european fight against piracy and counterfeiting has been ongoing for many years. unfortunately, dishonest 'businesses' are still coming in, especially through online sales, which have led to a 200% increase in the number of mail seizures of counterfeit goods in recent years. it is a worrying fact that as many as 69% of goods seized in 2010 were medicinal products that pose a risk to the health and life of consumers. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal for new arrangements for the enforcement of customs legislation on intellectual property rights (ipr). customs authorities are best placed to enforce them effectively at the eu's external borders and should be given sufficient powers to combat the counterfeiting wave also within the community. i support the introduction of a provision allowing the detention of goods, including those in transit, provided there is a clear risk of their entering the eu market, which on the one hand gives a specific right to detain suspicious shipments, while at the same time not blocking the import of so-called generic medicines by the community for the poorer regions of the world. the fight against counterfeits from online purchases will be facilitated by detailed records of small consignments of suspicious goods, which can now be destroyed under a simplified procedure without the need for formal judicial proceedings. such a record is a great saving of both time and money. i support the commission's initiative, but i am concerned that no european law will replace concrete solutions developed jointly with non-eu countries - in particular the strategy on iprs with such a 'counterfeiting' giant as china, which accounted for 85% of goods detained by eu customs in 2010.
in writing. − the proposed regulation aims to improve the enforcement of existing rules and indeed, by simplifying procedures or delegating appropriate powers to customs, enforcement will become more effective and thus better protect traders and consumers. it should be stressed that the new rules do not change anything in terms of intellectual property protection and do not concern non-commercial products carried by tourists in their luggage. however, they point out, for example, the need to better inform consumers about the risks they may face when buying counterfeit products and, more importantly, focus on improving the work of customs authorities. the european parliament and the council have adopted a number of amendments to the directive on the protection of personal data. the business owners whose products are counterfeited suffer, as do the consumers whose health and safety are threatened by counterfeit products, even as medicines are counterfeited. many of these counterfeit products enter the union market from third countries, which is why border security is so important. i supported the recommendation because it is the customs officers at the borders who have the best chance of blocking the entry of such products, but they must have the appropriate legal instruments to do so, which the proposed rules will ensure. the new enforcement rules will improve the work of customs officers and are an important element in the creation of a well-functioning internal market.
in writing. − trade in goods infringing intellectual property rights harms rightholders and law-abiding producers and traders. at the same time, the trade in such goods is misleading to consumers and it is therefore necessary to improve the legal framework in order to strengthen the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities and to ensure appropriate legal clarity, taking into account the changes in the economic, business and legal spheres. this will help to prevent the entry of infringing goods into the customs territory and prevent their release for commercial circulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal because the regulation will enable persons to protect their intellectual property rights by submitting an application to the competent customs authorities. in addition, the regulation lays down procedures for customs authorities to act in cases of suspected infringement of intellectual property rights, which will be an important step towards reducing, inter alia, counterfeit and pirated goods. the issue that needs to be considered is the storage and destruction of infringing objects and the associated costs.
in writing. − in the vote on food for infants, young children and special foods in plenary, i voted in favour of adopting the above document. i believe that food products which are intended for this age group require particularly strict standards in their production. as we know, infants and young children are most vulnerable to allergies and diseases, so we should monitor the whole process of food production very closely. the rules currently in force in the member states need to be simplified and harmonised so as not to interfere with the proper functioning of the internal market and to provide for the same level of consumer protection throughout the union. i therefore support the idea that food labels throughout the european union should contain clear and unambiguous lists of nutrients, while also drawing attention to substances such as gluten, lactose and toxic pesticides.
in writing. − the food market in poland and worldwide is undergoing continuous improvement processes. the development of new food production technologies and storage conditions is the basis for the evolution of the world market. every year, the knowledge of healthy eating reaches a wide range of consumers. of particular interest are foods intended for infants and young children. the consumer consciousness of modern mothers demands the production of safe and good quality food. high-quality food is natural, low-processed, from controlled crops and livestock. it is a staple in the diet of infants and young children. all products from which baby food is produced are carefully tested for the content of heavy metals, fertilisers and residues of plant protection products and preservatives. manufacturers of baby food should disclose its composition on the labels. food for special medical purposes is also in high demand. these are complete foods in terms of their vitamin and nutrient content, replacing the whole-day diet. they are given as directed by your doctor. they are intended for use in patients who have difficulty digesting some of the nutrients they contain. food quality and safety are an important element affecting the health of consumers. therefore, the production of safe food should be one of the priorities of the state policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation. i believe that simplification and deregulation of directive 89/389/eec is the right way to approach this issue. the regulation agreed abolishes foods that had no scientific evidence to support a particular need for their inclusion. good examples are the growing-milks for children aged 1-3 years old and the sports food. the new regulation limits the scope to only three types of food that have to be controlled. this recommendation symbolises smart regulation and i am pleased to support it.
in writing. − the original version of directive 2009/39/ec was adopted in 1977, and a revised version was adopted in 2009 to take account of the new committee procedure. over the past 36 years, the food market has changed to such an extent that a review of existing regulations is necessary. it is also necessary to simplify and clarify the provisions relating to them. it is particularly appropriate to abolish the vague concept of 'dietary foods' and to eliminate the differences between the national provisions governing foodstuffs for particular nutritional uses in the member states, which will have a positive impact on the creation of a level playing field. the regulations will facilitate the free movement of foodstuffs for particular nutritional uses in the member states.
in writing. − magnetic resonance imaging (mri) is a highly effective medical diagnostic technique that allows non-invasive detection of disease. although this method is not particularly dangerous for the health of the patient (apart from the possibility of an allergic reaction in case of administration of a shading agent), long-term work with electromagnetic field equipment may have a negative impact on the health of diagnostic centre staff. directive 2004/40/ec introduced very restrictive provisions which limited the scope of the mri method, and therefore, after the intervention of the medical community, the commission decided to postpone the deadline for transposition of the directive from april 2008 to april 2012. in recent years, very stringent control measures and safety training have been introduced in the mri sector, which has minimised the harmful effects of emf exposure on both patients and staff. it is therefore appropriate to exempt the mri sector from the restrictive provisions of the directive, thus maintaining a reasonable compromise between ensuring the safety of workers and the use of scientific and technical progress in diagnosis and treatment.
in writing. − the subject under discussion concerns the minimum health and safety requirements for the exposure of workers to risks arising from physical agents, in view of the particularly negative impact of the transposition of this directive on the use and development of magnetic resonance imaging (mri) techniques. the initially very strict limit values for internal exposure measures laid down in that directive have limited the scope of the mri method, which is essential for the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. i am pleased that the european commission has finally decided to present this proposal, in which it has proposed to exclude from the limit values the internal exposure measures of the mri sector and related activities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 of 18 december 2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. it is not possible to protect cod stocks effectively without long-term planning. if we are to enjoy cod for a long time as fishermen or consumers, we must manage the resources effectively, which are not infinite.
in writing. − maintaining fishing mortality rates at sustainable levels based on scientific advice should allow fish stocks to be rebuilt. it is therefore necessary to harmonise the methods of calculating the input by the member states. it is necessary to take into account scientific advice in order to improve the cod stock plan. the new projects aim to reduce cod catches as well as discards while maintaining sustainable levels of catches of target species.
in writing. − although the cod recovery plan is mainly focused on the north sea and celtic sea, the sustainability of fisheries and the recovery of cod stocks is of great importance for poland and the other member states. a long-term plan to consistently maintain cod fishing mortality rates at levels based on scientific reports should allow the recovery of cod stocks, which are in an alarming state in many fishing areas across the european union. member states should give priority to a sustainable management plan (including the protection of stocks against overfishing) and to the development of tools to eliminate illegal fishing practices.
in writing. - in today's vote i voted in favour of the report by mr iacolino. organised crime, corruption and money laundering are interlinked phenomena, which have increased with globalisation and the development of new technologies, and have a detrimental impact on both the economy and society. the report discusses in a systematic and detailed way the potential ways to combat these negative phenomena, including recommending the creation of a common and uniform legal framework for all eu countries in the area. it also recommends closer police and judicial cooperation at european and international level. i am convinced that the provisions of this document will contribute to the gradual elimination of phenomena such as: human trafficking, the sale of organs, the trade in wild flora and fauna, the smuggling of cigarettes and alcohol, child pornography, the illegal trade in pharmaceutical products or the theft and smuggling of works of art and many others. in this context, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the outcome of her work and express my support for the content of the document.
in writing. − i abstained from voting on this report. i fully support the intentions of this report to prevent many aspects of organised crime, corruption, and money laundering. i agree that globalisation has also spread into crime, and that the issue has to become a concern for the eu. however, this report involves many entities that i cannot support. some of these include: the harmonisation of the criminal law system, right to asylum, proposal on prison sentencing and conditions, and a more complete banking union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr iacolino's mid-term report, which contains important parliamentary initiatives to combat organised crime, a phenomenon not only present in our country but which is, in fact, mainly recorded in various parts of europe. in this sense, the main objective to be pursued in order to combat and counter criminal organisations effectively is to succeed in hitting the economic heart of organised crime, with an increasingly harmonised european legislative system. in this respect, the new technologies at our disposal, together with the joint willingness of the member states to cooperate in this field, are essential ingredients for improving and intensifying what has already been done.
in writing. − the report by mr iacolino on organised crime, corruption and money laundering is, in my view, critical to financial and economic order and to respect for the law and moral and ethical standards. the main reasons for my vote in favour were: strengthening the role of judges and prosecutors, who should receive additional training and exchange good practice internationally (the situation in poland in this area confirms the usefulness of this action), the proposal for a coherent system of sentencing and serving prison sentences in the member states, the call for increased budgetary expenditure on prosecution and punishment. the regulation in question is related to the issue of tax havens recently discussed by the european council. then the president of the european parliament, martin schulz, articulated the enormous losses we all suffer because of tax havens, corruption and money laundering. it is good that these two subjects were discussed almost simultaneously.
in writing. - the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering have recently become a global phenomenon. a similarly powerful response at european level is therefore needed. the ep took the initiative in this area and adopted a report which aimed to formulate a uniform and coherent legal framework. the priority is to promote a public administration with a transparent structure that is more susceptible to corruption. the report also provides for a more efficient and reliable way of functioning of the judiciary. the ep recommends that member states establish effective criminal justice systems that can ensure that the rights of the defence are respected, in accordance with the european charter of fundamental rights. it is also important to ensure greater transparency and cooperation between the banking and professional systems. the ep also recommends self-regulation and transparency for businesses. the main tools in this respect are to be codes of conduct and the introduction of control procedures, such as internal or external auditing and a public register of lobbyists. the report called for a more responsible policy. the ep reminds political parties of the responsibility of nominating candidates and drawing up electoral lists. it also advocates the principle of the loss of the right to vote in elections to the european parliament and the right to serve in the other eu institutions and agencies by persons convicted of money laundering and corruption offences.
in writing. - organized crime has now become a global economic actor disrupting the legal economy. criminal organisations have gradually extended their spheres of influence internationally, taking advantage of the opportunities offered by the opening of the european union's internal borders, as well as by economic globalisation and technological progress, by entering into agreements with criminal groups from other countries. the rapporteur is in favour of the idea of creating more effective european and national rules in the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering, in particular by harmonising the legal framework and enhancing cooperation between the judiciary and the police. it is also important to create a more transparent banking and professional system and adequate measures to combat money laundering.
in writing. - it is good that the ep is dealing with the fight against organised crime and corruption. these pathological phenomena are causing increasing economic and social losses and are increasingly international in nature. they are, unfortunately, increasingly effective at crossing borders. criminal organizations are increasingly active in such areas as public procurement, international transport, waste management, illegal trade in natural resources, and gambling and prostitution. statistics show that the losses incurred on a european scale are in the billions of euros per year. we must fight it decisively and effectively. the european union must take action, not only to respond to the crisis but also to prevent it. we need to prevent criminals from legalising the proceeds of their criminal activities and effectively seize such assets so that crime never pays. i find the idea of creating a european public prosecutor's office, particularly for the prosecution and punishment of cross-border crime, interesting. it would of course need to work with europol, eurojust and the european anti-fraud office (olaf). this would undoubtedly increase the capacity to combat the most serious transnational crimes.
in writing. − the aim of social housing is to provide habitable premises (taking into account the appropriate size, equipment and state of the art) for the poor, homeless or evicted. these facilities are usually provided by the state and granted by a court decision. however, eu countries have different rules on the standard of such housing and different criteria for granting it. it is therefore necessary to define the concept of social housing at european level, to introduce regulations specifying the technical requirements of such premises and determining the low cost of their maintenance. in times of economic crisis, well-managed investments in social housing, and in particular in the construction of such housing, will contribute to the economic recovery of the union countries. the appropriate use of funds (such as the european agricultural fund for rural development for social housing in rural areas) is key. in addition, by designing energy-efficient, low-maintenance buildings using renewable energy sources such as solar or wind energy, member states will contribute to improving the environment and achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - the figures in this report clearly show that the estimated number of european citizens living in social housing is now 25 million. they are distributed unevenly between member states and within each state, with different proportions between urban and rural areas. it is clear that in the context of the current economic crisis, even the eu's public housing sector is making demands and needs are increasing. the increase in the resources allocated to this type of housing is undoubtedly a testament to the commitment of parliament and the european union as a whole and a demonstration of our closeness to all people in need of affordable housing.
in writing. − social housing in the union, in terms of construction, maintenance, accessibility rules, the role of the state, are the key issues in this report. they are set against the backdrop of crisis, cuts and sacrifices, unemployment and the resulting new problems of millions of people in need. i fully supported the amendments tabled by my social democratic group on the advantages of social housing, the call for a framework for joint action and monitoring of social investment, and the criticism of the limitation of state aid for social housing. the proposal to establish a european housing observatory is noteworthy. i wish we had lost by one vote. we need a social inclusion strategy, and affordable housing is critical here, along with access to food, a doctor and transportation. i consider this problem to be particularly important and urgent in poland as one of the elements of the package of solutions needed for the young and the poor.
in writing. - housing should not be treated as a commodity, but rather as a right of every citizen. the market, especially in times of crisis, is unable to meet the housing needs of millions of citizens. 120 million europeans are affected or at risk of poverty, and unemployment is a growing social scourge. in this context, it is not surprising that already in 2010, the proportion of the population in the european union who were homeless was 5.7%, and 17.86% of the population lived in overcrowded or inadequate housing. there is a serious fear that the actual statistics would be even worse. in this context, member states should pursue an active housing policy. one of its elements should be the construction of new social housing for the most disadvantaged. investment in social housing should also be seen as a form of economic stimulus and support for the crisis-hit construction sector. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's climate action plan, including the implementation of the union's climate action plan, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's climate action plan. in view of the above, i have decided to support the report on social housing in the european union.
in writing. − the recent economic slowdown and the current crisis have led to a significant deterioration in the housing situation of the poorest citizens of the european union, especially in large urban areas. appropriate steps should be taken to develop the social housing sector. member states must develop comprehensive strategies for action, taking into account the social conditions and issues in each region. it is necessary to take into account the social groups that are particularly in need of assistance, such as single mothers and homeless people (especially in the winter months). strategies should be developed to facilitate the start of young people who, due to lack of conditions, do not want to decide to start a family. a great idea to support the social construction sector is to reduce the level of taxation of companies in this sector. it also appears necessary to expand the supply of social housing that meets safety and quality standards by bringing existing premises up to the required standards while harmonising those standards in all member states.
in writing. - i support the report by ms licija ronzulli, who is promoting the mobility of women within the european union to enhance their professional skills and improve their education, as guaranteed to citizens by the treaty on european union. promoting occupational mobility is also one of the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to increase employment for women and men aged 20 to 64 to 75%. improving the skills of women by enabling them to move around the eu and to access its labour markets more easily translates into a better functioning eu single labour market and thus contributes to economic and social progress. it should be noted that the economic crisis in the eu has had a very negative impact on the situation on european labour markets. unfortunately, women have been the hardest hit, with unemployment rates as high as 10.7% among them. in the light of the above, i believe that member states should pay particular attention to actively promoting professional mobility among women through local vocational training centres offering language or vocational courses, mutual recognition of diplomas between countries or by simplifying administrative procedures for applying for a job in another country. i am convinced that in the long term such actions will contribute to the effective fight against unemployment among women throughout the union.
in writing. - i want to congratulate licia ronzulla on an extremely interesting report. it is widely recognised that the union will not be able to develop fully unless its citizens are convinced of the need for greater mobility. particularly now, in times of crisis, when we are experiencing such a wide variation in unemployment rates between member states, it is important to seize the opportunities that mobility within the single market creates. the figures cited in the report show that almost twice as many women as men are taking advantage of this opportunity. so it seems that this is the easiest way to increase employment. i voted for mrs ronzulla's report today because i believe that taking action in this direction will allow us to make greater use of the high qualifications of women. the union cannot afford to waste their potential. however, this will not be possible without creating the right conditions, including, above all, the possibility of reconciling family life with working life and convincing men to take on some of the household responsibilities. for example, women's occupational mobility is very strongly dependent on the family model in place, regardless of their country of origin.
in writing. - modern women can be described as "mothers of europe". they have a university education, speak several languages fluently, and are able to balance motherhood with a secular career. yet, the european union still faces a shortage of skilled workers. this situation is linked, among other things, to the low availability of the labour market in european countries. the lack of up-to-date social benefits legislation in the country is another obstacle to worker mobility. this is true in many cases of women who often fear that because of motherhood they will not have a chance to return to the labour market quickly. the availability of labour markets has an impact on the level of education, increases the employment of women, and has a direct impact on gdp. therefore, every effort should be made to eliminate occupational segregation and wage discrimination and to adapt education, training and social benefits systems to the new requirements of the european labour market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i strongly support the mobility of women in the eu. on average, women in the eu have more university degrees than men. more than half of the degrees in the field of healthcare are held by women. there is no logical reason why we should not support these women moving to where there is employment and giving them the help to take their families with them. increased movement of women can only improve our economy and the lives of our citizens. the same is true for gender quotas in politics and business. the more women in management in the future, the better our society and the greater our economic prosperity will be. this is why i voted in favour of paragraph 23.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of educational and occupational mobility of women in the eu (2013/2009(ini)). this legislation will, among other things, emphasise that educational and occupational mobility are recognised as offering added value to the eu and stresses that the economic crisis is making it increasingly necessary to adapt one’s choice of occupation to what is available on the labour market, and that it is increasingly vital for women to be more adaptable to the demands of new career opportunities when changing occupations. furthermore, all citizens have the right to receive a decent level of education and the opportunity to update their knowledge and acquire new skills throughout their working lives. these are objectives which call for shared responsibility between governments, public authorities, employers, social partners and individual citizens. i feel strongly that education and training systems still need to adapt to the needs of the labour market and to an increasingly knowledge-based economy and society. with the further implementation of policies such as this our citizens can become more educated and therefore more adaptable to the ever-changing markets.
madam president! road tolls are a means of obtaining financial revenue for the use of the road network, intended in theory for coverage and for construction, maintenance and renovation. the amount of these fees is often inadequate to the degree and sometimes the quality of the service offered. however, i do not think that extending the charging scheme to other vehicle groups would be in the public interest. the low level of interest in the implementation of electronic charging suggests that it is not economically attractive. the national authorities should not be forced to do so. moreover, it should be the exclusive responsibility of the member states to decide on the use to which the funds thus obtained are put. it is also not reasonable to impose a single charging system. each country has its own transport characteristics and the system it uses should reflect these characteristics. however, for citizens of countries that have not yet introduced any charges, this would represent a completely unjustified cost.
in writing. - i voted against the resolution on the strategy for electronic toll collection and the vignette system for light private vehicles in europe. the proposed changes could lead to a significant increase in the financial costs that eu member states would have to bear in relation to the implementation of the european electronic toll system. they may also lead to a reduction in the revenue from the charges. i believe that the current arrangements, which leave member states free to choose their charging system (toll or vignette), are more reasonable. poland applies a system of tolls based on kilometres driven for all vehicle categories. it cannot be excluded that this system will be changed in the future for certain categories of vehicles. the current system implements the 'user/polluter pays' principle in practice. he is just and impartial. i think it's better than the vignette system. the cost of implementing and operating the changed system is also a problem. member states have different road networks and different geographical conditions. therefore, it is appropriate to allow both tolls and vignette systems to be applied to all vehicle categories. it is not surprising to me, therefore, that the draft resolution states that there is no political will to improve the european electronic toll system.
in writing. − i voted against this report because i cannot support a number of the proposed considerations. the largest setback is that the report pushes too strongly for strict actions to ensure an interoperable european electronic road toll service. force is not the right approach to making member states develop the eets. i believe that the problem lies with the implementation difficulties of the current directive. in addition, i do not agree that the eu should decide how the revenues collected from road charging should be spent. this should be completely up to the member states to decide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of an interoperable european electronic toll service for light private vehicles since we need to come to a playing field for all transport modes. external costs caused by the single modes of transport have to be taken into consideration. a sophisticated toll service for light private vehicles could be a tool to put a price tag on pollution, land use, accidents and noise.
in writing. − i voted against the report on the strategy for the implementation of the european electronic toll service and the vignette system, as i believe that the changes proposed in the report may lead to an increase in the financial burden associated with the adaptation of the infrastructure in the member states to eets unification. the current toll systems are so effective and have taken so long to develop that it seems completely unjustified to change them. moreover, the market itself generates its own needs and the current legal arrangements at union level leave member states free to choose the charging system. while the system of tolls for actual carriage is admittedly fairer, the system of vignette tolls seems to be much easier and much cheaper to maintain, especially for passenger cars.
in writing. − the rapporteur rejected the proposal to further develop the eets project, arguing that the programme has so far had more disadvantages than advantages. to introduce a project that so deeply interferes with the economic zone, with the use of the national road infrastructure, the legislator should first examine the appropriateness of the regulation and refine it, because at the moment the eets charging system introduced by the commission is resulting in protests and complaints about financial losses and discrimination instead of bringing benefits from its operation.
in writing. - unfortunately, i had to vote against the report on the implementation of the european electronic toll service and the vignette system for light private vehicles. the current market-based model for the introduction of eets is appropriate, as it is the market that should decide in what form and to what extent eets will apply and whether its use is considered legitimate by users. the market prefers to use other, simpler and cheaper solutions such as fleet card payments than eets services. the proposed changes could lead to a significant increase in the financial costs that states would have to bear in relation to the implementation of eets, or lead to a reduction in the revenue from the charges, which countries that are still in the phase of intensive road network expansion cannot afford.

mr. chairman, please! the commission's proposal for a directive on annual accounts is the next step in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy to create a sustainable and more business-friendly economy in the union. the project is particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises, which represent over 90% of european companies and which will have greater opportunities for growth and access to finance thanks to simplified conditions for their activities. i also support the commission's proposed system for disclosing payments to the administration, which will provide access to information on revenue flows, and help civil society actors to better account for government administration. the legal solutions proposed in the proposal aim at significant procedural and administrative simplifications, which are expected to reduce the administrative burden by 25% in the coming years and help save around eur 1.5 billion for all companies covered by the directive. it is a good initiative that reduces red tape, introduces uniform legislation and ensures well-established standards in the european area of company law.
mr. chairman, please! competition policy has been part of the european integration process almost from the outset. it is safe to say that without it there would be no union. we must therefore strictly observe the principle of free competition, especially now, in the second wave of the crisis. i fully agree with the rapporteur that competition policy cannot be used to simply strengthen existing businesses but to facilitate the entry of new players. in this context, my great concern is the banking market. the available data show that the ongoing consolidation in this sector has contributed to the increase in market share of several large financial institutions. this is particularly worrying because it was the banking system that caused the crisis to erupt in 2008. the corrective measures taken were intended to ensure that no bank was 'too big to fail' so that society no longer had to pay for the mistakes of private actors. the budgetary crisis in many member states has its origin in the state bailout of the large banks in distress. today, it appears that the measures taken have not worked, and have even led to the creation of even larger financial institutions. so who will pay for their mistakes? the public again?
in writing. to rebuild growth after the crisis, we need to ensure a high level of competitiveness so that entrepreneurs in each member state have equal access to the market. more emphasis should be placed on the development of the electronic market. in particular, we should work towards standardising and simplifying electronic payments. therefore, the elements of the consumer rights directive should be implemented as soon as possible. this includes the elimination of hidden costs for online payments and the prohibition of surcharges for consumers for payments made with bank cards and other means of payment. free and low-cost internet payments can significantly increase e-commerce within the union. according to ecommerce europe, the fastest growing countries in e-commerce are non-eu countries such as ukraine and turkey. moreover, online retail sales of goods and services in europe grew by as much as 19% in 2012. to develop the eu market, we need to remove existing barriers to the market by harmonising the law, which will support small and medium-sized enterprises operating on the internet. a large proportion of these are young people and removing barriers could make a significant contribution to reducing unemployment among this age group. the commission should monitor this market closely, as it is a very dynamic area - as dynamic as the electronic market is developing.
mr. chairman, please! illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is the dark side of fishing. they have a huge impact on the environment, reducing fish stocks and destroying habitats. they also have a serious impact on fisheries, distorting competition, harming the interests of honest fishermen and weakening coastal communities. it is estimated that iuu fishing may represent up to 19% of the world's catches. of course, the european union is working hard to close the legal loopholes that allow illegal operators to profit from iuu fishing. one such action is the report by mr romeva and mr rueda which is being discussed today. in addition, in order to combat iuu fishing effectively, the member states of the european union have been equipped with different tools and procedures. exports and imports from the european union of seafood products approved as legal by the relevant flag and exporting country or a european blacklist covering both iuu vessels and countries that tolerate illegal fishing are tangible examples of such tools. the report by mr romeva and mr rueda is only an adaptation of the lisbon treaty, but even these technical changes contribute to a better fight against this growing phenomenon, which has negative effects on an international scale. the effectiveness of the fight against iuu fishing therefore depends on the wide cooperation and mutual support of all states.

in writing. − i voted against the temporary reintroduction of border control at internal borders, because free movement within the area without internal border control is one of the union's greatest achievements and the temporary reintroduction of border control at internal borders restricts freedom of movement. moreover, migration and the crossing of external borders by a large number of third-country nationals should not be considered as a threat to public policy or internal security. pursuant to recital 5a of regulation (ec) no 562/2006, full freedom of movement within the area without internal border control should be guaranteed and it should be avoided that member states reintroduce internal border controls for political reasons, as reintroducing controls would constitute a serious setback in union legislation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council regulation establishing an evaluation mechanism to verify the application of the schengen acquis. i have mixed feelings about this, though. i understand that the aim is to have an 'effective and reliable monitoring and evaluation system to enforce common principles and to improve, adapt and extend criteria based on the eu acquis', which was accompanied by a reminder that the eu's external borders should be managed effectively and coherently, with shared responsibility, solidarity and practical cooperation. i am glad that the new evaluation system is an eu mechanism. on the other hand, i have the impression that the evaluation mechanism could be used in the future to justify the practical limitation of the schengen acquis. i hope that doesn't happen.
in writing. - the schengen agreement and the privileges it confers are among the european union's greatest achievements. however, free movement sometimes has undesirable consequences, especially when the movement of people adversely affects the internal security of the union and its individual members. the draft standardisation mechanisms for the periodic reintroduction of internal border controls are a step towards properly regulating this issue. however, such mechanisms must be used only in exceptional situations, while maintaining the proportionality of the preventive measures used to the situation in question. the schengen borders code already provides for the possibility for a member state to reintroduce internal border controls in the event of a serious threat to public policy or internal security or during major cultural or sporting events. currently, a member state can resume border controls for a period of 10 days up to a maximum of 2 months. such a decision shall be taken at national level only. the new rules will require a member state to ask the ec to reinstate border controls for a period of up to 6 months, which could be extended by a separate decision for up to 2 years. such a proposal will be assessed by the ec and then approved by the council. commission scrutiny will ensure that these new possibilities for reinstating borders are limited to genuinely exceptional situations. given the rational nature of the schengen reform, i have decided to support it.
in writing. - the benefits of the schengen area are easily recognised by most eu citizens. the creation of the zone also speeds up the transport of goods and the exchange of services, thus facilitating the development of the common market. the schengen area is based on trust; each country trusts that other countries are properly protecting their borders. but the zone is a heterogeneous creation. and since border protection in each country affects all the others, solutions are needed at eu level, not just at interstate level, and a new schengen evaluation mechanism is needed. one important measure the commission has received is the possibility to submit a request for approval by the council for the reinstatement of borders in the event of a serious and long-term neglect of border protection by a member state. restoring borders, even for a short time, would be a difficult task for the population, but it should be stressed that these provisions give the union greater flexibility to act in the event of difficulties. in the long term, this will be beneficial for the stability of the schengen area. restoring border controls is a drastic move, but the very existence of such a possibility will discipline states to better observe border security.
in writing. − the proposal to amend the 2004 transparency directive introduces effective changes within the eu companies and creates the necessary transparency to protect the investors. one of the aspects in the report that i strongly agree with is the country-by-country reporting. it is important to provide the proposed information in the annual report so that the investors have information and are protected. in addition, i also accept the abolition of quarterly reporting. this is a clever idea because companies will be protected from any significant financial burden that might result. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i welcome the report drawn up in the committee on agriculture and rural development on the setting of the correction coefficient for direct payments for 2013. the european parliament cannot accept the arbitrary conclusions of the european council of 7-8 february 2013, which first reduced the overall ceiling of the appropriations for financing direct payments in agriculture and secondly transferred the crisis reserve to heading 2 of the multiannual financial framework. this will lead to a linear annual reduction in direct payments when the reserve is mobilised, at the expense of all farmers. the contingency reserve, given its unpredictable nature, should be outside the scope of the multiannual financial framework. the correction rate for direct payments should be set on the basis of the financial ceiling proposed by the european commission for 2014, which would be in line with the european parliament's negotiating mandate of march 2013. i also welcome the maintenance of the eur 5 000 threshold for direct payments for the application of the financial correction. this will help to protect the interests of smaller agricultural producers and contribute to a more equal distribution of cap resources. for these reasons, i have decided to support the draft report.
in writing. − the european parliament today supported the european commission's proposal to exclude farmers who receive less than €5,000 from direct payments cuts in 2013 as part of the so-called financial discipline. it is also very important that we have managed to maintain the threshold of eur 5 000 and to reduce the rate of reduction of payments from the level of almost 5% proposed by the european commission to less than 0.75%. the financial discipline mechanism was triggered by the european commission when it prepared the 2014 draft eu budget, when it was found that the preliminary estimates of direct payments and expenditure related to market activities exceeded the ceiling established in the 2014 budget year. as a result, the level of direct payments had to be reduced to ensure compliance with this ceiling. on this basis, the commission is presenting a proposal for the establishment of a correction coefficient for the direct payments for calendar year 2013, to be adopted by the european parliament and the council by 30 june 2013. in the absence of agreement between parliament and the council by that date, the commission shall itself set this coefficient on the basis of the relevant provisions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. i am very pleased to see that this report is based on the practical experiences of the member states in the application of the schengen borders code. this gives credibility to this amendment. consequently, i agree with the aims underlined by the report, which are: to strengthen the rules that facilitate, simplify and further develop the free movement within the european schengen area and to support a rigorous framework for control and security at the external borders of the territory of the member states.
in writing. − the free movement of persons within the schengen area is one of the merits of european integration. freedom of movement is a fundamental right enshrined in eu law, and the abolition of internal border controls requires mutual trust between member states in their ability to fully implement the measures necessary to do so. it is necessary to amend the existing rules on the control of persons at the border and to strengthen the policy of integrated border management by improving the rules on the crossing of external borders. the adoption of the amended regulation establishing the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union ensures a further enhancement of the role of the agency in order to develop a policy towards the introduction of the concept of integrated border management.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the commission communication 'towards social investment for growth and cohesion' because it raises many issues that are crucial for the successful implementation of the social investment package and thus for getting back on the growth path and reversing negative social trends, especially the dramatic level of youth unemployment. i would particularly like to stress the importance of building partnerships between education and training institutions and local businesses to ensure high quality apprenticeships and traineeships and to better adapt curricula and training to labour market requirements. i also think it is crucial to introduce incentives for companies that employ young people, to reduce non-wage labour costs and to improve the availability of capital for small and medium-sized enterprises. i believe that creating conditions for social entrepreneurship increases the chances of creating new, sustainable jobs and is an important element in preventing poverty and social exclusion. the possibility for social enterprises to benefit from support under the progress microfinance facility would contribute to the development of this promising sector. while recognising the importance of social investment throughout the lifecycle of citizens, i would like to stress in particular the importance of investing in child development as a key way to increase employment opportunities and prevent marginalisation and poverty. it is worth noting that the potential of sport as a factor in the proper development of children's psycho-physical and social adaptation is still not fully exploited.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? aid to the less developed regions is an effective mechanism for equalising opportunities and enhancing competitiveness. there are regions, such as poland's mazowsze, which, because of the strong economic centre, no longer qualify as the weakest, even though almost all of their area is still characterised by a low level of development. i hope that the commission will take constructive action on this problem. i share the rapporteur's concerns about the proposed geographical coverage ceiling of the new state aid rules. especially in the face of the crisis, state aid to poorer regions is of great importance for increasing their economic potential. the complex political and social situation in many member states is a relevant argument against the introduction of territorial aid restrictions. the aid granted to the companies should also not be conditional on their size, but on their importance for the region, their contribution to its development through investment and the possibility of creating new jobs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the report effectively underlines the obstacles in the draft of the regional state aid guidelines that was drawn up by the european commission. one of the points with which i agree is that the exclusion of large enterprises from the receipt of aid in ‘c’ regions and setting limits in relation to productive investments from ‘a’ regions is not right. the large enterprises employ a large number of people, make a good contribution towards innovation, and create a supply chain with small and medium enterprises. it is not justifiable to restrict them from the aid. in addition, i think that the european commission should rethink the reduction of aid intensity to the poorest eu regions. this action will create an inadequate level of aid to influence decisions on investment location. it will undermine the member states’ ability to draw investment toward the disadvantaged regions.
in writing. - i voted with the ecr group to adopt the report on regional policy as part of the wider state aid programmes. i believe that regional state aid can play an effective role, provided that it is used sparingly and proportionately. it is worth noting several important points in the report: firstly, while state aid should be granted primarily to small and medium-sized enterprises, the exclusion of large enterprises (whose definition includes many family businesses) is not justified, given their contribution to employment, the supply chain they form with small and medium-sized enterprises and their joint commitment to innovation and research and development. the commission's proposals to reduce the intensity of aid for the poorest regions of the eu should be reconsidered, as there is a serious risk that the level of aid proposed by the commission will be insufficient to influence investment location decisions and thus undermine the ability of member states to attract investment to less-favoured regions. the report also highlights the issue of state aid.
in writing. − implementing a cohesion policy that contributes to the european union's competitiveness and to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, and rules on state aid schemes aimed at promoting local and regional investment and public-private partnerships, is essential to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion, regional and local development and job creation, and to help less developed regions to balance their development with that of more developed regions. the legislative package introduces conditions aimed at ensuring the effective implementation and application of eu state aid law in the context of cohesion policy.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? competition is the main driver of the economy. it promotes innovation and development. competition also helps us to achieve better pricing, higher quality products and a more efficient use of human and material resources. competition policy, by maintaining a level playing field, is a guarantee of the development of the single market. despite many attempts to reduce competitiveness in the wake of the crisis, it has proved to be the main stabilizer of the faltering economies of the member states. support for competition policy therefore seems to be the best remedy for difficult times. however, there are still a number of issues requiring urgent action. the lack of a single european market for electronic payments, the unfavourable operating conditions of logistics companies and the lack of transparency in the financial sector are just a few examples. the objectives of the single energy market are still not fully achieved. sound competition must also focus on consumer protection issues. in this respect, it is necessary to ensure the effectiveness of the recovery and redress procedures.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the annual report on competition policy by mr antolín sánchez presedo. i believe that competition is an essential element of a market economy. the financial, economic and social crisis has been going on for five years. in my view, competition is also an essential tool for responding to this crisis and contributing to economic recovery. by promoting efficiency, it contributes to smart and sustainable economic growth across the european union. it also allows member states to correct irregularities in the common market while ensuring high quality goods and services. i believe that we should support efforts to detect anti-competitive behaviour in europe. in summing up my position on the report in question, i would like to express my satisfaction with the outcome of today's vote, and hope that it will make a useful contribution to combating the negative effects of the crisis on the european market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the report successfully highlights the importance of the competition policy and the need for its proposed initiatives. i completely agree that it is a key factor in constant development and a necessary instrument to respond to crises. it encourages companies to pursue success and innovation, which are both essential aspects of growth. without competition, the european union would cease to exist. it is important to improve the current competition policy so that the future looks promising.
in writing. − competition policy is essential to combat the crisis and to support the europe 2020 strategy, the single market and progress towards the banking union, a genuine economic and monetary union and deeper integration and convergence. the annual report should be an instrument to increase the eu's competitiveness, to broaden competition and to open up to new players. the proper functioning of competition policy requires the commission to assess distortions of competition and their impact on the economy and to strengthen competition protection, to introduce state aid control measures and to ensure economic efficiency and the smooth functioning of the market by merging undertakings.

i'm not going to let you get away with this. in the past, preferential access to the european market has not translated into sustainable growth or sufficient integration of the acp group of countries into the world economy. the unilateral trade preferences granted by the european union were inconsistent with the principle of non-discrimination laid down by the world trade organisation. in 2007, it became clear that the negotiations on the conclusion of new comprehensive acp-eu economic partnership agreements would not be completed until the end of this year, when the wto derogation for acps on the trade rules agreed in the cotonou agreement was due to expire. a temporary solution has been found in the form of transitional framework agreements, preliminary economic partnership agreements. this ensured compliance with wto rules by allowing preferential access to the union market while negotiations on comprehensive full epas were still ongoing. of the regional group of central african states, only cameroon concluded a transitional agreement as recently as 2007, but this agreement can only become binding and effective if ratified by the national assembly. that's never happened before. the remaining central african states with the exception of congo and gabon, which have benefited from the generalised system of preferences since 1 january 2008 are the least developed countries with unrestricted duty-free access to the european market under the 'everything but arms' programme. the interim economic partnership agreement is an intermediate step towards deeper regional integration, which can be achieved by concluding a full regional agreement covering the whole of the central african region, not just individual countries. these countries should make political commitments to conclude negotiations on a mutually beneficial agreement, which must also take into account differences between countries and differences in development.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. − madam president, it is not always easy to marry transparency with business opportunity. this directive brings data closer to citizens, while creating a potential for business and growth which we seek in time of crisis. my general approach to re-use was to keep it as open and user-friendly as possible. i stressed two main issues: the format in which public information is made available for re-use, and charges imposed by the public bodies concerned. firstly i insisted that a clear preference was given to machine-readable formats, with other formats possible but exceptional. we also agree that open formats should be promoted, as should the use of electronic means when processing requests for re-use. my second message was to keep charges for re-use as low as possible. one should realise that lower charges for re-use will only attract business and boost innovation, and also bring benefit to the end consumer who would otherwise be charged more for the reused base products and services. i want to thank the rapporteur for putting those things into the report.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? i would like to thank all the members, advisers, organisations and institutions who have been involved in the work on my report. i have to say, the interest in this subject has been very high. although i did not support many of the amendments proposed to the draft report during the work of the development committee, i am glad that the topic of future development goals has attracted, and will continue to attract, so much attention and commitment. the millennium development goals set in 2000 have been met with success in middle-income and developing countries. however, we still have two years to achieve these goals more fully, which have not yet been achieved. the debate on future targets beyond 2015 is necessary and important, but it should not diminish our determination to achieve the targets we have set for ourselves. in the case of development objectives, the european union is only one element in a much wider partnership. it is therefore important to develop and adopt a common and effective and ambitious european union position on the principles and objectives that should be part of the post-2015 development framework. i thank the european commission, and in particular commissioner piebalgs, for working really hard to develop such a common position and for his activity in the un high-level panel, which will of course have even more to say on this matter than we do. our european position will be more forceful if member states fully implement their previous commitments on official development assistance. this may not be the right moment, but i would remind you that to date only four member states have fulfilled their earlier promises. the report recognises that there should be a single, comprehensive and integrated framework with clear benchmarks covering key issues related to sustainable development. the framework should also be universal and global, promoting prosperity, human rights and well-being for all, and defining the direct and active involvement of developing countries in its creation and implementation, but also the role of rich countries. it is also worth emphasising the need to maintain coherence between trade, agriculture and fisheries policies (as we discussed this morning, the epa) and development policies. any shortcomings in the coherence of european policies will always hamper the achievement of development objectives. another important issue is the need to reframe the global partnership for development. this is one of the least well-realized goals of the current development agenda. a renewed and strengthened global partnership for development will be crucial for the implementation of the post-2015 agenda and for ensuring effective accountability mechanisms at all levels. the global goals post-2015 should also include what will be a continuation of the millennium development goals and the sustainable development goals. i think that building two parallel sets, i.e. the development goals and the sustainable development goals, on a global scale would be a mistake. in this parliament we agree that the eradication of poverty, which is the main and treaty objective of eu development cooperation, and the achievement of sustainable social and environmental development should become mandatory priorities on the global agenda. the objectives we will adopt and their effective implementation require respect for the principles of democratic governance and human rights, transparency and accountability of institutions and actors at all levels, and a strong civil society systematically involved in the democratic process. and i'm also convinced that without good governance, we're not going to be able to achieve our primary goal of ending poverty on a sustainable basis, and the positive examples that we've seen around the world have mostly been in countries that have been very good governance. so the fact that this aspect is and will be emphasized is, i think, very important.

in writing. - i supported the report by mrs sirpa pietikäinen on the improvement and detailed re-examination of the eu's state aid rules. council regulation (ec) no 659/1999 aims to improve the way complaints are handled and to obtain information from the market more efficiently, as well as to increase the transparency of the whole procedure. it should be noted that as a result of the implementation of the provisions in question, the complainant will be required to provide information attesting to the validity of the verification and to demonstrate that it is an interested party. only if the above criteria are met will the application be considered as a complaint. the solutions proposed in the document will ensure the enforcement of the law and help to avoid a situation where unduly granted state aid restricts competition in the community.
