in writing. − aviation is a fast-growing sector of the european union's economy, employing up to 5 million citizens. in order to maintain an appropriate level of competitiveness of the sector on the global stage, it is necessary to implement the single european sky (ses) legislation package in all member states with a sufficient degree of speed and to modernise european air traffic management systems (sesar programme). unfortunately, there are significant delays in the implementation of these projects, which generate additional costs for airlines and result in inconvenience for passengers. the european commission should therefore pursue a punitive policy towards countries that do not comply with the recommendations on the functioning of airspace blocks. in addition, the aviation sectors in developing countries (in the asia-pacific, middle east and south america regions) are increasingly competitive with eu aviation. therefore, we need to make rapid progress in this area, including through increasing airport capacity, encouraging investment in aviation infrastructure, and fully implementing mechanisms such as ses and sesar.
in writing. − currently, the most important aviation markets are located outside of europe, for which reason we need to reform the aviation industry within the eu. reforms in policies ensure that our aviation industries stay competitive and up to date. they create important changes to the key sector in the european economy. aviation alone contributes eur 365 billion to european gdp and provides 5.1 million jobs. it is an industry that has to maintain a high level of efficiency to excel among its competition. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the aviation sector in the european union employs 5 million people and generates 2.4% of its gdp. this share could be even higher if the existing regional airports were better used. as the rapporteur rightly pointed out, regional airports that are located on the eastern borders of the eu, including, for example, rzeszów-jasionka in my region of podkarpatie, are an opportunity to increase capacity and further develop this sector. i also welcome the call on the european commission to conclude the ongoing negotiations with neighbouring countries, including, for example, ukraine. reducing congestion at major european hubs and increasing the competitiveness of the eu as a whole depends on the development of existing regional airports and the conclusion of new international agreements. that is why i shall be voting in favour of this report. thank you, sir.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? during the vote i welcomed and accepted the report on the eu's external aviation policy how to meet future challenges . i believe that, given the rapid technological development and demands in both passenger and freight transport, we must bring about rapid progress in european aviation. first of all, we need new, larger airports with increased capacity, because in the near future we may lose our competitiveness to other rapidly developing regions of the world. in addition, new technological solutions that promote both flight safety and efficiency require immediate implementation, such as ses, sesar, easa or gnss. to this end, we should, inter alia, focus on adopting a broader approach in negotiations with both third countries and the international civil aviation agency, as highlighted in the report. i'll have a little extra. we must not allow any further delays in the introduction of the single european sky.
in writing. − i lent my support to ‘the eu’s external aviation policy – addressing future challenges (2012/2299(ini))’. as my colleagues so accurately stated in the report, this is not an easy undertaking but it will provide for the establishment of a brighter future for eu aviation. the importance of this industry to the eu cannot be understated as the present statistics show that aviation ‘contributes eur 365 billion to european gdp and supports 5.1 million jobs’. that being said, it is vital that we make the necessary expansions and changes to accommodate the needs of not only the eu economy but also of passengers that travel worldwide. to do so i support the recommendation made by the rapporteur who stressed the importance of ‘developing and implementing eu mechanisms such as ses, sesar, easa and gnss. these tools, created to support the internal market, will by consequence help the eu in its external aviation policy. the completion of these mechanisms will consolidate the position of the european industry, leaving it stronger to face the new competitive challenges’.
mr. chairman, please! export credits are one of the important mechanisms to support trade, especially in times of crisis. banks, by lending to a foreign buyer, are transferring funds to domestic exporters, thus supporting their own country's economy. it is important that the annual report includes an assessment of the compliance of projects supported by the agencies with international regulations on such loans and with the principles of the union's external action. the proposal to the council and the commission to work together with european diplomacy to develop a methodology for the submission of in-depth reports, the quality of which is currently far too low, is interesting in this context. this should lead to increased transparency in lending. the requirement that oecd countries adopt new rules on export credits and high standards ensuring a level playing field for credit agencies is also welcome.
in writing. - i voted for the report by mrs sousa because i think it is a good document. given that the number of applications for egf support continues to increase and that this year marks the most important final phase of the ex-post evaluation of the functioning of the egf for the years 2007 to 2013, the amount of eur 750 000 for technical assistance seems to me justified. like the rapporteur, i hope that the commission's efforts to introduce an electronic application form and to standardise procedures will contribute to significant simplification and greater availability of the information needed. i also hope that the planned expert group meetings and the seminar for practitioners will help to increase the effectiveness of the projects supported by the egf. i hope that the ex-post evaluation that the commission is planning will help to make the egf more effective in the future and that the support from this fund will add value, be well coordinated with actions taken at national level and contribute to a real improvement in the situation of the workers made redundant and their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the recommendation of mrs evelyn regner on the statute of the european foundation. the institution is active in the fields of scientific research, environmental protection, education, sport and culture. a european foundation that carries out work in more than one country often encounters procedural difficulties (often having to use legal or tax advice) and incurs high costs as a result. however, these funds could be used for more useful purposes than the one mentioned above. the report proposes to introduce minimum standards that are uniform across the union, which will remove many existing barriers, facilitate cross-border activities and facilitate the flow of donations.
in writing. − the statute of the european foundation has been in the works for several years. in the meantime, various concepts and studies have emerged that anticipate the potential benefits and risks of this activity. i think that this form of activity still needs to be improved, which is why i voted against.
in writing. − it is estimated that there are currently over 100 000 public-benefit organisations with foundation status in the european union. almost half of them were created in the last ten years, which shows a lot of momentum in the nonprofit sector. these organisations make a huge contribution to the various aspects of the lives of eu citizens. their activities play a significant role in sectors such as scientific research, culture and the environment. unfortunately, the lack of harmonised rules for their operation is proving to be a formidable barrier to their development. the most problematic issues are the problems of recognition of the foundation's statutes by individual member states, the costs of each registration and the adaptation of the rules of operation to the rules applicable in each country. the proposal to create a statute for a european foundation aims primarily at reducing costs, guaranteeing legal certainty and facilitating the presence of a foundation beyond the borders of a single country through a legal personality recognised at union level. of course, it is difficult to establish a common, uniform definition of public benefit, so we have to be careful about issues such as unified tax breaks. in this context, i believe that the european parliament's proposal to introduce alternative solutions is a step in the right direction and deserves support.
in writing. − the establishment of a fair minimum standard for working and living conditions on board ships has always been supported by parliament. this report effectively highlights the features that the new minimum standards will include for the whole industry and successfully outlines the ways in which they will be enforced. it aims to improve workers’ rights, ship safety, security and environmental protection. consequently, i am pleased to see that one of the many objectives of this report is to emphasise the attractiveness of maritime professions to european citizens. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i supported the report on port state control because it is most appropriate to ratify the maritime labour convention quickly and to reform the current eu legislation. however, the creation of the appropriate legislative framework will certainly not be sufficient. this is partly because we need to employ a sufficient number of specialised and trained inspectors within the eu who are able to assess the living and working conditions of seafarers on board ships.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2009/16/ec on port state control (com(2012)0129 – c7-0081/2012 – 2012/0062(cod)). the shipping industry is of great significance to the eu and should provide within its workings the safety and quality standards to protect the employees of said industry. as a representative from northern poland, the shipping industry is the lifeblood of my city and region. therefore, i view this vote as yet another opportunity to improve the standards which ship employees deserve. while i can understand the burden placed on the member states to accommodate some aspects of the directive, it should be said that while the industry provides economic benefit, this should not be at the expense of the employees. i greatly look forward to the implementation of this directive and will be glad to see the positive outcomes from this piece of legislation as they pertain to the hard-working men and women of the shipping industry.
in writing. − the new system will not only harmonise the existing eu standards for port state control, but also, for the first time, provide a fully coordinated system covering all port state security inspections in the eu. a pan-european coordination and analysis system will allow for a more effective use of port control measures, in particular the identification of high-risk vessels and companies with poor safety performance. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs vilja savisaar-toomasty on the issue of vehicle registration documents. i believe that the changes in the report will make the vehicle registration system in the european union more uniform and transparent. in addition, the exchange of vehicle registration information between member states will be much more efficient due to the storage of data in the electronic national registers. this will avoid the need to register in several member states and will settle the issue of liability for the vehicle. the document will also help to reduce the illegal trade in stolen cars. it is crucial to reduce the number of vehicle documents required and to streamline the record keeping procedure. in addition, the report provides for a change in the form of the registration certificate to a more transparent and universal one. this decision will not only contribute to the more efficient registration of vehicles in the european union, but will also allow for more effective cooperation between member states.
in writing. − the procedures for registering a car bought in another eu country are often very cumbersome, and unclear rules on when and where the vehicle must be registered can effectively discourage movement within the internal market. it is a problem that european union citizens have identified as one of the 20 most common problems in their daily lives. the project aims to identify precisely the country in which a car that frequently crosses borders (e.g. commutes to work in another country) should be registered, and to streamline the vehicle re-registration process. i supported the report because reducing the administrative burden in this area would remove a major obstacle to mobility in the internal market. the road package adopted will harmonise the rules on vehicle testing and thus allow the validity of the technical test to be mutually recognised by all member states. importantly, not only will the burden be reduced for the offices, but also for all those affected, as it will be cheaper and more convenient for people buying cars abroad, students studying abroad and wanting to use their car during their studies, or for car rental companies and those carrying out orders in other member states. it is estimated that simplifying rules and eliminating red tape could save the eu up to €1.5 billion a year.
in writing. − although the number of road accidents has decreased in recent years, the priority objective of further reducing the number of road fatalities by 50% by 2020 remains. this proposal is part of the so-called 'review package', which contains three different reports in total. it aims to strengthen and enforce the rules on roadworthiness testing of motor vehicles to ensure that such vehicles are deregistered until their reliability is proven by a new test, if they pose a danger to road safety.
in writing. − reducing administrative burden is an important issue. being efficient when it comes to interlinking of national electronic registration databases is another task defined in this regulation. i strongly supported both of these improvements facilitated by the european parliament. in order to speed up the negotiation process with the lithuanian presidency i voted in favour of a referral back to the committee.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i voted for the report on vehicle registration documents because it may have the effect of reducing the number of documents that drivers must carry on board a vehicle. it also gives the vehicle owner the possibility of cancelling the registration of the vehicle, thereby relieving the owner of further liability and obliging the member states to mutually recognise the roadworthiness of the vehicle.
in writing. − compared to the current act, this proposal provides for a more precise definition of the place of registration of vehicles and introduces the possibility of withdrawal and cancellation of registration. withdrawal of registration until the roadworthiness test has been carried out with a positive result ensures that vehicles posing a direct threat to road safety are not allowed to enter the road. in order to reduce the administrative burden, a re-entry into the registration process should not be required after the revocation has been lifted. in addition, the original registration of a vehicle that has been re-registered in another member state shall be automatically cancelled. this will avoid parallel registration in different member states. the registration of vehicles which are to be scrapped as a result of the periodic roadworthiness test and of vehicles declared as end-of-life vehicles shall be cancelled following the notification. all of this is contributing to improving road safety, and therefore the safety of all of us, which is why i'm in favor of it. the proposal also sets out new requirements for electronic registration databases, tracking of roadworthiness test results, re-registration and recall of vehicles.
in writing. - road safety is a very important issue for society. vehicles deteriorate with use and time, and road safety declines. i supported the report on roadworthiness tests because the new measures will make it easier to improve road safety. we are currently seeing differences in the way roadworthiness tests are carried out in the different member states. the data indicate that the percentage of vehicles not complying with the roadworthiness requirements may be as high as 63% in some member states. however, there are countries where the percentage is very low. these differences are the result of the different ways in which the law on this matter is enforced in the different member states, which is why harmonisation is so important. it is also important that roadworthiness tests are carried out without discrimination, for example on the basis of the nationality of the driver or the country of registration. the mobility of europeans is important for the union's economy and the internal market, and efficient vehicles are an important element in promoting it.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the report shows the need for the roadworthiness testing and roadside inspection regime to be improved. car-accident related deaths are a problem all over the world. a large number of those accidents occur due to technical problems. this report aims to reduce those types of accidents and i support its proposed strategy.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on roadworthiness tests for commercial vehicles in the eu is one of three proposals in the roadworthiness package. the proposal aims in particular to define common rules for technical roadside inspections (tsi). we know that the reliability of vehicles is one of the causes of the decrease in road accidents, and i therefore believe that the harmonization of control systems for checking the technical condition of commercial vehicles in the period between the periodic technical inspections (ctp) is of fundamental importance.
in writing. − i voted in favor of this regulation because the strengthening and harmonisation of eu legislation on roadworthiness tests and on technical roadside inspections will improve safety on europe’s roads. more than 30 000 people die on europe’s roads every year. i hope that this regulation will reduce this number significantly. i especially welcome the fact that member states are now obliged to carry out a number of technical roadside inspections per year. in order to speed up the negotiation process with the lithuanian presidency, i voted in favour of a referral back to the committee.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i voted in favour of the report on roadworthiness testing of commercial vehicles because it introduces a risk assessment system using the erru register which sets common standards for testing. in the context of cargo security itself, member states will comply with the requirement to check cargo using european standards, but the results of the checks will not be taken into account in the risk assessment system until the rules are harmonised at eu level.
in writing. − technical checks on vehicles are essential for road safety. at least 5 people die every day on europe's roads in accidents caused by technical failures. vice-president siim kallas said: 'driving a car that does not meet the relevant road safety requirements is a danger to the driver as well as to his passengers, who may be his relatives, friends or colleagues.' so this is a very important issue, and i think that's why we need to work on this regulation.
in writing. − the new rules on roadworthiness testing are designed to further improve road safety and ensure a high level of environmental protection. the proposal is important for the construction of a single european transport area, another element of the internal market. i supported the report because setting common eu-wide minimum standards for vehicle testing, while allowing member states to go further and introduce higher standards, is an objective to be supported. the new rules are intended to help halve the number of road deaths by 2020. from the perspective of the internal market and consumer protection, it is important to ensure cross-border competition in the trade of used vehicles, to strengthen measures to combat fraud involving mileage falsification and to address the issue of the exchange of vehicle repair and maintenance data. it is also very important that roadworthiness tests are carried out by independent and qualified experts. with these minimum requirements set out in the report, standards for technical requirements and test methods can be raised, so that we can achieve a high level of road safety.
in writing. − i voted against this report. while i agree with this report’s aim to further enhance road safety, i cannot support the proposed increased intervention by the eu in the standards set in place respectively by the member states’ national governments. i believe that the aforementioned rules should be left to each national government’s discretion.
in writing. − the three proposals in the roadworthiness package present new technical inspection rules to improve road safety while ensuring a high level of environmental protection. at present, the legal framework varies widely from one member state to another, especially as regards road checks, and that is why i believe that there is a need to balance the rules so that they can be applied uniformly throughout europe. the main changes introduced by this proposal are the mandatory checks on motorcycles, scooters and light trailers (up to 3.5 tonnes) and the extension of the mandatory checks to trailers weighing more than 2 tonnes and to caravan trailers weighing more than 750 kg. in addition, it is intended to maintain the minimum threshold of four years for the first technical inspection of cars, followed by a test every two years.
in writing. − when working on such reports, attention should be paid to avoiding excessive interference with national powers in the field of transport policy. in the context of increased road traffic in the eu, it is necessary to strengthen cooperation between member states on the exchange of data on roadworthiness tests of vehicles that they carry out on their territory. as the technical requirements in different countries are not uniform, it is also important to disseminate the best practices of the eu member states in this regard, which will help to reduce the number of road accidents. however, it is important to strike a balance on this difficult issue in order to avoid over-regulation of the transport sector. harmonisation of technical inspections of vehicles should not go beyond what is strictly necessary to ensure road safety and the efficient functioning of the transport market in europe.
in writing. − heavy goods vehicles can be a burden on our society. they not only create congestion, pollution and accidents but they also damage road infrastructure. therefore, i voted in favour of this regulation which enhances road safety and ensures a high level of environmental protection. however, i do not agree with the fact that roadworthiness tests for motorcycles will not be mandatory. in order to speed up the negotiation process with the lithuanian presidency i voted in favour of a referral back to the committee.
in writing. - i think the regulations in this area were sufficient, and that's why i voted against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr richard seeber today because i believe that the european union must strengthen its measures to control chemical pollution of waters. water bodies are very often the outlet for hazardous man-made substances, and the progressive degradation of aquatic ecosystems is a serious threat to life. to avoid this, the rapporteur supports the european commission's proposal to update the list of priority substances in the field of water policy. it covers industrial chemicals, biocides and plant protection products, and for the first time three substances of pharmacological origin. regular inspections by the european commission are also necessary to ensure that water is clean in all eu countries. however, we must not forget that the efforts of governments and ngos (which play a huge role in raising public awareness of the harmful effects of chemicals on aquatic ecosystems) will not be enough if we do not respect and care for the environment ourselves.
in writing. - i'm not entirely convinced of the validity of these regulations. at the same time, i believe that information which is likely to mislead the public should be avoided. maps showing the chemical status of union waters should not suddenly show that surface water is not achieving good chemical status simply because of new, more stringent requirements or the addition of new substances. that's why i abstained.
in writing. − public services are a pillar of the european social model and are important for territorial, economic and social cohesion. since the mid-1990s, the eesc has been calling for a horizontal approach, which was originally intended to be reflected in the protocol annexed to the treaty of nice, which was intended to lay down more balanced rules aimed at increasing the legal certainty of public utilities (psus) in the context of the deepening of the internal market. however, i think that the importance of this subject calls for some further work on it, and i have therefore abstained.
the promotion of sustainable maritime development, maritime transport and tourism is a crucial element in the reconstruction of the european economy. the european union cannot develop properly without taking proper care of the development of the maritime sector. the mistakes of previous years have led to a complete loss of competitiveness with the far eastern countries in the shipbuilding industry, for example. the shrinking shipbuilding industry in the european union is partly the result of the lack of proper regulations to stimulate the industry. the european union, through unsustainable development, focuses on internal competition, accepting legal disparities in individual countries. as a result of this action, in my country, poland, the shipbuilding industry was abolished by an eu directive. this has led to, among other things, a collapse in the labour market, causing emigration on an unprecedented scale. i call on the european commission to carry out a deep reform of the maritime sector, which will allow the shipbuilding industry to recover and improve the competitiveness of the european union.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i voted in favour of the report on blue growth in order to exploit the european union's maritime potential, because i believe that most of the legislation in the eu today concerns road and rail transport, while shipping within the union is still burdened by excessive administrative and customs procedures, and there is a lack of clear guidelines on maritime cabotage and the so-called motorways of the sea. we are thus sending a signal to the european commission that we need a concrete legislative proposal for an intra-community maritime policy.
in writing. − in marine and coastal areas, human and economic activities are increasing, e.g. in offshore wind energy, submarine cables and pipelines, maritime transport, fisheries and aquaculture, but insufficient coordination can lead to competition for space and put pressure on valuable resources. the proposed proposal provides that member states will document these types of activities in maritime spatial plans to make more efficient use of the seas and develop coastal zone management strategies to coordinate actions under the different policy areas that affect activities in coastal zones. as part of the minimum requirements of the proposed directive, member states will have to ensure that their maritime spatial planning and coastal zone management promote sustainable growth, while involving relevant stakeholders and cooperating with neighbouring countries. i think it would be good to work out the details of this activity, which is why i abstained.
in writing. − with some 160 000 cooperative enterprises providing jobs for 5.4 million people and contributing to around 5% of member states' gdp, cooperatives and social enterprises are becoming increasingly important to the eu economy and society. as a model, cooperatives have proved to be able to respond to new market needs and stimulate job creation better than other models, largely due to the way they are managed and decentralised. given these advantages of cooperative enterprises, the current report calls for them to be given greater prominence and attention in eu policy. to achieve this, the report calls on member states to review their legislation on cooperatives, with the ultimate aim of establishing regulations that are favourable to the development of cooperatives in all fields and sectors. the report calls for the creation of a directorate within the enterprise and industry dg focusing on cooperatives and other economic social bodies. in addition, the report calls for more flexibility in the rules for awarding public contracts to employee-managed enterprises, for example by including fixed-term reservations. promoting the role of cooperatives is a way of promoting economic growth, entrepreneurship and innovation in the eu. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. - we often undervalue ready-made ideas that are just waiting to be reused, upgraded or simply remembered. so is the cooperative. even though co-ops have been around forever, they're underappreciated. and this is an innovative idea for an economy in crisis, a traditional model of cooperation that has worked perfectly for years. this form of enterprise adapts flexibly and efficiently to changing economic conditions, encourages entrepreneurship and creativity, creates new jobs and integrates society. democratic governance, common equity and budgetary control make this form of economic activity sustainable and efficient. i would therefore like to see this type of action supported both institutionally and financially.
in writing. − in the current economic crisis, social enterprises represent a huge employment opportunity for millions of people in europe. they reflect the principles of social solidarity and democracy and demonstrate that, if the right legal framework is put in place, citizens can best serve their own interests and those of others. i am very pleased that the report emphasises the role of cooperatives in integrating disabled and disadvantaged people. in the context of the recent draft new european commission regulation on block exemptions (gber), which may have negative effects on disabled people, as the european parliament we need to remind about the social groups particularly at risk of exclusion. cooperatives and other social economy enterprises are the best example of this. that is why i voted for this report. thank you, sir.
in writing. − as the 'socialist' model of a centrally planned economy no longer exists in practice in europe, the crisis of cooperative identity now concerns the disappearance of the differences between cooperative and private enterprises. what does it mean to me that i shop in a cooperative supermarket rather than an international holding company? this is a question that many consumers around the world might ask themselves and the answer would be difficult to find, although, of course, the protagonists of cooperatives in at least some countries might mention ethical business practices in cooperatives, activities aimed at the benefit of the consumer rather than the multiplication of the company's profit, various types of profits for members or regular customers (return on purchases), etc. however, many of these methods could also be used by a number of 'capitalist' companies seeking to attract an audience. the more obvious, though often less clear-cut, answer might come from those employed in a cooperative. and because i'm not convinced that it's right, i voted against it.
in writing. - i supported the report by mr paol bartolozzi on the bioeconomy for europe. the current efforts to develop this sector are the economic future of the community. by promoting innovation and investment, the european market has the potential to become more competitive. the proposed changes are designed to increase production and, as a result, create many jobs. the development of national and regional bioeconomy action plans provides clear prospects for development. the role of the regions and the exchange of knowledge remain particularly important. the funding will be used both for biomaterials research and for training specialists. it is also very important to create appropriate legal instruments to simplify the procedures for implementation and monitoring of the changes. the proposals in the report are clearly conducive to achieving smart and sustainable development in the european union, which will help to strengthen the community's position as a world leader in the bioeconomy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. developing a bioeconomy is an important goal to have within the eu. i agree with the report’s intention to trigger more innovations. they will lead to more efficient mechanisms for sustainable growth and will contribute to the proposed bioeconomy. in addition, more innovation will give us the ability to enhance the competitiveness of the eu’s industry. it is the right step for the eu to take and i am pleased to support it.
in writing. europe will soon face new realities that will seriously challenge our ways of living and working, including the growing world population, increased demand for food and energy, and the scarcity of resources. this is why the european union needs a real strategy for innovation, especially in the field of the bioeconomy. this report, which paves the way for a more innovative, resource-efficient, competitive and, above all, food security and sustainable development society, must be supported. that is why i have followed up my vote in the affirmative.
in writing. - explanation of vote: report on innovation for sustainable growth: the bioeconomy for europe. the human population is growing by millions every year. in europe, despite its low population density, the number of citizens is increasing, which may lead to food and energy shortages. new ways of developing the economy are therefore needed to ensure that production is not increased at the expense of the environment and quality, and that healthy, organic food is widely available. union support for agriculture, the short-chain food supply, and the production and use of biomass can only bring benefits. with european support, it will be possible to develop organic production, a market for healthy food using renewable energy. energy security is one of the most important challenges facing the developing union. year after year, the demand for electricity increases. as an energy importer, poland must develop new forms of production to become independent from its neighbours. over the next 40 years, europe will have to deal with many economic and social challenges. that is why i voted for innovation in this area, so that in the future no one will have to fear hunger.
in writing. − with the world's population continuing to grow, europe has decided to change the course of its economy towards more sustainable use of renewable resources. it will do so by developing new technologies and processes in the bioeconomy, developing markets and competitiveness of bioeconomy sectors, and encouraging closer cooperation between policy-makers and stakeholders. the provision of safe and healthy food and feed, as well as the production of biomaterials, bioenergy and other bio-based products, are the main objectives. such activities will enable us to have a more innovative and low-carbon economy and reconcile the need for sustainable agriculture and fisheries, food security and the sustainable exploitation of renewable biological resources for industry, while protecting biodiversity and the environment, and that is why i am in favour of this.

member of the commission. − madam president, as we all know, continuous and very heavy rains in late may and early june resulted in major floods in several of our member states. austria, germany, the czech and slovak republics, france and, to a somewhat lesser degree, poland, hungary, romania and spain were all affected. in many places, water levels reached the highest marks ever recorded. in some cases, the highest mark on record was reached in 500 years. more than 20 people lost their lives, and hundreds of thousands suffered severe damage to their homes and property. on behalf of the commission, i would like to send heartfelt condolences to the families and friends of the victims, and to express our sympathy and support for the people and authorities of the countries affected. the floods have caused enormous damage, but they have also shown that important lessons have been learned since the 2002 floods. we have seen the evidence that preparedness and prevention pay off. actions taken, including in some cases with financial support from the european structural and cohesion funds, meant that fewer people died and that there was less damage. all affected countries were able to cope with the effects of the floods through national means, in some instances complemented by limited support from neighbouring countries or regions. i was in one of the affected regions of austria – salzburg – last week. there i took part, together with ms mikl-leitner, the minister of the interior for austria, in an eight-country simulation exercise to respond to massive floods and landslides. i heard there, time and again, from the local authorities, the red cross, the army, the firefighters and the water rescue teams that, as a result of concerted efforts over the last years, the level of preparedness of the local population was much higher and the structural protection measures much better in 2013 than in 2002. secondly, the floods have shown once again the high quality of the rescue services in our member states. while the rescuers i spoke to were very modest in taking credit for their heroic efforts, it is very clear that the emergency services played a decisive role in saving lives and limiting damage. professionals and volunteers, civilians, the military and police forces have worked tirelessly to protect their communities. they deserve our highest appreciation and gratitude. thirdly, throughout the crisis the european commission’s emergency response centre (erc) was in constant contact with all affected countries and closely monitored the situation. one key role the centre plays is to be an information hub, and it was the only body which kept a round-the-clock overview of developments across europe for the benefit of everybody. information was regularly shared with all 32 countries that participate in the civil protection mechanism. from the beginning of the floods, the centre issued a daily ‘crisis flash’ on the floods, and my services also provided on-demand, high-resolution satellite images and regular forecasts for the flooded areas and at-risk areas. information is critical, but it has to be there on time. fourthly, now that the waters have largely receded and the long and expensive clean-up begins, the eu’s solidarity fund – established after the 2002 floods – is available to provide assistance to our member states in dealing with the costs of the emergency measures. we in the commission cannot activate the fund on our own initiative, but we stand ready to give any guidance and advice that may be required in preparing an application, and we are actually already doing so. let me finish by stressing once again the importance of prevention in our fight against the adverse effects of floods. europe is regularly hit by severe flooding; climate change only makes this situation worse. as we have seen, in just over 11 years central europe has experienced two once-in-a-hundred-years floods. in the light of this trend, in 2007 the eu adopted the floods directive, a comprehensive framework for the assessment and management of flood risks, including cross-border risks. flood risk management plans are due to be adopted by 2015, and eu structural funds are available to help with the implementation of these plans. as of this year, we have in place a framework for adapting to climate change. together, the member states and european institutions are working to make europe stronger in the face of more frequent and more devastating disasters. it is in this period that we are also are revisiting our civil protection legislation, currently being examined in trilogue negotiations. this new legislation will significantly improve the eu’s collective response capacity. it will also introduce – for the first time – legislative requirements on prevention and on the preparation of risk assessments. i would urge the co-legislators, those here in the parliament and of course in the council, to keep their level of ambition high, but also to do everything possible to reach an agreement without delay. we need it for our citizens.

in writing. - i voted with satisfaction in favour of the political agreement on the multiannual financial framework. the european parliament and its president, martin schulz, have made clear their expectations for the new financial framework, namely: a mid-term review of the budget, flexibility, giving proper priority to those most in need, i.e. the poorest and unemployed young people, and guaranteeing the necessary revenue as early as 2013. i would like to pay tribute to the parliamentary negotiators, especially those representing the s&d group, ivailo kalfina and goran farma. i am not happy with the amount of the budget (€908 billion in payments and €960 billion in commitments), but these amounts could not be radically changed. we have made a significant improvement in the ability to use these very limited resources effectively.

in writing. − the report on the timetable for auctioning greenhouse gas emission allowances was again on the agenda. the draft was referred back to the committee responsible in april and today it returns in almost unchanged form. the rapporteur limited the commission's power to adjust the auction schedule in accordance with article 10 (4) of directive 2003/87/ec to exceptional circumstances only and required that this be done only once during the third eu ets clearing period. the introduction of backloading, i.e. the partial postponement of the auctioning of allowances in order to increase the price of these allowances in later years, is still too drastic an intervention by the european commission in the emission allowance market. i remain of the view that such a temporary restriction on the introduction of new allowances to be auctioned by member states in 2013-2015 will have a negative impact on revenues to the budgets of countries applying for the possibility of allocating free allowances under the derogation, i.e. for poland, which may lose up to eur 1 042 million over the period 2017-2020. i voted against the new report because i believe that it is consistently too invasive and that the level of interference in the emission allowance market by the european commission as presented may destabilise the market and have a negative impact on the economies of many member states, including poland.
in writing. − the re-introduction of the provision allowing the commission to dictate the timetable for changes and other actions in relation to the auctioning of co2 allowances is an attempt to use democratic procedures to take undemocratic, economically important decisions without consulting the member states. as you can see, the commission is determined to do harm to the economies of the most economically weak countries. in the name of what? i say, in the name of the climate dogma, which unjustifiably links climate change to anthropogenic co2 emissions. baseless, because it's based on an unscientific hypothesis. we should move away from the ets because this european system has not passed the practical test and is inconsistent with the kyoto decisions on this issue (e.g. regarding the emission limits imposed by the ec between 2008 and 2012), and also does not take into account all market elements, e.g. the absorption capacity of agriculture and forestry and the profits that these sectors of the economy derive from this trade. the current structure of this trading market is artificial and resembles the medieval trade in indulgences, which, together with the rejection of this practice, led as we know to great historical shocks. the ets is intended to provide a sort of 'leave' for a new 'climate religion'. the report had to be rejected in a decisive manner without a decision being taken by the council.
in writing. − this is one of the most controversial reports, as it deals with a key issue for countries whose energy system is based on hard coal. from my point of view, this is a drive to artificially inflate the price of emissions trading. this solution is not beneficial at all, and is even harmful to poland. i understand the genesis: the root cause of the problem is the reckless political agreement of the state authorities in 2007, and then the situation worsened in 2008, accepting these 6 instruments, among them the emissions trading. the decision-makers were under the illusion that poland would be given the 1990 emission level as a basis, and in practice the 2005 level was set for it. the years 1990-2005 led to the collapse of many mines, smelters and other emitters. it took a lot of effort to make huge changes in the economy that don't matter now. that's what led me to vote against the amendment. i expect that there will be substantial changes before the final vote on the legislative resolution.
in writing. - the voted amendment no 21 and the granting of the rapporteur a mandate to negotiate with the council is de facto a proposal for intervention in the ets market. this is a clear sign of the instability of this market in the european union. the current ets was designed on the basis of market instruments and laws, promoting emission reductions in a low-cost and economically viable way. the european commission's proposal on backloading is a dangerous precedent for the development of a community approach to energy security. artificial co2 price regulation is not an appropriate tool for innovation policy, it negates the basic conditions for the functioning of various industries. europe cannot pursue an isolationist policy and introduce ad hoc legislation. that is why i am strongly opposed to this type of regulation.
in writing. - i voted against matthias groote's report on the one-off intervention in the carbon market. i believe that interfering with this free market mechanism is contrary to the principles on which the european union is based. withdrawing such a large number of allowances will not help to stimulate the european economy in the midst of the global economic crisis, but will rather increase unemployment and slow down economic growth in the future. the emissions trading scheme was designed to gradually reduce carbon emissions by 2020. a sudden reduction in emission allowances will hit those countries that, despite the process of switching to so-called green energy, still rely on coal for their energy. poland is one such country. the reduction of emission allowances will increase electricity prices, which will affect the already overstretched european industry and the pockets of ordinary citizens.
in writing. − once again we voted in favour of changes to the functioning of the european emissions trading system. this fact alone proves that this is a matter of enormous importance, both for the european economy and for efforts to protect the environment and adapt to climate change. but i think we're going in the wrong direction all the time. since the kyoto protocol was implemented, the european union has made significant progress in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the ets has introduced emissions limits that are disproportionate to those imposed on their industrial sectors by other major emitters: china, the us and india. the ets is a model for the functioning of the emissions trading scheme. however, this is an imperfect mechanism which allows us to be satisfied with a superficial reduction in emissions on the one hand, but on the other hand it is not a solution that treats all emitters equally, both geographically and sectorally. moreover, the new countries of central and eastern europe, whose economies are still based on fossil fuels through no fault of their own, bear a disproportionate burden of reducing emissions compared to western european economies. the future solution in this area would probably be to introduce a universal emission tax, applicable to both energy and industry as well as transport. but europe in crisis is not yet ready for this. for these reasons, i have decided to vote against the report.
in writing. − my abstention is a signal that both i and my europa plus group support a progressive energy policy based on the long-term interests of society. instead of blocking eu climate policy indefinitely, poland should consider how it can benefit from its implementation.
in writing. − the commission's proposal on backloading, i.e. the suspension of 900 million co2 emission allowances after 2013, is an attempt to administer a system that was supposed to be a market-based project. the introduction of backloading will raise energy prices in the eu, raise production costs and reduce the competitiveness of european industry in the context of the ongoing economic downturn. the exit from the crisis will be a natural market impulse to increase the price of allowances. that is why in today's vote and in the months of debate that have gone before, i have been clear in my opposition to this proposal. it should be noted, however, that today's decision is not final and does not presuppose that energy prices in europe will automatically increase. the project will now be the subject of debate and negotiation in the council, so it is up to the member states to decide whether and in what form the european commission's proposal will ultimately be adopted.
in writing. - i have expressed my support for the draft law prepared by mr gilles pargneaux on crossborder health threats. in view of the crises of recent years, such as the h1n1 influenza pandemic and the emergence of the e. coli strain, it is worthwhile to ensure that the health of community citizens is better protected. the range of cross-border health threats is very wide and it is therefore necessary to strengthen the system currently in place. it is therefore necessary to extend the means of assessing biological, chemical and environmental hazards. the legal guarantee of equal access to preventive measures in emergency situations is important. in addition, the measures proposed in the report are intended to improve coordination of crisis management measures. the responsibility for improving the existing system lies with the health safety committee. however, member states are required to develop preparedness and response plans for public health emergencies. to make it more effective, cooperation with the european commission, the european parliament, international organisations and third countries is envisaged. the introduction of an early response system will undoubtedly contribute to improving the safety and health protection of european union citizens.
in writing. − the financial transaction tax is an idea widely perceived as an opportunity to raise additional funds to fight the crisis of up to around eur 80 billion per year (eur 30-35 billion if implemented by 11 countries). given the eu's public opinion polls, about 65% of europeans are in favour of such a tax if it helps to fight the crisis. in addition, it should be noted that the financial transaction tax has a formula of so-called enhanced cooperation (realising the increased integration of eu countries based on the provisions of lisbon), i.e. it can only be adopted by countries that express such a will. it is a good thing that in order to protect the real economy, it was decided that the financial transaction tax will not be levied on the day-to-day financial activities of citizens or businesses, such as loans or insurance. the tax will also not be levied on traditional investment banking activities. nevertheless, the issue of the transaction tax is controversial and a source of concern. this is evidenced by the fact that only 11 countries have so far decided to adopt it. its functioning in these countries should be closely monitored for its impact on the competitiveness of the financial sector. past experience has shown that such a tax may have negative consequences for the financial markets of the countries that have adopted it.

in writing. − in view of the immense risk of bankruptcy of the banking sector in the eu and the consequent deterioration of the economic situation in europe, changes are needed in this area. the proposed reform introduces a regulatory framework that reduces the risk of a deepening crisis and increases the security of the community countries and their citizens. the actions of banks (particularly private ones) will be clearer, based on long-term projects, taking into account a wider range of risks (this is due to the fact that they do not always produce a true and fair accounting of their activities, which in a crisis situation affects the average payer). protecting taxpayers, retail customers is one of the reform priorities. banks should not be allowed to take precedence over the public interest. the weakness of the european banking system, which is closely linked to the crisis in europe, confirms the need to create an efficient system for effective financial supervision on the one hand and crisis management on the other. it is important to remember that we must do everything we can to avoid a deepening of the current recession, while at the same time thinking about avoiding further destabilisation of the banking sector. finally, as regards the issue of enhancing fair and sustainable competition, which is a problem today, we can safely say that it is essential to maintain a healthy banking sector and also allows the financing of the real economy through universal access to banking services.
in writing. - there is no doubt that it was risky financial instruments that contributed to the banking crisis. the key question to be asked is whether the taxpayer should bear the cost of such risky operations and to what extent banks can engage in such activities. the european union now faces the great challenge of creating a safe, stable and efficient banking system that meets the needs of the economy. national initiatives in the field of structural reforms require a european framework. they will protect the eu's single market and counter fragmentation, while respecting the diversity of national banking models. in principle, the reform should be based on reducing investment risk, ensuring competitiveness and introducing separate treatment of core activities, including payments, deposits and loans. enabling effective resolution and restructuring and orderly winding-up is also crucial for changing banking culture. the structure of the banking sector should be simplified. this may be done by legally separating certain types of risky financial activities from deposit-taking banks.

mr. chairman, please! first of all, a big thank you and congratulations to both alexandra thein and her colleagues and counter-rapporteurs who have dealt with an extremely complex and difficult subject. on the one hand, we had to deal with the great desire and need to improve the situation of crossborder couples (as we know, there are more and more of them in the european union every year), and on the other hand, it was a question of not interfering with the rules of family law, which remain the responsibility of the member states. so we had two things to reconcile - seemingly - irreconcilable. the rapporteur and the co-rapporteurs, as well as the entire legal affairs committee, have worked with the european commission to produce a draft which i am convinced has met this difficult challenge. on the one hand, we make life easier for eu citizens who enter into crossborder relationships, and on the other hand we protect the member states by not changing the substantive provisions of family law, in particular as regards the maintenance of their own definitions of marriage. nor is it compulsory for the member states of the european union to recognise legal institutions which do not exist in their own country, for example in matters relating to partnerships. i am therefore glad that this compromise has been reached and i am confident that a similar wise compromise will be reached by the member states in the council and that this law will soon come into force.

in writing. – there are approximately 16 million international couples (i.e. couples of different nationalities and/or living abroad) in the eu. in case of divorce, separation or death, these couples are likely to face legal difficulties and extra costs when dividing their property, due to uncertainties over which national laws apply to it. as european integration grows, so does the number of international couples in the eu. commission figures show that about 650 000 international couples apply for separation each year, and this equals 1.3 million people in legal uncertainty over their property. that is the problem we are addressing today, and i therefore strongly welcome the proposals made by the commission, backed by the committee on legal affairs. these proposals seek to give international couples a coherent set of rules that will determine which country’s court is responsible and which law will apply, on the basis of a hierarchy of objective connecting factors. it will also enable them to choose the applicable law for their property regime. equally importantly, it will facilitate the process for recognising and enforcing decisions and court settlements throughout the eu. we ought to ensure that life is made easier for international couples in the eu, and the proposals discussed are one important step in that direction.
