on paper. the proposals of the envi and itre committees for changes to biofuel production are not satisfactory. limiting conventional bio-components to 5.5% or 6.5% will not solve the iluc problem, but will create problems in the european union. a compromise of 7% bio-components in transport fuels was acceptable, although for many meps it was a difficult decision. the amendments proposed to the plenary session effectively limit the share of conventional biofuels to 7,25% by introducing a 2% target for advanced biofuels and 0,75% which could be achieved by using advanced biofuels or renewable energy in electric transport or using hydrogen in transport. achieving a 2.5 per cent share of advanced biofuels by 2020 will be very difficult or even impossible for many countries. therefore, it should be borne in mind that adopting such radical restrictions in the version proposed by the envi or itre committees will be a dead letter in practice and we will all be in trouble. the assumed emission values resulting from the proposed iluc for individual agricultural raw materials based on uncertain data are also seriously questionable. both the discussion so far and the analyses presented by the european commission indicate that there are very large discrepancies in the assessment of emissions caused by iluc factors, which makes this mechanism extremely controversial and unclear.
in writing. decisions to develop the biofuels sector in the european union were intended to help reduce co2 emissions, ensure diversification of energy sources and help farmers by providing them with a steady source of income and the possibility of replacing imported high-protein feed. it has only been a few years since these ideas were put into practice, and none of these goals has yet been achieved. meanwhile, the european commission is proposing changes to the regulations that will hit not only biofuel producers, but farmers first and foremost. the reduction of the threshold for the use of conventional biofuels by half in order to meet the 10% target for the share of energy from renewable sources in transport by 2020 will require a change in the production process and a reduction in the expected production. the funds allocated by producers to reach a sufficient production ceiling have still not been repaid the investment period is still running. moreover, farmers of rapeseed and maize assumed that by 2020 they would be able to base their production on these crops and obtain stable, regular incomes from them. the commission proposal needs to be substantially amended to minimise the impact of such a major policy change in this sector, both for producers and farmers. this can be achieved by, inter alia, introducing provisions guaranteeing continued support for the production of first-generation biofuels until 2020 and establishing appropriate transitional periods.
in writing. the main thrust of the original biofuels regulation was to achieve synergies between two objectives: protecting the environment by using biomass for energy production and promoting innovation and entrepreneurship. while the commission's proposed changes can be considered a legitimate update of eu policies, the envi report leads to an almost complete abandonment of the second objective in favour of the first. first, europe remains a high food security area and the use of some plant material for the production of first generation biofuels remains appropriate. this is all the more so as the waste generated in the production of such biofuels can then be successfully used as a valuable native component of protein feed. secondly, farmers and businesses have already invested heavily in crops and biofuel infrastructure, so any far-reaching change in eu policy priorities threatens to derail their efforts and undermine the reputation of european law in the eyes of citizens. thirdly, i believe that it is entirely appropriate to set intermediate targets to promote the production of second and third generation biofuels from non-consumable materials. this solution not only helps to exploit europe's ecosystem potential in this area, but also primarily drives innovation and entrepreneurship, especially in the small and medium-sized enterprises sector. and that is what europe needs today.
the next item is the joint debate on the report by mr buzek, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on the completion of the internal energy market (com (2012) 0663 - 2013/2005 (ini)) (a7-0262/2013) and the question for oral answer by mrs sartori, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on micro-generation (o-000074/2013) (b7-0217/2013).
the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i would like to congratulate commissioner oettinger and the european commission on the preparation of the communication, which we support in its entirety by a majority vote in the european parliament. i think this debate will not be as stormy and as heated as the biofuel debate because of this huge support. the counter-rapporteurs have worked very hard and i wanted to thank them for their excellent cooperation. the itre commission and the opinion committees have also been very helpful in providing comments and appropriate corrections. because the case is important, too. if we want to get out of the crisis, we have to be competitive, and the competitiveness of the economy depends very much on energy prices. the common market offers opportunities for producers and suppliers of energy to compete and thus to lower prices. at the same time, we must remember that our citizens are waiting for the opportunity to reduce energy prices. finally, this common market also allows us to maintain a stronger position in energy price negotiations with external suppliers. the second issue which is very important in the context of the common market is security of supply. the security of supply is obviously much higher when we can help each other in such a market. the report also stresses that member states will use all the energy sources available on their territory, such as hard coal and brown coal, which are present almost everywhere in europe, using the latest low-carbon technologies. we must do this and we must support the development of technology in the european union. finally, the third benefit is the more optimal use of renewable energy, as well as the implementation of all regulations on energy saving, energy efficiency. what is needed to create this common market? there are five points to consider: first, there must be connections between the countries of the european union (gas pipelines, electricity lines, etc.). member states have committed themselves to do so by 2015. the connecting europe facility provides another opportunity to strengthen this action. uniform network codes should be introduced, including common markets, for retail sales and, in particular, for wholesale sales. this is up to the european agency and the national regulatory authorities. we need to gradually harmonise the ways in which renewable energy is supported and the scope of support for renewable energy if we are to trade renewable energy in the common market. finally, and perhaps the fourth point is the most important, it must be clear to our consumers. they need to be able to choose a manufacturer, an energy supplier, they need to understand the bills. we need to bring the ict sector into this, so that it's just readable to the audience. and of course, as a fifth point, we need to implement eu legislation as soon as possible, especially the third energy package and energy efficiency solutions. without this, there is no possibility of creating a common market and of making it effective. finally, i would like to remind you that since may 2010 we have been implementing the idea that i put forward with jacques delors, which is called the 'european energy community'. it is also thanks to the efforts of the commissioner and the commission, and thanks to the support of the european parliament, that we are in fact on the verge of creating just such a community in the european union. i think the citizens are waiting for some kind of energy supply, possibly cheap energy. the economy is waiting for that, too.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. this is a report which certainly sends some very positive signals, also because of the amendments, the contribution that the conservative group has made to this report. i'd like to draw your attention to a few things. firstly - and this has been mentioned before - we really expect pressure from national and european regulators to eliminate the price mechanisms in the gas market that artificially link the price of gas to the price of oil. this indexation, these price mechanisms are now favouring the giants who simply don't want a customer market in the gas sector. secondly, we want the rules of the third energy package to be applied strictly, particularly to foreign investors. there can be no room for hesitation here. we would also like to see the derogations from the third package which the commission has authorised some investors to apply, critically reviewed after a few years of application. the serious flaw in this report is certainly that we are silent about the role of unconventional gas. this is the biggest factor in changing the energy market and our silence on this subject is making us, parliament, look ridiculous. we as conservatives are totally opposed to the idea of taxing energy consumption in article 27. the next charge from consumers is the worst possible signal we can send to consumers and industry. they are already paying enough for europe's experimentation in energy policy.
rapporteur. − mr president, let me say a few remarks at the end of our discussion. first of all, we do not need new legislation; we should implement the existing legislation. i can only support what my colleague mr turmes said: that we also should work in our own member states. that is absolutely necessary. mr rohde mentioned national capacity mechanisms and remuneration. i agree with him completely that there could be dangers, from some points of view, in the creation of an internal energy market. regarding the indexation of gas prices; of course this should absolutely be stopped, but that is not easy to do. i agree with the commissioner on this issue. perhaps in some cases we could renegotiate our long-term contracts, but not in contradiction with existing law. regarding the free trade agreement with the united states, this is possible only if we can achieve competitive and affordable energy prices. otherwise we will not have much chance. i also agree very much with the commissioner about price regulation on our continent. this should be stopped but of course step by step, so as to take into account vulnerable energy consumers. we could also check our energy market in central europe, in the scandinavian countries and in regional markets. this does work, so let us move things forward. before the european elections next year we can implement much of the legislation mentioned in my report. lastly, i would like to declare my full support for the european commission, and for commissioner oettinger, in the implementation all the rules in the internal energy market.
in writing. is the launching of the energy market in the union for the purpose of harmonising prices and increasing competitiveness, or is it solely for the purpose of ensuring energy security for the citizens of the member states? the creation of a proper european energy market, not just for citizens but also for industry, is a matter for the future, especially as the eu's energy policy is heavily influenced by post-industrial fiction and climate doctrine. i think that the current and fundamental objective of this policy should be to create interconnections between the individual national energy systems, that is, to build energy security for citizens. the question that needs to be answered is whether energy policy in the common market makes sense in isolation from industrial policy and, consequently, whether the current economic misery of the union could not be overcome by a better customs policy for energy fuels. the root cause of mass unemployment in the union and destructive industrial relocation is linked to the wto-imposed free trade principle, which in practice promotes unfair competition and social and environmental dumping, and this also affects the shape of the energy sector. i note that the main objective of the internal energy market - i.e. energy security for my country, poland, but also for several other member states - requires support for coal mining and coal-fired power. in launching the internal energy market, we must not only be concerned with security but also with the re-establishment of the competitiveness of our part of europe on the global market.
in writing. - i thank president buzko for his very good report and congratulate him on the support of all the political groups. the european commission has calculated that since 2005, energy prices in the european union have increased by 37%, while in the us they have fallen by 5% in the same period. this not only has a negative impact on consumers, but also makes it harder for european companies to compete on the world market. completing the energy common market and implementing the third energy package is needed to ensure security of supply, to better negotiate with external partners, and to bring down prices and make more efficient use of environmentally friendly energy sources. the report by president buzek stresses the need to develop own resources and to exploit the full potential of unconventional energy sources, which will help protect our consumers and businesses and increase competitiveness on the global market.
in writing. the european commission has reviewed the actions already taken and those needed in the near future to achieve the european council's objective of completing the internal energy market by 2014 and eliminating energy islands by 2015 by developing the necessary energy infrastructure in the eu. the report by jerzy buzek continues the path towards ensuring the supply of energy from local sources. the key to the creation of a common market is to focus on cross-border interconnections, the need to modernise and develop energy infrastructure between member states and national energy networks, the consistent application of the internal energy market rules, including the third energy package, to eu and third-country operators operating on the eu market, and the inclusion in future actions of the solution to the problem of disruption of electricity networks caused by unplanned flows of energy from renewable sources. the strong support expressed at the eu summit on 22 may, where member states confirmed their readiness to create a common energy market by the end of 2014, leaves us with a lot of work to do in terms of implementing previously adopted rules and arrangements, but also new investments.
in writing. i thank the rapporteur for his report on the crucial issue of the completion of the internal energy market. i am glad that we are supporting activities which do not go against the trend of using only renewable energy sources. we are thinking of the interests of individual member states, which could decide for themselves how to produce and process energy and use their own energy resources, such as natural resources, to increase the eu's competitiveness on the world market. support for the metal and mining industries is also an important issue. i support projects that are also crucial for poland, and do not exclude energy produced from coal. therefore, the individual rather than the uniform and unified approach to the diverse national realities presented in the report is satisfactory. this report also touched on the important issue of consumer protection, welfare and promotion. competitive supply and lower energy costs, taking into account the decline in wholesale energy prices, are key issues. the consumer has the right to information and choice. it is therefore important to take account of the regulation of energy prices on the market.
mr. chairman, please! equal pay for women and men is a fiction. women on average earn less than men because they work in lower-paid sectors of the economy, but they also earn less in the same jobs, and the higher the position, the greater the disparity. this is often hidden by a differentiation of designations that allows men to be paid more: a woman is a cleaner and a man is a specialist in maintaining order. lower wages mean lower living standards, especially in old age. 21% of women over 65 are at risk of poverty, compared with 16% of men. the elimination of the gender pay gap is a component and a factor of equal opportunities. we call on the commission to take decisive action, as the current directive is ineffective. europeans want to close the pay gap effectively, so it is crucial that parliament's recommendations are implemented. of course, improving existing legislation will not solve anything. there is a need for a broad education of the public, especially employers.
mr. chairman, please! the german press reported on the horrific scenes of the removal of four children from their parents in darmstadt. a few months earlier, in berlin, 15 german policemen had snatched a polish mother's six-week-old son from her arms. similar dramatic events are occurring more and more frequently in various european countries. the cruel practice of taking children away from their families is becoming more and more common. i strongly object to such cruelty. the trauma of a child being forcibly snatched from his parents' arms remains for life. the cruel practice of taking children away from their frightened mothers is recorded in the memories of victims of nazi german concentration camps during the war. let the modern european states not follow in their footsteps. only the violence of both parents justifies the taking of children. in other cases, the state should help the family, not destroy it.
mr. chairman, please! on 4 september 2013, the 50th anniversary of the death of robert schuman, a distinguished french politician who is now rightly regarded as one of the founding fathers of a united europe, was marked. he based his political thought on christian values, which led to the creation of the european community institutions. the implementation of his project was the embodiment of the aspirations of millions of europeans who dreamed of a europe that was safe, free and united. these principles were set out and put into practice by robert schuman in a difficult period for europe after the end of the greatest war in history, which cost the lives of many millions of people. it was a europe that was very divided, both politically and economically. today, 50 years after the death of this great visionary and democrat, many european nations are implementing and deepening his principles. also those countries which, because of geopolitical divisions, found themselves on the other side of the iron curtain after the second world war.
in writing. - the report we debate tonight assesses the current results of cohesion policy measures targeted at energy efficiency. energy efficiency is an increasingly important part of the cohesion policy, especially in the forthcoming programming period. however, in the current period, the effectiveness of energy efficiency projects under cohesion policy has been minimum and we should consider how to avoid such failure in the future. so much needs to be done in order to improve absorption rates and the subsequent implementation of funded projects. this is especially true as these projects are crucial for households and local communities. i welcome many of the report’s recommendations on how to solve these problems in the upcoming programming period. these recommendations will hopefully bring some clarity to how improve the compatibility of intertwined european, national and regional cohesion policy objectives with the energy efficiency goal. i am grateful to the rapporteur for her support to my position in this respect, and i hope this political cooperation between our two political groups will continue in future activities of our committee.
mr. chairman, please! for the first time in history, we are tackling the issue of mortgage regulation at european level. mortgage lending, as has been rightly said, is a very specific type of financial service of high social importance, due to its size and liabilities and its duration, and there is no doubt that the lack of regulation in this area is a kind of neglect at european level. the objective of this directive is to create a responsible, efficient, effective and competitive european mortgage credit market. the financial crisis has shown how damaging irresponsible credit policies can be for a large part of our societies. the directive on credit agreements relating to residential immovable property imposes obligations and more stringent requirements not only on creditors and credit intermediaries but also on borrowers themselves. first of all, it sets new standards for the reliability, accuracy and transparency of information. the solution developed by the econ committee is particularly noteworthy, as is the guarantee to the consumer of an adequate reflection period, i.e. the right to withdraw from the credit agreement within 7 days, and the prohibition of tying, as well as the right to early repayment, which seems to be particularly important. i also find the new solution - which i also sought in my amendments - in the area of foreign exchange loans, which will make it easier for people to earn in a currency other than the currency of the country in which they live, to be useful. a loan in the currency in which remuneration is received shall not be treated as a foreign currency loan. therefore, they will not be subject to stricter creditworthiness requirements in such a situation. this is a great advantage for the growing number of citizens, including my own, who live in border areas and earn in euro. it is also a real boost to the single market, as it will encourage the mobility of workers and at the same time facilitate transactions in euro, including in countries with a temporary derogation on the euro. i congratulate the rapporteur and all the co-rapporteurs on the smooth and efficient way in which this document was put to the vote. the mechanisms in the directive to combat abuses and unfair incentives will hopefully make us more effective in preventing housing market crises.

in writing. – i have lent my support to the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and on the right to communicate upon arrest (com(2011)0326 – c7-0157/2011 – 2011/0154(cod)). this directive would, among other things, lay down the main principle that every suspect or accused person should be given the right of access to a lawyer as soon as possible and in a manner that allows them to exercise their defense rights effectively. it also specifies that in any event these rights should be granted before the start of any questioning, upon carrying out any procedural or evidence gathering act and in case of deprivation of liberty. the proposal further identifies the content of the right, stresses that meetings between the suspect or accused person and the lawyer should be confidential, lists the derogations allowed to the general principles and provides for rules in case of waiver of the right to a lawyer. all persons should have the right to a fair trial when accused of a crime and that begins with legal assistance therefore this directive is paramount to uphold the democratic and free society that this union has rendered.

in writing. - i support the report by mr buzek on the completion of the internal energy market. the creation of a common energy market will be based largely on the rational exploitation of energy resources, which will enable consumers to pay less for energy and make the european union's economy more competitive. the market should be more transparent and any obstacles to competitiveness should be removed so that consumers can play a greater role in its creation. as the energy market is constantly changing, the european union must engage in new technologies such as smart grids, energy storage and clean coal technologies. i believe that the creation of an internal energy market would have a positive impact on the quality of life of the citizens of the european union and would provide better conditions for both producers and final consumers of energy, and that new energy technologies would contribute to improving the environment.
in writing. − the launch of the internal energy market is a step both towards europe's energy security and towards the integration of the continent. the current lack of systemic regulation causes problems with competition in the market, often resulting in excessively high prices or poor quality of services. so the decoupling of gas and oil prices is a success because these are the mechanisms used by the big companies that monopolize the market and avoid a flexible market. i hope that this report will attract investment that will make it possible to achieve its objectives. this is also important from an economic point of view, because cheaper energy is an opportunity to generate economic growth and new jobs. a good sign is the concern for consumers and their commitment to local alternative energy sources.
in writing. − i voted for and support mr buzekʼs report. if you take an energy map of europe and look at it in detail, you will see an interesting fact. for energy at least, the berlin wall did not fall in 1989. here east and west europe still exist: west europe with dense energy networks, east europe where all major pipelines go one way. it is a union where the west has a large number of gas suppliers while 12 member states have only one significant supplier. mr buzekʼs report is clear: only the completion of the internal energy market can truly unite europe. a fully connected europe, based on solidarity, is vital not only to our economy, but also to our energy security and social welfare. for this to work, we need infrastructure and political will. for infrastructure: we now have the cef and the ten-e. we have the plans. now is the time to build. to build a single physical european energy infrastructure that will remove the barriers left by a divided history. for political will: we need a new european energy community as the report says. we need a new spirit of cooperation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which i consider important because of the impetus it gives to the internal energy market, a crucial instrument for meeting the challenges of an increasingly expanding market which has until now been dominated by certain non-european competitors. it is important to harness the leverage of renewable energy, and to make the internal energy market effective by 2014, as planned. the prospect of approaching this market sector with a european and therefore common approach should encourage the commission and the council to accelerate this process and to continue the progress already made in this direction.
in writing. - energy and transmission networks, including cross-border ones, are one of the keys to economic success. the rapporteur drew attention to the fact that the launch of the internal energy market would bring many benefits, including, in particular, increased security of energy supply, lower energy costs for consumers and industry, and help to build a more sustainable economy. the report devotes a great deal of attention to renewable energy sources and energy efficiency. these issues are important not only from the point of view of environmental protection but also from the point of view of the need for diversification of energy sources and the aforementioned security of energy supply. what 's the matter ? however, it should be borne in mind that consumers should be at the centre of energy policy and that the most vulnerable should be protected so that they can all have access to the energy they need to function normally.

in writing. - i support the report by mrs esther de lange on more efficient and cost-effective interpretation services in the european parliament. the principle of multilingualism is the basis of the european parliament's work, and therefore, in order to enable each member of the european parliament to use the official language of his or her choice, the use of interpretation services is essential. however, the budget allocated to these services should be used to the best possible extent, while maintaining the highest standards. to this end, the number of late cancellations of interpretation contracts should be significantly reduced. the appropriations for the purchase of software to facilitate the management of translation services should also be increased. in conclusion, i would like to emphasise that improving the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of interpreting in the european parliament would bring many benefits to members of the european parliament and would greatly relieve the budget of the european union.
in writing. – i voted in favor of pursuing ‘resource-efficient full multilingualism’. millions were spent on late cancellations of interpretation services, a problem which could be solved by the implementation of a penalty clause. members’ language profiles should be updated every year to ensure efficiency as well.
in writing. the multilingualism of the european parliament guarantees the possibility for members to express themselves in their own official language and to ensure transparency towards all european citizens who can thus exercise their right of democratic control over the activities of the european parliament. however, there is a need to reduce the burden of the complex machine of multilingualism without compromising the high level of translation. i believe that mrs de lange's report takes the right approach to the interpretation service, taking into account both the need to rationalize costs and, at the same time, the need to make the service more efficient, thanks to a more careful management of resources, which can be fully shared in the context of the crisis we are going through.
in writing. - the alternative proposal proposed by the s&d group, which was eventually adopted, stressed the need to maintain multilingualism in order to maintain the transparency of the european parliament's activities so that every citizen could, for example, listen to debates in plenary sessions in his or her mother tongue. it is worth noting that when working in the european parliament, we often encounter highly specialised, technical texts. it is not easy to work with such texts in every area of the ep's work if they are not in the person's mother tongue. the rapporteur placed a strong emphasis on the availability of translation services for internal users, i.e. members and ep staff. in my view, and in the opinion of my group, it is the final recipient, the citizen, who must have access to the live debates and be able to hear them in his own language, especially since it is the only directly elected eu institution.
in writing. within the multilingual european community, community law in general force requires expression in each of the official languages, so that every citizen can have access to documents in his or her own language. this is a prerequisite for understanding and applying established law. in practice, the translation services appointed by the european commission are responsible for implementing the current language regime. they have a variety of tools to help them do their job better, and they are constantly being improved. that is why i am in favour of developing this area, which is a priority in the context of the eu's functioning.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? gambling is a specific sector of economic activity where consumer protection often remains highly unsatisfactory. some countries have adopted regulations that significantly restrict gambling services. however, online offers differ from traditional ones in that they can be used virtually freely by citizens throughout the community. a high level of consumer protection is therefore crucial in this respect. restricting access to minors is just one aspect. a well-functioning internal market cannot remain indifferent to these issues either, and must regulate them in accordance with community law. a more coherent policy should therefore be pursued within the european union in order to take account of the cross-border nature of gambling services, in particular with regard to the offending states. the fight against crime in the field of gambling services, which often extends to sports competitions, is a matter for close cooperation between all countries.
in writing. - i would like to say that i support the ashley fox report on online gambling in the internal market. the project, for which i was an expert on behalf of the legal affairs committee, aims to combat illegal online gambling services and to regulate them in order to protect consumers, especially young users. i would like to draw particular attention to the need for better cooperation in the gambling sector, both at community level and between the relevant competent institutions in the member states. at the same time, i would like to stress the principle of subsidiarity and the right of member states to control their own markets. i also consider it important that the member states cooperate in the fight against money laundering and the manipulation of sports results, including organised crime, which threatens the integrity of sport in the european union. i believe that the definitions of offences and criminal sanctions should be harmonised in order to be able to combat illegal sports betting and match-fixing more effectively. national bodies should be established to ensure coordination and exchange of information in this field. i also propose to use the french model, which allows for the financing of sport, social and charitable purposes and cultural works from a part of the income of the gambling industry, obtained from the right to organise sports betting.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs ashley fox on online gambling in the internal market. the document proposes, inter alia, the introduction of appropriate preventive measures, including verification systems, preventing players from creating an unlimited number of accounts and providing false personal data, educational programmes for young people to raise awareness of the risks associated with gambling, and restricting the advertising of gambling services or prohibiting the provision of misleading information about the probability of winning. it also focuses on combating money laundering and the fixing of sporting results by criminal organisations. the report proposed a variety of measures to prevent money from illegal sources from being traded. attention was also drawn to the need for specific support and protection of athletes and their associates against corruption in order to prevent the manipulation of sporting events. the report proposed by the honourable member deals with important issues which are of the utmost relevance in an age of rapidly progressing computerisation. the significantly easier access to gambling services not only increases the likelihood of more players taking up gambling, but may also result in an increase in the percentage of people who are addicted. i believe that the changes proposed in the rapporteur's report will prevent economic losses in the member states, but above all possible health problems for their citizens.
in writing. − the online gambling sector is a special sector because, on the one hand, it is a market activity if it offers fair and legal services, and on the other hand, it often has social costs and harmful effects. that is why it is so important to ensure a high level of protection of consumers in this sector, and in particular of the most vulnerable, such as minors. the report highlights the importance of this issue and calls for action to be taken to better protect consumers using gambling services. that's why i supported the report. it should also be stressed that it is for the member states to decide how to organise and regulate gambling services in accordance with their own values and general interest objectives, and that any action at union level must therefore respect the principle of subsidiarity. however, it is important to pay attention to the problems that arise in the context of online gambling, such as organised crime, gambling addiction, money laundering. it is crucial to make consumers aware of these risks and the legislation governing online gambling advertising, which cannot give the impression that gambling is a method of improving an individual's financial situation, is an important issue. a self-exclusion register would also be a useful solution. the register will allow consumers to opt out automatically of all licensed gambling operators. it is equally important to use age and identity verification mechanisms to protect minors.
in writing. europe is the largest online gambling market and one of the fastest growing online businesses. with almost 7 million users, the revenues of companies will increase to 13 billion euros by 2015. the size and specificity of this market means that its regulation and supervision must be effective and go hand in hand with social issues, in order to protect consumers and avoid fraud and match-fixing. with the rapid development of technology, online gambling is now available not only on computers but also via mobile phones and television. however, individual eu countries cannot, on their own, provide the high level of protection against the risks of unregulated gambling that every eu citizen deserves. in view of this, i want to support a coherent policy for online gambling in the european union, respecting the laws of e-monopoly. a comprehensive european gambling solution should contribute to licensing gambling and make it more attractive, discouraging consumers from using unregulated offers.
in writing. - thank you to the rapporteur for presenting your position on online gambling. the negative effects of gambling are well-known, and it often contributes not only to addiction but also to organized crime, sports betting, and money laundering. online gambling also involves greater risk because it is more easily accessible. i am therefore pleased that measures are being taken to control and restrict access, especially for minors and those at particular risk, to this type of activity. in the fight against crime and tax fraud, it is also important to ensure that any restrictions are not discriminatory. the key issue is that each member state has the right to define rules in the internal market to protect players, while respecting the principles of union law. the fight against corruption and the fixing of sports results were also discussed. the exchange of information between sporting bodies, both national and european, is essential to help combat suspicious and criminal activity. the positive aspects of lotteries, such as the financial resources that are donated for public and social purposes, have not been forgotten.

the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? i would like to start by thanking my colleagues for their input and commitment to the report. i would like to thank the two co-rapporteurs in particular for their constructive discussions and comments. despite the efforts of the european commission and the european parliament, and despite the many policy initiatives and actions taken since the beginning of this year, there has been no significant improvement in the statistics relating to youth unemployment. while some countries have managed to contain the general rise in unemployment, the situation among young people remains dramatic, particularly in countries such as greece, spain, portugal and italy. so today i would like to draw attention once again to the actions that must be taken in the near future. first, the implementation of the youth guarantee. before the holidays, a new group of graduates has entered the labour market, and they are likely to join the ranks of the unemployed youth. the guarantees are a solution that will not leave jobseekers without support. it will enable the unemployed person to obtain additional training or appropriate vocational guidance. i would like to stress here the justified need to extend the guarantee to persons under 30 years of age, particularly as this was not a requirement in the berlin declaration made after the meeting of the european union's labour ministers in july this year. there is an urgent need for employment promotion measures to support small and medium-sized enterprises to create new jobs and to employ young people. we need to focus on supporting young people through age-specific programmes, career guidance, promoting entrepreneurship and helping them to start their own businesses. i am a great believer in the creativity of europe's young people, but we need a system of tax breaks and administrative relief for self-employment. in addition to initiatives aimed at creating new jobs, we need a proper redistribution of labour, which is still available on the market. this requires a specific involvement of national employment services and the promotion of the eures portal. we should support those who are willing to move in search of work, both within their country of origin and outside it, within the european union. among the long-term actions that need to be taken to make the traineeship system work is to accelerate work on the quality framework for traineeships. that is what i am calling on the european commission to do today. the traineeship should be a genuine educational contribution to the young person's portfolio and not a form of exploitation. work performed during the traineeship should be adequately remunerated. the issue of neet involvement is also a pressing one and requires coordinated action between both the education sector (in the context of early leavers) and the employment services. they are the ones who, through a counselling system and an individual approach, can help the most vulnerable to social exclusion. another very important aspect of the long-term action is the reform of education systems to increase the amount of practical skills and vocational training that people entering the labour market should acquire during the training cycle. in conclusion, i would like to stress that the cooperation of all the actors involved, in particular educational establishments, employers, local authorities and youth organisations, is essential for the effective implementation of the recommended actions. youth organisations should be seen as a reliable partner for discussing solutions to remove barriers to young people entering the labour market.

the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? unfortunately, i cannot agree with the green group's statement that my report is a step backwards from the green group's report, which was prepared in 2009. it analyses the factors that exacerbate or maintain the difficult situation of young people in the labour market and indicates the direction of the further action to be taken by the member states to curb the rise in unemployment. i cannot agree with the statement that the plight of young people is due solely to the current economic crisis. we can't forget that this is a structural problem. the increase in jobs depends on the overall state of the economy and an environment that is friendly to entrepreneurs, because they are the ones who create jobs. the actions under the youth guarantee are intended to help young people adapt to the current situation on an ad hoc basis and to provide them with an alternative when it is not possible for them to take up work at that time. i agree with part of what mr romeva and mr rueda, from the green group, said about the need to adapt the education system to the needs of the labour market. i therefore urge the green group to support my report, because most of the points you have mentioned today and which you have put down in your alternative resolution are in my report. i think that the european parliament should be united on this issue in order to send a clear and strong signal. it's time we put words in place of deeds.
in writing the crisis that has gripped the world since 2008 has hit young people particularly hard. according to statistics, one in four young people in europe cannot find a job! the most visible consequence of this is not only the impoverishment of young people but also uncontrolled migration for the sake of earning a living. and it is the present generation of young people that is the future of any country. young people are characterised by a lack of experience and, consequently, by a reduced attractiveness for employers. some of them take advantage of the labour market situation to recruit young graduates for unpaid traineeships or offer so-called 'junk' contracts. in such a situation, the union has a duty to respond and member states should make use of all the possibilities available at this level to develop and co-finance initiatives aimed, inter alia, at adapting education and training systems to changing labour market conditions. in this respect, the report by mrs skrzylewska deserves the attention and support of parliament.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. in the youth debate, it is worth considering the introduction of market mechanisms that would reduce the public spending on training young people in skills that are less needed on the labour market, and thus promote the courses that are currently sought after by employers and in demand. i think we should now pay attention to vocational training and make young people aware of the situation on the labour market already in secondary schools. in addition, universities should pay attention to training qualified professionals from the outset, and provide and promote attractive internships with potential employers, so that young people have the opportunity to try their hand at a chosen profession immediately after graduation. it is therefore necessary to modernise education and to adapt curricula to current and future market needs. i would like to conclude by stressing that only the synchronised action of governments, local authorities, the european institutions and the various agencies can bring the expected results and allow us to look to the future with optimism.
in writing. the crisis has intensified negative trends that have been contributing to the labour market problems of young people for some time. on the one hand, competition from older and more experienced workers, and on the other, the lack of support in the form of traineeships and vocational training to enable young people to gain such important first experiences. high youth unemployment is not only an underutilization of human potential, but also a decline in consumption and low levels of investment. i believe that simply providing additional financial resources will not be enough, we need the most comprehensive approach possible. to make the impact of these 8 billion more effective, we need to improve the public support infrastructure for the young unemployed, and build modern institutions that are responsive to the dynamic changes in the labour market. the fight against youth unemployment will not bring about lasting change unless we involve the private sector in the process. we must encourage entrepreneurs to create jobs and support the work of ngos. i support the rapporteur's proposals in this respect. an effective incentive system should include, for example, tax breaks, reimbursement of social security costs and preferences in access to european funding.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. i would like to begin by thanking mrs isabella very warmly for her very good and balanced report and for the whole process of negotiation and her involvement. in the light of the conservation of eel species, two important arguments made in the report are worth mentioning. firstly, the rapporteur points out that the quantity and quality of scientific research is insufficient and that these studies do not provide a clear answer to the question of what are the causes of the decline in the eel population. secondly, as a result of a malfunctioning coding system, the eels reported by individual countries do not correspond to the data contained in eurostat statistics or published by eurostat. the reporting errors raise serious problems for the whole area of quotas and their reporting in the context of the assessment of the state of marine resources. as a result, missing or incorrect data become the basis for fisheries management. i must refer to the commission's present decision on the baltic sea, which increases the fishing quotas for pelagic species, thus extending the catches for fishmeal. this will lead to the destruction of the baltic's biological system and the destruction of small-scale fisheries. already the thriving cod is on the verge of collapse. i therefore call on the commission to reform the reporting of catches in particular.
in writing. in view of the ever-decreasing stock of european eel, the protection of eels and the promotion of their reproductive succession is a very important element for the sustainability of the fisheries sector. it is important to introduce legal rules providing for sanctions for those eu countries which do not provide the data necessary for the evaluation of eel stocks. this is a problem that affects many regions of the eu, including the warmia and mazury region, which i have the honour to represent. it's a very specialized subject, and there are many elements to make things better. the main reasons for the decline in eel populations are commercial and economic catches and artificial barriers to the natural migration routes of fish. it should be noted that the apparent improvement will not be achieved by overfishing, since it only allows local stocking and does not give global effects or further reproduction of this species. the only way forward is to ban the european eel and to find solutions by removing artificial barriers in the rivers. it is justified to designate streams and associated bodies of standing water where eels have a chance to migrate and homing naturally in order to protect them and to introduce a total ban on fishing for eels. therefore, as a first step, all open waters and the coastal zone should be subject to a prohibition of fishing.

the instruments for making the internal market more attractive and competitive. in this report, the european parliament rightly emphasises the objective of simplifying procedures and creating conditions favourable to entrepreneurs. the customs union is an essential element of the single market and only properly implemented, coherent rules will allow that market to function properly and to electronic data exchange between customs authorities and businesses. this will avoid duplication of procedures which could have a negative impact on the costs of doing business in europe. derogations easier for entrepreneurs, but also ensure uniform controls at a high level. another worthy demand is the introduction of provisions on the status of authorised economic operator in the amended regulation. this will allow sound entrepreneurs to make the most of the simplification and will also encourage them to comply with the letter of the law. in conclusion, i think it is worth noting that in her report the rapporteur not only focused on the alignment of the rules with the lisbon treaty and the necessary modernisation of customs legislation, but also treated the customs union as an instrument which is essential for the competitiveness of the internal market. there is no doubt that in the long term, simplification for businesses will have a positive impact on economic growth in the european union.
madam president! the single european market should ensure consistency in the regulation of intra-community trade. a significant part of this is the customs legislation, the harmonisation and modernisation of which will help to increase the union's competitiveness vis-à-vis other markets and economic growth. i am in favour of simplifying customs regulations so that traders do not have to repeat procedures related to their trading activities. a single electronic system in all countries will reduce the cost of doing business significantly. it should therefore have a positive impact on the prices of products, which are always in the interest of consumers to be reduced. the status of the favoured undertakings should be clearly specified in order to allow them to benefit from a wide range of facilities. valuable business time would also be saved by standardising the temporary storage declarations. the current requirement to submit the relevant declarations twice is often unnecessary and only prolongs the procedures. documents must be clear and precise so as not to give rise to difficulties of interpretation.
mr president, mr president of the commission! we are even arguing today about the state of the european union in the fifth and, hopefully, last year of a crisis that - it is true - did not start in europe, but has also painfully affected our continent. unlike many speakers, both on the left and on the far right of this chamber, i believe that the eu institutions have been able to respond properly to the challenges posed by the crisis. the latest example of this was the very clever compromise on the multiannual eu budget, which for many regions in europe, especially those in the throes of a serious crisis, will be the only source of funds for public investment and thus for growth and jobs. mr barroso, the crisis has also seen a rise in xenophobic sentiment, with calls to restrict the key eu freedom of movement of people within the single european market, with the right to choose where to live and work legally. i hope and expect, mr president barroso, that the european commission will continue to defend this fundamental right against the populist ideas that appear here and there, not only in public debate, not only in parliamentary debate, but also in the statements - and this is very worrying - of many members of the governments of the member states. the third thing i would like to draw attention to is our eastern neighbourhood. despite the internal economic troubles, despite the political fatigue of the enlargement of the european union, we cannot turn our backs on our eastern neighbours. especially now that these countries are under enormous political pressure from russia. i therefore appeal to you, mr president barroso, and to the lithuanian presidency, represented here by the foreign minister, not to waste the opportunity of the eastern partnership summit in vilnius to sign and immediately, even provisionally, implement an association agreement with ukraine and to start a similar process with the other eastern partnership countries. this is a chance for a historic shift in our new eastern neighborhood that we cannot afford to lose.
in writing. data coming in from the european economy show that the worst of the crisis is behind us. however, the economic recovery is very weak and does not translate into an improvement in the labour market. most analysts agree that the modest economic growth we are seeing in the next few years will not create many jobs. we must also remember that the ones that are created are usually temporary and low-cost. the eu therefore needs a new industrial policy. the recovery efforts of recent years have focused primarily on reducing public expenditure. the situation on the labour market shows very clearly that these measures were perhaps not wrong, but certainly too one-sided. they need to be complemented by initiatives to support job creation, which should be geared towards attracting industrial investment to europe. we must not deceive ourselves that new or green technologies will not create jobs for all europeans. we should look to the united states, which is becoming more and more effective in persuading entrepreneurs to invest in america. this was of course influenced by lower labour costs and lower energy prices, but it was also supported by the active attitude of local authorities at all levels. it seems that europe should follow the same path to improve the labour market situation.
in writing. there is a broad consensus in the european parliament that the main problem facing the european union today is unemployment, and in particular youth unemployment. it's good that the eu is trying to reduce unemployment. but let us not forget that neither the state nor international organisations - in general - create jobs. we should therefore focus on creating conditions for those who will in turn create sustainable jobs. we can help entrepreneurs create wealth, but we can't try to replace them. we believe that the european socioeconomic model is the best in the world. and that's probably true in reality, but we have to remember that this model is not a perfect being. it must be continuously improved and improved, and above all, it must be supported by the economy, which is the real and irreplaceable fuel for the european model. without a healthy european economy, the european model cannot and will not function properly.
in writing. with regard to the message from president barroso, it should be stressed that the state of the eu is currently difficult to define clearly, as a result of europe's high dependence on the global situation. the union institutions in the field of banking supervision are still lacking in clarity. the single market is undoubtedly the union's greatest asset, but it is still incomplete, with, among other things, a continuing lack of a community market for services and a slow pace of development of the banking union. economic governance in europe is often reduced to manual controls and there is a lack of system solutions. the food security of our continent is satisfactory, but european farmers have too little income; we have fewer and fewer young people willing to take over farms; we are losing out to food imports. our outer activities are still too small and disorganized. the president did not address the results of the recently created european external action service. however, it can be assumed that much remains to be done in this area. there was also no broader reference to the issue of the reduction of the eu's multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020, which for the first time in history will have a budgetary cut. how do these budget cuts relate to croatia's adoption of the europe 2020 strategy, which sets out ambitious plans for us? how do we close the huge development gaps between member states, regions or simply between the living standards of eu citizens?
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr françois alfonsi on the protection of endangered european languages and the preservation of linguistic diversity throughout the european union. the document provides for action to be taken to ensure the protection of endangered european languages. the actions presented in the report are to focus on, inter alia, funding language protection programmes, combating discrimination on the grounds of language and ethnic minority, promoting multilingualism and ensuring language sustainability by encouraging children to learn an endangered language as their mother tongue. the current legal framework does not sufficiently address the issue of language protection. this is one of the reasons for their disappearance, which in turn leads to the disappearance of entire language areas. i believe that clarifying the issue of endangered languages will translate into preserving them and thus preserving linguistic and cultural diversity, which is one of the principles of the european union.
in writing. - linguistic diversity, alongside cultural and religious diversity, is one of the fundamental principles of the functioning of the european union, enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. it is part of the heritage of the member state concerned and its survival must be encouraged, as it leads to the development of local communities and the building of regional identity. unfortunately, more and more languages are in danger of extinction, often a language that is recognized as a minority language in one country and an official language in another. their users are decreasing, they are not developing, they are not adapting to new ways of using language and modern communication channels, there is a lack of materials to teach them, and their users eventually lose all motivation to use them regularly. and yet, the survival of a language is the survival of the community that speaks it. therefore, we should take appropriate steps to protect endangered languages. the european institutions should develop programmes to help preserve endangered languages using financial support instruments. the teaching of these languages should be disseminated using modern technologies (digitisation of texts and recordings, their online availability) and all eu member states should sign and ratify the european charter for regional or minority languages and the framework convention for the protection of national minorities. unfortunately, there are still countries in the eu where even languages that are not endangered are discriminated against and not accepted, as exemplified by the situation of the polish national minority in lithuania.
in writing. − i voted in favour of protecting endangered languages within the eu member states. pro-active measures will lead to greater use of language across all levels of society. even though the initiative might require additional financial commitments, i believe that it is important to implement increased usage of endangered languages in all aspects of daily life.
in writing. - i would like to thank the rapporteur for referring to the issue of endangered european languages and linguistic diversity in the eu member states. the protection and promotion of minority languages, which are a sign of multiculturalism and diversity, is an important asset. these languages also have the same value and are an undeniable historical, social and cultural heritage. language is a way of identifying oneself, which is why it is so important to focus on promoting and protecting endangered languages. i am pleased that efforts are being made to combat prejudice and discrimination on the basis of language and those that do not aim at language uniformity. support at the pre-school, school and out-of-school education levels, such as the family, where the child acquires natural language skills, is also a key initiative. promoting the learning of endangered languages plays an important role in the cultural heritage of the communities themselves and of europe as a whole. the promotion of languages also contributes to the development of tolerance towards different ethnic or linguistic groups and has a positive impact not only on the cultural but also on the economic and social dimensions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report which seeks to correct an anomaly by which parliament does not possess the formal legal right to require candidates for the post of european environmental agency (eea) executive director to attend a hearing before the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. i support the proposal to insert formally the requirement for a hearing in the eeaʼs founding regulation, in order to align the eea with the procedures in the european chemicals agency, the european medicines agency and the european food safety agency. i support any move towards greater accountability for the eu agencies, and parliamentary hearings provide a rare opportunity to apply some scrutiny to these bodies.
in writing. − i voted for the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund for areas affected by flooding in autumn 2012, specifically slovenia, croatia, and austria. the commissionʼs proposal to provide assistance is in line with the regulation, and i support the use of the solidarity fund to provide aid based on estimates of total damage. my heart goes out to all those individuals who lost their homes during this natural disaster.
in writing. − draft amending budget no 5/2013, which is part of a package of proposals for amending the 2013 budget approved today and for which i am rapporteur, together with mr fernandes, concerns the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund, amounting to eur 14.6 million, following the disasters caused by the heavy rains and floods that hit slovenia, croatia and austria in autumn 2012. this is one of many examples of the importance of solidarity in europe and of the closeness of the community, including in terms of aid and economic support for the victims and those affected by these natural disasters.
in writing. - the report by mrs la via was put to the vote along with mr fernandez's report. they gave the go-ahead for the european union solidarity fund, which has been in existence since 2002, to support regions affected by disasters, in order to help, in this case, slovenia, croatia and austria to deal with the effects of last year's floods. the biggest success is that the €14.6 million allocated to these three countries will come from new funds and will not be covered at the expense of other policy priorities.
in writing. - i voted against the legislative resolution adopted by the parliament. the document would essentially limit the share of agricultural bio-based components from 10% to 6%, with the remaining 4% to be made up of 2,5% advanced biofuels and 1,5% biofuels from other renewable sources. i believe that the adoption by the council of the european parliament's resolution in its present form would significantly undermine legal stability, which would not only result in a loss of confidence on the part of producer groups or investors, but would also contribute to a reduction in employment in the sector. the production of biofuels from biocomponents is mainly undertaken by small companies, for whom a radical change in the production profile to advanced fuels may prove too difficult. it should be borne in mind that the changes proposed by the european parliament could have an impact on all sectors of the economy, including the eventual reduction of global production. i question the fact that the new assumptions are based on an unreliable and untested iluc (indirect land-use change) factor. especially because it uses uncertain data and a complicated methodology, and so it gives different results in each institution. in view of the arguments put forward, i believe that the document under discussion can be improved during the second reading to the extent that it ultimately reflects the interests not only of poland but also of the european union as a whole.
(s&d), in writing. - the european parliament adopted a controversial climate and energy package in the previous term, but life has shown that we were wrong. i think that the present report should be seen as the beginning of a move away from a package which is ill-conceived and harmful to the eu economy. first generation biofuels - bioethanol added to petrol, biodiesel (methyl ester) - which were supposed to replace at least 10% of the energy contained in fuels, have been shown to increase total co2 emissions. i don't think we can replace 10% of traditional fuels by 2020 and achieve a 6% reduction in co2 emissions. this is because the production of bioethanol does not take into account the co2 emissions during fermentation and the agricultural by-products, and the fact that dehydrated spirits contain less energy than petrol and need to be used twice as much, which leads to an increase in the fuel consumption of petrol engines, which means an increase in co2 emissions. methyl bio-esters, on the other hand, also contain about 20% less energy than regular petroleum. to get the right engine power, we'll increase fuel consumption and co2 and particulate matter emissions. although polish investors will lose economically because they have already complied with the previous regulations, i support this report. i do this because i hope that the other elements of the climate and energy package will also be changed accordingly. otherwise, the losses will be catastrophic.
in writing. - parliament adopted the wrong draft based on the wrong assumptions put forward by the european commission. the target for biofuels in final energy consumption in transport was set five years ago. it cannot be changed when the entrepreneurs, on the basis of the law adopted, are in the process of implementing investments, including many co-financed by union funds, including those that were conditional on the sustainability of the project. such behaviour undermines trust in the law and institutions of the european union. that is why i have opposed the commission's amendments from the outset. i hope that the second reading will remove the main flaws in this draft which could lead to the disintegration of the entire biofuels sector in europe.
in writing. − i support an eu biofuels policy which prevents the unintended promotion of polluting biofuels as well as the distortion of crop prices on a global level that encourages poverty. from my point of view, we should ensure appropriate market penetration of innovative and less harming biofuels that do not compete for land needed to grow crops. however, i would like to underline that the voting was only to amend the proposal but not on the legislative resolution.
in writing. − for 10 years, the european parliament has actively promoted the production of biofuels from oilseeds. the funds allocated to this purpose have had a real impact on the development of agriculture in many countries and the creation of thousands of new jobs. second generation biofuels, from organic plants or waste, are not yet produced on an industrial scale and therefore cannot be an alternative to first generation biofuels in the near future. the new regulations will reduce the competitiveness of biofuel companies operating on the european market compared to those operating in south america, for example, and the limits on food-based biofuels will have a negative impact on the whole sector. moreover, it is very likely that the funds allocated to research and development of new technologies in the biofuels industry will be reduced in the new perspective. given that the share of biofuels used in transport should be 10% on 1 january 2020, the european union should continue to actively promote the production of biofuels. unfortunately, the directive adopted will significantly reduce the volume of production of crops such as rapeseed and palm oil, which will result in the elimination of many jobs.
in writing. − i thank the rapporteur for the proposals on the quality of petrol and diesel and the promotion of renewable energy. in view of the eu's policy to promote renewable energy sources, it is gratifying to see that the biofuels industry is also having not only positive but also negative effects, for example on the food industry. biofuel production cannot compete for agricultural uses with the food and feed markets. the eu should support projects that benefit citizens, not harm them. as an opponent of co2 caps, i believe that sustainable action should be taken and that the good and interests of all member states should be taken into account.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposed solutions to restore the european eel stock. the eel population is now on the brink of extinction. the factors contributing to such a drastic decline include overfishing, climate change, significant pollution of water, and the construction of new dams and dikes that prevent eels from migrating freely. the protection of this species is therefore particularly important, also because of the lack of an effective method of reproduction in captivity. parliament decided to require member states to monitor eel rescue more closely than in previous years. if they fail to meet this criterion, countries will be subject to severe fishing sanctions. i believe that the measures taken by the members of parliament will contribute significantly to the increase in the number of eels in our waters.
in writing. − i voted in favour of amending existing regulations in an effort to tackle the long-term problem of declining eel stocks across the european union. the compromises contained in the report adopted by the committee recognise the importance of scientific study, community consultation, and impact assessments. i am in favour of working with the commission on ways to improve eel stock recovery, as this will address falling stock levels, the challenges facing the industry, and the importance of protecting rural industries and traditions.
in writing. - a customs union is one of the key aspects of a well-functioning internal market. without modern and common rules and systems that are applied consistently, the single market cannot function properly. i supported the report because it makes the necessary changes and brings the eu customs rules into line with the procedural requirements of the lisbon treaty and other changes in eu legislation. it should be stressed that the rules adopted today introduce changes that are beneficial for operators, as they simplify procedures while maintaining due diligence in controls. i would mention here the institution of the aeo, which has been in operation since 2008. once granted aeo status by the customs authorities, traders can benefit from the facilities related to customs controls on safety and security as well as from the simplifications provided for in the customs legislation. the adopted report enhances the importance of aeo status to enable credible, compliant operators to benefit to the maximum extent from a wide range of simplifications. this would mean, inter alia, that any criteria for the use of the business-related simplifications by an aeo should not be re-checked, which would be a significant facilitation for companies. i also believe that the key issue is the uniform implementation and application of the union customs code in all member states, so as to make the best use of electronic techniques.
in writing. − i voted in favour of proposed adjustments to the union customs code. the text states that the commission should ensure transparent consultation, well in advance, when preparing and drawing up delegated acts, of the member statesʼ experts and the business community. the adjustment to the code involves authorised economic operators (aeo), centralised clearance, use of electronic systems, rules of origin, and temporary storage. my group voted in favour of the outcome of the trialogue in committee, and the amended text was adopted by imco unanimously.
in writing. - in the era of the reform of the common agricultural policy, from which we want a fair, competitive and efficient cap, we cannot forget about modern solutions that will help achieve the other objectives of a transparent, simple and functional policy, a modern policy adapted to the needs of today's europe, to modern ways of obtaining information, practical for a new generation of farmers. to achieve these goals, we need the right tools. one such tool is the farm accountancy data network (fadn), which helps to determine the incomes and analyse the activities of a representative part of farms and which covers some 80 000 farms in 27 member states. it was established in 1965 and is the database on which the current economic and structural situation of eu agriculture is based. the proposal we are voting on introduces certain amendments to the fadn regulation, bringing it into line with the current legislative framework and calling for regular updates and modernisation of the network's website. this will make it much easier to access, faster to retrieve information, and more accurate and reliable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the amendment of food safety directives on coffee, chocolate, certain specified sugars, jams and preserved milks. the adopted report by the committee on the environment, approved unanimously in the committee, strictly limits the delegation of powers, ensuring that annexes relating to descriptions, definitions or names of products are considered as essential elements and can only be changed by way of the ordinary legislative procedure. the final text limits the commission’s powers to technical updates only, and the ordinary legislative procedure will apply where annexes relating to products’ names, definitions and characteristics are to be amended.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs maria gabriel on the agreements concluded between the european union and the republic of cape verde. the first of these guarantees a number of facilitations for the short-stay visa for both citizens of the republic and eu citizens. they may count, inter alia, on simplification of procedures for issuing multiple-entry visas, exemption from visa fees for some of their nationals and free extension of visas for those nationals of both countries who, for reasons beyond their control, are unable to leave the territory of the union or the republic of cape verde within the specified deadline. the readmission agreement also deals with the procedures applicable to eu and cape verdean citizens staying illegally in their respective territories. the parties agree to take back returned illegal immigrants and their families. i am confident that these arrangements will facilitate the movement of persons and intensify contacts between citizens of the union and the republic of cape verde.
