in writing. the situation of young people in the labour market is very difficult at present. the unemployment rate for this group is twice that of the general population, at 23%. this means that there are now more than 5.5 million young people unemployed across the european union. this long-term situation inevitably leads to social exclusion. to prevent this, action to combat youth unemployment must be coordinated with the overall anti-crisis response in the economy. the adoption by the epsco council of the youth guarantee is an important political impetus. these guarantees consist in providing young people with employment, further education, apprenticeship or traineeship. in the resolution adopted today, we decided to expand the circle of beneficiaries of this support by raising the age limit to 30 years. the priority now is to implement programmes and projects to make the most of the 6 billion euro allocated by the council. we also need initiatives in the eu to support entrepreneurship and promote self-employment. all activities aimed at developing entrepreneurship and self-initiative, and encouraging entrepreneurs to create new jobs, should be continued and supported. we therefore decided that the idea of promoting self-employment and facilitating access to start-up funding should be continued in the 2014-2020 programme for change and innovation.
in writing. − the unemployment rate among eu citizens under 25 is now already 23% or around 5.5 million people. uncertainty about tomorrow discourages young people from deciding to start a family and encourages the development of a demographic bottom-up. moreover, the lack of experience and education of young people is not in line with the requirements of the modern job market. the education system should therefore be reformed and a system of individual vocational guidance should be established, which is already available at secondary school level and based on the needs of the labour market. , the old professions and agriculture must also be restored. it should be possible to establish links between schools and workplaces by introducing training and traineeships. the lack of job opportunities condemns young people to social exclusion. the number of early school leavers is increasing. today, an estimated 14 million young people are not in school or in the workforce. particular attention should be paid to the low-educated, the disabled and ethnic minorities, whose chances of employment are even more precarious. the development and investment in international education programmes, such as erasmus plus, where the largest share of funding will be allocated to studies, international placements, training and volunteering, is also of great importance. it is also essential to maintain high standards of graduate and traineeship practice and to ensure that it is effective and practical in preparing for a specific job.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur for her report on the fight against youth unemployment. the solutions to a common problem seem to be appropriate. member states have seen an increase in unemployment, particularly among young people, for whom there is often a lack of jobs. europe needs to take appropriate and concrete action in times of crisis. the state has an important role to play in supporting its citizens by creating new jobs, encouraging self-employment and the creation of enterprises, and supporting education and training centres, thus ensuring the smooth functioning and increased productivity of employment sectors. it is gratifying to note that young people who leave school early are not forgotten when they are offered career counselling. the aim is to reduce the gap between men and women in the labour market. there is no doubt that there is a real need to modernise education systems, which often fail to meet the requirements of the labour market. the key is to adapt to the ever-changing environment. it also stressed the need to improve the quality of and facilitate access to vocational and higher education. we must act now and invest in young people, who are the future not only of our countries but of the union as a whole.
in writing. - the report adopted today is an important signal to the member states, who are responsible for the correct implementation of one of the most important directives of recent years - the services directive. the services sector is crucial to the eu economy, as it generates over 65% of the eu's gdp. the directive allows european entrepreneurs to expand their activities to other member states' markets, which is also an important incentive to start new companies. i regret that despite the existence of a mechanism with such great potential, member states have still not implemented it properly. in times of economic difficulties, difficulties in the labour market, we cannot allow the opportunity to enter the path of development and to create new jobs to be missed. i therefore fully support the report, as it points to key problems in the implementation of this law. the key is to adopt an integrated approach to implementation. the services directive does not operate in a vacuum and, even if fully implemented, can only function properly if other related provisions, such as the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications, are also fully implemented. citizens have a right to know that they are paying the price for member states' slow or inadequate implementation of eu rules. it is therefore necessary to increase transparency so that citizens, for example through national parliaments, can hold member states accountable for the state of implementation.
in writing. − the services sector generates over 65% of the eu's gdp, and also provides digital and mobile services that are changing the way the economy works. it is therefore important to start exploiting the full potential that lies within it, especially now, with rising unemployment. the commission's study on the economic impact of the services directive shows that if member states were more committed to its implementation, the overall economic benefit could be three times higher, i.e. 2,6% of gdp. the main problems are cumbersome legal form, territorial constraints, economic needs tests that hinder the operation of a business abroad, and in the case of the provision of online services, it is often difficult for consumers to purchase a product from another member state, leading to higher prices and less choice. the weak link between the services directive and other national or eu legislation also hinders job creation. the internal market information system (imi) and the solvit system would be helpful in reducing administrative formalities. the full and consistent implementation of the services directive is primarily the responsibility of the member states. this is why it is so important to work together so that countries that have successfully reformed the services sector can provide support and advice to those that are still facing this challenge.
in writing. - thank you to the rapporteur for reporting on the important subject of the internal market in services. the sector accounts for more than half (65%) of the union's gdp and is therefore a very important part of the economy. it is therefore gratifying to see that action is being taken to improve the social dimension of the legislative environment. the creation of stable jobs, where the right to equal pay, decent working conditions and workers' rights are fully respected in all member states, plays an important role. the key issue is to abandon practices such as discrimination, red tape and restrictions that only contribute to rising unemployment and a slowing economy. easier market access for smes and self-employed people also provides an opportunity to create stable jobs, foster innovation or improve competitiveness, thus contributing to a sustainable market economy. the governance of the internal market in services should also aim to improve the flow of services so as not to create internal constraints hindering cooperation and flows between eu countries. clear rules and increased accountability are the way to improve the market.

in writing. − in today's vote i supported the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2012. according to article 2 of the ep decision establishing the institution of the european ombudsman, the role of the ombudsman is to contribute to the detection of maladministration in the activities of the union institutions and bodies and to make recommendations with a view to putting an end to it. mr nikiforos diamandouros served two terms in office and made a significant contribution to raising standards of respect for civil rights. in this capacity, he organised information campaigns, focused on promotion and transparency of the activities of officials of the eu institutions, which was reflected in, among other things, a guide for officials on the application of good practices. the activities that led to the creation of the office of ombudsman in turkey are also noteworthy. thanks in part to the support of mr nikiforos diamandouros, the office has been functioning since march 2013. i would like to express my appreciation for the work of mr nikiforos diamandouros and, on the occasion of his departure, my best wishes for his future career.
in writing. − i voted for the proposed amendment to the visa regulation concerning third countries. following a ‘discriminatoryʼ visa requirement from a third country, the commission would have a two-year period in which to try and persuade the third country to give up this requirement. at the end of this period, if the third country has not changed its position, the commission will automatically issue a delegated act to reintroduce temporarily a visa requirement for citizens from that third country visiting the eu. in addition, if the eu grants visa-free travel to citizens from third countries, this can now be temporarily suspended when serious problems occur, such as a sudden influx of people from those countries overstaying their visa-free period.
in writing. − the eu's principles of reciprocity and community-based visa policy are not fully respected. the issue of immigration regulation is one of the pillars of national security, but it cannot be allowed to justify unjustified and unequal treatment of eu member states by third countries. eu citizenship entitles all nationals of the member states to be treated on the same basis. the regulation on third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the eu's external borders will allow a response and real pressure to be exerted on countries currently breaching the reciprocity clause. this problem concerns central european countries, including the us maintaining visa requirements for poles, despite poland meeting the criteria for visa-free travel (especially given the fact that negotiations on an eu-us free trade agreement are currently underway). the issue of the czech citizens who have been deprived of their right to stay in canada without a visa since 2009 also remains unresolved. in line with the principle of reciprocity in visa policy, i decided to vote in favour of the proposal on third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the eu's external borders.
in writing. − the collapse of lehman brothers in 2008, which evolved into the worst financial crisis in 80 years, demonstrated above all the need for better coordination. back in 2008 there were 27 different regulatory banking authorities relying on national rules and safety mechanisms. coordination between the systems existed; however it did not prove sufficient to respond to the crisis the eu has since endured. the understanding that an integrated financial framework is essential for the eu’s recovery and economic stability led to proposals to establish a european banking union. one important element of the union is the european banking authority (eba), which falls under the pillar of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). created in 2011, the eba works to ensure consistent regulation and supervision of the eu’s banking sector by harmonising rules for financial institutions throughout the eu. based on the inter-institutional agreement, the current report asks that the tasks, powers and capacities of the eba be reinforced and adapted to the ecb being the new european supervisor. this will ensure better accountability and transparency in the eu’s banking sector. the adoption of the report today is a positive step towards realising a fully-fledged banking union, therefore i supported the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution by mrs edith bauer on equal pay for men and women for equal work or work of equal value. despite significant changes in gender equality, the issue of the pay gap remains unresolved. the problem of wage inequality persists throughout the european union and is even worsening in some member states. the draft resolution calls for support for member states in combating this phenomenon. a reduction of the wage gap by at least 5 percentage points per year would allow the problem to be completely eliminated by 2020. equal pay would bring numerous social and economic benefits. this would, among other things, contribute to improving the economic situation not only of women but also of society as a whole by increasing economic growth. i believe that working to end the gender pay gap will be a great step towards full equality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliamentʼs resolution on the application of the principle of equal pay for male and female workers for equal work or work of equal value (2013/2678(rsp)). in so doing, i hope to limit the disparity in the pay men and women receive for the same work. while i firmly believe that people should earn what they are worth or their earnings should be based on merit or experience, gender should not be a factor. sadly however, progress in narrowing the gender pay gap is extremely slow and in some member states the gap has even widened. despite the significant body of legislation in force for almost 40 years, the actions taken and resources spent, the gender pay gap is still a persistent problem and currently stands at 16.2 % across the eu (disparity at eu level was 17.7 % in 2006, 17.6 % in 2007, 17.4 % in 2008, 16.9 % in 2009 and 16.4 % in 2010). thus different factors need to be considered and addressed properly, such as differences in activity and employment rates, in wage structures, in the composition of the workforce and in remuneration, as well as other macroeconomic and institutional factors.
in writing. −the security of the virtual space is very important for its proper functioning. meanwhile, cyber attacks are becoming more serious and more complex, threatening the security of users and causing economic losses. the union's cybersecurity strategy 'open, secure and protected cyberspace' aims to prevent and respond to disruptions and attacks as effectively as possible. this strategy aims to promote values such as freedom and democracy and ensure the secure growth of the digital economy. member states have already adopted national cybersecurity strategies this year, but fragmentation can be inefficient in some areas. the resolution therefore stresses the need to create a single market for cybersecurity. information systems in the european union are highly interconnected. the internet is a global tool, which means that most cyber-attacks are cross-border in nature and can threaten the proper functioning of the internal market and undermine consumer confidence in the digital single market. the resolution calls, inter alia, for action to raise awareness and educate europeans about cybersecurity, and the organisation of european cybersecurity month will be a great initiative.

in writing. - in today's vote i voted in favour of the report by mrs gomes on the maritime dimension of the common security and defence policy. the issue of maritime protection regulation has been debated in the ep on many occasions, leading to the development of relevant provisions in this area. foreign trade now accounts for 90% of the eu's trade relations. regulations on the protection of marine nets, the safety of maritime transport or fisheries resources are therefore crucial. with the increase in traffic on sea lanes and communication lines, ensuring safety has become a priority for eu policy. the report also considers potential threats at sea, including terrorism, international crime, piracy and environmental degradation, and develops actions to prevent them. i hope that the solutions proposed will contribute to the development of further economic cooperation between member states and to an increase in investment. in the long term, these actions could translate into tangible benefits also in other areas.
in writing. − i voted for the report which seeks to achieve further integration and coordination of defence and security matters across the european union through its maritime dimension. the euʼs maritime strategy has taken on greater significance given recent events in the southern mediterranean, and the threats posed by drug trafficking, organised crime and terrorism.
in writing. − the report by marietta giannakou raises important issues such as the eu's capacity to respond to international crises, cooperation between member states in the field of security, and a common approach to defence policy. military structures are very important given the diversity and complexity of the eu member states' relations with other countries around the globe. the eu is supported by nato, of which poland has been a member since 1999. the eu's membership of nato structures should therefore be taken into account in order to avoid duplication before implementing specific instruments in the field of inter alia military relations. in my view, a more favourable solution would be cooperation between the existing eu and nato structures, and in the absence of appropriate regulations, to complement them within the framework of solutions already developed and tested. i believe that in the face of the crisis we are facing, it is important to value the expenditure and to use any available funds to minimise its impact.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. it provides a valuable assessment of the european unionʼs military capabilities in the context of the common security and defence policy (csdp). joint eu action through the csdp has helped establish stability, in areas such as the balkans, and the eu mission in afghanistan is also playing a central role alongside nato in increasing the capacity of the afghan police force, and in the international effort to counter piracy and to protect the world food programme.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the situation of unaccompanied minors in the eu. these children might arrive during or after a period of conflict, or they may be the victims of human trafficking. the standard of care which is given to children varies hugely across europe and in some cases is to the detriment of child protection. i advocate a coordinated approach to issues concerning minors, including establishing the age of a child without using intrusive medical techniques; the appointment of a guardian who can speak the same language as the child; child protection training for those who work with child asylum-seekers; provision of suitable accommodation for children (separated by age group and gender); access to schooling, healthcare and activities relevant to child development and the collection of data on child asylum-seekers which would assist in forming childrenʼs policy in the future.
in writing. − the cultural and creative sectors (ccs) are evident in every aspect of our daily lives: in the architecture we live in, music we listen to, films, performing arts and books we occupy our free time with. furthermore, these sectors carry an economic value. the european competiveness report 2010 stated that ccs accounted for 4.5 % of gdp and 8.5 million jobs in the eu. nonetheless, ccsʼs contribution has yet to be fully recognised or developed, especially under current economic conditions. this report calls for this to change. pointing to the innovative potential of the ccs and their ability to create jobs and stimulate growth, the report calls for the competitive and export potential of these sectors to be strengthened. the means proposed include establishing clear conditions needed for ccs development, promoting cultural access and education from an early age, and making funding more accessible by establishing a favourable regulatory and tax framework. creativity and culture shaped our past, influence our present and will better prepare us for challenges in the future, so it is important to recognise and maximise the beneficial effects of ccs. i voted therefore to support the report.
in writing. − i abstained from voting on the report on the european cultural and creative sectors as sources of economic growth and jobs. this report calls on the european union to take measures to support and improve access to funding, to broaden the market and to increase the international and trans-sectoral scope of cultural and creative sectors. i admit that this report is timely and important given the economic and cultural importance of the cultural and creative sectors, especially at a time of economic crisis. however, i do not support the final committee report because of the amendment adopted which gives strong support to the idea of making further progress towards tax harmonisation.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i will try to address some of the points we have just heard – except for this cdm thing because, as you know, this is not a europe-only thing, it is something that has to be dealt with globally. but when it comes to europe and the ets, as you know, the commission already in the summer of 2012 undertook steps to correct the shortcomings of the eu emissions trading scheme and strengthen it, based on a two-step approach. on the one hand we should in the short term slow down the increase of supply/demand imbalances by backloading part of the auction supply and, on the other hand, we should identify structural measures to enable the eu ets to address the imbalances in a sustainable manner. this was done through the carbon market report that should have come out only this year, but we brought it forward and sent it out in november last year with six structural options included. since then the commission has conducted a public consultation on the basis of these six options for structural measures and we are now in the process of reducing the six options to significantly fewer. for instance, there appears to be a growing view among stakeholders that the eu ets needs some kind of objective and rule-based mechanism to adjust supply and thereby strengthen market stability. i think mr florenz referred to this – it was mentioned – and it is true that last week the commission organised an expert meeting on this additional option and is currently analysing the feedback received. in order for the eu ets to reduce emissions in a cost-effective manner beyond 2020, the ongoing work on the 2030 climate and energy framework obviously is also central. in relation to the part of the question on promoting linking, the commission very much supports global cooperation on climate change, including on trading systems as well as other means of carbon pricing. korea, china, australia, in the us at state level – california but also many other states – and some of the provinces in canada: there are a lot that have actually set up their own systems, some of which can be and will be linked to the eu ets. as a first example, the eu and switzerland will envisage a full link to start on 1 january 2015. linking different emissions trading systems, however, is challenging, as significant differences in the design of such systems exist, for example on the acceptance of international credits. mr florenz just mentioned earmarking and we have some elements of that already with the new entrants’ reserve 300. but of course other models can be sought out to promote innovation, and i take the message from the distinguished member. thank you very much for the strong support for structural measures to address the current market imbalances in the previous resolutions, thereby acknowledging that the eu ets is a flexible and cost-effective measure. it should remain a key tool to gradually decarbonise the eu power and industry sector. of course i regret that parliament did not adopt a motion for a resolution on the report on the state of the european carbon market in 2012. for the reform to work, we will need to work together so that we can find constructive solutions, but i also heard from mr florenz that there is still a will to try to do this.

i have to inform you that i have just been informed by the chair's colleagues that i will no longer be awarded the 'blue card' because i wanted to ask a question to one of the speakers, disagreeing with his thesis and wanting to know what he had in mind. unfortunately, i have been informed that the blue card will be treated with a restrictive approach, which i understand limits our right to debate and shows the undemocratic nature of our house, even in such matters.
i respect all the views expressed in this chamber, but i would ask that you do not create an atmosphere of suspicion towards those who have any doubts about this directive, about lobbying on behalf of the tobacco companies. well, it's not like that. one might wonder if we were actually discussing a complete ban on smoking. but we don't do that and therefore you can advocate for smoking control (which i wholeheartedly support - i don't smoke and i support solutions to reduce smoking), but that doesn't mean i have to support all the solutions in this bill in secret, even those that are cloaked in hypocrisy. that's the word that came out of this room today, and i'm going to use it. what else is there but hypocrisy in the solutions to eliminate slim or menthol cigarettes? there are no studies that show that more people start smoking these milder cigarettes, or what is the number of people who quit smoking these cigarettes. i know a lot of people who switched to menthol cigarettes and then quit completely. it's not about health, it's about business. let's face it. some countries that produce menthol cigarettes will stop producing them and their production will be moved to other countries that produce strong cigarettes. it's not just health that's at stake in this directive, but business as well. and here, unfortunately, is the hypocrisy i see, and that is why i cannot support this directive in its present form. answer the question asked by raising the blue card. i am in favour of reducing smoking and appreciate the good intentions, but some of the measures in the directive may have the opposite effect. i share your concern, but i fear that banning menthol and 'slim' cigarettes will not reduce smoking, and may even increase it, because those who smoke these cigarettes now will smoke stronger cigarettes, even more harmful. my goal is the same: i want people to smoke less cigarettes, but not all the measures lead to that goal.
mr. chairman, please! since several colleagues have spoken about lobbyists, i will begin this brief statement by saying that as a longtime ngo activist i think it is an absolute scandal for lobbyists to impersonate ngos, social organisations, whether from the pharmaceutical side or the tobacco industry side. it's not that we have worked so hard to build civil society - i myself come from a post-communist country - so that it can be used by lobby groups. come to us as lobbyists, which you do anyway, because otherwise you undermine the most important element of democracy, which is authentic civil society. the second point is for those who think we need to impose very strict bans. of course, it would be great if people were healthy, happy, reasonable, did not smoke and did not have addictions, but they smoke and have addictions, so we have to create a law for man and for the citizen so that he does not suffer too much. let's make transitions, let's make them sensible, because we are sensible envoys. let's give mrs. mcavan a mandate to repeal anything that encourages it, but let's not cause any more suffering to the public.
mr. chairman, please! the lack of consistency and sincerity of those who tell us that they want to reduce the production and consumption of cigarettes and tobacco in europe is evident in this case. on the one hand, certain categories of cigarettes are prohibited, while others are not. for example, slim cigarettes are banned, which are produced in poland or bulgaria, but extra forte cigarettes, which are produced in france or other countries, are not. it's a discrepancy that shows that there may be a business connection. so if we're going to ban it, maybe it should be for all cigarettes. but if we are selectively imposing these restrictions and hitting producers in certain countries, then there may be some business behind it and it's not honest. i'm anti-smoking - i don't smoke - and i'm for education that gets to people and convinces them not to smoke. but let us not introduce restrictions which cause serious economic problems in some countries and favour and support some and throw stones at others.
in writing. i support the general aims of the directive to reduce smoking, in particular to prevent young people from initiating tobacco use and to raise awareness of the negative effects of smoking. however, i am opposed to certain provisions of the draft which create legal problems. the legal basis chosen by the commission, namely article 114 (1) tfeu, which is intended to adapt the requirements for the better functioning of the single market, is questionable. the commission's objective of health protection falls within the competence of the member states under article 168 (5) tfeu, which expressly excludes any harmonisation of measures whose purpose is directly to protect public health in relation to tobacco products. moreover, the prohibition of the sale of cigarettes of the 'slim' or 'menthol' type and the exclusion from the scope of the restrictions of products such as cigars on the basis of unsubstantiated claims that some are more attractive to young people than others have nothing to do with improving the functioning of the single market. moreover, it may lead to discrimination against certain undertakings and to the favouring of others, which will distort competition on the union market. the standardisation of packaging raises further doubts as to the respect of the rights enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. in addition, the imposition of 'uniform packaging' may infringe intellectual property rights, in particular trademarks expressly covered by the property rights of article 17 of the charter and article 20 of the trips agreement. the commission has also proposed a number of delegated acts which, under article 290 tfeu, should only concern ancillary legislation. however, the draft law applies to cases of high importance, which gives the commission the de facto right to even set a maximum nicotine content of 0% in cigarettes, which could lead to a total ban on the marketing of these goods and to move cigarettes to the 'black market', which would only increase the problem rather than solve it.
in writing. the main aim of the so-called tobacco directive is to reduce the number of smokers in the eu. studies carried out by the european commission show that flavoured and slim cigarettes are the main cigarettes used by young europeans, and it has been proposed to withdraw these products from the market. however, this decision has very serious implications for the tobacco industry, which is of great economic importance in many member states. of course, in the interests of public health, especially the health of young people, we should restrict access to tobacco products to minors, support education and information activities to raise awareness of the effects of smoking and require manufacturers to provide reliable information on the harmfulness of their products on their packaging. however, the introduction of such restrictive provisions would have fatal consequences for the agricultural sector, industry and trade. tobacco growers, producers and retailers will suffer, and a huge number of jobs will be lost. furthermore, if we reduce cigarette production in the eu, it will certainly increase in the neighbouring countries, i.e. russia and belarus, and this in turn will increase the illegal trade, especially on the eu's eastern border. that is why i am in favour of rejecting such a rigorous proposal. if we want to reduce trade in tobacco products in the eu, we must do so gradually, with transitional periods and compensation for producers, without negative consequences for the agricultural sector, industry and trade.
in writing. in its draft new tobacco directive, the european commission is trying to impose a single model of action on all member states. in pursuing the goal of reducing smoking in europe by a paltry 2%, the commission is resorting to measures whose effectiveness is not at all confirmed, but the expected side effects in the form of a decrease in employment or an increase in smuggling and organised crime are significant. poland is one of the largest european producers of raw tobacco and tobacco products. menthol and 'slim' cigarettes are noticeably more popular in poland than in other member states. this is an expression of european diversity: just as in sweden people use snus, in finland they use candy that looks like a pipe, and in portugal they use traditional short cigarettes, so in poland people smoke mentole and slimy. i also oppose regulating e-cigarettes as medical products. e-cigarettes should always be tested for quality, but treating them like drugs will certainly raise their price and hit their manufacturers mainly small and medium-sized enterprises. there is no doubt that all tobacco products are harmful and can lead to disease and death. that is why i am a strong advocate of informing europeans about the harmful effects of smoking and, in particular, of the need to protect young people. however, such regulation must not lead to discrimination against agriculture, industry and local businesses in the same country.
in writing. – while the tpd addresses many important facets of public health i fear that it also infringes on the rights of our citizens while preventing them and their member states from determining what tobacco products can and can’t be sold. i am concerned that historically traditional products that are used in certain member states are in danger. in saying that, i want to emphasise that i support the pursuit of protecting the youth of this union; however, adults should retain their right to purchase products that have long been part of their culture. also, certain bans, such as those outlined in this directive, have the effect of imposing on our internal market, and subsequently impede our ability to not only improve the economies of certain member states but also reduce our ability to control and/or regulate the sale of tobacco products on the black market, which are, without a doubt, going to drastically increase given the restrictions put forth by the tpd.

in writing. the report by mr zanoni, which is being discussed today, cannot be seen as a positive development. one of the errors is the provision that requires an environmental impact assessment to be carried out for the exploration phase of unconventional hydrocarbons. the commission therefore concludes that the measures at issue are imputable to the state and that they constitute state aid. it is difficult to understand the intentions of the rapporteur, since no studies have been published to date confirming the negative environmental impact of exploration for unconventional hydrocarbons. the inclusion of the extraction phase in annex i to the amended directive, irrespective of the quantity of ore extracted, is another error. the question is therefore how and on what basis the daily exploitation level for such deposits will be determined. it is also unjustified to distinguish coalbed methane from other fossil fuels and to require its extraction to be subject to an environmental impact assessment. could europe, which is setting itself increasingly ambitious climate targets, not take a cue from the us? this country, which has been exploring shale gas on a large scale for a long time, is becoming a real winner not only in terms of access to cheap fuel, but also in terms of reducing emissions fairly easily. the same should apply to those member states whose economies are based on high-carbon technologies and which have large shale gas reserves, which are much less polluting.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. i would just like to refer to the question of the inclusion of shale gas exploration and production projects in annex i to the directive. mandatory environmental impact assessment of all stages of activities related to unconventional hydrocarbon deposits is decidedly far-reaching and unauthorised. on this point, i have tabled an amendment with a group of 40 members which deserves support in tomorrow's vote. the adoption of the proposed regulations would mean a slowdown or complete halt in the process of shale gas exploitation in, for example, my country and the flight of investors to countries where such procedures are not in place, as is the case in ukraine. european experience to date and environmental studies carried out in the member states most advanced in the work on unconventional hydrocarbon deposits show that exploration and production activities in compliance with current legislation and best practices are carried out in an environmentally safe manner. it is worth recalling that the european commission is preparing an appropriate legal framework to manage the risks and fill the legal gaps in shale gas extraction in the european union. i believe that the european commission's new initiative on environmental impact assessment should include a comprehensive and balanced set of rules for industry in europe that will clearly facilitate the development of this industry rather than hamper it.

mr. chairman, please! corruption is a phenomenon that has a devastating impact on the functioning of any administration, and in some countries it perpetuates discriminatory practices with regard to civil and political rights. it is no accident that the administrations of authoritarian states are considered to be highly corrupt, driven primarily by the desire to maintain power, because they are highly susceptible to this type of dependence. corruption is a direct threat to democracy and the enforcement of human rights, and is often a source of conflict. in combination with the lack of access to information for citizens, it effectively guarantees impunity for dictatorial authorities who subjugate the societies they govern. when we give financial aid to third countries, we need to monitor its use properly. it cannot be a source of illegal income for their officials, and unfortunately, there are cases like this. expanding the definition of a human rights defender to include anti-corruption activists or those who expose these pathological practices, such as investigative journalists, seems like an interesting proposition.
in writing. − corruption, understood as the abuse of power for private, individual or collective, direct or indirect benefit, and the fraud, nepotism and illegal subsidisation of political parties and electoral campaigns that are closely linked to it, pose serious threats to democracy and the development of civil society. the european union can and should become a credible leader in the fight against corruption by addressing the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its own borders. i am in favour of the commission imposing the obligation to apply the highest standards of fairness in procurement procedures for the implementation of eu-funded projects, in particular by promoting greater availability of calls for tender for local organisations. it should be stressed that this approach to public procurement, i.e. based on respect for human rights, creates favourable conditions for the authorities to empower disadvantaged groups. as a watchdog of human rights, the eu should promote the exchange of good practices in anti-corruption activities both between member states and third countries, stimulating a process of mutual learning and strengthening democratic values.
in writing. − according to a report by the hertie school of governance in berlin and the bertelsmann foundation, the real cost of corruption in europe is well over the €100 billion previously estimated. the estimated amount of corruption therefore amounts to almost one third of the eu budget for the years 2014-2020. corruption thus costs eu countries €323 billion a year, undermining the union's image as a world leader in the fight against corruption. that's why we need to step up our efforts to fight this disease. the gomes report, which we are voting on today, fully captures the scale of the problem and points to the basic actions we should take. that's why i endorsed the record of this document. to fight this problem, we must work together. the mutual exchange of information and experience will benefit not only the eu but also the partner countries.

the adopted report rightly pointed out that in certain cases relating to labour law disputes, it may be difficult to determine the jurisdiction of the court having jurisdiction over the case. employment matters have rightly been excluded from the scope of the brussels i regulation and left to the jurisdiction of the member states. without calling into question the correctness of this approach, it is necessary to consider how the protection of workers' interests will be regulated in the future. in a situation where the defendant is the employer, and due to the cross-border nature of the employment relationship, for example in terms of the place of work, the employer's registered office or the employee's country of origin, it is not possible to establish unequivocally the jurisdiction of the court.
in writing. − following the changes introduced by the brussels i regulation signed on 12 december 2012, the future enforcement of judgments in another member state will be considerably simplified. although the changes in the recast version are substantial and purposeful, the scope of the recast procedure has not covered a very important issue of jurisdictional provisions in labour law. i believe that clear rules of conduct in this area are very much needed, especially at a time when the european labour market is open to all community citizens and many of them take advantage of earning opportunities in another member state. i support the initiative of the legal affairs committee which aims to introduce further amendments to the brussels i regulation to address the issues of jurisdiction in labour law. workers should know how to assert their rights in any disputes arising from the cross-border nature of their work. i therefore support the request for action to improve the rules on jurisdiction applicable to individual contracts of employment and to collective dispute settlement. i agree with the amendments proposed in the report to the brussels i regulation with regard to the establishment of an exclusive jurisdiction in collective disputes in the place where such a dispute is to be or has been brought and the establishment of a guarantee for the worker that he will be able to sue his employer in the court of the member state in which the worker is habitually resident. i believe that these changes will contribute to improving the judicial system and strengthening the legal position of the employee, regardless of where he is employed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report by mrs pervenche berès on the proposal for a directive on the flag state's responsibility for the enforcement of council directive 2009/13/ec implementing the agreement between the shipowners' association of the european community and the european transport workers' federation on the maritime labour convention 2006 and amending directive 1999/63/ec. in my view, the maritime labour convention makes a significant contribution to establishing a level playing field in the global economy by establishing common minimum standards for all flags and seafarers. i also sincerely hope that it will help to make maritime professions more attractive to the people of the union. however, in order to do so, we must bear in mind that in most eu member states national rules are already more restrictive and provide a higher level of protection than the international labour organisation standards. i am therefore pleased that the report includes a clause which points out that the application of the directive should in no case lead to a reduction in the level of protection of seafarers that they currently enjoy in the member states of the union. furthermore, i believe that the directive rightly specifies the obligations of the member states to establish a system to ensure that supervisory organisations operate at an appropriate standard. i believe that this will contribute to a more efficient and effective enforcement of the provisions of the convention.
in writing. - the work on the tobacco directive was fraught with difficulties. the confrontation of two reasons, namely health aspects and economic interests, forced me to take a position that took into account the arguments of both sides. i voted in favour of measures to combat the problem of young people becoming addicted to tobacco, including the introduction of a warning label covering 65% of the surface of a cigarette pack. i would point out that the draft directive proposed by the commission did not, in principle, focus on measures to promote health and protect against the negative effects of smoking. if implemented, i would expect to see the relocation of tobacco production and factories from poland rather than a real reduction in the number of smokers. in the context of the instruments covered by the proposal for a directive, i regard the 2% reduction in the number of smokers expected by the commission over five years as being on the verge of statistical error! on the other hand, concrete data is an undeniable argument! poland is a key producer of tobacco and tobacco products in europe, producing around 40 000 tonnes per year, of which more than a third is grown in the lublin province. among polish tobacco products, slim cigarettes, whose production is to be maintained, and menthol cigarettes, for which a transitional period has been negotiated, occupy a significant position. i therefore welcome the outcome of the vote in the ep and hope that a compromise will be found in the council which is in line with this position.

in writing. - i welcome the european parliament's consent to the ratification of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the islamic republic of mauritania. the document negotiated by the european commission addresses issues such as fishing rights and the associated financial compensation. the main objective of the negotiations was to guarantee the european fleet access to the surplus fish stocks of mauritania. the agreement thus reached would allow these areas to be developed in a sustainable way, both environmentally and economically. the protocol in question is of particular importance for polish fishermen who fish intensively in mauritanian waters. these waters are rich in fish species such as mackerel and sardines and are the main source of these for polish vessels, which currently have no alternative fishing grounds. failure to agree to ratify the protocol would therefore have a number of negative consequences and would cause a lot of difficulties for the polish fleet.

in writing. - abortion is a violation of the universal human principles of a universal and universal nature. all public authorities, including those of the european union, have a duty to protect human life from conception to natural death. therefore, any form of abortion should be opposed. the phenomenon of selective abortion (due to the sex of the child) is the result of widespread access and approval by some communities of abortion as a method of birth control. every child, regardless of gender, has the right to adequate legal protection both before and after birth for survival and development. it is important to emphasize that according to the un convention on the rights of the child, girls have the same status as boys. i would also point out that there is no 'human right to abortion' in international law. it is not provided for in any international agreement, nor does it derive from customary law. any other reasoning is completely unfounded and completely absent from the principles of international law. in this context, it is important to note that no one can effectively invoke any international legally binding un treaty as establishing or recognising the right to abortion. every human being has the full and inalienable right to refuse to act against his conscience in accordance with article 18 of the universal declaration of human rights.
in writing. - gender-based genocide is a widespread problem, not only in the poorest countries of africa, asia and latin america, but also in north america and europe. it is also a serious crime, one of the most brutal violations of fundamental human rights, and therefore requires immediate action. gender selection is carried out by means of sex determination during pregnancy through selective abortion, and after birth, through infanticide or abandonment, and is related to the cultural conditions of some societies where daughters are considered a burden on the family. it is therefore necessary to take action to implement measures to support girls and women. these measures should be aimed at building a society based on the principle of gender equality, where educational materials would strengthen women's chances of living in an environment that respects gender equality and where stereotypical perceptions of the roles of women and men would appear as an archaic and unnecessary concept. supporting women in the exercise of their rights should be through the creation of legal measures that constitute their capacity to make decisions independently, without the interference of their spouses. giving women access to education, employment, health care, free access to contraception, a bank account without the consent or permission of a spouse or other person is crucial in this case.

in writing. violence affects women regardless of age, education, wealth or social status. several million european women experience it every day. the european parliament and ngos, including the women's sejm of the left, which i co-organised and which was attended by 3 000 polish women, call for the council of europe convention of 11 may 2011 on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence to be signed and ratified as soon as possible. the convention recognises that women and girls are more vulnerable to violence than men and boys, but it is intended to apply to all victims of domestic violence, regardless of gender. so far, only five countries have signed the convention. the signing of the convention creates a legal framework to prevent violence against women. the convention provides a set of practical tools to help victims of violence, such as 24-hour emergency telephone services, legal aid and a network of shelters for victims of violence, and electronic surveillance of perpetrators. currently, only 12 eu member states guarantee funding for specialised support services for women victims of violence. however, there are no proper standards for such services. only four member states have introduced a definition of domestic violence based on the socio-cultural category of gender identity into their criminal codes. protection orders have been improperly implemented in many countries.

in writing. − the current directive covered projects with a production capacity of at least 500 000 m3 of shale gas per day. in future, a full environmental impact assessment is to be mandatory for all projects related to the extraction and exploration of unconventional hydrocarbons (shale gas and oil, coalbed methane, etc.), including shale gas projects, when hydraulic fracturing technology is used, regardless of the size of the production. the environmental impact assessment (eia) directive covers a wide range of projects, both public and private. it lays down the criteria for the project, including the information that must be provided to the national authorities for the project to be accepted. i am in favour of environmental protection and sustainable development, but i cannot accept that the same criteria apply to exploration and research as to the regular exploitation of the resource. i also have reservations about the voting procedure itself, which was not clear to everyone, in particular the automatically invalidated amendments.

in writing. − in a time of economic crisis across europe, i regard the adoption by the european parliament of a directive on the recognition of professional qualifications and administrative cooperation through the internal market information system as a great success. through a number of innovative solutions, it will increase the mobility of eu citizens and facilitate their taking up work abroad, especially in countries facing a growing demand for skilled personnel in the health, education and construction sectors. the document ends a long-standing dispute over the recognition of qualifications for many occupational groups in the eu, and makes the process simpler and faster, mainly thanks to the electronic information exchange system (imi) between member states. the provisions of the directive which was voted on cover issues such as the voluntary introduction of the european professional card for selected professions, partial access to a profession allowing access to work abroad in accordance with the education or training received, or updating of minimum training requirements. the early warning system for the medical professions is also an important solution, which will allow for effective fraud detection in the event of a loss of the right to practise in one of the member states. the adoption of this directive is of particular importance for nurses and midwives in poland who are graduates of medical schools or medical studies, whose qualifications will be recognised on the same basis in this professional group throughout the european union.
in writing. − the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications is a key document for the internal market, as it will increase the mobility of europeans. freedom of movement within the european union can be achieved if qualifications acquired in one country are recognised quickly and efficiently in other eu countries. the european professional card or the updating of minimum training requirements will help to achieve this, as will better cooperation between member states through the wider use of the internal market information exchange system. the directive will not only make it easier to find work in the internal market, but is of particular importance for polish nurses and midwives, who have until now had to meet special, additional requirements in terms of recognition of qualifications. today's vote is the culmination of my many years of work, in which i have stressed that these requirements are not justified, because all nurses in poland are treated equally and as nurses they perform the same professional activities and have the same competences. the polish demands were accepted today and as a result polish nurses and midwives will be treated in the same way as all other nurses from other eu countries. the new rules offer an opportunity to find work faster and to make better use of the opportunities of the internal market.
in writing. − in times of ongoing financial, economic and social crisis, action is needed to stimulate entrepreneurship and innovation, where job mobility can be a lifeline for many, especially young people, affected by unemployment. although the legal framework on this issue has existed since the 1970s and the possibility for workers to move is a key means of reducing unemployment, difficulties in this area are still felt due to the lack of clarity on the rules for the recognition of professional qualifications. it is therefore essential to simplify the procedures for citizens wishing to take up employment in another member state by creating an appropriate legal framework, while ensuring a high level of safety for consumers, patients, workers and all eu citizens. the european professional card in the form of an electronic certificate will contribute to a significant improvement in the procedure for the recognition of professional qualifications, enabling professionals to provide services without having to meet additional formal requirements.
in writing. − i believe that professional mobility is fundamental to competitiveness and employment in europe. i voted in favour of this report because i support aims to speed up and simplify the recognition process of qualified professionals throughout the eu to enhance mobility and growth, while making sure essential safety checks are in place for health professionals. i agree completely that the fundamental right to freedom of movement is still not regarded as self-evident, and this legislative proposal must play a part in changing that by simplifying the procedures which people wishing to work in another country have to complete. i applaud all efforts to improve communication between member states, which generates mutual trust and allows all eu professionals to live and work wherever they choose.
in writing. − freedom of movement and of occupation is one of the fundamental rights of every eu citizen. mobility is not only a value in itself, but also a condition for competitiveness and a tool to combat unemployment in europe. this is why it is so important to ensure that it is implemented in practice and to put in place concrete solutions to implement it. at present, the right to move, although it is a legal right - we have schengen and the right to work in any eu country - is severely restricted by the lack of simple and clear rules governing the recognition of professional qualifications. only a few professions have the possibility of automatic recognition of qualifications, and even in these cases the procedures are not always clear. often, the actual recognition of qualifications depends only on the arbitrary decision of the potential employer. it's not supposed to be like this. it is therefore necessary to introduce a new regulation to eliminate those shortcomings. the problem is not only the very existence of differences in education, employment, health care, consumer protection, etc., but also, and perhaps most of all, the ignorance of these differences. citizens, not knowing what to expect, often prefer not to take risks, which has a negative impact on the mobility of workers. this in turn leads to a reduction in competitiveness and a situation where there is a shortage of workers in one country and a shortage of jobs in another in the same sector.
in writing. − i thank the rapporteur for the report on the recognition of professional qualifications and administrative cooperation through the internal market information exchange system. this resolution will undoubtedly contribute to the opening up of the labour market, particularly for professions such as doctors, nurses, dentists, pharmacists, etc. the european professional card allows professional documents and qualifications to be recognised outside the country of residence. this process will undoubtedly contribute to the free exchange of specialists and experience. the key task is also to facilitate the work of the administration. however, it should be ensured that the requirements for the process of applying for such an authorisation are clear, understandable and generally available in different languages to all applicants.
in writing. − the introduction of visa facilitation with armenia, as well as with other developing countries and democracies, is crucial for the implementation of the eastern partnership project or similar partnership and cooperation agreements. through the provisions that open borders, we allow the citizens of these countries free access to cultural and economic exchange. it is also an indispensable tool for building democracy and shaping civil society. the point is in the recent developments in the political arena and the signing of the customs union between armenia and russia. to avoid russian domination in this politically unstable region, we need to do more to ensure good and close relations with countries like armenia and the others in the region: georgia, moldova, azerbaijan. the agreement, which will help citizens to strengthen their human ties and exchange intellectual and economic capital, will therefore allow closer relations and integration with the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation because this agreement will make it easier and cheaper for citizens of armenia (especially those who travel most frequently) to acquire short-stay visas which would allow them to travel freely throughout the eu. i believe that the citizens of our european neighbours, especially those from the eastern partnership, should be allowed to travel and undertake academic studies in the eu and this process is the best tool of european integration that we have.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported, like the other ppe group representatives, the draft resolution on the health claim on carbohydrates. i am of the opinion that it would be possible to achieve the opposite effect to the objectives of the basic act by allowing that statement only in specific conditions of application. such authorisation could also promote and encourage the consumption of foods containing sugars other than those naturally present in the food. such labelling of products is, in my view, a contradictory and unclear message for consumers, especially in the context of national dietary recommendations to reduce sugar intake. i think the average consumer is increasingly looking at the product groups that provide the body with the nutrients it needs. however, with the wide variety of foods available on the food market today, particularly processed foods, it is becoming increasingly difficult to make healthy choices that meet individual nutritional needs. the information on the label should therefore help to inform consumers quickly about the health value of a given foodstuff, rather than creating confusion, which the draft regulation submitted to parliament can help to do. the rejection of the resolution is therefore a clear signal to all of us that we should do even more to raise food awareness in the european union by providing consumers with proper and reliable information on the specific characteristics of food products.
mr. chairman, please! one of the major causes of the imbalance in the eu-china relationship is the numerous restrictions imposed on european businesses wishing to invest in the middle east. the eu has also been active in the fight against money laundering, which is a major source of fraud, and has been a key driver of the eu's financial and economic growth. if we realise that one of the few assets europe has is know-how, we can see the scale of the problem. investing in china often means giving our partners in china the unique know-how that our companies have developed. in addition, there is limited access to the chinese public procurement market and numerous trade barriers imposed by the chinese central and regional authorities. as a result, nearly 50% of european businesses investing in china have experienced some form of discrimination, and the scale of this phenomenon is increasing year by year. the commission should therefore make every effort to ensure that the negotiated agreement is as precise as possible, that it is able to safeguard the interests of european businesses and that its provisions can be fully enforced. those were the reasons why i decided to vote for this document.
in writing. − the eu and china have grown steadily and dynamically over the past 30 years, reaching a record total trade volume of eur 433.8 billion in 2012, but since 1997 there has been a trade imbalance in china's favour. following the 2012 eu-china summit in beijing, the european commission asked member states to accept its negotiating guidelines for an investment agreement with the people's republic of china. these guidelines concerned investment protection and market access. the main emphasis in the draft resolution was that the agreement should not include investments in special zones that allow workers' rights requirements to be circumvented and labour standards and other laws not to be respected, nor should it promote the production of goods in laogai labour camps and their export from china to the eu. in addition, the draft calls for china to allow other legal arrangements for foreign investors in addition to joint ventures, combined with due protection of intellectual property rights, industrial property rights, trademarks and geographical indications of products, so that they can establish enterprises in the chinese market. i voted with the ecr group in favour of the resolution because it calls for greater openness and transparency in china's business and for fair competition.
in writing. − china is playing and will continue to play an increasingly important role in the global economy, making it one of the eu's most important partners in this field. because of the fundamental cultural differences between china and europe, this cooperation faces many serious problems, such as china's failure to respect certain human rights that are fundamental to european culture. china is both a partner and a rival, and it's not something that's going to change anytime soon, because it's a situation that goes back thousands of years. however, where possible, through mutual dialogue, we should seek to deepen cooperation and narrow the range of issues on which we differ. it is important that any negotiations with china take place at eu level, not at the level of individual member states. in the face of a powerful partner like china, it is the united voice of all eu countries that has the power to make a difference. only in this way can we have a dialogue as equals, which is a key element of fruitful cooperation. the agreement currently being negotiated, which is intended to replace the individual bilateral agreements that have been in place until now, is therefore of great importance. importantly, the eu is seen as a neutral partner of china (as opposed to, say, the us), and china-eu economic cooperation dates back to the 1970s. it's worth continuing this good, though not always easy, tradition.
in writing. − i thank the rapporteur for reporting on the eu's negotiations with china on a bilateral investment agreement. as is well known, china is the eu's largest trading partner. the two sides have also been engaged in a dialogue on human rights for many years. this report has addressed a very important issue, namely the respect of labour rights and the preservation of fair competition. the key here is that investors pay particular attention to these issues when concluding contracts, with an emphasis on both labour standards and regulations. the conclusion of an investment agreement with china is an opportunity to improve both the economic and political situation, which would facilitate negotiations and discussions on the respect of human rights in the country. the standards must also be strictly adhered to so that intervention is possible in the event of non-compliance. in addition, it is necessary to emphasize the need to block certain divisions in order to protect our market from cheap products from china. i'm thinking here primarily about the footwear industry.
in writing. − i wholeheartedly voted in favour of this resolution. i have brought this issue to the commission’s attention in several of my written questions. the eu is taiwan’s biggest source of foreign direct investment. the eu held 31.5% of all fdi flows and 21% in fdi stocks in taiwan in 2010. taiwan is eu’s 7th largest trading partner in asia, and the eu’s 23rd largest trading partner in the world. the eu must give a positive response to taiwan’s willingness to launch negotiations for bilateral agreements on investment protection and market access in order to further strengthen the legal certainty of investments, and increase our volume and quality of investment flows.
in writing. − the commission resolution called on the european union to respond positively to taiwan's readiness to negotiate a bilateral agreement on investment protection and market access. the aim of these negotiations is to increase legal certainty for investment and to increase the volume and quality of trade between the european union and taiwan. the european parliament welcomed the improvement in relations between taiwan and china. this improvement resulted in the conclusion of 19 trade and economic agreements between the straits exchange foundation on behalf of taiwan and the association for relations across the taiwan straits on behalf of the prc. the commission resolution also called for the inclusion of a corporate social responsibility clause and social and environmental clauses as part of the sustainable development chapter (in the event of an effective conclusion of the agreement). i voted with the ecr group for a bilateral agreement between the european union and taiwan. the reason for my decision is that the european union is the main source of direct investment in taiwan. the eu is the 7th largest trading partner of the eu in asia and the 23rd largest trading partner of the eu in the world. since 2010, the eu has accounted for 31,5% of total foreign direct investment turnover and 21% of the value of this foreign direct investment in taiwan.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-taiwan trade relations. we must not be blind to the growing trade between the eu and taiwan. as the motion for a resolution stipulates, there is still potential to improve and i feel obliged to support our efforts to make trade with taiwan easier and cheaper. we are still fighting the crisis and in my opinion good partnership with our trade partners can be a main tool to handle this. today taiwan is known as one of the ‘asian tigersʼ. its economy is still growing with a 4 % rise in gdp every year and is based on high-technology production. the eu needs to continue to cooperate with such partners. growing trade with taiwan could act as a driver for domestic producers to innovate their production and make it more efficient. cooperation with taiwan is proof that the eu and trade organisations, for instance the wto, can work with each other successfully and benefit from it at the same time. we have to take care of such relations because we are now part of a globalised world.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr mulder on the establishment of a european border surveillance system (eurosur). the activities of the agency will in future enable the early detection and reduction of illegal migration at the external borders of the european union. eurosur, through its cooperation with the various union agencies, such as the european maritime safety agency and the european asylum support office, will contribute to improving security, which will result in a reduction in organised crime across europe. in the light of the mass and often tragically desperate attempts by migrants to cross the union's external maritime borders, we must also draw attention to the need for close cooperation and monitoring between eu member states and neighbouring third countries. i fully support the establishment of a european border surveillance system which, through effective monitoring, will contribute to the effective control and tracing of migration flows, both at the land and sea borders of the european union.
in writing. − free movement between countries is one of the european union's fundamental principles. the abolition of border controls serves to facilitate easy and fast movement, while reflecting the idea of european unity. however, the opening of borders also brings with it many dangers, such as illegal migration and international organised crime. the european border surveillance system eurosur was created to facilitate the exchange of information and operational cooperation between national authorities of the member states. effective cooperation and rapid response are made possible by national coordination centres, which are designated and supervised by each member state. eurosur's main task is to provide each country with information on the situation at its external borders. the messages from the national coordination centres are continuously enriched by the use of the latest technologies. the extension of the border control system will certainly help to reduce the extent of illegal immigration into the european union. the activities of the intelligence services, which will be able to respond immediately, should also be intensified. as a consequence, the deaths of migrants caused by improper transport conditions can be prevented. crossborder crime is a very difficult issue, as it goes far beyond the competence and activities of a member state. therefore, the continuous and above all the close surveillance that eurosur ensures will minimise cross-border crime, which in turn will significantly improve internal security throughout the european union.

in writing. − in vitro diagnostic medical devices include various tests such as self-testing of blood sugar, testing for hiv and dna testing. the european commission proposal is largely focused on product quality. the withdrawal of these low-quality products from the market is a matter of public health protection. in the past, there have been cases where a low-quality product has been placed on the market and tested negative, while the person was actually infected with hiv. this was a health risk for patients receiving blood transfusions and was associated with the risk of spreading the virus. similar cases have been reported in the case of the life-threatening disease hepatitis c. these situations show the very important need for improvements in the system. the new improvements for in vitro diagnostic medical devices are similar to those introduced for other medical devices and are aimed at improving the work of notified bodies, strengthening market surveillance and the surveillance system. i believe that the proposed network of european reference laboratories will help to eliminate high-risk medical devices. i fully support the introduction of the new conclusions with amendments, as i believe that this will significantly improve patient safety.
in writing. − in vitro diagnostic medical devices are classified according to the potential risk associated with their use: list a, list b, in vitro diagnostic medical devices for use on their own, in vitro diagnostic medical devices for performance evaluation and other in vitro diagnostic medical devices. self-contained in vitro diagnostic medical device is an in vitro diagnostic medical device intended by the manufacturer for use by a lay person in the home.
