in writing. − i voted in favour of the rapporteur on medical devices because i fully agree that the safety and health of patients is an unquestionable public health priority in the european union. in order to guarantee a high level of health for its citizens, it is necessary to establish transparent and scientifically sound internal market rules in the field of medical devices. in addition, stricter controls are needed to ensure that only safe medical devices enter the european market. however, it should be noted that in the case of innovative high-risk medical devices, the decision to place them on the market cannot be taken by the notified body alone. every medicinal product entering the market should be subject to the same assessment according to the same criteria. at present, there are no common verification methods available in the european union, either for manufacturers or for notified bodies. in view of the above, i am in favour of the establishment of new evaluation mechanisms in this area, which would reduce administrative procedures while ensuring the highest level of safety for patients and healthcare professionals.
in writing. − health safety is a fundamental principle that we must uphold to ensure adequate healthcare and to reduce the incidence of ill health resulting from the use of inadequate medical devices. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i believe that it, together with the report on in vitro medical devices, maintains the related horizontal approach between the two subjects, while at the same time distinguishing their fields of application where appropriate. greater safety and consistency in the use of medical devices and their authorisation is a good way forward on the positive path indicated by the guidance in this report.
in writing. − we voted today on the draft proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on medical devices amending directive 2001/83/ec, regulation (ec) no 178/2002 and regulation (ec) no 1223/2009. this regulation aims to ensure the functioning of the internal market in medical devices, taking as a basis a high level of health protection for patients, users and operators of the devices concerned. at the same time, this regulation sets high standards of quality and safety for medical devices in response to widespread concerns in this area. both objectives are pursued simultaneously. they are inseparable, and none of them is inferior to the other. the desire to ensure easy access for patients to new medical devices should never take precedence over the need to ensure patient safety. in line with the first hippocratic principle, which states that healthcare professionals have a duty to do no harm, the amendments we voted today will make it easier for clinical data to be publicly available to both professionals and citizens so that they know which product they should use. we're talking about products that are supposed to alleviate patients' suffering and illness. we should help eu citizens, as well as doctors, to have access to the best products, which is why i voted in favour of the regulation.
in writing. −safe and innovative medical devices are of great importance to patients, doctors and the medical technology industry. these include a wide range of different products, from patches, to pregnancy tests, contact lenses and x-ray machines, to pacemakers and hiv tests. the new regulations on medical devices proposed by the european commission are important because they aim to improve market surveillance, empower notified bodies and ensure transparency of product traceability. i believe that these regulations will help to avoid situations like this, where the implantation of defective breast implants that contained cheap, industrial silicone and that have been available on the market for over a decade has been revealed, and to avoid disasters related to hip implants, intracranial stents, etc. in order to ensure better assessment of the efficacy and safety of high-risk medical devices before they are placed on the market, improvements by the european parliament are necessary. in view of the improvement of patient safety and the protection of public health, i fully support the proposal for new rules, together with the amendments to the roth-behrendt report.
in writing. − based on the definition in directive 93/43/eec, a medical device is a 'tool, instrument, apparatus, appliance, material or other article, used alone or in combination, including software necessary for the proper use of the device, intended by the manufacturer to be used in humans for the purpose of: • diagnosis, prevention, monitoring, treatment or alleviation of disease; • diagnosis, monitoring, treatment, alleviation or compensation of injury or disability; • examination, replacement or modification of anatomical structures or the performance of a physiological process; • regulation of conception and gestation; and, at the same time, which does not achieve its intended action on the human body by pharmacological or immunological means, or whose action cannot be aided by metabolic means.

in writing. − over a thousand large commercial vessels, such as tankers and container ships, are recycled for scrap every year. many european ships are also dismantled in low-standard facilities on the beaches of south asia. these facilities often lack the environmental and safety measures necessary to handle hazardous materials contained in decommissioned ships. these materials include asbestos, polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs), tributyllocin and oil residue. this situation results in high accident rates, risks to workers' health and significant environmental pollution. the new rules, which will take the form of a regulation, provide for a system of inspections, certification and authorisation for large merchant seagoing vessels flying the flag of an eu member state, covering their entire life cycle, from construction to operation and recycling.
in writing. - thank you to the rapporteur for the report on ship recycling. the report focuses on the negative impact of ship recycling on human life and the environment. the key to the proposed convention is to take care of the entire process of both building and stocking ships to ensure social and environmental safety. the regulation of the law and the clear definition of requirements first within each member state, then within the european union, in order to reach an agreement on the international stage, is undoubtedly an important issue. this will allow for better enforcement, control and enforcement by individual countries. in the interest of the public, particular attention should be paid to the proper management of hazardous materials on board ships.
in writing. − the european parliament adopted a legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics in the field of demography. i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to introduce clearer statistics on demography. member states shall undertake to provide eurostat with information on their population on an annual basis. the adopted document aims to standardise and refine the data that member states transmit to the european union, which can then use this data to produce reliable demographic statistics on the population living in its territory.
in writing. − it is interesting to look at the population issues in the classic european philosophy of plato: first we must determine what the number of inhabitants should be, then agree on how many and how large parts to divide them into, and then divide the land and the settlements as evenly as possible between them. the number of citizens will be determined in an appropriate way, taking into account the area of the country and the neighboring country. the area of the land should be such that the land can satisfy the modest needs of the inhabitants - not much more - and the inhabitants must again be enough to be able to defend themselves against the attack of the neighboring tribes and their neighbors, if they were attacked, to be able to come to their aid effectively. according to this concept, there are strong lobbies in europe to achieve 'optimal world population'. one of the most active is the optimum population trust (opt) in the united kingdom. using the population ratio (ha/person), this group considers the optimal number of people to be between 2.7 billion and 5.1 billion. and on current trends, by 2050, there will be over nine billion people on the planet. in order to reduce the projected population by 60%, the opt promotes having no more than two children. but with the current population of the earth at over 6.8 billion people, such a plan can only be achieved by a radical reduction.
in writing. − according to the world health organization, sexual and reproductive health is a positive, rational approach to sexual relations, the ability to decide whether to have children, and the right to access information and methods of birth control and health care. these are freedoms linked to existing civil, social and political rights, often determined by the religion and culture of the region. they should be available to every man and woman in every country of the european union. to ensure citizens' health in this respect, eu legislation should support actions to guarantee europeans proper sex education, information campaigns and access to counselling services and adequate quality healthcare. the report's demands touch on very important issues, such as maternal mortality and sexual violence, which must be addressed without debate. however, some of the articles that speak about, for example, the 'interaction between teachers and students' in the case of sex education, or the free expression of one's gender, have been formulated in my opinion simply wrongly and in this form i do not agree with them. decisions on very sensitive issues such as abortion should be taken by the member states. that is why i have decided to vote against the report in the final analysis.
in writing. the sexual and reproductive health and rights report is an initiative report and a catch-all. it contains proposals not only on women's health and access to reproductive care but also in a scholarly mix: "taboo-free and interactive" sex education for young children in school, assisted reproduction for lesbians and unmarried women... given the confusion of the political ideas defended in this own-initiative report, which very often fall under the subsidiarity of the member states, i voted for its referral back to committee and i am sticking to the political line laid down in france for more than 35 years by the veil act, especially since simone veil (epp) was the first female president of the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the edite estreli report on reproductive and sexual health and rights. in view of the difficult situation of the poles, which is the result of the application of restrictive anti-abortion laws, i consider the most important aspects raised in the estreli report to be: 1. recognition of the right of women to decide freely and responsibly whether to have children, and if so, how many, when and at what intervals. such a right is essential for their personal, social and economic development. the consequence of this position is that access to legal, safe abortion is a women's right and lack of access is a human rights violation. 2. emphasize that member states should regulate and monitor the use of the conscientious objection clause by doctors in order to guarantee respect for the individual's right to reproductive health care and to ensure access to legal services provided at an adequate level and to an affordable system of medical referrals. 3.call on all member states to provide compulsory sex education tailored to the age and perception of children. the higher rates of childbirth, abortion and sexually transmitted diseases among adolescents are often explained by a lack of access to sex education of the right level and scope. statistics confirm that the highest rates of teenage pregnancy and abortion occur in the eastern european member states.
in writing. - the resolution is a response to the mass support of eu citizens for the 'one of us' initiative, which has already been signed by almost 1.5 million eu citizens. the initiative aims to stop eu funding for abortion, while the ep's draft resolution calls for continued funding for organisations providing abortion services. such action undermines confidence in the european parliament, as it clearly goes beyond the competences that member states have granted to the eu. this is an area where each member state is entitled to pursue its own policy. we oppose the disregard for the division of powers between the european union and the member states, as demonstrated by the abovementioned resolution, and call for its rejection. we also recall that before poland joined the eu, the sejm of the republic of poland adopted a resolution on the sovereignty of our state in ethical and family matters.
madam president! the sahel is the poorest region in the world. the people of this city are facing a humanitarian catastrophe. reports indicate that it has the highest infant mortality rate. regular ethnic conflicts are not conducive to the pursuit of sustainable development. the situation is made worse by such factors as widespread corruption and organized crime. so bringing peace, democracy, good governance should be the absolute priority for the sahel. although the conflict in mali has raised international attention to the region's problems, it is still home to some of the worst human rights abuses by islamic militants. particularly disturbing are the repeated incidents of child abuse. i hope that the european union will be committed to preventing the risk of further destabilisation of these countries. their full cooperation with neighbouring countries is also needed to combat transnational crime.
in writing. − i have lent my support to the report on the situation of human rights in the sahel region (2013/2020(ini)). the current situation in the sahel region is at a dire stage and deserves international attention and assistance. as one of the poorest regions in the world the ideas of democracy and human rights are often overshadowed by hunger and armed conflict. thus, it is very important for the international community to stand together to eradicate these issues and offer assistance in developing democratic governance and providing a platform for the recognition of fundamental human rights. in this day and age it is unfathomable that there are countries in such a state. we must do more for the greater good of mankind, as it reflects on everyone, especially those of us who are in a position to act. this report offers shocking data regarding the current situation and it is not pleasant by any stretch of the imagination. therefore i call on this house to continue its efforts and encourage those responsible to extend their efforts further.
in writing. as the libyan uprising escalated into civil war and the regime of muammar gaddafi began to regain control, france, italy and the united kingdom decided to take military action to save libyan democracy. as a result, they funded the world (and especially libya itself) in a conflict that lasted for months, and in which nato was dragged into. mr gaddafi lost his life and his power, but the world was not enriched by another fully democratic and law-abiding state. on the contrary, libya is now a black hole in regional security, with a negative impact on the entire maghreb and sahel region. the second anniversary of the arab spring is a good time to summarize the strategic implications of this process. the most important of these are geopolitical, affecting the long-term transformation of international processes in the middle east and often beyond. in this dimension, the arab spring has a distinctly negative impact on western interests.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur for the report on the human rights situation in the sahel. the very important issue of the continuing violation of human rights, particularly in mali, was raised. according to reports by the international human rights organization, there are mass executions by islamic militias in the region. political, social and economic conditions are continuously deteriorating and therefore action is needed to improve the situation in these areas. the key issue is also the vulnerability of borders in the sahel region, which results in the penetration of weapons, which only exacerbates the fighting and is a serious obstacle to building peaceful relations. the eu should do more to support and focus on eliminating threats to life and fundamental human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the corina creţu report on local authorities and civil society: europe's commitment to sustainable development. it should be stressed that the creation of a democratic europe is not only at governmental level, but above all at local level. it is civil society organisations, through their contact with citizens, that form the important link between local society and national governments. in addition, these organisations are a key tool in the fight against corruption and tax fraud. local authorities, which ensure the proper development of the regional economy, also have a very important role to play in ensuring a coherent policy for sustainable development. civil society organisations and local governments as implementing partners have a significant impact on the development and implementation of policy strategies. i believe that active cooperation between these organisations, regional institutions, private partners and individual citizens will contribute to building sustainable development at social, economic and cultural levels.
in writing. − a country's rapid and comprehensive development is possible with a well-functioning state apparatus and a developed civil society. it is when the people of a region take an interest in what is happening around them that the chances of prosperity and prosperity increase. when power is decentralised and competencies are distributed at lower levels, decisions are made more quickly and more effectively. their effects and consequences are immediately apparent. so self-government is a responsibility for the region, the local community, the small homeland. civil society organisations and local authorities play a huge role in shaping attitudes and building a democratic system. the union should therefore support civil society in partner countries through assistance to these structures. we need to develop educational programmes that make the youngest of us aware that every human being can make a difference by being active. support should also be provided to marginalised groups so that they can also actively participate in the formation of civil society. it is in local action, in local traditions and solidarity, that the greatest strength lies.
in writing. − the diversity of each country is a fundamental value of the european union as a whole. it is the balanced development of each individual country that guarantees successful cooperation that produces tangible results. active citizenship is the implementation of the principles of democracy on which the european union operates. the proper functioning of local authorities is essential for the smooth functioning of the whole structure. so it is the local authorities and civil society organisations that have the greatest responsibility. finally, local authorities have an important role to play in supporting education for development and raising awareness. it is necessary to define precisely the boundaries of the powers of the authorities at each level. many groups within civil society feel marginalised, so it should be the european union's task to effectively involve them and to enhance the diversity of the society. empowering and respecting diversity is key to building a democratic society. cooperation between local authorities and civil society organisations should also be encouraged, as it ensures territorial development and strengthens democracy at local level. the functioning and the law of the european union are changing at a very fast pace, so it is only natural that local authorities and organisations in different countries present different levels. the european union should therefore also be responsible for encouraging the exchange of knowledge and experience between the new and old member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of adopting the report on local authorities and civil society: europe’s engagement in support of sustainable development, because it is my belief that there is still a lot to do in the civil society building process. a report like this offers a chance to move to the next and higher level. much is said about the positive aspects of societyʼs participation in local governance, the result of which is prosperity and consequently social satisfaction. civil budgets are an interesting example of that kind of activity, engaging citizens in discussing the future of their cities. the recommendations outlined in the report could allow for strong and wide networks being developed between local authorities and civil organisations which could contribute to the sustainable development of the eu. the report highlights that citizen engagement is one of the substantial factors of decentralisation. my duty as a member of the european parliament is to support all activities which could provide a positive impulse for sustainable development.
in writing. - the concept of civil society has developed from the notion of self-determination presented by j. j. rousseau. originally, self-determination was understood as a limitation of the sovereignty of state power and an extension of the sovereignty of public authority. in this case, the power contract is replaced by a social contract. power loses its character of violence: the remnants of the violentia will be removed from the auctoritas of state power. according to this concept, everything is decided by the will of the people, which unites and reconciles everyone and everyone in a situation where everyone decides about everyone and everyone decides about everyone. the starting point for any consideration of civil society is the self-actualizing, autonomous, accepting, and also seeking approval from others. it participates in economic, cultural, domestic, associational and any other activity that arises and develops in local environments. these, in turn, are the source of such initiatives unconstrained by the pressure of state power. the opposite is true where the state does not create a legal framework for this type of activity.
in writing. - today we can observe several problems facing the current education system in the european union. the social group facing the greatest problems in the labour market is young people who apply for their first job immediately after leaving school. as the statistics of march 2013 show, the unemployment rate for people under 25 years of age in the union is 23,5%. to prevent such high unemployment, universities must put more emphasis on more effective education, which focuses on acquiring language skills and entrepreneurial knowledge and promotes a system of vocational placements. another major problem is the mismatch between the skills acquired and the needs of the labour market. to this end, close cooperation between educational institutions, businesses, regional authorities and employers' and students' organisations is essential. this cooperation would enable us to identify precisely what the market really needs for specific occupational specialisations or training. in the face of the current economic crisis and the ageing of the population, we must take special care to ensure that adequate financial resources are secured to support education, quality training and education among young europeans, because investing in education is investing in europe's future.
in writing. - one of the most serious problems and challenges facing the european union today is the alarming rate of unemployment, especially among young people. effective, accessible to all citizens and representing a high level of education is the most important instrument to prevent the current situation on the labour market. the union should support programmes for adult and lifelong learning so that people in employment have the opportunity to re-qualify and change jobs during their careers. every citizen should have the chance to live a life of value, and therefore education and training should be more accessible to the most vulnerable groups, i.e. socially disadvantaged groups, people with disabilities, minorities, older citizens and women. the attitude of the people concerned is no less important than education that is modern and adapted to the requirements of the labour market. active citizenship and social inclusion are crucial. therefore, non-formal learning, youth work and volunteering should be promoted and recognised on an equal footing with formal education.
in writing. − europe is facing the challenge of changing education systems that are not adapted to the needs of the labour market, leading to increased unemployment on the one hand and a shortage of skilled workers on the other. this situation results in thousands of young graduates being unemployed, while many employers have difficulty finding qualified workers. this is a situation that is disadvantageous to both sides. the only way to address it is to fundamentally overhaul the education system as a whole, starting at the lower levels of education, and ending at the higher levels. a thoughtful approach and sustainable educational solutions are needed to prepare learners for the challenges of a constantly changing labour market. such action should be taken at both union and member state level. dialogue and cooperation with regional authorities as well as with various educational institutions, businesses, social services and ngos is also necessary. the union is certainly in a position to facilitate the free movement of young people within europe and the mutual recognition of professional qualifications and skills, which leads to the penetration of national labour markets may result in at least partial saturation of these markets, both with suitably qualified workers and with decent work.
in writing. − the european commission presented its latest education strategy under the heading 'a new approach to education: investing in skills for better socioeconomic outcomes'. there are many elements that etwinners might be interested in. these relate both to specific subjects and to the use of technology in the learning process; some of them are briefly described below: • increased emphasis on the development of general and basic skills at all stages of education, in particular entrepreneurship and it skills. • a new benchmark for language learning. • investment is needed to create world-class vocational education and training systems and to increase the use of learning by doing. • member states must recognise more qualifications and skills, including those acquired outside the formal education and training system. • make full use of technological solutions, in particular the internet. access to education should be increased through open educational resources. • these reforms must be supported by well-trained, motivated and enterprising teachers. one of the main elements of this strategy is to support teachers to achieve better learning outcomes. the aim of the strategy is to improve the quality of teacher education and the efficiency and effectiveness of education.
in writing. - thank you to the rapporteur for the report on the new approach to education. the high rate of unemployment, especially among young people, is prompting action to prevent this. it is therefore necessary to provide young people with support and to orient the education system to the needs of society and the labour market. the european commission has published a report on the implementation of the european year of lifelong learning in the european union. however, it is crucial that each member state is able to decide for itself the future of its education system. i therefore believe that the european union should not interfere with these powers in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the management of the european union's preaccession funds in the areas of judicial systems and the fight against corruption in the candidate countries. the fight against corruption and organised crime is one of the priorities of every country applying for membership of the european union. the rule of law is the basis for the functioning of the market economy, which is the domain of the union. recalling the experience of the croatian accession negotiations, it should be noted that a strong political commitment to combating organised crime and corruption was key to the success of the european union integration process.
in writing. − with the end of the 2007/2013 budget period, which included the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa) for countries wishing to join the european union, lessons from previous years should be drawn to apply more strategically the measures under the new instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa ii) to allow for more effective assistance. the fight against corruption and crime should be a priority on the road to full membership of the european union. a state governed by the rule of law and a democracy cannot exist without a fully independent, predictable and effective judicial system. in a state governed by the rule of law, the judiciary must inspire the confidence of both business and the public, and judges, prosecutors and other officials should be able to undergo continuous professional training, continuously improving their qualifications and thus the level of the judiciary as a whole. another instrument of civil society is a free press and independent media, which are essential tools in the fight against corruption. the ipa should therefore cover not only governments, the judiciary, administrative structures, but also the media. free access to information, freedom of expression are what a well-functioning civil society, a state based on the rule of law, is hard to imagine without, and this is what both candidate and potential candidate countries are striving for.
in writing. - there's a long line in the lobby waiting for the community. some of them are quite impatient, they've been waiting for over 30 years... so far, only one rider has a ticket with a date on it. the european parliament voted on its 'enlargement' position in mid-april. the document provides an assessment of the progress made in preparing for eu membership by eight candidate countries: croatia, fyrom (former yugoslav republic of moldova), iceland, montenegro, serbia, bosnia and herzegovina, kosovo and turkey. the eu as a nobel peace prize winner maintains its will to enlarge the community with other countries in the name of strengthening peace, security and prosperity on the continent and enhancing the eu's standing on the international stage despite the economic crisis. the report on the enlargement strategy, beyond assessing the progress of countries on their way to the eu, focused on the reforms these countries need to undertake to join the community. membership of the eu is subject to very specific conditions for achieving 'full democratisation', including: effective participation of the public in political life, an independent and efficient judiciary, an efficient public administration, effective tools to fight corruption, guarantees of freedom of expression, assembly, equal opportunities for all citizens with respect for minority rights. in addition, economic stabilisation is required.
in writing. −patient safety is the first principle of health protection. every point in the care process has a gap that needs to be closed to protect the patient as best as possible. adverse reactions may be due to problems in practice, products, procedures or systems. improving patient safety requires improving a comprehensive, nationwide system that includes a wide range of measures to improve efficiency, environmental safety and risk management, including infection control, safe use of medicines, equipment safety, safe clinical practice and a safe patient care environment.
in writing. − protection of businesses against misleading advertising practices remains low in many countries. the most prominent example is the offering of business directory listings on unfair terms, resulting in the evasion of fees. the victims of such practices are mainly micro-enterprises. this is why close cooperation between governments, business organisations and company management seems necessary. i hope that the european commission will study this problem in depth and take action to inform the public. a european-wide list of misleading practices would be helpful, but not necessarily a list of companies subject to penalties. the idea of tax authorities monitoring companies that engage in dishonest practices is a source of mixed feelings. fiscal controls should concern fiscal irregularities and not cases of abuse of powers in relation to the activities carried out.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the cornelis de jong report on misleading advertising practices. as we know, advertising is now ubiquitous in the media and has a huge impact on the image of any company. it is also a very important element of any marketing strategy. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. this is particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the main driving force of the economies of many member states. dishonest advertising is sold in the form of erroneous payment forms, entries in business directories and is also very common in the domain environment, thereby negatively affecting competition in the internal markets. i therefore believe that it is appropriate to introduce a uniform level of protection for companies in the european union and to create a common database of companies engaged in fraudulent activities. i am also convinced that international cooperation between the national law enforcement authorities of the member states will greatly improve the detection and prosecution of dishonest service providers.
in writing. − misleading marketing practices have developed and may take many forms; one of the most prominent practices is misleading directory company schemes. in this scenario, a company sends out forms inviting businesses to complete or update their business name and contact details ‘for free’, only for the businesses to discover later that they have, in fact, unintentionally signed up to a contract to be listed in a business directory at a yearly charge of eur 1 000 or more. given the frequency of these practices and the fact that the level of protection varies between member states, the commission published a communication on protecting businesses against misleading marketing practices and ensuring effective enforcement. the current report supports the communication but asks for additional measures, particularly in the field of prevention and information, enforcement and prosecution. seeing that misleading marketing practices are not a purely european phenomenon, the report further stressed the importance of international cooperation in combating these practices. taking into account the vulnerability of businesses and smes, especially in the current financial circumstances, i believe that the eu should adopt a common position to minimise the practices of misleading advertisements. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − unfair advertising practices are a serious barrier to the internal market and make it difficult for businesses to operate. i voted in favour of the report because it points to the need for better information exchange between member states and also supports the commission's intention to explore the possibility of drawing up an eu-wide blacklist of misleading marketing practices. international cooperation to combat such practices is key here, as misleading marketing practices are often cross-border in nature. it is equally important to inform companies about the forms of these unfair marketing practices. companies often do not realize that, for example, agreeing to a free listing in a business directory can result in hidden costs of up to several thousand dollars, and these unfair practices can take many different forms. the commission and the member states should therefore work together to promote awareness and information initiatives for all businesses and to exchange best practices between them to raise awareness of the risks. the european commission's communication on this issue is a step in the right direction, but we can be even more ambitious and take additional measures, for example in the areas of prevention, information, enforcement and prosecution, to protect businesses from unfair trading practices. the report adopted today also addresses these issues.
in writing. - today, each of us, often without realizing it, is the target audience of advertising. when we watch television, listen to the radio, read the newspaper, or surf the internet, we are bombarded with all kinds of advertisements. this is justified (advertising is often the biggest source of income for a tv, radio, publishing house or website owner) if it is presented in a transparent way, clearly separated from the rest of the content and presents a genuine commercial offer. however, the situation is radically different when advertising is hidden between the lines of a programme or text, presented as part of the content of a publication or broadcast, or when it offers false goods and services. the consumer is simply being deceived, exposed to financial loss and sometimes even to breaking the law. attempts to extort money are also common (who among us has not received an offer to use the money of an african millionaire who is legally obliged to transfer his fortune to an account we provide?). unfair advertising practices are extremely widespread and cause serious problems not only for individual consumers but for entire businesses, harming the citizens and economies of the member states. regulations are therefore necessary to simplify complaint procedures, to ensure assistance to victims of fraud and to eliminate sources of unfair practices.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the report on misleading advertising practices because i feel obligated to support every action to prevent smes in europe from illegal practices exposing them to loss. the report states that smes lose amounts of several billion euro because of misleading advertisements. all can agree that the european economy depends on such entrepreneurs. it is important to protect them especially in a time of crisis. we should remember that smes provide two out of every three private sector jobs and contribute to more than half of the total value-added created by businesses in the eu. one of the main ideas of the founding fathers was a free market in the eu. nowadays we are close to it. in my view a free market is not only about liberalisation but also about fair play regulations and this report is the perfect tool to enforce these kinds of rules. our work and care for smes could be a great motivation for people who want to set up a business. therefore the eu should itself encourage entrepreneurs to invest and develop.
in writing. − if an act of unfair competition or unfair market practice infringes the collective interests of consumers, the president of the occp may take action to eliminate the practice. some businessmen, in order to increase their profits, resort to methods that have little to do with honest competition for customers. many abuses are associated with advertising products and services. however, it is not only other traders (competitors) and the advertisers themselves (consumers) who can fight misleading advertising, but also the president of the office for competition and consumer protection. misleading advertising is any advertising message which, by any means, including the manner in which it is presented, misleads or is likely to mislead the persons to whom it is addressed or to whom it is sent, with the result that it is likely to affect their business conduct or, for that reason, to harm or be likely to harm competitors.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his comprehensive report on all the main issues related to the fight against corruption. corruption must be fought because it is a pathology that destroys social life and the state, and leads to injustice and injustice. we should fight it not only by prosecuting it, but also - and above all - by preventing it, by eliminating the corruption-producing mechanisms, the pathologies that occur, for example, in the creation of laws that encourage corruption and allow the arbitrary conduct of state institutions. i have a problem with this report, however, that paragraph 13, which proposes the introduction of a european public prosecutor, is unacceptable and if the proposal to delete this entry is not adopted, i will not be able to vote in favour of this report. let us not create new european institutions, let us cooperate within the framework of the existing state institutions.
mr. chairman, please! i sometimes get the impression that criminal organisations have less difficulty in establishing rules for each other to operate in the european single market than member states do in establishing rules to combat this criminal activity, and that is a poor summary of our work over the last year and a half. the content of the excellent report drawn up by mr iacolino makes us aware that the scope of the activities of criminal organisations is growing, that they are increasingly affecting the social and economic life of the member states. the security of our citizens is at stake, and the eu economy is suffering billions of dollars in losses. it seems that in our hearings and workshops over the past year and a half, we have been able to map this crime and identify what actions should be taken to effectively counter it. the problem is that we now, together - the member states and the institutions of the european union - have the will and the strength to fight corruption and money laundering, the activities of organised crime. two things are needed: a willingness to cooperate and the introduction of community minimum standards at criminal and civil law level to combat this crime more effectively. i would also like to stress very strongly that perhaps nowhere is the speed and efficiency of the response of both the legislative and the executive powers so necessary as in the fight against crossborder crime, which uses increasingly sophisticated instruments and takes on increasingly surprising forms.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. ignorance of the law is no good. we all know that. however, it is difficult to expect every citizen to be well versed in the law, especially when the case is complex and involves, for example, a cross-border dispute. the e-justice portal is therefore intended to be an easy way to access both national and union legislation. however, the e-justice portal should not be merely a platform for the exchange of good practice or a training tool for judicial staff. we need to reach out to citizens who often do not know where to go for advice, initial information or help in civil, criminal or commercial matters. we need to put more emphasis on promoting such online platforms among the citizens of the european union, thereby increasing legal awareness and the opportunities that community law gives us. in its resolution, the european parliament underlines the importance of this portal in terms of disseminating knowledge and quick access to standardised forms or promoting online tools allowing for efficient communication between different legal systems. we are now in the final stages of the 'justice' programme for 2014-2020, in which we emphasise the importance of easy and rapid access to justice for all citizens. i believe that the e-justice portal has the potential to become a window on the world of the rule of law for all citizens of the union. it is therefore absolutely essential to promote and develop it further. to this end, it is necessary to clearly define the basis and detailed forms of its operation for the following years, including the financing of this project. i would like to thank mr leškevičius for the proposals which the council is already putting forward and to assure him of parliament's willingness to cooperate so that this programme can function as well as possible.
mr. chairman, please! the e-justice platform has been in operation for over 3 years and we are that much closer to the goal of turning the european portals into a universal contact point in the field of justice. today, every european can access legal and judicial procedures from all the union's national systems, in all the official languages. we have the european prosecution order, the european payment order, and after the implementation of the reforms in the brussels i package, we will also have the european civil litigation tool. however, in order to ensure the proper use of these instruments, citizens must have access to information about them and the possibility to report their possible ineffectiveness. i am currently dealing with a very sad case of a child abduction from poland by a greek father who has been deprived of parental rights, and i can see how flawed the european arrest warrant system is in this case. the requirements of a legally effective injunction are ignored by the greek authorities and there is no effective way to enforce them. in such cases, the e-justice platform could be used to bring a complaint for negligence or simply to put pressure on a state that is not complying with european rules. in addition to calling for practical and substantive improvements to the e-justice platform, i would also like to call on the committees of the member states to promote the portal more and to disseminate its ideas among citizens.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to point out that the idea of the e-justice platform is a good idea. the experience of the last four years confirms this. this web-based tool speeds up the flow of information above all. but the fundamental question is: who benefits most from this system? if you look at it, it's mostly the national administrations that benefit. i think that much more care should be taken to ensure that citizens can benefit from this system. i have two specific proposals to make in this connection. the first proposal is that translations of judgments, including those of the european court of human rights, should be published on this platform. second sentence there should also be precise models of the individual pleadings.

a recent report from the european commission clearly confirms that the vast majority of european union citizens move to another member state primarily for the purpose of taking up employment. the commission also made it clear that the so-called 'benefit tourism' is neither widespread nor systematic. studies show that citizens who migrate within the european union are a great asset to the host country. between 2004 and 2009 alone, migrants contributed 1% to the gdp of the eu-15. in addition, by working hard, they pay taxes in the receiving countries and contribute to the common budget, thereby gaining the right to the social benefits they have earned. it should also be noted that immigrants from the european union represent only a small proportion of those receiving benefits and their impact on national budgets is also insignificant. of course, there will always be individuals who want to exploit the system, and i think everyone in this room would agree that these practices should be fought. but let's not let this kind of behaviour fuel the anti-immigration and anti-european rhetoric that we've been dealing with lately. it is also depressing that the criticism often directed at workers from central and eastern europe is a populist attempt to win over the electorate or a manifestation of the irresponsible attitude of some governments, which effectively hinders citizens from functioning together in europe. when we talk a lot about the alleged abuse of the social systems of the member states, we rarely talk about how often migrant workers are deprived of their rights and the difficulties they face before they take up work. many member states continue to increase the barriers to access to their labour markets, forgetting the value of people who are willing to work, dynamic and full of ideas. so let's not discourage them at the outset and instead focus on proper implementation and enforcement.

in writing. the european semester, or european period of evaluation and coordination of economic policies, was established by one of the six-pack regulations in november 2011 and is intended to provide a framework for the implementation of the european semester. it is the basic framework for enhanced economic governance in the eu. it is intended to combine the actions provided for in the europe 2020 strategy and the so-called 'euro plus' pact. we are now in the fourth cycle of the european semester. it should be noted that the priorities set out by the commission in the context of the european semester are similar to those of previous years, i.e. continuing diversified and pro-growth fiscal consolidation, promoting economic growth and competitiveness, tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, and improving the functioning of public administration. importantly, there are already some signs of improvement in the european economy this year. the crisis-ridden euro area countries, which have undertaken difficult reforms, are slowly coming to grips with the situation. their imbalances in economic contacts are reduced and their competitiveness is increased. this in turn translates into a slow recovery in financial market confidence and a decline in the cost of debt financing.

in writing. − exports of drug precursors which require a customs declaration, including exports of drug precursors leaving the customs territory of the community after being stored in a free zone with control type i or in a duty-free warehouse for at least 10 days, require an export authorisation. exports of category 3 drug precursors require an export authorisation in cases where pre-export notification is required or where these substances are exported to certain destination countries (annex iv to commission regulation (ec) no 1277/2005).
in writing. − as with all drugs, the question of their potential precursors is controversial. on the one hand, we must bear in mind the possibility of illegal use of these substances on the black market, and on the other hand, we must bear in mind that they are legal components of many legal products. they are also often produced by small and medium-sized enterprises, for whom stricter rules on monitoring and registration of these substances may represent an additional burden. a careful balance must therefore be struck between the control of their " leakage " into the illicit market and the related burden on manufacturers legally using these substances . the report focuses on anhydrous vinegar, which is used legally to make perfumes and aspirin, but can also be used to make heroin, amphetamines and cocaine. according to the centre for drugs and drug addiction, it is one of the most commonly used and seized precursors in europe. i support the commission's proposal to improve the monitoring of the trade in acetic anhydride, but without imposing additional bureaucratic administrative burdens on the operators. i also think it is appropriate to create a european database on drug precursors. my only concerns are the numerous delegated acts that have been applied, which in my view leave too much decision-making power in the hands of the commission, which could lead to future tightening on further substances without clear grounds and without consulting the council and parliament.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals used in many industrial processes that can be misused for the illicit production of drugs. the european union has recently been accused of weak control measures, especially on the use of acetic acid. in order to improve the control of the illicit diversion of drug precursors, i voted in favour of this report, supporting the desire to overcome the problem by strengthening the monitoring of the trade in acetic acid, the rules on registration and the establishment of a european database of operators authorized to produce it. i believe that a revision of the regulation in this direction will allow for more extensive checks and, as a result, improve both their capacity and their effectiveness.
in writing. - today in the plenary we voted on the drug precursors. these are chemicals that are commonly used in various industrial processes (plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes and detergents) but which may be used in ways that are not intended, i.e. to produce drugs. criminals rarely produce the drug precursors they intend to use for illicit drug production themselves, as their production often requires extensive infrastructure. instead, they often try to obtain drug precursors illegally, either through legitimate trade or by stealing. i believe that we should establish a european database on drug precursors, which will, among other things, make it easier for member states to report seizures and detentions of consignments as anonymously as possible and as minimally burdensome as possible in terms of the processing of personal data, taking into account the principle of limited data availability and modern privacy technologies. a european register of authorised operators and users should also be established to facilitate the verification of the legality of trade transactions involving scheduled substances and to enable undertakings to provide information to the competent authorities on their legal transactions involving scheduled substances.
in writing. − precursors are the main ingredients used to make synthetic and semi-synthetic drugs. although most people don't realize it, they are a key segment of drug crime. the polish law on drug addiction criminalizes the production, smuggling, trade, possession and storage of precursors. any of these acts committed for the purpose of illicit synthesis of drugs is punishable by a fine or imprisonment of up to 5 years. in this case, the most important thing for law enforcement is to prove that the precursors found are intended for the production of drugs. without this, only a fine is possible. another shortcoming is the absence of any provision in the legal act regarding the significance of the number of precursors. this means that in the eyes of the law, a person who smuggled a ton of bmk can be treated the same as a person who smuggled just one litre of the substance. there is also an article that punishes with a fine for failure to comply with the recordkeeping obligations of persons legally producing, transporting or trading precursors. this is very important because most precursors are dual-use substances, some of them very widely used in industry. such a provision in the law gives you some leeway to prevent precursors from being leaked from the legal market to the black market.
in writing. − the european e-justice portal is intended to act as a 'one-stop shop' providing information on european justice and european judicial proceedings. the portal is addressed to citizens, businesses, legal professionals and judicial staff.
mr president, i would like to make a few comments on mr brok’s report. firstly, ‘to establish a new and credible foreign policy’ is an indirect admission that we do not have such a policy. indeed, we do not – and we never will, unless it is imposed by those in the eu who are more equal upon those who are less equal. such a danger is not a figment of my imagination: the report states that the common foreign policy should be used ‘to overcome the inappropriate use of the veto within the council’. i do not know what an inappropriate use of the veto is – nobody does – but the statement is unabashed encouragement to intimidate those who dare to disagree. secondly, the report calls for the development of european media ‘to raise awareness of the common foreign policy’. this looks like an official blessing for political propaganda. for two-thirds of my life i lived in a communist system that tried to raise my awareness. it failed. please, baroness and dear colleagues, do not raise awareness – either mine or anyone else’s. thirdly, the report calls for a permanent seat for the eu on the security council. giving the eu a seat on the security council would make the eu a state, which it is not, and – god willing – never will be. such a statement is, in fact, an explicit affirmation of the federalist project, which is another reason why we should look at the common foreign policy with suspicion. fourthly, given the fact that the eu is notoriously undemocratic, a common foreign policy must mean another area of political unaccountability. do we not have enough of that already?
we are discussing today the common foreign and security policy of the european union. the european parliament's resolution, in paragraph 12, expresses its regret that the eu has not yet developed a clear strategy for its relations with the rest of the world and that its actions are defined more as reactions than as actions. the european parliament therefore acknowledges that four years after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which was supposed to give a new impetus to the union's so-called common foreign policy, the project has proved to be, to put it mildly, flawed. some in this room are calling the common foreign and security policy a joke, a costly joke for taxpayers. in this context, i would like to ask the high representative, mrs ashton, whether she thinks it is possible at all for the 28 member states to work out such a unified and clear strategy, and if so, what is the time horizon.

in writing. the creation of a single online market is clearly in the interest of the union as a whole. the obstacles and barriers that still exist prevent it from reaching its full potential. i agree with the commission that a market made up of 28 separate national telecommunications markets, with over 200 operators, cannot be friendly to either businesses or consumers. i therefore understand the commission's intentions in drawing up the legislative proposal. but i think the problem is so serious that it requires deep reflection and careful analysis. we cannot allow the legal arrangements adopted to make it even more difficult for the electronic market to function. the potential benefits are great, but the potential for harm from misregulation is also great. it is therefore perhaps surprising that the commission has decided to work at such a rapid pace. the doubts about the lack of sufficient public consultation on this proposal therefore seem justified. on the other hand, the internet sector is so dynamic that every month of delay can weaken our competitiveness in the global market. the european parliament must therefore do its utmost to ensure that the work on this regulation proceeds smoothly and leads to the adoption of solutions combining business facilitation with high consumer protection.

member of the commission. - madam president, even if you think i am a great carpathian specialist, because i come from a member state which has a large part of the carpathian area on its territory, i will speak today on behalf of the commission, in particular on behalf of my colleague johannes hahn, who is in charge of this dossier and who, unfortunately, was unable to be present. in general, the commission encourages closer cooperation between regions in order to improve the implementation of policies with a cross-border impact. for this reason, the commission supports and facilitates cooperation in the framework of macro-regional strategies. there are two of these: the baltic sea region and the danube region. i shall refer to them as they relate to the agenda. the aim of macro-regional strategies is to provide a coordinated response to problems which are more effectively tackled together than separately. the two existing strategies aim to overcome the obstacles to the development of the regions concerned and to exploit their potential. they encourage participants to overcome not only the limitations of national borders but also the barriers that restrict a more strategic and creative design of the assets in hand. the aim of macro-regional strategies is to mobilise new projects and initiatives to create a sense of shared responsibility. they are an important innovation for territorial cooperation and cohesion. in april this year, the commission published the first report on the implementation of the european union strategy for the danube region. it welcomed the good start of the strategy after two years of implementation. progress so far has included the establishment of innovative transnational projects, the creation of interconnections in the fields of energy and transport, the creation of joint measures to limit environmental risks, investments in education and training, and support for smes and new technologies. in june, the commission published a report on the added value of macro-regional strategies, in which it examines the work done so far in the baltic sea and danube regions. the report states that the strategies are effective from a strategic point of view, but also from a political point of view. it also stresses the need to improve their implementation and preparation. it is therefore necessary to adapt the strategies at all levels and to allocate sufficient staff to enable their effective implementation, and to align the available resources with the objectives of the strategies. as regards the countries in the carpathian chain, the commission would like to stress that almost all of them are included in the danube region strategy. only poland is not included. the challenges facing the carpathians are also already mentioned in the action plans of this strategy and are taken into account in its implementation. the same is true of the carpathian convention. in view of this, the commission does not see any reason at present to create an eu strategy for the carpathian region. it suggests that the countries of the region should instead use the danube strategy, which already provides a framework for cooperation in 11 priority areas covering a wide range of issues, including, probably, issues related more specifically to the carpathians. poland, which is not directly covered by the danube strategy, may nevertheless benefit from it on a case-by-case basis, in accordance with the principle of the open functional approach governing the operation of the strategy. the commission's report on the added value of macro-regional strategies, which was published on 27 june 2013, also highlights this aspect in the chapter 'new strategies'. the commission states that these strategies should be used only in specific cases where the participation of the european union is appropriate. this involvement is already guaranteed by the commission's strong involvement in the danube strategy, which, i repeat, could also cover the carpathian issues, since the member states concerned are also covered by this strategy.

in writing. - we voted today on the draft for the european maritime and fisheries fund. this project has caused a lot of controversy, and in the last few weeks i have received many emails and letters asking for the protection of polish interests. fish stocks are a commodity of vital importance for global food security. the fisheries sector and related activities are very often the main, if not the only, source of livelihood for citizens in many european regions. i supported the idea of investing in the modernisation of small fishing vessels that are over 35 years old. one of the conditions for receiving such aid was to reduce the energy consumption of such a vessel by 40%. the same applies to the possibility of replacing the engine in small vessels. the new engine shall have at least 40% less power than the previous one. the baltic fishermen's communities consulted in kołobrzeg highlight the alarming state of cod caused by the industrial fishing of sprat for fodder, which has upset the biological balance in the baltic waters. i therefore particularly support all the provisions concerning the restoration of the resources and the preservation of the biological balance of the baltic sea. financial support is important for the change of fleet, but it is even more important to ensure that there is something to fish.
in writing. − on 10 july, the european parliament's fisheries committee held a preliminary vote on the new subsidy framework, the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). amendment 32b to the emff allows for financial assistance of up to eur 80 000 for the construction of new fishing vessels. such aid makes it possible to continue the vicious cycle of overfishing. in practice, this will mean that more vessels will be coming into the seas and oceans to reach the last of the unfished stocks, causing a drastic decline in their numbers. the last chance to change this is to vote in the european parliament's plenary session. i therefore call on members of the european parliament to oppose such use of public money for the next decade. if this does not happen, there will be no fish in the future, and therefore no fishermen! experience shows that funding for the construction of new vessels contributes to the problem of overfishing. this is why this aid has been phased out since 2004, following the 2002 reform of the common fisheries policy. in a situation where two thirds of the eu's fish stocks are overfished, resulting in annual losses of eur 2.2 billion, opening up the possibility of financing the construction of new vessels would be a huge step backwards and a serious misuse of taxpayers' money.
mr. chairman, please! i hope that, as this year's forum is taking place in warsaw, poland's strategic climate interests will be reflected in the decisions taken at the forum. the only question is, why is the conference being organized on the most important polish national holiday? i am particularly grateful to the visegrad group countries for their commitment to softening the text of the eu declaration for the november conference. the controversial provision calling on the community to increase its carbon dioxide emissions reduction to 30% by next year has been removed. the more difficult it is to accept the demands of some groups, such as the unilateral target of reducing emissions by up to 50% by 2030. given the current economic situation in less prosperous member countries, such rigorous proposals cannot win wide approval.
in writing. − cop 19 is the conference of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change. the treaty, which has been ratified by 195 parties, sets out a framework for international cooperation on the issue of climate change on earth. we voted on the resolution which will be the position of the european parliament at cop 19. the draft resolution put to the vote proposed that provisions be included which would lead to a sharp increase in energy prices. the adoption of such legislation is very unfavourable for poland, as it threatens to increase unemployment and energy poverty of families. that's why i voted to reject the resolution. and i also made seven amendments to the bill itself, all of which were designed to prevent the greenhouse gas reduction targets from being raised. i'm pleased to see the majority vote on my three amendments. they concern, inter alia, the withdrawal from the resolution of the 50% emission reduction target for 2030. i also voted against amendment no 12 tabled by the left-wing faction, which called for a total ban on shale gas extraction. the adoption of such an amendment would be contrary to the interest of poland, where shale gas deposits are estimated to be the largest in europe.
in writing. - i am in favour of supporting clean energy sources, preceded by an environmental analysis for shale gas. i see the potential value of unconventional hydrocarbon deposits, including shale gas, which can contribute to the diversification of energy sources, in line with the eu's climate policy guidelines. i support the efforts of the polish government to provide a full and reliable estimate of the location, availability and resources of shale gas deposits in poland, in conjunction with the demands for independent cost-benefit analyses of potential extraction of unconventional hydrocarbons. renewable energy sources should be used on a preferential basis so that poland's energy balance corresponds to the objectives set by the european union. low-carbon fossil fuel-based sources such as shale gas should be included in the energy mix in order to balance market demand and reduce the risk of energy price increases and energy poverty.
in writing. - at the heart of these negotiations is the world's largest energy transition to date. in the past, it would have taken a long time for such a transformation to occur. the first source of energy was firewood, which was used until the 18th century, when it was replaced by coal. in just one century, the rapid pace of technological development has replaced coal as the primary energy source. climate change has forced a shift to renewable energy and increased energy efficiency. they've definitely accelerated evolution, which would have happened over a longer period of time anyway. we have an obvious challenge of capital circulation in our existing energy systems, and time is not our ally. scientific research shows that global greenhouse gas emissions cannot be higher than they are this decade, but must fall rapidly. moreover, if we are to reduce the costs to humanity, the peak of emissions must come soon. extreme weather events around the world provide ample evidence that these costs are rising and that they are particularly painful for the most vulnerable populations.
mr. chairman, please! corruption, organized crime, and money laundering are global pathologies. they are destroying the very fabric of democratic states, and they are a serious problem for societies in developing countries. the elimination of similar threats is essential for the proper functioning of an international organisation such as the european union, which should take concrete measures to that end. a comprehensive legal framework and enhanced judicial cooperation between member states are essential elements for effective crime prevention in the face of the opportunities offered by the free movement of persons and the internet. the creation of a separate european public prosecutor's office would not necessarily be a good solution in my view. the deepening of centralisation is unlikely to improve the mobility and efficiency of national law enforcement agencies, nor will the unconvincing extension of eurojust's powers.
in writing. - the report by mr iacolino, as well as the work of the crim special commission over the past year and a half, has given the problem of organised crime a european dimension at last, and the instruments to be adopted to combat it. the proposal to set up a single european prosecutor's office, which must involve as many member states as possible, is one such step, if the fight against organised crime and money laundering is to be truly effective and robust. the crim commission's final report was intended to set the stage by giving a particular impetus to cooperation between each member state in order to defeat organised crime.
in writing. − the mandate given by the european parliament to the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering (crim) was to analyse and assess the extent of organised crime, corruption and money laundering in terms of their impact on the activities of the european union. it also included an assessment of eu legislation on organised crime and money laundering. the crim final report recalls recommendations on, among other things, the definition of corruption at eu level, the harmonisation of criminal law on money laundering, the abolition of banking secrecy, and the blacklisting of corrupt companies in public procurement. the network of the judicial system in the european union should also be strengthened. organized crime is no longer bound by territorial boundaries. the european union has 3 600 criminal organisations that are taking advantage of the opportunities offered by economic globalisation and new technologies by entering into agreements with criminal groups in other countries. in order to tackle the economic interests of criminal organisations, we should create a uniform and coherent legal framework and strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the report on organised crime, corruption and money laundering: recommendations on action and initiatives to be taken (final report) (2013/2107(ini)). in doing so i am supporting the pursuit of justice over organised crime and cartels that are having a negative impact on our union. this report sets out a consistent and uniform regulatory framework designed to strike at the economic heart of organised crime and strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level. in doing so it provides the european citizen with safety and a mindset of justice. we all know that organised crime costs us millions of euros every year and the implementation of this legislation will cut the costs to the taxpayer significantly. at the same time this legislation will allow for a freer flow of information between authorities in order to catch and prosecute those associated with crime rings. all citizens have the right to live safely in our union and this report furthers our ability to give them this safety.
in writing. - the european union must take up the challenge of responding to crime on a global scale with the same impact. new and sophisticated forms of organised crime, corruption and money laundering require new political commitments at the highest levels and new social paradigms to tackle and combat these crimes. law enforcement and banks must prepare for a long battle against money laundering and terrorist financing, especially in a transit country like poland.
in writing. − it is worth noting that, unfortunately, these types of crime continue to develop in europe. the following figures illustrate this: europol estimates that as many as 3600 transnational criminal organisations are currently active in the european union. these groups are involved in trafficking in human beings and human organs, forced prostitution, and labor camps. this alone generates profits of eur 25 billion per year. the number of forced labourers in the eu exceeds 880 000, of whom 270 000 are victims of sexual exploitation. the illegal trade in cigarettes is worth over eur 10 billion. cybercrime is becoming a plague, causing increasing economic losses, affecting millions of consumers and costing europe an estimated eur 290 billion a year. we cannot effectively eradicate corruption. it is estimated that more than eur 1 billion is paid in bribes in europe each year. so the question is, can we fight this?
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft resolution on the european neighbourhood policy because i agree with the authors that the european parliament must be fully involved in the implementation of the neighbourhood policy and regularly informed about the progress of the reform process in these countries. joint action by all the institutions of the european union to promote development and reform in neighbouring countries is a key element in the drive to improve the situation in the union's neighbourhood and leads to closer political, economic and cultural relations between them. i agree that the union should consistently set demands on the authorities in the partner countries, while at the same time not forgetting to support the development of civil society and ngos in all its aspects. we must remember that integration with the european union is based above all on the sharing of fundamental values such as democracy, the rule of law and human rights. they can only be implemented if there is real social change in the partner countries. therefore, funding for the neighbourhood policy should be directed not only to support institutional reforms, but also to the citizens of these countries, through support for civil society organisations and associations, educational programmes and international youth exchanges.
