in writing. − the european union's neighbourhood policy is geared towards supporting the strengthening of democracy and promoting economic growth. the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument, on the other hand, should support those neighbourhood policy objectives. the various advantages, such as visa facilitation and the prospect of a visa-free regime, should be based on a 'neighbours first' policy. the vienna summit in november will be a significant development milestone for the eastern partnership and an important step in the review of the eu's neighbourhood policy in order to achieve the desired outcome. cooperation in ensuring the security of energy supply is one of the priorities of the eastern partnership and the european neighbourhood policy 2014-2020 and the vienna summit should therefore provide an impetus for closer cooperation in the energy sector as well. there are also territorial disputes between the eastern partnership countries themselves; therefore, the eastern partnership must be linked to and respect the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity and the right of self-determination of peoples, including the settlement of the nagorno-karabakh conflict. russia is using aggressive fighting tactics to persuade the eu's eastern partners to move closer to the eu and invite them to join its customs union. moscow's pressure has already led armenia to abandon the eu agreement and instead 'voluntarily' opt for the russian customs union. it is important that the eu provides the necessary support to the eastern partnership countries facing similar pressures.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp), launched in 2004, is the european union's policy towards neighbouring countries not currently covered by the membership perspective. the legal basis for the functioning of the epc is article 8 of the treaty on european union, which provides that the union shall develop special relations with its neighbouring countries, aiming to establish an area of prosperity and good neighbourliness, based on the values of the union and characterised by close and peaceful relations based on cooperation. the eps currently covers the european union's relations with the 15 neighbouring states and the palestinian authority. the political basis for relations with these countries is the association agreements (with the southern partners) and the partnership and cooperation agreements (with the eastern neighbours, now also replaced by association agreements). the action plans are the central element of the enp and their implementation is supported by the union and co-financed from the budget of the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument. russia, whose relations with the eu are based on the implementation of the four space programme, has chosen not to participate in the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − i thank the rapporteur for presenting the report on the european neighbourhood policy, which takes account of the desire to strengthen the partnership. as you know, all the partner countries are pursuing political, economic and social reforms in different ways, declaring their support for and desire to join the european union. it is gratifying that concrete action plans have been put forward to improve relations with partner countries. this will allow for greater economic integration between the eu and these countries. the partnership policy is primarily about promoting democracy, respect for human rights, combating illegal immigration, and supporting the economic, financial and social sectors. however, mutual needs and different aspirations should not be forgotten, while the good of the policy and the balance between the eu and the partner countries should be taken into account.

in writing. − after the introduction of the euro, the sound public finances were ensured by the stability and growth pact, which set clear rules setting well-known limits on the budget deficit and public debt (3% and 60% respectively). however, the global economic and financial crisis has exposed shortcomings in economic governance and budgetary surveillance at eu level. the european semester for economic policy coordination launched in 2010-2011 and the six package legislative proposals, which strengthened various aspects of the stability and growth pact, have effectively addressed these challenges. however, given the increased interdependence of fiscal policy in the single currency area, there is a clear need for even stronger mechanisms for the euro area. in november 2011, the commission therefore proposed two further regulations to strengthen budgetary surveillance in the euro area.

in writing. − calls for stricter border controls across europe will increase rather than reduce the risk of tragedies like the one near lampedusa, says an immigration expert. this is why the union should reform its asylum policy in the first place. the boat fire on 3 october off the coast of lampedusa, which claimed the lives of some 200 refugees and migrants, has already prompted a loud call from governments and international organisations for urgent action against human trafficking. it's not new. in the last decade, this has been a typical response to this kind of tragedy in the southern reaches of europe. this kind of logic turns everything upside down, because what is in these events is the effect is taken as the cause. after all, it is the tightening of border controls that forces migrants to make dangerous journeys and makes them increasingly dependent on human traffickers in their efforts to cross the border. this migration is mainly driven by the continued demand for cheap labour in agriculture, the service sector and other informal industries. a significant minority of these immigrants are refugees from their violence-ridden home countries. until more legal channels of immigration are established and refugees have access to asylum procedures, most of these people are likely to continue to arrive illegally.

in writing. the culture and education committee adopted the regulation and budget for the erasmus+ programme for 2014-2020 of €14.8 billion. this is an opportunity for a hundred thousand europeans to gain new scientific experience and to improve their language skills. this budget will offer master's students not only scholarships but also loans. a new system of guarantees and credits will also be created, allowing for the completion of a two-year master's degree at a european university. erasmus has already benefited nearly 3 million students from the european union and eastern partnership countries over the past 12 years, including over 130 000 from poland. our universities have accepted over 35,000 foreign students. the network of the programme includes 4 000 eu universities, including 315 polish universities. poland is one of the countries that makes the best use of the erasmus programme. the tempus and erasmus mundus programmes have been a great success in the eastern partnership countries since their inception. i welcomed the extension of the erasmus+ programme to the eastern partnership countries, which is a continuation of cooperation with third countries. quality education is the foundation of the prosperity and stability of our societies. without a good education system, we will not grow or develop.
in writing. the adoption by the european parliament of a new extended erasmus programme with an increased budget, called erasmus+, is a much-anticipated decision. the new eu erasmus+ programme will have a budget of almost €15 billion and will bring together all eu education and training programmes such as comenius, erasmus, erasmus mundus and leonardo da vinci under one name, as well as supporting sports programmes for the first time. there is no doubt that erasmus+ is the best way to contribute to the europe 2020 strategy, as it serves the education, openness, innovation and entrepreneurship of young people. this is why it is one of the few eu programmes to have increased its budget by 40%, even though the eu budget for 2014-2020 is smaller than the current one (2007-2013). it is hoped that the new programme will reduce the number of job vacancies (around 2 million) that remain unfilled due to a lack of suitably qualified people. increasing the skills of young people is likely to contribute to reducing unemployment not only through increased employment opportunities for erasmus participants, but also through their future entrepreneurial and job-creating activities. the new programme is also a certain inspiration for the direction of change in which we should go in the future. erasmus+ will not solve all the problems and is not a substitute for other youth activities that need to be undertaken at different levels of european and national policy, including regional and local development programmes.

rapporteur. − mr president, first of all i want to thank all my colleagues in the committee on constitutional affairs who worked on preparing our position on the interinstitutional agreement. we welcome the completion of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework (mff). everyone in europe has been working for that result to be put in place and for the money to start trickling down to the economies which need it. our job was to pronounce our view on how it was done in institutional terms, and after long deliberations we came to the conclusion that we could say ‘yes’ to the interinstitutional agreement. however, it has to be said that we are not fully satisfied with the way the negotiations were conducted. there were some who did not really recognise the nature of the reform we introduced with the lisbon treaty. so, while saying ‘yes’ in this context, we also want to look to the future and to take the greatest care that parliament’s prerogatives will be taken into account in a much more serious way when we look at the budget in 2016 and carry out the review, and especially when we start working on the next mff. when it comes to these future negotiations, parliament’s prerogatives must be taken much more seriously, especially with regard to agenda setting and decision making. we all know, especially if we look outside the committee on constitutional affairs, that in some cases too many things were pre-cooked and that our prerogatives, as written into the treaty, were not observed in full. however, as i said at the beginning, the time is ripe for a decision and it has been ripe for a number of months. that is why the committee on constitutional affairs has pronounced its views in an unequivocal way, saying ‘yes’, we think that we can go ahead.

in writing. - i voted with conviction for the budget of the european union for the next seven years. this is the first time that the budget has been lower than the previous one, but we must remember that europe is still in the midst of a financial crisis. the budget provides for expenditure for all eu countries of €690 billion, with poland receiving the largest share of €105 billion. i think this decision is right, because despite the progress poland has made, its average per capita income is still almost 40 percent below the average per capita income in the union. the use of eu funds therefore increases the chances of closing these disparities, and it is not only the size of the eu funds that is crucial, but also their wise use. i expect the european commission, when it analyses the proposals of individual countries, including poland, to give a strong preference to spending money that would create new jobs. the basic problem in europe today is not the construction of more swimming pools or museums, but youth unemployment. the european union budget must therefore be directed more towards the development of new technologies and the support of small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for 75% of new jobs.

in writing. − in march 2013 the commission tabled a request for an additional eur 11.2 billion on the 2013 budget to pay outstanding bills accumulated this year in many policy areas. these bills constitute the eu’s legal obligations stemming from past and current budgetary commitments made under the 2007-2013 multiannual financial framework (mff). reacting to the commission’s request, the council proposed a two-tier approach: a first tranche of eur 7.3 billion, followed by a second tranche of eur 3.9 billion at a later stage. while parliament wanted to remedy the shortfall as quickly as possible, in order to avoid the risk of a payment deficit and the rolling-over of unpaid bills into 2014, the member states failed to find agreement among themselves. given the council’s attempts to delay the transfer of the funds, parliament took a firm stand in its july 2013 resolution on the mff. in this resolution, parliament made the payment of eur 3.9 billion (draft amending budget (dab) 8/2013) a prerequisite for approving a deal on the 2014-2020 mff. the adoption of dab 8/2013 by the council on 30 october clearly reflects the success of parliament’s negotiation efforts, but most importantly it is the way forward to the adoption of a new financial framework.
in writing. − the spanish authorities argue that the financial and economic crisis led to a sudden collapse of the economy with an enormous impact in particular on demand for building construction. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the case at hand meets the requirements of the european globalisation adjustment fund, which has been created in order to provide additional assistance to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. in spain, where the annual growth rate of construction activity was higher than the european average, a slowdown in construction activity was anticipated for the medium term. i understand, however, that manufacturers of building materials could not have anticipated the combination of rising imports of construction materials and the extreme slowdown of construction activity as a consequence of the financial crisis.
in writing. − the egf aims to help workers who have lost their jobs as a result of changes in the global trade pattern to find new employment as quickly as possible. the fund, set up by the european union in 2007, will have a budget of up to 500 million per year. the egf may finance actions under an active labour market policy focusing entirely on the provision of assistance to workers made redundant as a result of globalisation, such as job-search assistance, career guidance, personalised training and retraining, including it skills and the certification of experience gained, assistance for supervised dismissals and the promotion of entrepreneurship or self-employment, specific measures limited in time such as job-search allowances, relocation allowances or allowances for persons undertaking training courses and training, motivation measures, in particular for disadvantaged workers or older workers, to enable them to stay on the labour market or to re-enter the labour market. applications for funding shall be submitted by the member states.
in writing. − the eu public procurement market is one of the most liberal and open markets in the world. on the one hand, this gives non-eu companies enormous opportunities to win contracts in the eu, but on the other hand, our european companies, and smes in particular, compete on their home market with companies from all over the world, from markets that remain virtually closed to them. this not only blocks the internationalisation of european companies, but also creates conditions for unhealthy competition. the government procurement agreement defines the parts of the public procurement market open to international competition, but its proper functioning depends, inter alia, on the number of countries that join it. given that the agreement entered into force many years ago, it is necessary to modify it in order to adapt it to the changing trade environment and to make it more attractive to states. i supported the recommendation adopted today as it provides greater clarity and transparency of the rules, also in the context of the current reform of eu public procurement. the eu has gained market opportunities by increasing the number of entities covered by the agreement or by extending the scope of the agreement to goods and services. this guarantees the eu around eur 30 billion in additional market access opportunities and thus greater opportunities for european businesses.
in writing. − the changes proposed in the government procurement agreement bring significant simplifications to the computerization of the procedure. this concerns in particular the introduction of electronic auctions and an electronic database containing tender notices. it is also important that the agreement guarantees the exclusion of the participants in the tendering agreement if they are found guilty of a criminal offence, misdemeanour or breach of professional ethics. the revised agreement also includes favourable conditions for developing countries to participate and a wide range of instruments they can use under the transitional arrangement, such as price preferences or offset commitments. the application of the agreement to countries such as switzerland, china, canada and taiwan allows the european union to increase its market opportunities. the agreement is an important marker for the procedures in the individual member states.
in writing. − the government procurement agreement (gpa), to which some wto members are parties, is a legally binding international agreement on access to public procurement markets. the gpa was unattractive to a large majority of wto members. changes to the existing agreement were also necessary in view of the changes in the general trading environment. the eu's interest in extending the scope of the gpa was driven by the fact that in many countries governments and their controlled agencies are the largest group of buyers of goods of all kinds, from basic goods to high-technology equipment. despite the fact that the eu has an open public procurement market, many countries give preferential treatment to domestic suppliers. the gpa provides european companies with legal certainty in accessing foreign markets. the new rules include a number of new elements. the possibility of using electronic auctions is provided for and the amended qualification rules will ensure that companies found guilty of serious crime, other serious misconduct or breach of professional ethics can be excluded from the procurement procedure. in addition, the revised rules introduce a reference in line with eu public procurement directives to technical specifications, which enables contracting authorities to include environmental considerations in technical specifications. at the same time, the existing statistical reporting obligations have been simplified. i therefore voted in favour of the agreement.
in writing. − i welcome the report on the conclusion of the protocol amending the agreement on government procurement. i am hopeful that the negotiated changes and the extension of the current membership will contribute to a better functioning of the public procurement market. it is very important to draw attention to the rules and regulations that will increase the transparency of public procurement rules. this will make it possible to achieve greater effectiveness in the fight against corruption or bribery, especially in third countries not covered by the gpa. i hope that this will also contribute to improving the quality of goods and services offered, as well as promoting high employment standards.

in writing. − the trans-european transport network (ten) is an important instrument for achieving growth, economic recovery and job creation by connecting and integrating the union, especially in the field of transport. the union clearly needs modern infrastructure that will facilitate the free movement of people, goods and capital and optimise the capacity of the transport network, while enhancing economic, territorial and social cohesion. tnt also has a positive impact on the competitiveness of the economy. with the schengen area in place and movement within europe easier than ever, the union should ensure that its citizens can travel and transport goods quickly and safely. poland is one of the countries that can benefit from a more efficient transport network to europe. the proposal to add the via carpathia road route to the list of transport corridors, to build a road under the transport priorities of the ten-t programme and to support the construction of the s19 road was a particularly important amendment. unfortunately, we were unable to gather enough votes to pass it.
in writing. − the eu's transport network is essential for the development of the internal market, for mobility and therefore for job creation. a functioning trans-european transport network will allow the free movement of people and goods to be fully realised and will also be a tool for sustainable economic growth and regional cohesion. i supported the report because it deals with issues that are key to the single market and as the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, of which i am a member, rightly pointed out transport infrastructure should be considered not only from the perspective of its local usefulness but above all by pointing out its european added value. the current challenges in implementing the network are delays in the implementation of many projects, difficulties in financing projects or lack of coordination between the different financial instruments, and the new rules address these challenges. the report also rightly points out that the planning process should ensure appropriate consultation and participation of the citizens who are affected by the project. the transport network cannot be considered in isolation from the citizens, since these investments directly concern them. i agree that draft guidelines on the appropriate involvement of local and regional authorities and civil society in network-related projects should be developed and implemented jointly with these parties.
in writing. − the large legislative package on the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is one of the key projects of the european union. it is a fundamental pillar that generates development, employment and growth in the territories of interest. however, the current legislative package, as we know, has encountered some challenges that the new programming will have to overcome. i am referring in particular to the delay in the construction of the ten-t network, the difficulties in financing in a period of crisis and the problems encountered in coordinating the different instruments and the different actors involved. i believe that the package of regulations which has been approved proposes important strategic changes which will be able to solve these problems and give impetus to the construction of important infrastructure projects.
in writing. − europe must build missing links and remove bottlenecks in transport infrastructure, and strive to ensure sustainable transport for future generations. the new, improved union transport policy focuses on creating a coherent network, not on funding isolated projects as before. the core transport network will be built by 2030 and will be the basis for transport within the common market, while a dense network at regional and national level will be established by 2050. efficient transport will not only enable faster travel between our villages, cities and regions, but will also create new jobs. from now on, member states will be able to benefit from 26 billion euros. the only conditions that an infrastructure project must fulfil are that it must be in an advanced planning phase, create added value and be completed within a certain timeframe. the multimodal corridors defined in the connecting europe facility will allow for coordinated infrastructure development. they will help member states to obtain the best possible returns from the planned projects. they will also strengthen the involvement of regional and local authorities in the planning and implementation phase of projects that benefit all citizens.
in writing. − i have lent my support for the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on union guidelines for the development of the trans-european transport network (com(2011)0650/3 – c7-0375/2012 – 2011/0294(cod)). the reason for doing so is that this programme will have a substantive impact on the free movement of goods and persons. an accessible and efficient transport infrastructure is essential for the provision of operative transport services, is fundamental for freedom of movement and is vital for the ability of all regions in the european union to remain competitive within the single european market. a prerequisite for a well-functioning transport system is the presence of smart infrastructure. infrastructure investments have a very long pay-back period and offer advantages if correctly built or conceived for many generations. i think that we can all agree that for the newer member states this programme is very important for the connection with other states which will drastically improve commerce with the west. moreover the improved and new transport system will allow for an increase in safety particularly by way of building new roads.
in writing. − in the 2014-2020 budget, the european union foresees for the first time a dedicated pool of €33 billion at european level for the development of common infrastructure. finally, the priority european corridors for transport, energy and telecommunications were defined. two of the ten corridors are to run through the territory of poland. one from north to south, connecting the baltic states to the adriatic countries, and the other through berlin, poznań and warsaw to the eastern border of poland. but i would like to point out two important problems. first, we must ensure that investment is made in all modes of transport, not just road and rail. it is a serious mistake to underestimate inland transport, the development of which is important for many regions, including my kujawy-pomorskie province. secondly, the european commission should actively verify the detailed infrastructure proposals submitted by individual countries, which, as we know, always requires the approval of the european commission for investments exceeding 50 million euros. the network must connect the main cities in the regions, otherwise the roads and railways will not be used properly.

in writing. – the purpose of cohesion policy is to reduce disparities between the eu’s various regions by promoting economic growth, job creation and competitiveness. it is therefore considered one of the eu’s most important pillars, representing one third, or eur 325 billion, of the next multiannual budget. the agreement on this dossier was reached after 90 trialogue meetings, and over one year of negotiations. the final compromise is not to the full satisfaction of parliament. however, it includes many of our political priorities. on macroeconomic conditionality, the parliament gained a right of scrutiny, in structured dialogue with the commission, over decision-making procedures affecting the suspension of funding. suspensions will be adjusted in line with social and economic circumstances in the member states concerned. parliament also succeeded in raising the pre-financing rates (i.e. allowing support to beneficiaries immediately from programme adoption from 2.5% in 2014-16 to 3% in 2020-23) and co-financing rates (from 50% to 85% for the outermost regions and cyprus) and in limiting the performance reserve (to 6% instead of 7%). while the deal is not perfect, the finale compromise is an important step towards a more effective, better and more targeted use of the policy in the eu’s next financial framework.

mr. chairman, please! the main disadvantage of the reform of the agricultural policy is the lack of objective criteria for determining the amount of direct payments. as commissioner cioloş said in the previous debate, subsidies also have a non-treaty function of balancing financial flows between net payers and the eu budget. unfortunately, this is true, but it strikes at the fundamental principle of a level playing field in the single market and has nothing to do with fairness and integrity in such an important area of policy. the positive aspect of the reform is certainly the high degree of flexibility and even variety in the choices made, which is due to the wide diversity of agriculture in the european union. i am also pleased to see the introduction of the definition of an active farmer and more support for young farmers. it was also the right decision to postpone the entry into force of the new rules for the unw, i.e. farmers who work in difficult economic conditions.

in writing. − the agreement between the european union and the russian federation on drug precursors is a very important step in the attempt to tackle the problem of drug dependence. for both the european union countries and the russian federation, the problem of drug addiction is a difficult one to combat. the agreement is not only a tool for controlling the trade in drug precursors but also an expression of the implementation of an overall strategy on the approach to the production and consumption of drugs. it should also be remembered that the fight against drug crime is not only about fighting illegal substances of marginal production, but also about strict control of the very legal substances used to produce them. the agreement will certainly contribute to this objective also due to the fact that russia is a destination country for precursors. the mutual benefits of the provisions of the agreement and the mutual trust which the parties have in each other are an additional guarantee for the implementation of the provisions of the agreement.

in writing. − the better use of eu funds in times of economic crisis has become a priority. it is not always possible to allocate a higher amount of funds to certain activities, and changing economic and social circumstances also change the challenges. it has therefore become crucial to look for ways to make a greater impact with existing measures. the simplification of policy implementation is to become one of the main features of the 2014-2020 programme. experience shows that the diversity and fragmentation of rules governing spending programmes create an unnecessarily complex system. this not only places a burden on the administration and beneficiaries, but also discourages them from using the programmes. the full potential of the european funds is thus not being used. i support measures that make it easier to obtain funds and thus to use them better, but we cannot introduce rules that are detrimental to less prosperous countries. cohesion policy and the instruments implementing it are essential for the single market. they are an investment tool for growth and job creation by precisely meeting the investment needs of all regions. cohesion policy has not only contributed to reducing inequalities between member states and regions, but also to improving the union's economic situation and development. a common set of rules will maximise the effectiveness of all instruments under cohesion policy, the full operation of which ensures a sustainable economic recovery and enhances competitiveness.
in writing. − the esf has become a particularly important tool in times of economic crisis, when so many people, especially young people, are having difficulty finding employment in the labour market. it is from this programme that training and other activities to help people find employment can be financed. from the perspective of the internal market, professional mobility is particularly important and can be promoted through the esf. with the coming financial perspective, new challenges await us, and it is therefore important that the esf is adapted to the changing employment and economic situation, so that it can also be fully used in a dynamically changing reality, for example by responding efficiently to labour market needs by funding the acquisition of skills in areas where workers may be sought in the labour market of the future. i support the creation of a new instrument because it focuses on such key issues as promoting employment and occupational mobility, investing in education, skills and lifelong learning and promoting social inclusion. support for young people is particularly important. it is necessary because at present 21% of them are not employed within the european union and many young people have left training systems without obtaining a qualification. the adopted report will enable us to respond to these problems efficiently.
in writing. − the european social fund is the main instrument for combating unemployment and social exclusion. in the euro area, the unemployment rate is above 10%, while in spain alone it is already above 26%. therefore, actions to increase the mobility of community citizens, both occupational and geographical, should be encouraged. any regulation on the european social fund is also important because the funds derived from it are directed to specific groups of people rather than to institutions. therefore, any changes that promote education, combat poverty, prevent precarious employment, and activate people of post-productive age are very important. the fund also works to increase the integration into the labour market of people who are in a disadvantaged financial situation. it is also important to create a network of social partners, with the main involvement of ngos supporting the socially excluded and the unemployed. stimulating employment and fostering new jobs is one of the main factors that creates economic growth.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european social fund and repealing regulation (ec) no 1081/2006 (com(2011)0607/2 – c7-0327/2011 – 2011/0268(cod)). in doing so i hope that the current unemployment issues may find a solution. there is currently a 21% unemployment rate amongst young people in the eu and this is unacceptable. the esf is a vital part of resurrecting the workforce and an opportunity to move toward a stronger europe. to continue to improve social cohesion, the four main thematic objectives of the commission proposal on the esf will have to be applied for the 2014-2020 period: ‘promoting employment and labour mobility’, ‘investing in education, skills and life-long learning’, ‘promoting social inclusion and combating poverty’ and ‘enhancing institutional capacity and efficient public administration’. these steps will play an important part of the esf’s success. we must continue to support these programmes as they will lead to a better future for all.

in writing. − the european regional development fund is closing the gap in economic development, productivity and employment levels between eu member states. the erdf is the most important instrument in this respect and the approval of its new shape for 2014-2020 will provide flexibility and allow better tailoring of erdf support to the diverse needs of regions across the union. the new rules set a more limited number of objectives, but they are consistent with the europe 2020 strategy. i am pleased that the regions will have to allocate a certain percentage of the funds to innovation and support for small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the engine of economic growth and employment in the european union. the erdf funds will help to increase the competitiveness of european companies and strengthen their position at international level. support for cities and urban areas will be a particularly important element. in this context, the funds will enable integrated, sustainable urban development. it is very important to give greater weight to the urban dimension of cohesion policy. the rules provide the necessary flexibility in this respect so that the resources are allocated in the most wise way. in this respect, improving coordination between systems was key, precisely to deliver investments for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in line with the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the rules of the regional development fund and the investment for growth and jobs goal. i'm fully satisfied with the outcome of the vote. today's europe needs a new european regional development fund, which provides flexibility for regions to adapt to their situation and needs, while at the same time forcing a concentration of resources on several thematic areas, such as research, technological development and the transition to a low-carbon economy. we're seeing a number of new elements that are expanding the scope of future investment. the fund will support not only infrastructure but also the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, and thus create new jobs. it is worth noting that over the next seven years, up to €300 million has been earmarked for innovation activities in the framework of the sustainable development of europe's cities: this will ensure a stronger focus on the development of urban areas at a strategic level.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur for the proposal for a european regional development fund with the objective 'investment for growth and jobs'. however, the provisions contained in the draft of the fund in question do not meet polish expectations. first of all, much of the space is devoted to low-carbon policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gases, which is a disadvantage for poland, given the role of coal as the main raw material in energy production. there is no doubt that the project's advantage is to support small and medium-sized enterprises, to contribute to the development of infrastructure and to reduce disparities in development between regions. however, it should be ensured that each country is able to decide, inter alia, on its own energy infrastructure, which best corresponds to and serves the interests and security of the country concerned.
in writing. − european territorial cooperation is an important objective of cohesion policy. the lisbon treaty lists territorial cohesion as one of the key objectives of the union, and european territorial cooperation is one of the ways to achieve this objective. the challenges faced by member states and regions increasingly transcend national and regional boundaries and require joint action at the appropriate territorial level. european territorial cooperation allows for joint actions and exchange of experience not only with eu member states but also with border regions of non-eu countries. i supported the report because this instrument needs the appropriate legal framework for its proper functioning. better coordination of programmes, focus on results, simplification are the features that will allow better use of funds. european territorial cooperation is particularly useful in addressing cross-border problems and common local challenges. the identification of investment priorities is an important element of the report and will allow funds to be directed where they are most needed.
in writing. − the european regional development fund is an instrument used to reduce disparities between the regions of the european union. actions and investments to improve territorial cooperation, especially between richer regions and rural, excluded and very high unemployment areas, are important. territorial cooperation is one of the key objectives of cohesion policy, and it is therefore necessary to improve integration between the various actors at both national and regional and community level, and to improve their cooperation with the european union's border regions. support for territorial cooperation initiatives from the european regional development fund is the pursuit of the aspirations of most institutions at all three levels. it is also worth noting that the erdf assistance for territorial cooperation with third countries will increase the efficiency of the expenditure.
in writing. - i have advocated the adoption of new rules on one of the most important european funds, the cohesion fund. it is part of the legislative package of cohesion policy, which, as one of the main areas of union policy, plays a very important role in its development. the cohesion fund is intended to provide financial support for transport investments, environmental projects and innovative energy projects. in view of the above report, we must realize how important it is that we vote unanimously today to adopt it. the cohesion fund is part of the package of proposals governing cohesion policy for 2014-2020. its adoption opens up the possibility of a number of new investments in roads, railways as part of the trans-european transport networks, subsidies for low-emission transport systems, additional investments in the water sector and in the urban environment, the creation of a network of 'smart cities' and many other projects. i am convinced that the new rules of the eu's cohesion policy will guarantee europe economic growth and, consequently, the millions of new jobs so needed in an era of high unemployment in europe.
in writing. − the new framework for the funds aims to improve coordination between the funds and thus to spend funds more efficiently. the new structure of the tasks and objectives of the funds is intended to better achieve the union's overriding objectives of growth and jobs. the cohesion fund will contribute to these objectives by helping member states to reduce the disparities in economic and social levels between the countries and regions of the european union. we cannot talk about genuine european integration when there are still such large differences in the economic performance of individual member states. the cohesion fund is therefore one of the key instruments to bridge these gaps by providing financial support for large-scale investments in infrastructure development or modernisation or environmental protection. the new rules do not significantly change the objectives of the cohesion fund, but subordinate the principles to thematic objectives that translate into specific investment priorities, an approach that ensures clearer procedures and consistency with the objectives pursued by other funds. in view of the scale and importance of the projects financed by the cohesion fund, the support for improving institutional capacity is also explicitly provided for in the regulations.
in writing. − the cohesion fund is of great importance for the development of the european union because of the purpose for which it is intended. it is therefore essential that the provisions and mechanisms governing the operation of this instrument are aligned with the objectives set out in the treaties. the social fund primarily finances investments in the modernisation of railway lines, the improvement of drinking water quality and the management of municipal waste. the cohesion fund is also very important because it is currently financing one of the most important investments in the european union, the trans-european transport network. this in turn contributes to the integration of the community as a whole and to the increased mobility of citizens, especially for professional reasons. investments in maritime and inland waterway transport are also important, as are those aimed at modernising road and air traffic management systems and promoting the development of intelligent transport.
in writing. − strengthening social and economic cohesion in the eu remains an important objective. the european grouping of territorial cooperation (egtc) is helping to achieve this, enabling local authorities and other bodies to carry out joint crossborder projects with partners from other eu countries. i supported the report because the changes it introduced provide simplification, legal certainty and flexibility in the application of the rules, reducing red tape for the group and its potential members. the amendment is particularly important as it provides for approval by tacit agreement after a time limit of up to 6 months for the competent national authorities to examine the application for authorisation to form a pool. this will provide legal certainty to those seeking to form a pool and avoid unnecessary delays. the amendments will also facilitate territorial cooperation in areas such as public transport, energy and water supply, health, education and vocational training by being open to all public utilities. we will also achieve closer territorial cooperation by defining third countries more precisely and more broadly, so that actors from neighbouring countries can engage in cooperation. the key now will be to raise awareness among the institutions, member states and regions of the potential of the european grouping of territorial cooperation so that as many actors as possible can benefit from its resources and opportunities.
in writing. − the european grouping of territorial cooperation is a very important institution to promote and facilitate crossborder cooperation. the lack of a simplified procedure for granting authorisations for the establishment of egtcs discouraged potential stakeholders from setting up these institutions. therefore, the amendment to the tacit approval of the establishment of an egtc after the six-month period for the member states concerned to examine the application should be welcomed. it is also very important to de-bureaucratize procedures and to introduce a division into statutes and conventions and to differentiate the procedures for the constitution of each of these groups. the euct is very important in strategic areas of cooperation such as transport, education, energy and health. another important and well-received change is the clarification of the conditions for the participation of third countries in the grouping, which strongly encourages cooperation. the review of the regulation is also of major importance for strengthening the principle of legal certainty, which in turn is in itself an incentive for cooperation between economic partners.
in writing. - i have never opposed the principle of equal rights for women and men, but the report presented by the femm committee and the amendments proposed by the commission are unacceptable in my opinion. moreover, the union should not interfere so much in the national legislation of sovereign member states. many women hold high and responsible positions and consider that the creation of parities and the guarantee of positions to them on the basis of gender is an insult to their dignity. according to current data, two thirds of all university graduates in poland are women. unfortunately, they often have to overcome the difficulties of balancing work and family life. in poland, unlike in countries such as belgium or france, the state does not provide free care for preschool children. the financial and territorial availability of kindergartens is far from sufficient.
in writing. − the proposed directive on the increase of women's representation on the non-executive boards of companies, aiming to achieve a 40% share of the under-represented sex, is an important step towards better respect for equality as a core eu value. article 157 (3) tfeu provides the appropriate legal basis for the adoption of any binding measures aimed at ensuring the application of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation. between 2003 and 2011, the share of women on company boards increased from 8,5% to 13,7%, an increase of 5,2 percentage points in just over eight years. that's far too little. in march 2011, the commission challenged the top management of listed companies to take part in the 'women on boards - a commitment for europe' initiative, which aims to increase the representation of women on boards to 30% by 2015 and 40% by 2020, but the results were still unsatisfactory and uneven, ranging from 5 to 25%. this confirms the decision to create binding rules requiring member states and companies to put in place appropriate procedures to achieve the objective. a strong common framework will be essential to promote gender balance on boards of all listed companies, offering women greater opportunities to take up senior decision-making positions and to improve the economic performance of companies through their skills. moreover, the introduction of greater transparency in the procedure for the nomination and selection of members of the management board is so far the only way to effectively guarantee diversity and selection on the basis of substantive criteria.
in writing. − as a member of the european parliament, i have been supporting the promotion of women entrepreneurs and their increased presence in business for many years. in the european union, there is currently a shortage not only of women running their own businesses, but also of women on the boards of listed companies. the ambitious target of increasing the representation of women in non-executive directors to 40% over the next 7 years is certainly a major challenge. i welcome the fact that the proposed actions focus on ensuring transparent recruitment practices that ensure equal access for women and men to the highest positions, rather than on creating preferential conditions for women based solely on gender. i also agree with the provision that any sanctions will be imposed on companies by the member states' authorities only if they fail to implement a transparent recruitment procedure, and not if they fail to reach the required 40% female representation threshold.
in writing. - i voted in favour of adopting the report on the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy. this report introduces a number of new approaches to the reform of the cap for 2014-2020. i share the rapporteur's view that simplifying the administrative procedures of the cap will generate additional savings and make the policy more efficient. i also support the proposal to reduce the number of accredited paying agencies to one per member state or region. in addition, a monthly early warning and monitoring system for agricultural expenditure is a good solution to avoid the risk of exceeding the annual budgetary limit. in addition, a common list of indicators to objectively assess the effectiveness of the cap in meeting food production, sustainable management and environmental objectives should be considered. i believe that the new solutions proposed in the report will improve the functioning of the common agricultural policy in the new financial perspective and will be a step forward in simplifying administrative procedures, which will ultimately benefit farmers across the european union.
in writing. − the adoption of the package of regulations for the common agricultural policy between 2014 and 2020 will allow for the timely entry into force of all programmes and timely financing of the cap both in pillar i, i.e. direct payments, and in pillar ii, i.e. investment expenditure. the new cap especially in the case of a country like poland will provide significant support for rural areas and their sustainable development in the coming years, although overall the budget has been reduced by as much as 11%. it should be stressed that rural development with such a reduction requires support from cohesion policy. this is one of the key factors for rebuilding rural jobs and sustainable development.
in writing. − this regulation prepares the financial rules for the future common agricultural policy, improves the functioning of the principle of interdependence and develops the farm advisory system, bringing together provisions on the payment of payments, controls and penalties, the crisis reserve, agricultural advisory services and management and control systems, with regard to direct payments, rural development and the single organisation of agricultural markets. farmers will be able to choose between consultancy services provided by the state or by private companies. an early warning system has been introduced, whereby the farmer is informed in advance of irregularities that are not serious enough to constitute a threat to public or animal health. only after verification that the farmer has taken appropriate action in relation to the irregularity will the decision to impose a penalty be taken, if necessary retroactively. simplification of procedures will apply, for example, to the submission of payment applications by small farms not every year, but once every few years, with annual confirmation of continuation. the rapporteur seeks to link cap financing with management and control mechanisms in a way that is understandable and beneficial to farmers and consumers alike. it focuses on sustainable development, innovation and improving the competitiveness of farms, especially smaller ones.
the rural development fund is the cornerstone of the common agricultural policy and its overriding objective remains economic development and competitiveness in rural areas, including the creation of conditions conducive to employment growth. i hope that in the coming years the regions with the greatest economic backwardness will be the ones most likely to benefit from the aid. agriculture, for example in the masovian region, needs urgent support. investment is the best and most important element to stimulate growth today. the increase in the funds for their direct implementation should therefore have a tangible effect. unfortunately, a number of the solutions proposed in this report do not seem to be conducive to these projects. in addition, the agricultural funds are concerned about proposals that may have excessive environmental burdens that many farms, especially in poorer countries, may find difficult to cope with.
in writing. − the european fund for rural development in the new financial perspective will build on the solutions of the previous programming period. member states will be able to prepare programmes tailored to their specific needs within the framework of union legislation, focusing mainly on improving the competitiveness of agriculture, sustainable management of natural resources and climate action, and sustainable territorial development of rural areas. the priorities of the eafrd include support for knowledge transfer, the promotion of innovation and modernisation in agriculture and forestry, improving the functioning of the agri-food chain, increasing the competitiveness of farms, support for producer organisations, environmental protection and climate change action, and broad economic development of rural areas (infrastructure investment, education, culture, support under the leader programme, etc.). although the negotiations were difficult to win a reasonable position on the issue of disadvantaged areas, the final shape of the document contains provisions that allow the application of the existing rules, so that the farmer receiving unw support today will continue to receive it. the instruments available under the second pillar of the cap will give member states greater freedom to support their own regions, ensuring sustainable rural development.
in writing. − the new single cmo regulation amends existing rules to improve the functioning of the agri-food chain by increasing the benefits of cooperation between farmers through producer and inter-branch organisations. it also proposes to maintain the 'safety net' as a tool to support the industry in the event of crises on agricultural markets. the aid scheme for the most deprived will now be an instrument in its own right. during the negotiations it was agreed that the reference prices would now be considered as 'standard' reference prices, that durum wheat was added to the list of products eligible for public intervention and that the number of products eligible for private storage support was increased. the 'fruit and vegetables in schools' and 'milk in schools' programmes will become more important, using mainly local products. we also won support for hop producers. the sugar quota system will end in 2017 and the milk quota in 2015 (we also call for the creation of new instruments to counter the disturbances in the dairy sector). the european commission has committed itself to report regularly on the activities of the european food price monitoring tool and to publish advice for competition authorities in the member states.
in writing. − the equalization of payment differences between member states is the most frequently used topic in policy discussions. it was negotiated that the payments would be gradually levelled out by increasing them in those countries where farmers receive less than 90% of the eu average, and that the difference between the level of these payments and the eu average would be reduced by one third between 2015 and 2020, so that by 2020 the payments in all member states would not be lower than eur 196/ha. this is not, of course, the immediate leveling of aid that some countries would like, but let us not forget that this is what compromise is all about. the other issues addressed in the document are no less important for the new cap. greening is in a sense to legitimize cap spending. while it does impose additional requirements on farmers, the application of these will not be as drastic as commonly thought. the small farmers' scheme, in its initial proposal of a flat-rate nature, will take account of the size of the holding. support for young farmers under pillar ii will be further increased by increasing their direct payments by 25% and, thanks to the definition of an active farmer, the money will go to those who actually carry out agricultural activities. together with the other solutions, these provisions make the reform of the common agricultural policy really absorbable.
in writing. − due to the prolonged work on the reform of the common agricultural policy, it will not be possible to implement it as of 1 january 2014 as originally envisaged. the report is the result of a process of legislative work that is needed to ensure the smooth functioning of the cap in the next 'transition year'. it is also intended to help european agriculture to enter the new, reformed system easily and efficiently. the rapporteur proposes to extend the rural development actions under the current axis i and ii (competitiveness and environment and land management) which could be applied for in 2014. as the current funding period has been exhausted, new actions will be able to be financed from new envelopes already earmarked for the next financial perspective. axis iii (economic diversification and quality of life) activities, together with the leader programme, will be financed under the current programming period, as the european commission believes that there is sufficient funding for them. the negotiations also agreed that certain provisions of the new cap could be applied as early as 2014. these include the possibility of transferring funds between pillars and redistributing payments to small farms, new transitional national support provisions for countries applying the single area payment scheme, as well as an increase in the maximum level of national coupled support.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the proposal for a regulation on the financial allocation for certain member states, including poland, from the european social fund, which is the main financial instrument of the european union. it improves working conditions and, by investing in people, it equalises opportunities for all eu citizens. i welcomed the vote: 11 billion euro for poland under the esf for 2014-2020 was approved. this money will be used to fight youth unemployment and job creation, which is very important today, and to fight poverty. the money will be available from january 2014. importantly, administrative simplifications and facilitations for small operators have been introduced, which will significantly speed up the use of the above-mentioned funds. this gives us a positive outlook, with the hope that the situation on the european labour market will improve in the near future.
in writing. − with the ep being the only directly-elected eu institution, meps have long been requesting to be allowed to decide when and where to meet. unfortunately, our appeals cannot be granted under the current eu treaty. but treaties can – and must – be changed to adapt to present-day circumstances. in our current reality, between eur 156 million and eur 204 million, and 19 000 tonnes of co2, are spent each year on parliament’s geographic dispersion. ending the multiple seat arrangement is the way forward to ensure greater efficiency and responsibility of our institutions, in both budgetary and environmental terms. one key achievement in our campaign is illustrated by the current report. this report is asking to invoke parliament’s new powers, under article 48 of the lisbon treaty, to propose a treaty change, which will give parliament the right to decide on its seating arrangements. the report is an answer to the appeals of the over 1.27 million eu citizens who signed the online petition calling for a single seat. it further illustrates the efforts of the majority of meps, who have repeatedly and consistently voted in favour of a single seat, to break free from being taken hostage by the member states.
in writing. − the right of the european parliament to decide on its own seat and working schedule is of the utmost importance in the context of the principles of democratic legitimacy and the continuing efforts to reduce the costs of administering the institutions of the european union in the context of a very unfavourable economic situation throughout the community. the estimated cost of the current organisational deployment of the european parliament is up to eur 204 million, representing up to 10% of the annual budget. in addition, consideration should be given to the environmental costs, the time lost in travelling and commuting and the logistical organisation. the building in strasbourg is currently unused for approximately 320 days a year, which generates additional maintenance costs. any organisational changes are therefore necessary to improve the organisation and functioning of the european parliament's work and to remove the regulations which constitute barriers to the institution's ability to determine its own seat and work schedule.

national and union statistical systems, as well as on professional and independent national statistical authorities. the commission’s proposal was driven by these considerations. the european parliament has consistently supported the commission’s agenda in statistics. this was clear in the draft report by the committee on economic and monetary affairs that was adopted almost unanimously last december. however, i have to admit that, after numerous negotiations, the proposal on european statistics has lost some of the ambition and objectives of the original text. firstly, more focus is now given to the eu interinstitutional set-up – such as eurostat status – than to real systemic solutions. in particular, we need to clarify and strengthen the coordinating role of national statistical institutes within their national statistical systems and to ensure that member state governments commit to preserving the professional independence of national statistical institutes, by signing commitments on confidence in statistics. european statistics are dependent on the data provided at national level. the standards and necessary safeguards must, therefore, be the same for all actors at all levels of the european statistical system. furthermore, the amendments do not maintain the union’s institutional balance. that creates an additional imbalance between the european and national levels, in terms of the status of the heads of statistical authorities. therefore, the commission has difficulty in accepting the current amendments in this form, in particular, some of the provisions on the director-general of eurostat. however, the commission is ready to continue negotiations in order to point things in the right direction in this strategic reform. in this respect, i rely on parliament’s support and ambition.

in writing. − the cosme programme aims to support all small and medium-sized enterprises and focuses on economic growth. the programme allocates over eur 2 billion for the period 2014-2020 to enterprises and smes and entrepreneurial activities. the programme supports the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and will contribute to the competitiveness of european smes. the promotion of entrepreneurship is an important objective of the programme. businesses, and smes in particular, are the engine of the european economy, creating jobs and contributing to prosperity, and europeans should be more willing to engage in their own business. unfortunately, the lack of funding for activities can often be a barrier, but the programme also addresses this challenge by facilitating access to finance. i think it is particularly important to support target groups such as young people and women. i am glad that the rules of the new programme do indeed reduce the administrative burden, because these are the kinds of barriers that have discouraged entrepreneurs from setting up companies. it is also important to increase the involvement of organisations representing smes, as they are essential to achieving the objectives of the programme. self-employment and business development, as well as the integration of target groups into business activities, are important sources of growth and jobs at eu level, and the new programme will further support entrepreneurship in the eu from next year.
in writing. - the new programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme) is aimed in particular at entrepreneurs who will benefit from easier access to finance for their business activities, as well as at citizens who have problems setting up or running their own business. it's a step in the right direction. access to finance for smes should be facilitated, an enabling environment for new business creation should be created, entrepreneurship in europe should be promoted and the competitiveness of the european economy should be strengthened. this programme will help unlock the growth potential of enterprises by focusing on stimulating existing industry. this will strengthen the competitiveness of businesses and create new jobs, which should lead to a strengthening of the growth potential of the union economy. it is good that measures are also provided to promote entrepreneurship, which will include the development of business skills and entrepreneurial attitudes, especially among young entrepreneurs and women. according to the european commission, the programme can help 39,000 companies create or maintain 29,500 jobs and bring 900 new products, services or processes to market each year. entrepreneurs, especially those intending to start cross-border activities, will have easier access to credit.
in writing. - i welcome the recognition of competitiveness as a guarantee of employment growth and economic stability in the eu. i also believe that the potential of smes lies primarily in the smooth functioning of the market, both at regional and global level. facilitating access to finance and reducing red tape encourages the development of new businesses and thereby contributes to strengthening economic competitiveness in europe and beyond. in particular, in times of unemployment, action is needed to create new jobs and self-employment.

in writing. − the european programme for social change and innovation (psci), which will be renamed the 'european programme for employment and social innovation' (easi), has a budget of €815 million (for the years 2014-2020) and combines three existing programmes: facilitating access to microcredit, promoting the geographical mobility of workers across the eu and exchanging experience and good practice. we can provide a common, coherent programme structure with clear funding priorities for innovative projects, so as to increase employment and help combat social exclusion. the programme will focus on helping young people to find work, reducing long-term unemployment and social exclusion, combating discrimination and promoting gender equality. we have ensured the continuity of the crossborder partnerships that were threatened in the commission's original proposal. the compromise reached in the informal negotiations between parliament, the council and the commission has enabled us to support this project, which is so important for the future of europe.

in writing. − the customs action programme pursues the fundamental objective of strengthening the internal market through cooperation between customs authorities and officials of the member states. it is a key element in the consistent implementation of union customs law. a number of useful elements have been proposed to promote the financial and economic interests of the community. these include provisions on combating fraud, protecting intellectual property rights, enhancing the competitiveness of enterprises and protecting consumers. the emphasis on computerisation and modern customs procedures and control strategies is reflected in the need to adapt the mechanism to rapidly changing conditions. the concrete solutions will facilitate legitimate trade or reduce the cost of doing business by reducing administrative burdens. they will also improve the functioning of the customs authorities. at the same time, the programme guarantees a certain degree of the necessary budgetary flexibility.
in writing. − the facilitation of trade or the security of products entering the european union from third countries, as well as the effectiveness of the fight against illegal trade, is linked to the operational capacity of border services. the effectiveness of their actions depends to a large extent on the customs action programme approved today, which will provide over eur 547 million to improve the functioning of the customs union. these measures will support cooperation between customs services of different member states, which is crucial to ensuring the integrity of the eu's external borders. the programme will enable joint activities, training and the introduction of fully operational computer systems. to ensure that the programme runs smoothly, the report adopted today divides the programme into general, specific and operational objectives. it is also important to harmonise and standardise customs control procedures to combat fraud, so that it is easier to respond to the dynamic challenges of new customs challenges. it is worth mentioning that one of the priorities of the programme is to facilitate legitimate trade, reduce compliance costs and administrative burdens and protect against unfair competition, which is essential for the competitiveness of european companies, but also for consumers. the programme is very important for the internal market, as it will be significantly strengthened by an efficient and effective customs union.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the current common fisheries policy has been met with general criticism from all fisheries communities and a number of environmental organisations. the effects of the directive were felt most strongly by fishermen, and they were associated with excessive restrictions. the new fisheries policy must give the entire fishing industry a chance to develop. it is not perfect, but it does remove the previous constraints, which were often deeply irrational and at odds with the nature of the fishing industry. the key issue that the new policy introduces is the promotion of the fishermen's profession. this is a fundamental value for the future and development of the industry. the second element is to support the development of small-scale fisheries, which are the basis for the future shape of fishing in europe. the report adopted is also an appeal to fishermen not to abandon their fishing profession.

in writing. the fisheries sector has been waiting for this reform for a very long time. until now, it has struggled with inefficiency, illegal fishing and arbitrariness. it was devastating to the environment and to fish stocks in europe and the world. the sector is now set to benefit from new regulations that aim to restore sustainable fishing and put an end to uneconomic practices. it is also an opportunity to create many new jobs in coastal areas and to develop them further. however, the most important problem to be solved is overfishing in european waters. the new rules will help to restore fish stocks by means of 'fishing quotas'. equally important will be the elimination of discards, with all fish caught counting towards the quota. this is very important in view of the many endangered fish species and the decline in the diversity of the aquatic ecosystem. the positive aspect is that the policy is flexible, allowing many specific issues closely linked to the specificity of the region to be adapted to its general objectives. it is also pleasing to note that the new document is to be implemented as from the beginning of next year.
in writing. the agreement on the common fisheries policy is intended to resolve very important issues. overfishing must be completely eliminated by 2015 to allow fish stocks to recover. the objective should be to achieve a survival rate of the herd. the agreement on the prohibition of excessive discards is also a good step in this direction. excess of wasted fish should be eliminated. in order to avoid the problem of excessive fishing capacity in the future, member states should be obliged to carry out an annual analysis of the fishing capacity of their fleets in accordance with the criteria set by the european commission. the decentralisation of decision-making is also a very important point in the agreement. certain disputes concerning technical rules in specific maritime regions should be resolved by the parties concerned rather than centrally in brussels. this will allow for faster implementation of those elements of the eu environmental directives that are related to fisheries. member states will have to allocate fishing opportunities between fishermen in an objective manner. the criteria for the allocation of responsibilities should include environmental, social and economic criteria. this will help to increase employment and reduce environmental degradation. i hope that the new common fisheries policy will help to stabilise the sector.

mr. chairman, please! deep-sea fishing, above 400 m, can certainly be a threat to the environment. we're aware of the number of species that live in the deep, and we're also aware of how limited our knowledge of the ocean floor is. i therefore appreciate the efforts made to make the proposed project a compromise between environmentalists and fishermen. the draft includes provisions to ensure that the granting of fishing licences is based on scientific analysis, while at the same time requiring fishermen to record and report on deep-sea species. member states will be responsible for assessing the impact of fishing on the state of the marine ecosystem before renewing the authorisation for further fishing. all of this ensures that the principle of sustainable development is being implemented. i would like to add that i am pleased that the market for fishing rights has not been frozen. the possibility of switching allowances will be an opportunity for many fishermen to use their boats and crew more efficiently. finally, i would like to thank the rapporteur for his cooperation and for having taken into account the polish requests for the exchange of fishing opportunities between member states.
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. the european union's agreement with the kingdom of morocco, after many years of negotiations, has a chance of being accepted. this is particularly important in the context of increasing fishing areas with mutual benefits and the sustainable exploitation of natural resources. this agreement is of great importance to both the european union and morocco as a result of their mutual cooperation. thanks to a multi-year negotiation period by the european commission, this agreement guarantees respect for human rights and safeguards economic benefits in a way that is appropriate for all ethnic groups in morocco. the primary objective of the european union, subject to the above conditions, should be to respect the territorial, economic and social integrity of morocco and to focus on economic matters in the fisheries sector. it is a very important and necessary agreement, which i unequivocally support.
madam president! i realize there's some controversy surrounding the new protocol. i have heard many opinions which present this case as a choice between the interests of european fisheries and the struggle for freedom of the people of western sahara. i think that this black and white presentation of such a delicate issue is going too far. i think the fisheries committee's proposal is a sensible one. it takes into account the benefits and consequences for the people of western sahara, while taking into account the moderate legal framework. this has enabled us to find a compromise between the fisheries interests in question and the rule of law that we demand from morocco. the agreement will bring economic benefits while maintaining appropriate fishing standards and environmental consideration. i would like to conclude by saying that i have heard some people say that the agreement with morocco is in breach of international law, but it seems to me that if the matter is not resolved by the un, the agreement should be concluded as it stands.

in writing. – the situation of roma women is far worse compared to that of men. this is partially due to patriarchal and sexist traditions that prevent women from exercising their freedom of choice on issues concerning their lives. as a result, most roma women live in greater poverty then men. they face severe exclusion in the field of employment and are hampered by limited education opportunities, inadequate housing, poor healthcare, general marginalisation and discrimination by majority communities. while national reports on implementing the eu framework for national roma integration strategies (nirs) still fail to take account of the situation of roma women, the current report offers important recommendations to remedy these issues. the report stresses the need for member states to allocate adequate funds to nirs and further develop plans to provide roma women with the means to facilitate their access to education, employment, housing, and healthcare. the report further calls on member states and the commission to strengthen gender mainstreaming, conduct gender impact assessments, and involve roma and womenʼs ngos in the process. adopting this report is an important step towards helping to improve the social inclusion and integration of the roma, in particular of roma girls and women.
