mr. chairman, please! the justice programme proposed by the commission for the period 2014-2020 aims to create a european area of justice by promoting cooperation in civil and criminal matters, the effective and consistent application of union law and facilitating access to justice. in practice, the justice programme is intended to replace the three existing programmes, allowing for a more comprehensive approach to the financing of the justice area. in order to achieve the objectives of the programme, it must be implemented effectively, with due respect for sound financial management and full access to potential applicants. to this end, the commission must ensure transparency in all aspects of the procedure for collecting and analysing applications, while minimising procedural and administrative burdens. in addition, it will also be necessary to monitor the programme systematically both for its effectiveness and for compliance with the principles of equality and non-discrimination in accordance with articles 8 and 10 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i hope that this tool will contribute to improving cross-border cooperation in the area of access to justice.

in writing. − the european commission, acting on a mandate from the council, has opened negotiations with the kingdom of morocco to renew the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the kingdom of morocco. as a result of those negotiations, a new protocol was initialled by the negotiators on 24 july 2013. the new protocol shall cover a period of four years from the date of its entry into force. the main objective of the protocol is to make available to european union vessels fishing opportunities in the waters of the kingdom of morocco, within the limits of the available surplus. the commission relied, inter alia, on the results of an ex-post evaluation carried out by external experts. the overall objective is to strengthen cooperation between the european union and the kingdom of morocco and to establish a framework for a partnership for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the moroccan fishing zone, which is in the interest of both parties.

in writing. - explanation of vote - agreement between the eu and china in the form of an exchange of letters. the european union entered into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights on concessional letters after the accession of bulgaria and romania in 2007 to ensure that the customs union is compatible with wto obligations. negotiations with wto members were aimed at agreeing a mutually satisfactory countervailing duty compensation for the increase in related duties and the resulting significant losses. the compensation issues covered by the agreements concern, first, the compensation of the higher rates and, second, the addition of a pre-accession tariff quota erga omnes for bulgaria and romania (not allocated to a particular country but open to the whole world). following the authorisation by the council to the commission to open negotiations with the countries entitled to compensation, a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters with china was concluded. the compensation agreement mainly concerns agricultural products, i.e. garlic, mushrooms, chocolate, confectionery and tea. the agreement will be implemented on the basis of an implementing regulation to be adopted by the commission. the eu has already concluded similar compensation agreements with australia, new zealand, argentina and the usa. i fully support the conclusion of an agreement on concessional lists for china so that the eu can ensure that the customs union is in line with its wto obligations following the accession of bulgaria and romania to the eu, while ensuring that the people's republic of china remains our reliable trading partner.
in writing. - with the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged the customs union. therefore, in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) (article xxiv (6) of gatt), the european union was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members having negotiating rights on concessional lists of any of the acceding countries in order to agree on a countervailing duty. such compensation is due where the adoption of the eu external tariff system results in an increase in rates above the level to which the acceding country concerned has committed itself under the wto, taking into account the reductions in duties in the same tariff heading made by other partners of the customs union at the time of its establishment. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations under article xxiv:6 of the gatt 1994. the commission has therefore been negotiating with the wto members with negotiating rights the withdrawal of individual concessions in view of the withdrawal of the concession letters of the republic of bulgaria and romania in view of their accession to the european union. negotiations with the people's republic of china resulted in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters, initialled on 31 may 2012.

in writing. − the development of the european union's space policy has enormous benefits for economic development. the technologies used in this sector can be applied in many fields apart from information technology and telecommunications also in agriculture and forestry. satellite monitoring of climate change may even help to prevent disasters. the two most important projects we support in the space policy are the copernicus programme (formerly known as the environmental and safety monitoring programme gmes), whose main task is to prevent emergencies, and the galileo programme, which will soon allow us to use our own satellite navigation system, controlled by civil authorities. the benefits to our aviation, logistics, emergency response and energy sectors, for example, will be enormous. according to the european commission, the value of the satellite technology market (currently around eur 125 billion) will almost double by 2020. the development of the space sector is therefore not to be overestimated. with the right investment support and a forward-looking approach to eu space policy, we can significantly boost the competitiveness of our economy and develop the achievements of humanity alongside other leading countries in this field.
in writing. − the establishment of a space policy at european level shows the eu's willingness to take action of strategic importance. this policy aims to exploit europe's space potential. the use of space is becoming increasingly relevant to the needs of the market and industry. the provisions of the treaty of lisbon constitute the legal basis of european space policy. article 189 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union gives the eu broad powers to shape space policy. on the basis of the provisions of this article, in addition to strengthening the partnership with the member states and coordinating the efforts necessary for the exploration and use of outer space, the union shall establish appropriate relations with the european space agency. european space policy is being implemented in close cooperation between the european commission and the european space agency (esa). esa's mission is to harness the skills of member states by engaging them in the development of space technologies and by supporting industrial innovation. esa's activities have been limited to civilian cooperation with space programmes. in fact, most solutions have a dual purpose, and therefore also for safety. today, services, trade, security, defence depend on the use of space and are interconnected.
in writing. − cloud computing is an innovative technology that enables the use of data and applications, upon accessing the internet, anytime and anywhere. this technology has many economic benefits in terms of reducing costs, improving accessibility and increasing productivity. however, ensuring the safety of data privacy and security of the infrastructure used for the cloud is essential for reaching the full potential of this technology. the report offers important recommendations in that direction; it calls on the commission to invest more in strong fixed and mobile communication networks, which are prerequisite to developing cloud infrastructure; it supports a high degree of interoperability and open specifications for cloud computing, as well as increasing competiveness. additionally, the report underlines the importance to provide users with clear information, particularly when it comes to the jurisdiction covering the data stored in these cloud services. finally, the report urges the commission to establish a clear legal framework on copyright content in the cloud, principally regarding licensing regulations. as rapporteur of the opinion on this report on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, i welcome the final text. i am hopeful its adoption will pave the way to creating an eu strategy for cloud computing – based on our own values and principles.
in writing. − in an era of rapid technological change, the digital internal market is crucial for employment, research and development and the other europe 2020 objectives, especially as we grapple with the consequences of the economic crisis. new technological solutions such as cloud computing contribute to lowering the cost of it infrastructure, job creation, labour mobility and improving competitiveness, and should therefore be informed and encouraged to be used primarily by smes and public administrations, which can benefit from increased efficiency and flexibility of services and reduced costs and red tape. however, it is important that the innovative potential of cloud computing ensures adequate protection of personal data of internet users, in particular sensitive data such as health data, and universal and equal access to online services for all citizens.
in writing. - i voted for the adoption of the report on cloud computing because i am in favour of any action that responds to the challenges that technology and the people who use it present. we've been using cloud computing for a relatively short time, and i think the report on this has come at a very good time. it's time to put some things in order. the market for cloud services is developing very dynamically. according to the european commission, in 2014 it will be worth €148.8 billion. this number means that a huge amount of data will be processed virtually, outside of our computer. this is about ensuring that our data is adequately secured and that we have constant access to it. the project is aware of these problems, which must have found my appreciation. i also appreciate the fact that the rapporteur has taken consumer protection issues into account. the fragmented market, the lack of clear rules governing the change of operator, and the multitude of regulations, which the report shows are unclear to 90% of the users surveyed. all of this makes it imperative that we pass the appropriate regulations as soon as possible. i would like to express my satisfaction once again that the european union is responding to emerging phenomena with the aim of protecting users and further developing technology.
in writing. − cloud computing is a type of data processing model based on the rental of services provided by a service provider in the field of: technical infrastructure (e.g. computers, memory, network equipment, networks); software platforms (e.g. databases, identification systems, tools for building ai, start-up modules) and user applications (e.g. financial, personnel, statistical systems). among clouds, we distinguish those that are: private (corporate), which is part of the organization, but at the same time an autonomous service provider; public, which is an external, generally available provider; hybrid, which is a combination of the philosophy of the private and public cloud. the european commission has taken action to facilitate the adoption of the cloud computing model across all sectors of the economy. this can help to reduce ict costs and can also contribute to increased productivity, growth and employment.
in writing. − berec (body of european regulators in electronic communications) was established in 2009 by regulation (ec) no 1211/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 25 november 2009 establishing a body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec). berec replaced the european regulators group, established by a decision of the european commission in 2002, with the task of developing cooperation and coordination between regulatory authorities and the commission in order to support the development of the internal market for electronic communications networks and services and to strive for a consistent implementation of the provisions of the regulatory framework in all member states.
in writing. - i am in favour of the adoption of the report by mrs ulrike rodust on the common fisheries policy. i believe that the cap as it is today has not met its objectives, and that the union needs a new, reformed policy to manage fisheries resources in a sustainable way. the document in question, which was the result of lengthy negotiations, has a number of positive features. the most important regulation concerns the persistent problem of overfishing. the new rules require that it be eliminated by 2015 and, in specific cases, by 2020 at the latest. the development of a common position on the ban on discards, to be implemented in stages from 2015 to 2019, is also a great success. another regulation concerns the overfishing capacity of the fleet, which member states are obliged to maintain at a level consistent with the available resources and to carry out an annual analysis of the fishing capacity of their fleets. in addition, the new rules provide that member states allocate fishing opportunities among fishermen according to transparent and objective access criteria. in my view, the reform of the common fisheries policy in the form proposed will guarantee the sustainable development of the aquaculture sector, thus ensuring food security. at the same time, it will have the effect of accelerating economic growth, resulting in increased employment for the coastal community.
in writing. − eu agriculture ministers agreed on monday on a fisheries fund for 2014-2020 of around €6.4 billion. it is intended to be a tool for reforming the eu's fisheries policy to combat overfishing. after intensive talks, we reached a compromise agreement on the draft european maritime and fisheries fund and new financial measures for 2014-2020. this is a key decision for the european fisheries sector, because the fund will allow us to reform the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - i am in favour of adopting the reform of the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products. it is an integral part of the common fisheries policy. one of the main objectives of this regulation is to strengthen the role of producer organisations, which should play an even greater role in the fisheries management process. they should be guaranteed adequate funding and have the appropriate tools to monitor the work of their members. i also support the initiative of bringing together producer organisations from different member states, which will guarantee them better competitiveness. it also covers the labelling of products. they will be more readable for consumers by providing information on fishing areas, fish species or the dates of freezing of products. i believe that a common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products is needed in the european union to improve the profitability of the sector, to ensure better sales of these products and to ensure sustainable fishing.
in writing. − the european commission has put forward proposals for the size of deep-sea fishing opportunities in eu and international waters in the north-east atlantic for the years 2013-2014. in line with the scientific advice, the commission proposes to increase the total allowable catches (tacs) for three stocks, to reduce them for 13 stocks and to maintain the tacs at the current level for eight stocks (including zero tacs for six stocks) compared to 2012. the commission proposes to increase the tac for red seabream in waters west of the british isles by 77% in 2013 (up to 4500 tonnes). catches at this level will allow this stock to reach its maximum sustainable yield (msy) by 2015. the commission also proposes to increase the tacs for two stocks of redfish in the western waters (west of scotland and ireland respectively) by 20% and 5%.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i welcomed the extension of the civil protection mechanism to cover all areas of disaster management: prevention, preparedness and response. i consider this to be extremely important, as natural disasters are not limited to the remote philippines, but also occur regularly in central european countries, among others, and threaten the lives of citizens in many eu countries, as this year's floods in the czech republic and germany have shown. the programme implements the lisbon treaty's successive foundations for the protection of the population and is part of a wider policy of 2020 targets to increase the safety of eu citizens, taking into account in particular the risk of natural and man-made disasters. although it is the individual member states that have the primary responsibility for the safety of their citizens, the union has repeatedly shown that the role of coordinator can be beneficial for citizens. that is why i support the draft eu civil protection mechanism and voted in favour of mrs gardini's report.
in writing. - i supported the report on credit agreements relating to residential property. mortgages are the biggest financial burden for many europeans, and they have been for decades. this directive is all the more timely in the light of the economic crisis, which has also had a serious impact on the citizens of the european union. in the light of the above, the institutions of the european union have focused on developing coherent regulations on the taking out of mortgage loans, which until now have not had a common eu legal framework. this document applies to lenders, credit intermediaries and consumers themselves. these rules cover information and the provision of sufficient time for the consumer to compare offers and to obtain reliable advice before the conclusion of the contract. in addition, the report clarifies the definitions of special risk contracts, the principles for assessing creditworthiness or the possibility of early repayment of the borrowed loan. i hope that the proposed regulation on credit agreements relating to residential property is a step forward in restoring the confidence of european union citizens in financial markets. i hope that this directive will guarantee a fair and responsible single market for consumers, lenders and credit intermediaries alike.
in writing. − for many european citizens, a mortgage is one of the biggest financial obligations they have for many years. these loans are necessary for most eu citizens to acquire property, are also of great economic importance and therefore need protection. while there are limited possibilities for harmonising eu legislation on credit agreements relating to residential immovable property, it is important to focus on ensuring a high level of protection for consumers throughout the european union and on ensuring that consumers are informed accurately about the total cost of the credit borne by them. this cost should include interest, commissions, taxes, fees for credit intermediaries and any other fees and the cost of insurance or other ancillary products, if these are mandatory to obtain the credit on the terms offered. it is also important to guarantee the consumer the right to withdraw from the credit agreement within 7 days of the conclusion of the contract, the right to exchange or early repayment of the credit. i also support the introduction of regulations to protect consumers from unfair or misleading advertising practices in mortgage credit advertisements.
in writing. - we have adopted today a directive on credit agreements for residential immovable property. the main objectives of the directive are to protect the interests of borrowers, inter alia by preventing unfair selling practices and by increasing the information obligations of banks. the directive also aims to promote the development of an efficient and competitive european mortgage credit market and provides for the harmonisation of standards for the examination of creditworthiness and the provision of information on credit interest rates and prohibits so-called tied sales. the decision to take out a home loan is one of the most important financial decisions people make in their lives. that is why it is so important that the market for such loans is transparent and consumer-friendly. that is why i voted for this document.
in writing. − global warming caused by the emission of harmful pollutants into the atmosphere, especially co2, is one of the major challenges facing developed countries. the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) has reduced co2 emissions by more than 10% since 2008. the economic crisis, combined with the planned transition to the third accounting period (2013-2020), has resulted in a significant surplus of allowances, leading to a decrease in carbon prices from eur 30 to around eur 7 per tonne. the fall in prices is affecting the lack of use of innovative low-carbon technologies and the commission has therefore proposed the so-called ets backloading, i.e. the suspension of the auctioning of part of the emission allowances, which would in turn stimulate co2 prices. just as i support strengthening climate policy and investing in renewable energy, i am opposed to similar interference in the emissions market. the sharp increase in their prices may have a direct impact on even higher electricity prices for households and industry, especially energy-intensive sectors. analysis shows that the coal-based energy sector in poland will generate costs of around eur 1 billion in 2013-2020, which will be borne by ordinary citizens.
in writing. - compared with wheat, international trade in rice appears to be small. but that doesn't mean that this raw material doesn't matter in the world. rice is a staple food for nearly half the population and is considered strategically important in many regions of the world. however, a large part of the trade is concentrated in local markets, never going to export. southeast asian countries - china, india, indonesia, and bangladesh - are the world's leading rice producers. these countries also account for the majority of the world's consumption of rice, and therefore the rice market is not very internationalised. thailand, vietnam, india, and the united states are among the world's largest rice exporters. rice is not and will not be a strategic raw material for the polish economy. despite the growing preference of native consumers for asian dishes, per capita rice consumption does not exceed the european union average and is much lower than the average consumption in spain or portugal, for example. interestingly, the majority of rice on polish shelves is not sourced from asia but is produced in the european union, mainly in italy and spain. the high duties on agricultural products imported into the union mean that, despite the fall in the price of rice on world markets, polish consumers are unlikely to expect significant price reductions in shops.
in writing. − the greenhouse gas emissions trading system (ets) is designed to reduce the negative environmental impact of european industry. however, the introduction of this method of co2 reduction has created a kind of 'virtual' market, generating huge costs for the operators involved and limiting the operation of plants and power plants in the eu. today, we are in a situation where supply has exceeded demand and the surplus of allowances is driving down their prices. to address this, the european commission has proposed to suspend 900 million allowances after 2013 (backloading). in this way, it seeks to increase the price of the current licences. unfortunately, for countries whose economies are largely based on coal, such interference with the ets can cause a dramatic increase in energy prices. moreover, as a result of this market manipulation, many production facilities may relocate outside the union. i am firmly opposed to this solution, which is likely to have negative economic consequences for many community countries, undermine the credibility of our market and seriously reduce europe's competitiveness on the world stage.
in writing. - today in parliament, despite the strong opposition of polish meps, parliament unfortunately gave the green light to the report of the head of the envi committee, matthias groote, on the freezing of 900 million co2 emission allowances, the so-called backloading. the integration of the co2 market, which the eu says is intended to increase the price of emission allowances and thus encourage companies to invest in low-carbon technologies, is, in my view, another step towards the union's suicidal climate policy, which reduces the competitiveness of european economies. poland may lose pln 4 billion as a result of the implementation of backloading. environmental protection cannot be at the expense of the proper functioning of our industry. about half a million people are employed in the polish mining industry. our job is to protect their jobs. that's why i've consistently opposed interference with the emissions trading system. i regret that the polish government has not succeeded in creating a blocking dinner of states in the eu council that could oppose this legislative proposal.
in writing. − the introduction of the third vote on the provision allowing the commission to dictate the timetable for changes and other actions in relation to the auctioning of co2 allowances is an attempt to use democratic procedures to take undemocratic, economically important decisions without consulting the member states. the commission is clearly determined to do harm to the economies of the most economically weak countries in the name of a climate dogma that unjustifiably links climate change with anthropogenic co2 emissions. baseless, because it's based on an unscientific hypothesis. we should move away from the ets because this european system has not passed the practical test and is inconsistent with the kyoto decisions on this issue (for example, regarding the emission limits imposed by the ec between 2008 and 2012), and does not take into account all market elements, such as the absorption capacity of agriculture and forestry and the monetization of these sectors of the economy on emissions trading. the objective of directive 2003/87/ec is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, not the high price of emission allowances themselves. emissions have already been reduced to the level that was supposed to be reached in 2020, and so by 20 percent last year. the impact of the intervention on individual member states, which will in many cases be associated with a deterioration in the competitive position of the industry, has not been properly assessed. the report had therefore to be categorically rejected.
in writing. - i disagree with the report. yes, i fully agree that as users of this planet, we should care for it so that future generations can use its resources in the same way. but there is a need to be reasonable in all things and not to do anything at all costs. i think that's what happened in this vote, and the vote shows that my vote is not isolated. i'm not sure that the continent's economy is prepared to raise energy prices and reduce its competitiveness, especially at such a volatile time of emerging from the crisis. this is all the more so as the unforeseen decline in carbon prices has not worked to support sustainable scientific and technological innovation and has contributed to reducing incentives to invest in low-carbon technologies and even to making the european market dependent on infrastructure that generates even higher co2 emissions. the predictable result is that when our industry collapses or is moved to a place where it can develop better, europe will be forced to buy these products from somewhere else. regardless of the amount of carbon dioxide emissions at which they occurred.
in writing. − the report on emissions trading was already debated in the european parliament this year. this is one of the most controversial reports, because it addresses a key issue for countries whose energy system is based on hard coal. from my point of view, this is a drive to artificially inflate the price of emissions trading. this solution is not beneficial at all, and is even harmful to poland. i understand the genesis: the root cause of the problem is the reckless political consent of the state authorities in 2007, and then the situation worsened in 2008, accepting these 6 instruments, among them the emissions trading. the decision-makers were under the illusion that poland would be given the 1990 emission level as a basis, and in practice the 2005 level was set for it. the years 1990-2005 led to the collapse of many mines, smelters and other emitters. it took a lot of effort to make huge changes in the economy that don't matter now. that's what made me vote against it.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i voted against the proposal to intervene in the ets market because i believe that the temporary withdrawal of allowances from the market changes an essential element of the ets directive, since it violates the accepted principle of an annual reduction of the market's allowance pool by 1,74%. the eu's emissions trading system, which once again fails, is a pillar of the eu's strategy to combat climate change. the results of the two plenary votes so far are seen as a clear sign of the instability of this market. the compromise proposal voted on today between the council, the commission and parliament sets a dangerous precedent. there should be no agreement in this house to turn the current emissions trading system into a tool for artificially raising the price of allowances, which will in turn lead to higher energy prices in europe. i hope that this kind of interference will not lead to the escape of industry outside the eu.
in writing. - i voted against the report because i believe it will make the situation of european businesses worse. it will lead to an inherently energy-intensive and high-emission industry with higher operating costs, making production in europe even more expensive. this will contribute to the relocation of factories and industrial plants outside the european union. this is particularly worrying given the crisis in which the european economy is mired. withdrawing the co2 allowance from the auction is nothing more than a change of rules in the game. the market mechanism, imperfect but consensual and nonetheless market-based, was turned upside down by a single decision of the european parliament. under the law, the european commission is supposed to assess whether the market is functioning properly or not, and whether the price levels for emission allowances are appropriate.
in writing. − europe needs an eu climate policy and it is always worth striving for ambition. as an organisation of industrialised countries, the european union has a duty to combat the negative effects of climate change and to set a good example of sustainable development for the world to follow. for these reasons, i support european climate policy. but we cannot remain blind to the current economic and social situation and to the disparities in development within the union itself. withdrawing part of the greenhouse gas emission allowances from the market will increase their price, which may lead to curbing of the emissions themselves. in reality, these are just assumptions that could carry much more serious risks, for example in the form of the migration of high-emission industries outside the eu. and that means thousands of jobs. in times of crisis, europe cannot afford to do this. climate policy cannot be an automatic policy; it must always go hand in hand with concern for the employment and well-being of europeans. i am convinced that just as today the majority of germans, french and swedes support the reduction of industrial emissions in the eu, i hope that in the near future the majority of poles will also support this. but it will be difficult to convince them to do so by taking away their jobs and limiting their opportunities to improve their living standards. for these reasons, i have decided to vote against the resolution.
in writing. − the european greenhouse gas emissions trading system (ets) needs to be reformed. this central instrument of eu climate policy was adopted to promote emission reductions. the prices of allowances reflecting the cost of greenhouse gas emissions from electricity generation and industrial production are set in a market-based manner. at the beginning (in 2005) they were around eur 30 per tonne, but recently they have fallen even below eur 3. the economic slowdown, the increase in energy efficiency and the share of cleaner fuels in the energy mix, as well as the accumulation of additional allowances from previous years, have led to a surplus and, consequently, to a large fall in prices. low prices mean that it is not profitable for companies to switch to cleaner fuels or invest in low-carbon technologies. this undermines the credibility of the eu's flagship climate policy instrument. the european commission (ec) is therefore seeking to change the way the ets operates. firstly, it proposes short-term solutions, or so-called backloading, and secondly, structural changes.
mr. chairman, please! the european parliament once again calls for respect for human rights and protests against discrimination on grounds of gender, ethnic and racial origin. this time our focus is on the situation of roma women. the report adopted today shows how dramatic the situation is. roma women in their communities, due to cultural conditions, have a much lower status than men, have a lower education, have difficulty accessing professional work, and are more likely to experience poverty than men. this lower status of women in roma communities is also compounded by the stigma and prejudice against roma in some societies. we often see the isolation of roma from the wider society in which they live every day. the european parliament cannot tolerate such attitudes, which is why it is good that the report has so clearly shown the problems of discrimination against roma women. i am very pleased to have been able to support this report today.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the action plan for a competitive and sustainable automotive industry in europe. it is a very important sector of the economy, employing 12 million union citizens and representing a quarter of world production. unfortunately, as a result of the economic crisis, the car market is now experiencing adverse changes and the biggest decline in car sales since 1995. car production is increasingly being shifted to the countries with the highest demand for cars, the emerging world economies. in this context, i support the proposals of the rapporteur and the european commission to develop a cars 2020 action plan, which aims to develop a strategy to increase the european competitiveness of the sector. in the context of the current situation in the automotive markets in europe, i believe that the focus should be on the strength of their innovation potential. the proposed cars 2020 plan envisages the promotion of new and advanced technological solutions in the automotive industry and the introduction of clean energy vehicles on the market. i believe that investment in research and development of green technologies is the key to maintaining and further developing europe's manufacturing base. i am convinced that in the near future these measures will contribute to the recovery of the labour market and to the competitiveness of the european automotive industry on a global scale.
in writing. - the automotive industry is the litmus test of the entire industry. its corporate structure is conducive to monopolization of industry, elimination of competition and delocalisation. the cars 2020 project has reduced the global competitiveness of european industry to solutions within the countries where the car companies are based. it does not address how cooperation can increase competitiveness and demand. the continuous price competitiveness in the so-called value chain has been underestimated. the solutions resulting from the european environmental objectives are a great opportunity to create sustainable competitiveness. electric cars are the automotive revolution that depends on better batteries. the competitiveness policy of some automotive companies is to underestimate the cost of the final product and to recover it by scraping the price of authorised parts. for this reason, unfortunately, the repair clause is rejected by the countries in which the companies are located. the repair clause across the european market would provide a unique opportunity to create lasting competitiveness for the european automotive industry. this would require the rules on industrial designs to be made more flexible. the union's automotive policy should take into account, through the liberalisation of the production of low-cost spare parts, the improvement of environmental performance and the purchase of cheaper, quality-compatible and safe automotive products.
in writing. − the automotive industry is one of the most complex and complex sectors in the european union. it provides millions of jobs and makes a huge contribution to the european economy. however, the sector has been particularly hard hit by the economic crisis, which is why comprehensive action is so important for a competitive and sustainable automotive industry in the european union. the union internal market is certainly the most important factor for the future success of the european automotive industry. common technical standards, rules on road safety and product safety, and noise and pollution emissions provide a high level of protection for over 500 million european consumers. it should also be borne in mind that the automotive industry, including smes in this sector, is a leader in innovation and advanced technologies (e.g. the ecall system). this is why support for this sector from eu programmes and funds such as horizon 2020, cosme and the esf is so important. it will not only help to maintain competitiveness on the global market, but above all to improve road safety and consumer protection.
in writing. - we are all aware of the crisis the european automotive sector is going through. the figures speak for themselves: in 2012, europe recorded about 12 million units sold, compared to 17 million in 2007. this is the lowest figure since 1995. in this respect, the commission's proposal with the cars 2020 plan was a good starting point, enhanced by the rapporteur's work. the european automotive industry needs new and more efficient financial instruments to boost its growth; it also needs an industrial policy that anticipates the challenges of the future, investing in innovation and competitiveness, and, ultimately, it needs adequate regulatory safeguards to combat unfair competition. the coordination and effective use of the many instruments europe has at its disposal to advance the industrial sector (internal market, international trade, etc.) will be the keys to the recovery of the automotive sector in europe.
in writing. − the coming decade will likely bring a significant increase in car sales in emerging economies. this will give the eu car industry opportunities, accompanied, however by strong pressure to improve sustainability and face increasing global competition. the most important issue is reinforcing the automobile sector as this mean creating jobs and wealth in europe through increasing competitiveness, innovation and the increasing adoption of a sustainable approach towards mobility. the completion of the internal market for cars, including the aftermarket, and an international trade policy aiming at reciprocity are key elements for improving competitiveness. i voted in favour of the report because cars 2020 is a good solution for the ever-growing automotive industry in europe.
in writing. the european automotive industry generates 16% of the eu's gdp and 12 million jobs. since the start of the economic crisis, the european car market, which is considered to be one of the 'mature' markets, has reduced demand for cars from 17 million units per year to 12 million units per year. at the same time, there was a sharp decline in employment directly in production and in services, as well as in ancillary production. today's hearing is to analyse the phenomena associated with the loss of global leadership by the european automotive industry and its social consequences. today's cars 2020 debate was organised under the leading theme 'jobs and the competitiveness of the automotive industry in an economic crisis'.

in writing. − today's rejection of the bill adopted by the parliamentary committee on women's rights and equality (femm) is above all a spectacular victory for pro-life values. it is also a reminder that member states are sovereign states and that parliament has a duty to respect the principle of non-interference in areas reserved to national legislation. the estreli project included a recommendation to eu member states that 'high-quality abortion services be legal, safe and accessible to all within healthcare systems'. the report was controversial not only because of its attempt to legitimize the right to abortion itself, but also other sexual health rights such as sex education. european union law recognises the freedom of parents to raise their children in accordance with their own beliefs and values as a fundamental human right. this freedom was violated by the report's provision of mandatory sex education, according to accepted standards. for this and many other reasons, i strongly condemn the disgraceful report by mrs estreli and i am glad that parliament has adopted an alternative version of it.
in writing. − sexual and reproductive health and rights (srhr) are essential elements of human dignity, and a core basis for social and economic progress. these are also fundamental human rights which all eu countries have committed to respect and protect. today, 10 december, international human rights day, parliament was presented with the opportunity to support and advance the principles of freedom, equality and non-discrimination with the resolution to support srhr for all, in the eu and beyond. today, parliament could have made a real change to the lives of so many women and girls, by voting to support equal access to affordable, high-quality healthcare services, reliable information and counselling. all are essential services for allowing women, men, girls and boys to make free and responsible decisions on sexual matters. unfortunately this opportunity was missed due to persistent campaigns by conservatives and right-wing groups to reject the resolution. acting in this way, these groups have thrown away years of progress on womenʼs rights and gender equality. that is to be deplored. nevertheless, srhr are a common european responsibility; thus we must continue our fight for the right of everyone to have access to affordable healthcare, education and information on srhr.
in writing. - the report on sexual and reproductive health and rights, which is being put to the vote today, raises fundamental questions both in the ethical sphere and in its compatibility with eu law. the european union may act only within the limits and on the basis of primary law. nothing in the treaties reserves to the union the competence to deal with matters of ethics of human life. these issues, including the regulation of abortion, are the exclusive jurisdiction of the sovereign member states. the european parliament cannot impose and promote abortion. the union's task is to promote economic development, not to introduce regulations that are deeply contrary to europe's christian heritage and common sense. i call on all people of good will to reject this unlawful and harmful resolution to the human family!
in writing. − while surrounded by controversy, the decision on the report regarding sexual and reproductive health and rights (a7-0426/2013) is in fact an important document. it outlines the necessity for vital healthcare for women and their rights to obtain said care. in the report however there are certain things that prevent me from fully supporting it. therefore, i have voted in favour of the items that directly assist women in need and have not supported particular matters that are not presented clearly or have conflicting attributes. that being said, i fully and completely support the wellbeing of all eu citizens and will continue to contribute where possible to upholding the highest standards of healthcare for all.
in writing. − the idea of volunteering is a vehicle for the values on which a united europe is based. its role is invaluable in pursuing the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy by generating social capital, stimulating growth and supporting economic and social cohesion in the european union, even if the nature of these activities is not directly linked to economic interest. this is why it is so important to create an enabling environment for volunteering and its widespread availability in all eu member states, and to promote it especially among pupils, students and young people, especially as the role of volunteering is crucial in gaining experience and skills that will then help them to find their place in the labour market. it is therefore necessary to continue the work started in 2011 during the european year of volunteering in order to promote volunteering in all eu countries, to reward the commitment of volunteers and to help tackle the challenges faced by volunteering in the economic crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the scurrie report because i believe that a strong and well-organised volunteering service is an invaluable asset for society as a whole and has a positive impact on the development of human capital. it also helps volunteers to acquire the skills that employers are looking for. the european year of volunteering has shown how much energy and potential there is in volunteering. the activities initiated then and continued have helped to improve the climate around volunteering and to draw public attention to the importance of volunteering. at the same time, however, it became clear that there was still much to be done in the organisational and legal area. unfortunately, non-formal and informal learning, such as volunteering, has not yet been fully integrated into the process of recognition of education. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the member states should implement the council's recommendations in this area as soon as possible. i also fully support the idea of creating a single contact point responsible for volunteering policy and coordination throughout the european union. recognition of volunteering activities and their good organisation will contribute to improving their quality.
in writing. - fellow workers! volunteering has always been a way of supporting other people. i am glad to see that more and more young people in many countries are getting involved in this initiative, which is a great alternative to the existing tools for activating young unemployed people. volunteering is part of the basic labour market service counselling and vocational information. it is an opportunity to gain professional experience, meet interesting people, make new contacts, develop self-realisation and, above all, to strengthen your own skills in the labour market. i believe that volunteering contributes to the development of intercultural dialogue, builds civil society and allows young people to enter the labour market. i am always a supporter of volunteering, i meet young volunteers in my activities and i am full of admiration for their activities, which i always support, and that is why i voted for the marco scurria report on volunteering and volunteering in europe.
in writing. - i abstained in the final vote on the marco scurri report. while i support the idea of volunteering and welcome the broad definition of volunteering, which covers the different forms of volunteering in the member states, i do not think that there is a need for a common european approach to this issue. i also think that there should be no european status for voluntary organisations. this would lead to over-regulation of the sector. this proposal, like several others, falls within the competence of the member states. as a pro-free market mep, i do not think it is right to order member states to introduce compulsory insurance for volunteers or to set up a european voluntary development fund.
in writing. - i voted for the report because i am a huge supporter of the idea of volunteering. i've always thought of it as the purest form of helping other people. not only because volunteering is selfless, but also because it is a self-development activity, and so it is chosen by those who want to expand their skills and qualifications. i'd like to bring up one aspect of the volunteerism that bothers me. well, i often get the impression that volunteers are meant to replace paid labor. the amount of work that volunteers have to do, and the amount of time they have to devote to the tasks involved, sometimes seems overwhelming to me. i understand the times we live in and the difficulties in the labour market that people in the union have to face, but they can in no way justify the behaviour of people responsible for the various types of events and organisations where volunteers are used. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to promote the use of the internet in the european union. i would like to thank the rapporteur for taking up such an important matter and i fully endorse the solutions proposed to promote volunteering in europe.

the next item is the report by marian harkin, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european globalisation adjustment fund (2014-2020) (com (2011) 0608 - c7-0319/2011 - 2011/0269 (cod)) (a7-0005/2013)
madam president! the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to support countries and regions experiencing major difficulties as a result of an increasingly globalised economy. however, it has unexpectedly proved to be a useful instrument in combating the negative effects of the global financial crisis and the associated budgetary crisis in some member states. this is demonstrated by the fact that more than 80% of the applications were motivated by the crisis. many experts point out that it is extremely difficult to prove that the difficulties faced by a company are the result of the process of globalisation. it's much easier to document that they're the result of a crisis. it is good that this possibility has been made permanent for the next financial period. it is also worth noting that the funds will be able to be spent in solidarity to support all workers, including those working through temporary employment agencies or on a self-employed basis. it is important to remember that more and more europeans are working in flexible forms of employment and it would be a mistake not to include them in this programme. finally, i would like to stress that we should all want the eu economy to be in a state where the funds from this fund never have to be used.
madam president! today, more than 2.5 million people are employed in households in the european union. it is a professional group that has a contribution to make to the creation of economic growth in europe. in addition, persons working in households often enable households to take up employment, which has an even more positive impact on growth and employment. unfortunately, many countries still lack adequate legal solutions to regulate the basic issues of employment in households. i am talking about working hours, the right to rest, clear and transparent information about working conditions and employment rates. in many countries, and unfortunately also in the european union, domestic work is characterised by high uncertainty, no employment contract, delayed pay, no social security, as was reported by colleagues here during the debate. moreover, almost 90% of those employed in households are women, very often immigrant women in difficult personal situations. in this context, member states must urgently develop instruments to provide legal certainty for this category of workers. in addition, persons working in households very often form a grey area, which has a negative impact on member states' budgets. we need to put in place solutions that encourage workers to register their activities and ensure job security.
in writing. - mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. ladies and gentlemen! i have no doubt that the adoption of the convention will only bring benefits. we often hear reports of the slave-like treatment of domestic workers. they work without any guarantee of employment, without social rights, for little pay. no one can control the conditions under which these people work and live. it's hard to believe this is all happening these days. the convention proposes a number of solutions to civilize domestic work. these may include the setting of a minimum age for work, provisions on respect for dignity and leisure, recommendations on the preparation of contracts setting out the terms of employment, or the inclusion of these persons in minimum employment provisions. these are just examples to show that we're moving in the right direction. the rapporteur stresses that many of the principles enshrined in the convention are human rights. it is difficult to understand why, until now, it has been possible in europe for people to be deprived of them. i hope that the member states will succeed in developing mechanisms to monitor compliance with the provisions of the convention, despite the difficulties this will entail. in conclusion, i would like to thank the rapporteur for her report. i believe it will change the difficult fate of many people in the european union. their work deserves it.

information on the taxation of this capital. without receiving information from other member states, a single country is not able to manage its internal tax system effectively, especially with regard to direct taxes. the extension of the scope of the exchange of information to new categories, as proposed by the draft directive to categories of capital income, such as dividends or capital gains, of course i consider it useful from the point of view of the effectiveness of tax collection. in my view, we in the econ committee have succeeded in improving the commission's original proposal. i would like to make a special mention in my speech of the amendments which i consider important. we have pointed out that the legal definitions of the various categories of income and capital which will be covered by the automatic exchange of information in the framework of the amendment of the directive are not sufficiently precise. the lack of precision in the definition can cause a number of problems, as the difficulties of interpretation and the ambiguity of the concepts will hamper the effective fulfilment of the tax authorities' duties. moreover, the lack of clarity may result in the scope of the amendment being partly the same as that of other directives. the second important element of the proposal, in which the econ committee took a position, is the presentation in the original proposal of the so-called accessibility condition. the accessibility condition allows member states to retain a certain discretion in the exchange of tax information. by invoking this condition (but subject to certain limitations), a country may not exchange information on a category if it does not keep a register for it for its own tax purposes. not all member states have information on all the categories of income and assets listed in the directive. therefore, it seems to me that removing the availability condition too early may generate inadequate costs. i find the amendment by mr cutaşa to the european commission's mandate to negotiate framework agreements on the automatic exchange of information with third countries extremely valuable. i believe that this amendment, which requires member states to relinquish some of their powers, will strengthen the single market and thus the international negotiating position.

in writing. − this report concerns the european parliament's consent to the ratification by the member states of those elements of ilo convention 189 which fall within the competence of the union. domestic work is one of the most invisible and at the same time unprotected forms of work. the international labour organisation's convention, which requires the protection of domestic workers, is therefore a very important convention. women and migrants are the most likely to be domestic workers, and are often the most exposed to various forms of discrimination and abuse, including serious human rights violations. an important element is the definition of a domestic worker as a person who performs work in or for the home, while at the same time obliging the signatory states to protect the fundamental rights associated with the traditional employment relationship. i voted in favour of this important report.

in writing. − the transport of radioactive materials is often international, cross-border, and therefore needs to be regulated at community level in addition to national regulations. it would be desirable to establish a common system of registration of carriers and to transfer some of the national competences to the european commission. the sometimes divergent national procedures would be replaced by common union procedures for the authorisation of carriers of radioactive materials, reporting and surveillance. this unification of procedures would reduce the administrative burden in practice and ensure more effective control of transport throughout the eu. unfortunately, this regulation does not take due account of the problem of carriers who are unable to provide full protection against the dangers of ionising radiation. if such incidents occur, the transport of radioactive material should be stopped immediately, all countries where such transport was foreseen should be notified of the risk and the carrier should be required to comply with strict transport rules, as this is fundamental for the safety of people and the protection of the environment.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the problem of milk production in mountain areas, less-favoured areas and the outermost regions. given that the milk quota system will be abolished by 2015, it is the milk producers in those areas who will be most affected by the changes. the situation is all the more dramatic because for the inhabitants of mountain farms, milk production is the main source of income, an integral part of the culture of these areas and often the main driving force of the local economy. the commission notes that the milk quota system is not a system of quotas, but a system of quotas for milk. i therefore believe that a specific programme to support the dairy sector in less-favoured areas is necessary to prevent negative economic and environmental impacts in these areas.
in writing. − one of the key objectives of the new cap is to support agriculture in less-favoured areas, mountain areas and the outermost regions. due to the cultural and social conditions linked to tradition, agricultural activity in these areas is usually directed towards animal husbandry and milk production. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market and that it is compatible with the internal market if it is granted in accordance with the rules on state aid. almost 10% of the milk produced in the union is produced in mountain areas, and this percentage is much higher in countries such as austria, slovenia and finland. very often they are provided by small and medium-sized family farms, for which this production is the only source of livelihood, and withdrawal from it would result in migration to urban areas. the small variation in agricultural activities due to the terrain and climate, the higher production and transport costs and the specific infrastructure are challenges that producers in disadvantaged areas have to deal with on a daily basis. we must therefore support regional programmes for the development of mountain areas, the nuw and the outermost regions, which guarantee the development of markets, increase competition and the quality of the products produced there. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road.
in writing. − the european dairy sector is important in the new common agricultural policy for 2014-2020. at its last meeting in strasbourg (9-12 december 2013), it voted to maintain milk production in mountain areas, less-favoured areas and outermost regions following the expiry of the milk quota system. for the first time in 31 years, the dairy quota, which expires in 2015, is not included in that sector. i support the abolition of milk quotas and the liberalisation of the milk market, which will take place in 2015. however, some negative developments can be expected in less-favoured areas and in the outermost regions, as milk production is often the only source of income for these regions. the local community is heavily dependent on the dairy sector and should be supported. further action at european level is most needed to ensure a secure future for this sector. the creation of decent living conditions for farmers must be ensured, with a focus on the most vulnerable areas. in view of the population living in mountain areas, as well as in disadvantaged or remote areas, i vote in favour of the report presented by the committee on agriculture and rural development and agree that this issue cannot be ignored or left unresolved.
in writing. − the european dairy sector faces major challenges after quotas expire in 2015. this substantial change is likely to cause disruption in the dairy sector, in particular in smaller farms and in disadvantaged and outermost regions. for these regions, milk production is often the only source of income and the local community is largely dependent on the dairy sector. further action at european level is necessary to ensure a secure future for this sector and to avoid the rural depopulation and the negative economic and environmental impacts. milk production is associated with high costs for small farms and milk producers' associations should be supported in order to allow small farms in those areas adequate market access and income. the rapporteur believes that the so-called milk package, which aims to strengthen the negotiating position of producers, is only a first step, but it is not enough to ensure the future of milk producers in the least-favoured areas. furthermore, it is of great importance to continue monitoring the effects of the abolition of quotas, especially in less-favoured areas and in the outermost regions. i fully support the evaluation report and the proposals contained in it, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of adopting a report on disaster resilience and risk reduction in developing countries. the recent tragic events in the philippines after the typhoon show us how often we are witnessing all kinds of natural disasters today. they are the result of ongoing irreversible climate change, improper land use or environmental degradation. as a result, millions of people worldwide suffer from hunger and malnutrition. i therefore believe that action to reduce the risk of natural disasters is a matter of priority. continuous work is needed to improve early warning systems, especially in countries most at risk of natural disasters. another method of prevention is to put in place risk assessment programmes, to finance preventive procedures, which are much less expensive than repairing the effects of a disaster. i hope that through long-term risk assessments, effective cooperation between governments, local authorities and humanitarian organisations, we can work together to reduce the risk of natural disasters worldwide.
in writing. - i voted to accept the report. particular attention should be paid to the situation of women with disabilities in developing countries, where 80% of the disabled population live. a key aspect of eu action towards women with disabilities should be direct action aimed at them to build their acceptance of disability and their ability to cope with the next stages of life.
in writing. - the draft resolution deals with a very important issue. it raises the issue of discrimination against women on grounds of gender and, in addition, discrimination on grounds of disability. we have repeatedly drawn attention to the unacceptable practices of women being treated worse in terms of access to employment, equal pay, a higher risk of unemployment than men, and lower pensions due to shorter periods of employment due to childcare or disabled family members. in addition to these negative effects of gender discrimination for women with disabilities there is also discrimination on the basis of their disability. this double discrimination very often contributes to the social exclusion of women with disabilities and makes these women, deprived of the support and tools to make their lives easier, experience deepening poverty. this is why we need to develop and promote programmes for women with disabilities, both at eu and national level, which will give them opportunities for greater social inclusion. i therefore call on the commission to work with the member states to develop the solutions needed to achieve this and to integrate them into the social policies of the european union.
in writing. − the retail sector is one of the pillars of the single market and is of strategic importance to the eu economy, accounting for 11% of gdp and 15% of all jobs in the european union. it is also of great social importance, as it is composed mainly of thousands of micro- and family-owned businesses. unfortunately, the retail sector still faces many obstacles, barriers and unfair trading practices that make it possible for it to develop sustainably within the internal market. long-term measures are therefore needed to help the sector develop, especially in times of crisis. the european retail action plan should, on the one hand, focus on removing barriers that undermine consumer confidence and directly harm the interests of the retail sector, such as unfair trading practices, product reclassifications or territorial supply restrictions. on the other hand, it should stimulate its development by promoting e-commerce, lowering vat and improving access to sources of finance and capital markets, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the retail sector is one of the main components of the labour market, providing employment at 15% of all jobs in the member states of the european union. retailers operating in more than one country should be provided with harmonised requirements for their products so that compliance with administrative requirements does not create additional barriers to doing business.
mr president, commissioner, the directive on maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management is a landmark development for the eu’s maritime policy. it sets up, for the first time, a framework for coordinated and systematic management of maritime space in all member states. its usefulness derives primarily from the certainty that it provides for projects and new industrial transport investments. usefulness comes also from the capabilities it offers for environmental protection. maritime activity spills across national borders and, as a result, cannot be managed effectively without eu action. in this respect really we need community methodology. the position of the parliament was formed through close cooperation between members of the committee on transport and tourism and the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. it will, without doubt, help to make maritime spatial planning the driving force for many new investment projects concerning sustaining growth in our seas and land around. madam rapporteur meissner: congratulations!
the green infrastructure project, which was prepared by the european commission and for which salvatore tatarella was responsible in the environment committee, is a very important project. we must remember that natural resources are not inexhaustible, especially when they are misused. nature has not only aesthetic value, but is also the element behind such sensitive parts of our lives and economy as providing drinking water, retention, purifying the air from pollutants or regulating the climate at a local level. this is why this eu project, which involves the sustainable use of nature in infrastructure projects, is so important. for example, in poland we are faced with the problem of river regulation, and therefore this programme can be an opportunity to use the most advantageous and naturally neutral methods of retention, minimising the use of so-called grey, i.e. conventional infrastructure. i also welcome the proposal to integrate green infrastructure issues more widely in other areas such as transport, agricultural policy and spatial planning. the projects under discussion may be part of a wider eu policy to reconcile economic development with environmental protection. this document should be an inspiration for regional policies in europe and should be the subject of debate amongst those politicians and citizens who will be involved in the development of sustainable development agendas in urban and municipal policies.

in writing. − in view of the increasing number of cases before the ets and the increasing length of time it takes to deal with them, an increase in the number of judges in the court seems to be the most sensible solution. i hope that the guidelines adopted today by a large majority on the next step towards reforming the eu judiciary will provide the impetus for the council to break the deadlock on this issue. i understand that finding a formula for selecting additional judges that satisfies all parties is not an easy task, but it is time to look constructively at possible solutions. the european parliament is proposing one of them and wants to start a discussion with the council which i hope will lead to a concrete proposal in the near future on how to elect additional judges to the court. i believe that any further delay in this decision can only have a negative impact on the efficiency and effectiveness of the union's judiciary, which is why i voted in favour of the proposals put forward by mrs thein.
in writing. − given that a clean and healthy environment is one of the european union's priorities, support for eco-innovation is essential to achieving this. environmental challenges such as climate change and limited resources require change and radical action, in which green technologies can play a key role. eco-innovation is not only beneficial for environmental reasons, but also a response to the crisis that is engulfing europe, especially among young people. the organic industry already creates 3.4 million jobs and, with the help of the union, can become a major employer of high-quality jobs. europe is currently a leader in the development of new technologies, but there are many barriers, such as access to finance or consumer awareness, which will further accelerate their development. with clear rules that support eco-innovation, europe can create competitive manufacturing companies and become a leader in environmentally-efficient production too.
in writing. −eco-innovation is a form of innovation that aims to make significant and visible progress towards sustainable development, with the aim of making more efficient and responsible use of natural resources. environmentally friendly innovation aims, for example, to reduce co2 emissions and to use resources such as water and other natural resources more efficiently. the report highlights the potential of eco-innovation to stimulate the economy and increase competitiveness and employment. this is further supported by the fact that eco-innovation generates environmental benefits and can play a significant role in an efficient, low-carbon economy, thereby addressing global challenges such as climate change, scarcity of natural resources and other food security issues. in order to accelerate the development of green innovation and to better exploit its potential, further action is needed in various areas, such as strengthening the legal framework for sustainable development in different sectors, investing in education, training and retraining, facilitating access to finance through better use of existing financial instruments. improving the use of resources and energy and engaging in a wide range of innovations will improve the environment and lead to new industries and new jobs in the coming years. the eu should support and promote successful eco-innovation.
mr. chairman, please! access to basic banking services is a prerequisite for participating in socioeconomic life in today's world. however, the world bank estimates that 58 million people in the european union do not have a bank account or have difficulty opening one. unfortunately, this problem also affects people who take up employment in another member state but do not have a permanent address. in view of the increasing mobility of workers and the principle of free movement of persons, these disadvantages must be eliminated. some of the proposed provisions, however, concern matters that should be left to the national banking legislation, for example, requiring all providers to offer basic payment services would mean that non-banks that deal with money transfers would also have to develop such products.

in writing. − i strongly supported the joint resolution on the outcome of the eastern partnership summit in vilnius, mainly because of the issues related to ukraine. despite the lack of an association agreement at the summit, ukraine must not close the road to the union. recent events on the maidan show the strong support of the ukrainian public for pro-eu ideas. the disagreement with the decision of the authorities is obvious, which is why meps should not limit the european aspirations of ukrainian society. we need concrete solutions to help with integration. one such desirable solution is the abolition of visas for ukrainians. it's a remedy that can change the current stalemate in relationships. i strongly support the resolution's strong condemnation of the violence used on the night of 9-10 and 10-11 december against peaceful protesters. another important point in the resolution is the condemnation of russia for exerting economic and political pressure on ukraine to pull it away from the european union. the resolution calls on the member states to open up to ukraine by strengthening cooperation in research, youth exchanges and increasing the rates of available scholarships, and further emphasises that further steps should be taken to integrate ukraine into the internal energy market.

in writing. − the constitutional characteristic of each state is its sovereignty, i.e. the free, independent and autonomous exercise of political power within its own territory. unfortunately, too much integration of the european union can threaten this sovereignty, and therefore we must be very cautious about any legislative initiative that interferes in this area. the report by mr gualtieri and mr trzaskowski calls for further unification of the european union, for the creation of a de facto economic and monetary union, which must necessarily come at the expense of taking away certain powers from the authorities of the member states. the report's basic recommendation to strengthen the union's competences, in particular in the field of economic policy, and to increase budgetary capacity and the role of the commission and the prerogatives of parliament is, in my view, unacceptable.
