on behalf of the ppe group. the conflict in the central african republic is clearly escalating. as of mid-2012, the seleka forces have been engaged in a number of violent acts against the civilian population. moreover, women and children are victims of this violence with alarming frequency. the scale of the violence, which i have to speak of with great concern, is confirmed by the fact that on december 5 alone, 400 people were killed in 72 hours in bangui. the fact that these acts of violence are being carried out by armed groups with modern weapons, including heavy weapons, is even more worrying. it's good that the un security council has asked for the preparation of a possible peacekeeping mission. i am convinced that the european union should support these efforts. france cannot be left alone in its efforts to stabilise the situation in the central african republic. the european union should be involved in the preparation of a political plan for this country that would lead it to the establishment of a rule of peace and law.
mr. chairman, please! the central african republic is a classic example of a country that, despite its economic potential, is embroiled in regional, ethnic and religious conflicts due to its disastrous geographical location and has become one of the poorest parts of africa. the country has been mired in a political and humanitarian crisis for a long time. there is an increasing number of clashes between christians and muslims, and a nationwide wave of sexual violence, torture, executions, and religious clashes. various organizations, including the united nations, have long warned that further escalation of the conflict could lead to mass killings and outright religious warfare. all attempts to alleviate the situation have been in vain. we all need to be aware that without outside intervention, the crisis in the central african republic will only deepen.
in writing. in 1984, the chinese regime passed a law legalizing organ harvesting from executed prisoners. however, both the law and the practice seem to fall far short of the requirements of the world health organization. the lack of transparency in the process is due to the fact that the rules are vague and difficult to control. the practice of the chinese authorities to kill religious and political prisoners in order to sell their organs for transplantation is also reprehensible. this also coincides with the brutal campaign of persecution of falun gong practitioners in china for many years, who are not allowed to receive organ transplants because of their faith. organs are also harvested from them, in violation not only of international legal standards but also of religious and ethical ones. i will continue to stress that the european parliament has a duty to respond to situations where fundamental values and human rights are violated. in this respect, i note that the declaration by the goc that it will gradually withdraw from the above practice from 2015 is insufficient. i therefore support today's resolution and call on the chinese government to immediately stop harvesting organs from prisoners who do not consent to it. at the same time, i believe that it is necessary to punish those responsible for these reprehensible practices. i also hope that our resolution will draw the attention of the relevant international organisations to this issue, thereby forcing an appropriate response from the chinese institutions.

in writing. how to reconcile economic development with increasingly stringent environmental requirements is a crucial issue today. one of the possible answers is certainly eco-innovation. eco-innovation aims to introduce new products that not only benefit producers and consumers, but also drastically reduce the negative impact on the environment. this eu project, which is designed to support entrepreneurs in all sectors, will, however, place particular emphasis on the following sectors: waste, construction products and food products. research and development funding can help to remove barriers to competitive business solutions that are sustainable. at the same time, innovation gains can have a positive impact on the competitiveness of union products in the world, by contributing to growth in outlets and jobs within the union, which is particularly important in times of economic crisis. at the same time, i believe that support for this type of innovation can have a positive impact on the eu's wider climate goals. investments, if properly targeted, can bring potential emissions reductions and energy efficiency gains to the union economy. i would therefore like to support the current wording of the report.
